   180→
   181→## Demos
   182→
   183→This repo comes with _lots_ of examples to demonstrate how to solve common and complex problems with
   184→Sharing. Check out [this](./Examples) directory to see them all, including:
   185→
   186→  * [Case Studies](./Examples/CaseStudies):
   187→    A number of case studies demonstrating the built-in features of the library.
   188→
   189→  * [API Client](./Examples/APIClientDemo):
   190→    A demo showing how shared state can be powered by an API client.
   191→
   192→  * [FirebaseDemo](./Examples/FirebaseDemo):
   193→    A demo showing how shared state can be powered by a remote [Firebase][firebase] config.
   194→
   195→  * [GRDB Demos][sharing-grdb-demos]:
   196→    [SharingGRDB][sharing-grdb-gh] is a lightweight replacement for SwiftData and the `@Query`
   197→    macro, powered by Sharing and [GRDB][grdb]. The library contains a number of
   198→    [demos][sharing-grdb-demos].
   199→
   200→  * [WasmDemo](./Examples/WasmDemo):
   201→    A [SwiftWasm][swiftwasm] application that uses this library to share state with your web
   202→    browser's local storage.
   203→
   204→  * [SyncUps][syncups]: We also rebuilt Apple's [Scrumdinger][scrumdinger] demo application using
   205→    modern, best practices for SwiftUI development, including using this library to share state and
   206→    persist it to the file system.
   207→
   208→[firebase]: https://firebase.google.com
   209→[grdb]: https://github.com/groue/GRDB.swift
   210→[swiftwasm]: https://swiftwasm.org
   211→[scrumdinger]: https://developer.apple.com/tutorials/app-dev-training/getting-started-with-scrumdinger
   212→[sharing-grdb-gh]: https://github.com/pointfreeco/sharing-grdb
   213→[sharing-grdb-demos]: https://github.com/pointfreeco/sharing-grdb?tab=readme-ov-file#demos
   214→[syncups]: https://github.com/pointfreeco/syncups
   215→
   216→## Installation
   217→
   218→You can add Sharing to an Xcode project by adding it to your project as a package.
   219→
   220→> https://github.com/pointfreeco/swift-sharing
   221→
   222→If you want to use Sharing in a [SwiftPM](https://swift.org/package-manager/) project, it's as
   223→simple as adding it to your `Package.swift`:
   224→
   225→``` swift
   226→dependencies: [
   227→  .package(url: "https://github.com/pointfreeco/swift-sharing", from: "2.0.0")
   228→]
   229→```
   230→
   231→And then adding the product to any target that needs access to the library:
   232→
   233→```swift
   234→.product(name: "Sharing", package: "swift-sharing"),
   235→```
   236→
   237→## Community
   238→
   239→If you want to discuss this library or have a question about how to use it to solve a particular
   240→problem, there are a number of places you can discuss with fellow
   241→[Point-Free](http://www.pointfree.co) enthusiasts:
   242→
   243→  * For long-form discussions, we recommend the
   244→    [discussions](http://github.com/pointfreeco/swift-sharing/discussions) tab of this repo.
   245→
   246→  * For casual chat, we recommend the
   247→    [Point-Free Community Slack](http://www.pointfree.co/slack-invite).
   248→    
   249→## Companion libraries
   250→
   251→Sharing is built with extensibility in mind, and there are a number of community-supported libraries
   252→available to enhance your applications:
   253→
   254→  * [SharingGRDB](https://github.com/pointfreeco/sharing-grdb): A lightweight replacement for
   255→    SwiftData and the `@Query` macro.    
   256→  * [SharingCloud](https://github.com/KeithBird/sharing-cloud): Sync shared data across devices via
   257→    iCloud.
   258→  * [SharingFirestore](https://github.com/bitkey-oss/sharing-firestore): Real-time synchronization and real-time queries powered by Firebase's Firestore.
   259→  * [SharingRemoteConfig](https://github.com/zunda-pixel/sharing-remoteconfig): Real-time Remote Config via Firebase.
   260→
   261→If you'd like to contribute a library, please [open a PR][library-pr] with a link to it!
   262→
   263→[library-pr]: https://github.com/pointfreeco/swift-sharing/edit/main/README.md

## Swift Actor Isolation Patterns (2025)

### Swift 6.2 Default Actor Isolation
Default Actor Isolation in Swift 6.2 allows you to run code on the @MainActor by default. This new Swift compiler setting helps improve the approachability of data-race safety, which was set as a goal for the Swift team in their February 2025 vision document.(no content)You can run your code on the main thread without explicit @MainActor annotations using the new option to isolate code to the main actor by default. This option is ideal for scripts, UI code, and other executable targets.

### Key Actor Isolation Concepts

By making use of the nonisolated and isolated keywords, we gain precise control over actor isolation.(no content)Using the isolated keyword for parameters can be pretty useful for preventing unnecessary suspension points. In other words, you'll need fewer await statements for the same result.(no content)The actor model defines entities called actors that are perfect for managing shared mutable state. Actors allow you as a programmer to declare that a bag of state is held within a concurrency domain and then define multiple operations that act upon it. Each actor protects its own data through data isolation, ensuring that only a single thread will access that data at a given time.

### Distributed Actors for Real-Time Systems

Swift's take on location transparency is expressed and enforced in terms of actor isolation. The same way as actors isolate their state to protect from local race conditions, distributed actors must isolate their state because the state "might not actually be available locally" while dealing with a remote distributed actor reference.(no content)The capability to share actor references across to other (potentially remote) distributed actors is crucial for location-transparency and enables developers to implement "call me later" style patterns.

### Modern Data Layer Patterns

For proper actor boundaries, network calls should happen on background actors while UI updates stay on the main actor. The recommended approach is to use explicit actor boundaries with a separate NetworkManager actor for network calls.(no content)For non-UI repository and data layer code, safe concurrency patterns should be used without @MainActor shortcuts.

### Best Practices

Key recommendations include: Actors protect mutable state—use actor to encapsulate and protect data that needs to be accessed concurrently, preventing race conditions. @MainActor is for UI updates—always use @MainActor for code that directly interacts with UIKit or SwiftUI. @globalActor is for shared instances—when you need a single, globally accessible actor for managing shared resources.(no content)Prefer structured concurrency (child tasks, task groups) over unstructured tasks. Use Task.detached only with a clear reason.

**Note:** The search didn't return specific results for WebSocket-based real-time sync engines with actor isolation. You may want to search more specifically for "Swift WebSocket actor" or "Swift real-time sync actor" for more targeted information on that particular use case.

## Point-Free 2025 Updates on Swift Concurrency & TCA

### Upcoming Concurrency Changes

Swift and Xcode's new concurrency defaults—"approachable" concurrency and main actor isolation—force Point-Free to completely rethink how their libraries approach concurrency.(no content)As a result, they have many major releases in the works, including Case Paths, Dependencies, Swift Navigation, and more.(no content)A lot has happened in the Swift language since they first covered concurrency, and they are working on an updated series that goes back-to-basics and explores a topic that is paramount to Swift's concurrency paradigm: isolation.

### Composable Architecture 2.0

Their flagship library, the Composable Architecture, is getting major updates that will make it both easier to use and more powerful. They have assessed every bit of feedback from their large user base and are bringing improvements to nearly every facet of the library.(no content)In the Composable Architecture 2, you will be able to achieve all functionality (presentation, navigation, bindings, lists, and more) with fewer concepts and in fewer lines of code.

### Approachable Concurrency Considerations

When using Approachable Concurrency with NonisolatedNonsendingByDefault enabled, you need to make nonisolated client closures `@concurrent @Sendable` to avoid crashes.

### Related Libraries

Point-Free also maintains:
- **Concurrency Extras**: A library that includes tools to help make your concurrent Swift code more versatile and more testable.
- **Dependencies**: A dependency management library inspired by SwiftUI's "environment."

### AI Skill Documents

Point-Free is working on a collection of AI skill documents they call "the Point-Free way." These documents are hyper-tuned to seed AI editors with context needed to work optimally with their libraries, covering domain modeling, controlled dependencies, embracing value types, and making code easier to preview and test.(no content)These documents will be free to all subscribers in early 2026.

## Swift 6 MainActor UI Updates Pattern

### Key Concepts

The compiler with Swift 6 language mode will prevent you from mistakes when using the @MainActor attribute.(no content)If you try to change UI-related values from a background thread, Swift 6 won't let you — and that's a good thing.

### The Problem Swift 6 Addresses

If you launch a task with `Task{...}` and update some state without using @MainActor, things can go wrong. And with Swift 6's strict concurrency model, the compiler will now tell you immediately when something is unsafe.

### Recommended Patterns

**1. Mark the entire class with @MainActor:**

You could create an @Observable class with two properties, and because they will both update the UI you would mark the whole class with @MainActor to ensure these UI updates always happen on the main actor no matter where they are triggered from.

Example pattern:
```swift
@Observable 
@MainActor 
final class CounterModel {
    var count: Int = 0
    
    func incrementAfterDelay() {
        Task {
            try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(1))
            count += 1 // ✅ Safe, isolated to MainActor
        }
    }
}
```

Because it's clean, simple, and now all methods and properties become safe by default.

**2. Use @MainActor on specific functions:**

When calling an @MainActor function from a background thread, Swift automatically ensures it runs on the main thread.

```swift
func fetchData() async {
    let data = await fetchFromNetwork()
    await updateUI(data)
}

@MainActor 
func updateUI(_ data: String) {
    // Safe UI updates
}
```

**3. Use with SwiftUI's .task modifier:**

@MainActor Annotation ensures that property updates occur on the main thread.

### Important Considerations

There's no need to use DispatchQueue.main.async anymore. However, using the global attribute to restrict any access to the main thread is recommended.(no content)All of this only works when using Swift's new concurrency system. When using other concurrency patterns, for example completion handlers, the @MainActor attribute has no effect.(no content)@Observable and @MainActor can be used together, and when using both, otherwise unmanaged State updates all occur on the main thread.

### Best Practices

Marking an entire class with @MainActor might lead to unnecessary main-thread execution. Use it only where needed.(no content)In Swift 6, @MainActor isn't just a "nice to have"— it's essential for writing safe, modern SwiftUI code. But don't overuse it. Use it only when working with UI-bound state.

## Swift Macros: @Observable and Attached Macros

### Overview of @Observable Macro

The @Observable macro can help you simplify models and improve your app's performance. It's designed to help you learn the fundamentals of the macro and find out how to migrate from ObservableObject to Observable.(no content)With the introduction of the new Observation framework and the @Observable macro at WWDC23, Apple kicked off a significant transition in how SwiftUI handles state, data flow, and view updates. Now, in 2025, this model has matured into the default way of building reactive SwiftUI applications.

### How @Observable Works

To declare a type as observable, attach the @Observable macro to the type declaration. This macro declares and implements conformance to the Observable protocol to the type at compile time.(no content)The @Observable macro uses the new macro system in Swift. It tells the Swift compiler to transform your code from what you wrote to an expanded form that makes the type able to be observed.(no content)The @Observable() macro generates source code at compile time, providing an observing capability to your code. Invisible @ObservationTracked macros are also generated in the background during this time.

### Types of Swift Macros

On a broader level, we can divide macros into two categories: freestanding and attached. While attached macros are put in front of a declaration, freestanding macros are placed on their own. Both freestanding and attached macros have knowledge about their context.

### Benefits Over ObservableObject

The @Observable Macro was first introduced during WWDC 2023 to replace ObservableObject and its @Published parameters. The macro allows you to remove all published properties while still being able to redraw SwiftUI views when a change occurs automatically. The new macro prevents unnecessary SwiftUI redraws.(no content)In iOS 17, we gained the new @Observable macro.(no content)When you're working with an ObservableObject in SwiftUI, you have to explicitly opt-in to observing. With @Observable, this is no longer needed.

### Macro Expansion Details

The Observation module includes two additional macros that can annotate properties of observable types. The @ObservationTracked macro is added to stored properties by the @Observable macro expansion, and converts a stored property to a computed one with access and mutation tracking. Developers generally won't use @ObservationTracked themselves.(no content)The @ObservationIgnored macro acts as a marker for properties that shouldn't be tracked. The @Observable macro expansion adds @ObservationIgnored to the underscored stored properties it creates. Developers can also apply @ObservationIgnored to stored properties that shouldn't be included in observation tracking.

### Important Considerations When Migrating

You need to use the @StateObject property wrapper with ObservableObject and use the @State property wrapper with @Observable. This is the key difference and the underlying cause for the difference in initialization behavior.(no content)The correct way to architect your app is to store all (app-level or global) @State properties in your top-level App struct, which does not get repeatedly destroyed and rebuilt like SwiftUI View objects.

### Using @Bindable with @Observable

To create bindings to the mutable properties of an observable class, we need to mark it as bindable using the @Bindable property wrapper. This allows us to create bindings directly from the observable properties, which can then be passed down to child views.

For comprehensive tutorials, I'd recommend checking out the WWDC23 session "Discover Observation in SwiftUI" from Apple, along with the articles from Donny Wals, Swift by Sundell, and the QuickBird Studios blog on Swift Macros.

Here's what I found about the **swift-macro-testing** library from Point-Free:

## Overview

swift-macro-testing provides magical testing tools for Swift macros.(no content)With the release of Swift 5.9 and its new macros feature, Point-Free released this open source library that includes powerful tools for writing tests for macros.

## Key Resources

### Official Documentation
- **GitHub Repository**: [pointfreeco/swift-macro-testing](https://github.com/pointfreeco/swift-macro-testing)
- The library is available on Swift Package Index as "swift-macro-testing by Point-Free."

### Point-Free Video Episodes
Point-Free has dedicated episodes explaining macro testing:

- Episode #250 covers how Xcode 15 and Swift 5.9 brought macros—little compiler plugins that allow extending the Swift language in ways that don't require going through Swift evolution.

- The episode addresses how to debug and test macros, since macros are compiler plugins run during compilation, you can't simply put a breakpoint in the macro code and step through it line-by-line. This can be frustrating since SwiftSyntax is complex.

- SwiftSyntax provides a tool for testing macros that allows you to provide a string with sample code using a macro, then provide another string with the expected expanded code. If they don't match, you get a nicely formatted failure message.

### Using assertMacro

Point-Free's `assertMacro` tool can be used to verify macro expansions and diagnostics.

### Package Integration

To add swift-macro-testing to your package, include it as a dependency: `.package(url: "https://github.com/pointfreeco/swift-macro-testing", from: "0.6.0")`

### Tutorial Series (2025)

There's a Swift Macro Testing article series that explores "a useful triad of testing approaches" covering:
- Expansion testing using Point-Free's assertMacro tool, followed by unit testing to fine-tune macro expansion.
- By following this testing triad, you can create macros that are robust, flexible, and ready for production use.

   667→  /**

   675→   * // usage

   677→   * const unsubscribePresence = room.subscribePresence({}, console.log);
   678→   * room.publishTopic("hello", { message: "hello world!" });
   679→   * room.publishPresence({ name: "joe" });
   680→   * // later
   681→   * unsubscribePresence();
   682→   * unsubscribeTopic();
   683→   * room.leaveRoom();

   685→  joinRoom<RoomType extends keyof RoomsOf<Schema>>(
   686→    roomType: RoomType = '_defaultRoomType' as RoomType,
   687→    roomId: string = '_defaultRoomId',
   688→    opts?: {

   702→      publishPresence: (data) =>

   704→      getPresence: (opts) => this._reactor.getPresence(roomType, roomId, opts),
   705→    };
   706→  }

   757→function schemaHash(schema?: InstantSchemaDef<any, any, any>): string {
   758→  if (!schema) {
   759→    return '0';
   760→  }
   761→
   762→  const fromStore = schemaHashStore.get(schema);
   763→  if (fromStore) {
   764→    return fromStore;
   765→  }
   766→  const hash = weakHash(schema);
   767→  schemaHashStore.set(schema, hash);
   768→  return hash;
   769→}
   770→
   771→function schemaChanged(
   772→  existingClient: InstantCoreDatabase<any, boolean>,
   773→  newSchema?: InstantSchemaDef<any, any, any>,
   774→): boolean {
   775→  return (
   776→    schemaHash(existingClient._reactor.config.schema) !== schemaHash(newSchema)
   777→  );
   778→}

   780→/**
   781→ *
   782→ * The first step: init your application!
   783→ *
   784→ * Visit https://instantdb.com/dash to get your `appId` :)
   785→ *
   786→ * @example
   787→ *  import { init } from "@instantdb/core"
   788→ *
   789→ *  const db = init({ appId: "my-app-id" })
   790→ *
   791→ *  // You can also provide a schema for type safety and editor autocomplete!
   792→ *
   793→ *  import { init } from "@instantdb/core"
   794→ *  import schema from ""../instant.schema.ts";
   795→ *
   796→ *  const db = init({ appId: "my-app-id", schema })
   797→ *
   798→ *  // To learn more: https://instantdb.com/docs/modeling-data
   799→ */
   800→function init<
   801→  Schema extends InstantSchemaDef<any, any, any> = InstantUnknownSchema,
   802→  UseDates extends boolean = false,
   803→>(
   804→  // Allows config with missing `useDateObjects`, but keeps `UseDates`
   805→  // as a non-nullable in the InstantConfig type.
   806→  config: Omit<InstantConfig<Schema, UseDates>, 'useDateObjects'> & {
   807→    useDateObjects?: UseDates;
   808→  },
   809→  Storage?: any,
   810→  NetworkListener?: any,
   811→  versions?: { [key: string]: string },
   812→  EventSourceImpl?: any,
   813→): InstantCoreDatabase<Schema, UseDates> {
   814→  const configStrict = {
   815→    ...config,
   816→    useDateObjects: (config.useDateObjects ?? false) as UseDates,
   817→  };
   818→  const existingClient = globalInstantCoreStore[
   819→    reactorKey(configStrict)
   820→  ] as InstantCoreDatabase<any, UseDates>;
   821→
   822→  if (existingClient) {
   823→    if (schemaChanged(existingClient, configStrict.schema)) {
   824→      existingClient._reactor.updateSchema(configStrict.schema);
   825→    }
   826→    return existingClient;
   827→  }
   828→
   829→  const reactor = new Reactor<RoomsOf<Schema>>(
   830→    {
   831→      ...defaultConfig,
   832→      ...configStrict,
   833→      cardinalityInference: configStrict.schema ? true : false,
   834→    },
   835→    Storage || IndexedDBStorage,
   836→    NetworkListener || WindowNetworkListener,
   837→    { ...(versions || {}), '@instantdb/core': version },
   838→    EventSourceImpl,
   839→  );
   840→
   841→  const client = new InstantCoreDatabase<any, UseDates>(reactor);
   842→  globalInstantCoreStore[reactorKey(configStrict)] = client;
   843→
   844→  handleDevtool(configStrict.appId, configStrict.devtool);
   845→
   846→  return client;
   847→}
   848→
   849→function handleDevtool(
   850→  appId: string,
   851→  devtool: boolean | DevtoolConfig | null | undefined,
   852→) {
   853→  if (
   854→    typeof window === 'undefined' ||
   855→    typeof window.location === 'undefined' ||
   856→    typeof document === 'undefined'
   857→  ) {
   858→    return;
   859→  }
   860→
   861→  if (typeof devtool === 'boolean' && !devtool) {
   862→    return;
   863→  }
   864→
   865→  const config: StrictDevtoolConfig = {
   866→    position: 'bottom-right' as const,
   867→    allowedHosts: ['localhost'],
   868→    ...(typeof devtool === 'object' ? devtool : {}),
   869→  };
   870→
   871→  if (!config.allowedHosts.includes(window.location.hostname)) {
   872→    return;
   873→  }
   874→
   875→  createDevtool(appId, config);
   876→}

   887→ *
   888→ * // After

   892→const init_experimental = init;

     3→/// A type that can load and subscribe to state in an external system.
     4→///
     5→/// Conform to this protocol to express loading state from an external system, and subscribing to
     6→/// state changes in the external system. It is only necessary to conform to this protocol if the

    11→public protocol SharedReaderKey<Value>: Sendable {
    12→  /// A type that can be loaded or subscribed to in an external system.
    13→  associatedtype Value: Sendable
    14→

    16→  associatedtype ID: Hashable = Self
    17→
    18→  /// The hashable identity of a shared key.

    21→  /// the ``AppStorageKey`` uses the string key and `UserDefaults` instance to define its ID.

    23→
    24→  /// Loads the freshest value from storage.
    25→  ///
    26→  /// - Parameters
    27→  ///   - context: The context of loading a value.

     5→final class PersistentReferences: @unchecked Sendable, DependencyKey {
     6→  static var liveValue: PersistentReferences { PersistentReferences() }
     7→  static var testValue: PersistentReferences { PersistentReferences() }
     8→
     9→  struct Weak<Key: SharedReaderKey> {
    10→    weak var reference: _PersistentReference<Key>?
    11→  }
    12→
    13→  private var storage: [AnyHashable: Any] = [:]
    14→  private let lock = NSRecursiveLock()
    15→
    16→  func value<Key: SharedReaderKey>(
    17→    forKey key: Key,
    18→    default value: @autoclosure () throws -> Key.Value,
    19→    skipInitialLoad: Bool
    20→  ) rethrows -> _PersistentReference<Key> {
    21→    if let reference = lock.withLock({ (storage[key.id] as? Weak<Key>)?.reference }) {
    22→      return reference
    23→    } else {
    24→      let value = try value()
    25→      let reference = _PersistentReference(
    26→        key: key,
    27→        value: value,
    28→        skipInitialLoad: skipInitialLoad
    29→      )
    30→      return lock.withLock {
    31→        if let reference = (storage[key.id] as? Weak<Key>)?.reference {
    32→          return reference
    33→        } else {
    34→          storage[key.id] = Weak(reference: reference)
    35→          reference.onDeinit = { [self] in
    36→            removeReference(forKey: key)
    37→          }
    38→          return reference
    39→        }
    40→      }
    41→    }
    42→  }
    43→
    44→  func removeReference<Key: SharedReaderKey>(forKey key: Key) {
    45→    lock.withLock {
    46→      _ = storage.removeValue(forKey: key.id)
    47→    }
    48→  }
    49→}

     1→# sharing-instant
     2→
     3→[![Swift 6.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/Swift-6.0-orange.svg)](https://swift.org)
     4→[![Platforms](https://img.shields.io/badge/Platforms-iOS%20|%20macOS%20|%20tvOS%20|%20watchOS-blue.svg)](https://developer.apple.com)
     5→
     6→Real-time, local-first state management for Swift apps using [InstantDB](https://instantdb.com) and 
     7→Point-Free's [Sharing](https://github.com/pointfreeco/swift-sharing) library.
     8→
     9→## Demo
    10→
    11→`v0.1` Demo
    12→[![SharingInstant Demo](https://img.youtube.com/vi/wuGd6pt1reA/0.jpg)]([https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wuGd6pt1reA](https://youtu.be/KqUGbV2rIiY))
    13→
    14→> **Note:** This library depends on [instant-ios-sdk PR #6](https://github.com/instantdb/instant-ios-sdk/pull/6) 
    15→> which adds presence support and threading fixes.
    16→
    17→> **⚠️ Demo Status (December 19, 2025 1:00 PM EST):** The demos are a little flaky right now. 
    18→> I'm actively working on fixing them.
    19→
    20→  * [Overview](#overview)
    21→  * [Quick example](#quick-example)
    22→  * [Getting started](#getting-started)
    23→  * [Modeling data](#modeling-data)
    24→  * [Permissions](#permissions)
    25→  * [Sync](#sync)
    26→  * [Presence](#presence)
    27→  * [Schema codegen](#schema-codegen)
    28→  * [Demos](#demos)
    29→  * [Documentation](#documentation)
    30→  * [Debugging & troubleshooting](#debugging--troubleshooting)
    31→  * [Testing](#testing)
    32→  * [Installation](#installation)
    33→  * [License](#license)
    34→
    35→## Overview
    36→
    37→`sharing-instant` brings InstantDB's real-time sync to Swift using the familiar `@Shared` property 
    38→wrapper from Point-Free's Sharing library. It provides:
    39→
    40→- **`@Shared(.instantSync(...))`** – Bidirectional sync with optimistic updates
    41→- **`@Shared(.instantPresence(...))`** – Real-time presence (who's online, typing indicators, cursors)
    42→- **Schema codegen** – Generate type-safe Swift structs from your TypeScript schema
    43→- **Offline support** – Works offline, syncs when back online
    44→- **Full type safety** – No `[String: Any]`, everything is generic and `Codable`
    45→
    46→## Quick example
    47→
    48→Get started in seconds with the sample command. This generates a sample schema and Swift types 
    49→you can use immediately:
    50→
    51→```bash
    52→# Generate sample schema and Swift types
    53→swift run instant-schema sample --to Sources/Generated/
    54→```
    55→
    56→This creates:
    57→- `instant.schema.ts` – A sample TypeScript schema with a `todos` entity
    58→- `Sources/Generated/` – Swift types (`Todo`, `Schema.todos`, etc.)
    59→
    60→Then copy this into your app. **Run on multiple simulators or devices to watch changes sync instantly!**
    61→
    62→```swift
    63→// TodoApp.swift
    64→import SharingInstant
    65→import SwiftUI
    66→
    67→@main
    68→struct TodoApp: App {
    69→  init() {
    70→    // Get your App ID at: https://instantdb.com/dash/new
    71→    // Then push the schema: npx instant-cli@latest push schema --app YOUR_APP_ID
    72→    prepareDependencies {
    73→      $0.defaultInstant = InstantClient(appId: "YOUR_APP_ID")
    74→    }
    75→  }
    76→  
    77→  var body: some Scene {
    78→    WindowGroup {
    79→      TodoListView()
    80→    }
    81→  }
    82→}
    83→```
    84→
    85→```swift
    86→// TodoListView.swift
    87→import IdentifiedCollections
    88→import SharingInstant
    89→import SwiftUI
    90→
    91→struct TodoListView: View {
    92→  // Uses generated Schema.todos and Todo types
    93→  @Shared(.instantSync(Schema.todos))
    94→  private var todos: IdentifiedArrayOf<Todo> = []
    95→  
    96→  @State private var newTitle = ""
    97→  
    98→  var body: some View {
    99→    NavigationStack {
   100→      List {
   101→        // Add new todo
   102→        HStack {
   103→          TextField("What needs to be done?", text: $newTitle)
   104→            .onSubmit { addTodo() }
   105→          Button(action: addTodo) {
   106→            Image(systemName: "plus.circle.fill")
   107→          }
   108→          .disabled(newTitle.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces).isEmpty)
   109→        }
   110→        
   111→        // Todo list
   112→        ForEach(todos) { todo in
   113→          HStack {
   114→            Image(systemName: todo.done ? "checkmark.circle.fill" : "circle")
   115→              .foregroundStyle(todo.done ? .green : .secondary)
   116→              .onTapGesture { toggleTodo(todo) }
   117→            Text(todo.title)
   118→              .strikethrough(todo.done)
   119→            Spacer()
   120→          }
   121→        }
   122→        .onDelete { indexSet in
   123→          $todos.withLock { $0.remove(atOffsets: indexSet) }
   124→        }
   125→      }
   126→      .navigationTitle("Todos (\(todos.count))")
   127→    }
   128→  }
   129→  
   130→  private func addTodo() {
   131→    let title = newTitle.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)
   132→    guard !title.isEmpty else { return }
   133→    
   134→	    let todo = Todo(
   135→	      title: title,
   136→	      done: false,
   137→	      createdAt: Date().timeIntervalSince1970 * 1_000
   138→	    )
   139→	    $todos.withLock { $0.append(todo) }
   140→	    newTitle = ""
   141→	  }
   142→  
   143→  private func toggleTodo(_ todo: Todo) {
   144→    $todos.withLock { $0[id: todo.id]?.done.toggle() }
   145→  }
   146→}
   147→```
   148→
   149→When you call `$todos.withLock { ... }`, the change is applied locally immediately (optimistic UI), 
   150→sent to InstantDB, and synced to all other devices in real-time.
   151→
   152→## Getting started
   153→
   154→This guide walks you through creating an InstantDB project, defining your schema, generating Swift 
   155→types, and building your first synced view.
   156→
   157→### 1. Create an InstantDB project
   158→
   159→Go to **[instantdb.com/dash/new](https://www.instantdb.com/dash/new)** and create a new project. 
   160→Copy your **App ID** – you'll need it to configure the client.
   161→
   162→### 2. Define your schema
   163→
   164→Create an `instant.schema.ts` file in your project. This TypeScript file defines your data model 
   165→and is the source of truth for both your backend and Swift types.
   166→
   167→See [Modeling Data](https://instantdb.com/docs/modeling-data) for the full schema reference.
   168→
   169→```typescript
   170→// instant.schema.ts
   171→import { i } from "@instantdb/core";
   172→
   173→const _schema = i.schema({
   174→  entities: {
   175→    todos: i.entity({
   176→      title: i.string(),
   177→      done: i.boolean(),
   178→      createdAt: i.number().indexed(),
   179→    }),
   180→  },
   181→  
   182→  // Optional: Define rooms for presence features
   183→  // See: https://instantdb.com/docs/presence-and-topics
   184→  rooms: {
   185→    chat: {
   186→      presence: i.entity({
   187→        name: i.string(),
   188→        color: i.string(),
   189→        isTyping: i.boolean(),
   190→      }),
   191→    },
   192→  },
   193→});
   194→
   195→type _AppSchema = typeof _schema;
   196→interface AppSchema extends _AppSchema {}
   197→const schema: AppSchema = _schema;
   198→
   199→export type { AppSchema };
   200→export default schema;
   201→```
   202→
   203→### 3. Push your schema to InstantDB
   204→
   205→Use the [Instant CLI](https://instantdb.com/docs/cli) to push your schema to the server:
   206→
   207→```bash
   208→# Login to InstantDB (first time only)
   209→npx instant-cli@latest login
   210→
   211→# Push your schema
   212→npx instant-cli@latest push schema --app YOUR_APP_ID
   213→```
   214→
   215→### 4. Generate Swift types
   216→
   217→`sharing-instant` includes a schema codegen tool that generates type-safe Swift structs from your 
   218→TypeScript schema.
   219→
   220→> **Important:** The generator requires the **input schema file to be committed** and the 
   221→> **output directory to be clean** so that generated changes can be traced back to a specific 
   222→> version of the schema.
   223→
   224→```bash
   225→# Generate Swift types
   226→swift run instant-schema generate \
   227→  --from instant.schema.ts \
   228→  --to Sources/Generated
   229→```
   230→
   231→This generates:
   232→
   233→- **`Entities.swift`** – Swift structs for each entity (`Todo`, etc.)
   234→- **`Schema.swift`** – Type-safe `EntityKey` instances (`Schema.todos`, etc.)
   235→- **`Rooms.swift`** – Presence types for rooms (`ChatPresence`, `Schema.Rooms.chat`, etc.)
   236→- **`Links.swift`** – Link metadata for relationships
   237→
   238→### 5. Configure the InstantDB client
   239→
   240→In your app's entry point, configure the default InstantDB client with your App ID:
   241→
   242→```swift
   243→import SharingInstant
   244→import SwiftUI
   245→
   246→@main
   247→struct MyApp: App {
   248→  init() {
   249→    prepareDependencies {
   250→      $0.defaultInstant = InstantClient(appId: "YOUR_APP_ID")
   251→    }
   252→  }
   253→  
   254→  var body: some Scene {
   255→    WindowGroup {
   256→      ContentView()
   257→    }
   258→  }
   259→}
   260→```
   261→
   262→### 6. Use in your views
   263→
   264→Now you can use `@Shared(.instantSync(...))` in any SwiftUI view with the generated types:
   265→
   266→```swift
   267→import SharingInstant
   268→
   269→struct TodoListView: View {
   270→  // Type-safe sync using generated Schema and Todo types
   271→  @Shared(.instantSync(Schema.todos.orderBy(\.createdAt, .desc)))
   272→  private var todos: IdentifiedArrayOf<Todo> = []
   273→  
   274→  // ... your view code
   275→}
   276→```
   277→
   278→## Modeling data
   279→
   280→InstantDB uses a **schema-first** approach. Your `instant.schema.ts` file defines:
   281→
   282→- **Entities** – Your data types (like tables)
   283→- **Links** – Relationships between entities
   284→- **Rooms** – Real-time presence channels
   285→
   286→### Entities
   287→
   288→```typescript
   289→entities: {
   290→  todos: i.entity({
   291→    title: i.string(),
   292→    done: i.boolean(),
   293→    createdAt: i.number().indexed(),  // .indexed() for faster queries
   294→    priority: i.string().optional(),   // .optional() for nullable fields
   295→  }),
   296→  
   297→  users: i.entity({
   298→    email: i.string().unique().indexed(),  // .unique() for uniqueness constraint
   299→    displayName: i.string(),
   300→  }),
   301→}
   302→```
   303→
   304→### Links (Relationships)
   305→
   306→```typescript
   307→links: {
   308→  // One user has many todos
   309→  userTodos: {
   310→    forward: { on: "todos", has: "one", label: "owner" },
   311→    reverse: { on: "users", has: "many", label: "todos" },
   312→  },
   313→}
   314→```
   315→
   316→### Rooms (Presence)
   317→
   318→```typescript
   319→rooms: {
   320→  chat: {
   321→    presence: i.entity({
   322→      name: i.string(),
   323→      isTyping: i.boolean(),
   324→    }),
   325→  },
   326→}
   327→```
   328→
   329→📚 **Learn more:** [Modeling Data](https://instantdb.com/docs/modeling-data)
   330→
   331→## Permissions
   332→
   333→InstantDB uses a **CEL-based rule language** to secure your data. Define permissions in 
   334→`instant.perms.ts`:
   335→
   336→```typescript
   337→// instant.perms.ts
   338→import type { InstantRules } from "@instantdb/react";
   339→
   340→const rules = {
   341→  todos: {
   342→    allow: {
   343→      // Anyone can view todos
   344→      view: "true",
   345→      // Only the owner can create/update/delete
   346→      create: "isOwner",
   347→      update: "isOwner",
   348→      delete: "isOwner",
   349→    },
   350→    bind: [
   351→      "isOwner", "auth.id != null && auth.id == data.ownerId"
   352→    ]
   353→  },
   354→  
   355→  // Lock down creating new attributes in production
   356→  attrs: {
   357→    allow: {
   358→      create: "false"
   359→    }
   360→  }
   361→} satisfies InstantRules;
   362→
   363→export default rules;
   364→```
   365→
   366→Push permissions with the CLI:
   367→
   368→```bash
   369→npx instant-cli@latest push perms --app YOUR_APP_ID
   370→```
   371→
   372→### Key concepts
   373→
   374→- **`auth`** – The authenticated user (`auth.id`, `auth.email`)
   375→- **`data`** – The entity being accessed
   376→- **`newData`** – The entity after an update (for `update` rules)
   377→- **`ref()`** – Traverse relationships: `data.ref('owner.id')`
   378→- **`bind`** – Reusable rule aliases
   379→
   380→📚 **Learn more:** [Permissions](https://instantdb.com/docs/permissions)
   381→
   382→## Sync
   383→
   384→The `@Shared(.instantSync(...))` property wrapper provides bidirectional sync with InstantDB.
   385→
   386→### Basic usage
   387→
   388→```swift
   389→// Sync all todos
   390→@Shared(.instantSync(Schema.todos))
   391→private var todos: IdentifiedArrayOf<Todo> = []
   392→
   393→// With ordering
   394→@Shared(.instantSync(Schema.todos.orderBy(\.createdAt, .desc)))
   395→private var todos: IdentifiedArrayOf<Todo> = []
   396→
   397→// With filtering
   398→@Shared(.instantSync(Schema.todos.where(\.done, .eq(false))))
   399→private var activeTodos: IdentifiedArrayOf<Todo> = []
   400→
   401→// With limit
   402→@Shared(.instantSync(Schema.todos.limit(10)))
   403→private var recentTodos: IdentifiedArrayOf<Todo> = []
   404→```
   405→
   406→### Mutations with `withLock`
   407→
   408→All mutations go through `$todos.withLock { ... }`, which:
   409→
   410→1. Applies the change locally immediately (optimistic UI)
   411→2. Sends the change to InstantDB
   412→3. Receives confirmation or rollback from the server
   413→
   414→```swift
   415→	// Create
   416→	$todos.withLock { todos in
   417→	  todos.append(Todo(title: "New todo", done: false, createdAt: Date().timeIntervalSince1970 * 1_000))
   418→	}
   419→
   420→// Update
   421→$todos.withLock { todos in
   422→  todos[id: todo.id]?.done = true
   423→}
   424→
   425→// Delete
   426→$todos.withLock { todos in
   427→  todos.remove(id: todo.id)
   428→}
   429→
   430→// Batch operations
   431→$todos.withLock { todos in
   432→  for index in todos.indices {
   433→    todos[index].done = true
   434→  }
   435→}
   436→```
   437→
   438→### Query modifiers
   439→
   440→Chain modifiers for complex queries:
   441→
   442→```swift
   443→Schema.todos
   444→  .where(\.done, .eq(false))      // Filter: only incomplete todos
   445→  .orderBy(\.createdAt, .desc)    // Sort: newest first
   446→  .limit(20)                       // Limit: first 20 results
   447→```
   448→
   449→📚 **Learn more:** [Reading Data](https://instantdb.com/docs/instaql) | [Writing Data](https://instantdb.com/docs/instaml)
   450→
   451→## Presence
   452→
   453→The `@Shared(.instantPresence(...))` property wrapper provides real-time presence – know who's 
   454→online and share ephemeral state like typing indicators and cursor positions.
   455→
   456→### How it works
   457→
   458→The generic type `T` in `RoomPresence<T>` is inferred from your schema's room definition. When you 
   459→define a room in `instant.schema.ts`:
   460→
   461→```typescript
   462→rooms: {
   463→  chat: {
   464→    presence: i.entity({
   465→      name: i.string(),
   466→      color: i.string(),
   467→      isTyping: i.boolean(),
   468→    }),
   469→  },
   470→}
   471→```
   472→
   473→The codegen produces `ChatPresence` and `Schema.Rooms.chat`, which you use with `@Shared`:
   474→
   475→```swift
   476→@Shared(.instantPresence(
   477→  Schema.Rooms.chat,           // RoomKey<ChatPresence> - determines the generic T
   478→  roomId: "room-123",
   479→  initialPresence: ChatPresence(name: "", color: "", isTyping: false)
   480→))
   481→private var presence: RoomPresence<ChatPresence>  // T = ChatPresence, inferred from RoomKey
   482→```
   483→
   484→### Basic usage
   485→
   486→```swift
   487→struct ChatView: View {
   488→  @Shared(.instantPresence(
   489→    Schema.Rooms.chat,
   490→    roomId: "room-123",
   491→    initialPresence: ChatPresence(name: "", color: "", isTyping: false)
   492→  ))
   493→  private var presence: RoomPresence<ChatPresence>
   494→  
   495→  var body: some View {
   496→    VStack {
   497→      // Show who's online
   498→      Text("Online: \(presence.totalCount)")
   499→      
   500→      // Your presence
   501→      Text("You: \(presence.user.name)")
   502→      
   503→      // Other users
   504→      ForEach(presence.peers) { peer in
   505→        HStack {
   506→          Text(peer.data.name)
   507→          if peer.data.isTyping {
   508→            Text("typing...")
   509→          }
   510→        }
   511→      }
   512→    }
   513→  }
   514→}
   515→```
   516→
   517→### Updating your presence
   518→
   519→```swift
   520→// Update a single field
   521→$presence.withLock { state in
   522→  state.user.isTyping = true
   523→}
   524→
   525→// Update multiple fields
   526→$presence.withLock { state in
   527→  state.user = ChatPresence(
   528→    name: "Alice",
   529→    color: "#FF0000",
   530→    isTyping: false
   531→  )
   532→}
   533→```
   534→
   535→### Presence state
   536→
   537→The `RoomPresence<T>` type provides:
   538→
   539→- `user: T` – Your current presence data
   540→- `peers: [Peer<T>]` – Other users in the room
   541→- `totalCount: Int` – Total users including you
   542→- `isLoading: Bool` – Whether the connection is being established
   543→- `error: Error?` – Any connection error
   544→
   545→📚 **Learn more:** [Presence, Cursors, and Activity](https://instantdb.com/docs/presence-and-topics)
   546→
   547→## Schema codegen
   548→
   549→`sharing-instant` includes a powerful schema codegen tool that generates type-safe Swift code from 
   550→your InstantDB TypeScript schema.
   551→
   552→### Quick start with sample
   553→
   554→The fastest way to get started is the `sample` command:
   555→
   556→```bash
   557→# Generate sample schema and Swift types (no git requirements)
   558→swift run instant-schema sample --to Sources/Generated/
   559→```
   560→
   561→This creates a sample `instant.schema.ts` and generates Swift types you can use immediately.
   562→
   563→### CLI usage
   564→
   565→```bash
   566→# Generate Swift types from a schema file (schema must be committed, output dir must be clean)
   567→swift run instant-schema generate \
   568→  --from path/to/instant.schema.ts \
   569→  --to Sources/Generated
   570→
   571→# Pull schema from InstantDB and generate
   572→swift run instant-schema generate \
   573→  --app YOUR_APP_ID \
   574→  --to Sources/Generated
   575→```
   576→
   577→> **Note:** The `generate` command requires the **input schema file to be committed** and the 
   578→> **output directory to be clean** for traceability. The `sample` command has no git requirements 
   579→> – use it for quick experimentation.
   580→
   581→### Generated code
   582→
   583→For a schema like:
   584→
   585→```typescript
   586→const _schema = i.schema({
   587→  entities: {
   588→    todos: i.entity({
   589→      title: i.string(),
   590→      done: i.boolean(),
   591→      createdAt: i.number().indexed(),
   592→    }),
   593→  },
   594→  rooms: {
   595→    chat: {
   596→      presence: i.entity({
   597→        name: i.string(),
   598→        isTyping: i.boolean(),
   599→      }),
   600→    },
   601→  },
   602→});
   603→```
   604→
   605→The codegen produces:
   606→
   607→**Entities.swift:**
   608→```swift
   609→public struct Todo: EntityIdentifiable, Codable, Sendable {
   610→  public static var namespace: String { "todos" }
   611→  
   612→  public var id: String
   613→  public var title: String
   614→  public var done: Bool
   615→  public var createdAt: Double
   616→  
   617→  public init(
   618→    id: String = UUID().uuidString.lowercased(),
   619→    title: String,
   620→    done: Bool,
   621→    createdAt: Double
   622→  ) {
   623→    self.id = id
   624→    self.title = title
   625→    self.done = done
   626→    self.createdAt = createdAt
   627→  }
   628→}
   629→```
   630→
   631→**Schema.swift:**
   632→```swift
   633→public enum Schema {
   634→  public static let todos = EntityKey<Todo>(namespace: "todos")
   635→}
   636→```
   637→
   638→**Rooms.swift:**
   639→```swift
   640→public struct ChatPresence: Codable, Sendable, Equatable {
   641→  public var name: String
   642→  public var isTyping: Bool
   643→}
   644→
   645→extension Schema {
   646→  public enum Rooms {
   647→    public static let chat = RoomKey<ChatPresence>(type: "chat")
   648→  }
   649→}
   650→```
   651→
   652→### SPM build plugin
   653→
   654→For automatic codegen on every build, add the plugin to your target:
   655→
   656→```swift
   657→.target(
   658→  name: "MyApp",
   659→  dependencies: ["SharingInstant"],
   660→  plugins: [
   661→    .plugin(name: "InstantSchemaPlugin", package: "sharing-instant")
   662→  ]
   663→)
   664→```
   665→
   666→#### Where to place `instant.schema.ts`
   667→
   668→The plugin looks for `instant.schema.ts` in your target's source directory. Here are example 
   669→project structures:
   670→
   671→**Single-target app:**
   672→```
   673→MyApp/
   674→├── Package.swift
   675→├── Sources/
   676→│   └── MyApp/
   677→│       ├── instant.schema.ts    ← Place schema here
   678→│       ├── MyApp.swift
   679→│       └── ContentView.swift
   680→```
   681→
   682→**Multi-target workspace:**
   683→```
   684→MyProject/
   685→├── Package.swift
   686→├── Sources/
   687→│   ├── Shared/                  ← Shared code target
   688→│   │   ├── instant.schema.ts    ← Schema in shared target
   689→│   │   └── Generated/           ← Generated types here
   690→│   ├── iOSApp/
   691→│   │   └── iOSApp.swift
   692→│   └── macOSApp/
   693→│       └── macOSApp.swift
   694→```
   695→
   696→**Xcode project with SPM:**
   697→```
   698→MyApp.xcodeproj/
   699→MyApp/
   700→├── instant.schema.ts            ← In your main app folder
   701→├── Generated/
   702→├── AppDelegate.swift
   703→└── ContentView.swift
   704→```
   705→
   706→> **Note:** You only need the schema in **one** target. Other targets can import the generated 
   707→> types from that target. You don't need to duplicate the schema for each platform.

   750→## Debugging & troubleshooting
   751→
   752→SharingInstant is intentionally “boring” in the best way: your models update locally immediately,
   753→and then reconcile with the server. When something looks correct optimistically but later “flips”
   754→after a refresh, it’s almost always because the server and client disagree about schema or link
   755→metadata — not because SwiftUI is doing something mysterious.
   756→
   757→This section documents the debugging tools and failure modes we’ve hit in real apps, in the
   758→spirit of Point-Free’s libraries: explain the why, keep the defaults safe, and make the sharp
   759→tools opt-in.
   760→
   761→### Logging philosophy
   762→
   763→- **Quiet by default**: Real-time systems generate a lot of state changes. Unbounded `print(...)`
   764→  output makes logs unusable and slows tests down.
   765→- **Opt-in verbosity**: When you need to debug a tricky ordering issue, you should be able to
   766→  turn on the firehose without changing source code.
   767→- **Prefer structured sinks**: Use `os.Logger`/Console.app for high-volume diagnostics, and keep
   768→  stdout for human-facing “something is wrong” signals.
   769→
   770→### Controlling log output
   771→
   772→#### InstantDB Swift SDK (transport/query/schema)
   773→
   774→The upstream Swift SDK defaults to **error-only** stdout logging. Enable more output with:
   775→
   776→- `INSTANTDB_LOG_LEVEL`: `off`, `error`, `info`, `debug` (default: `error`)
   777→- `INSTANTDB_DEBUG=1`: forces `debug`
   778→
   779→Examples:
   780→
   781→```bash
   782→# High-signal connection events
   783→INSTANTDB_LOG_LEVEL=info swift test --package-path sharing-instant
   784→
   785→# Verbose protocol + query tracing
   786→INSTANTDB_LOG_LEVEL=debug swift test --package-path sharing-instant
   787→```
   788→
   789→#### SharingInstant internal diagnostics
   790→
   791→SharingInstant keeps a few internal diagnostics (like TripleStore decoding failures) behind
   792→an `os.Logger` gate so they don’t spam stdout.
   793→
   794→- `SHARINGINSTANT_LOG_LEVEL`: `off`, `error`, `info`, `debug` (default: `error`)
   795→- `SHARINGINSTANT_DEBUG=1`: forces `debug`
   796→
   797→For convenience, the internal logger also respects `INSTANTDB_LOG_LEVEL` / `INSTANTDB_DEBUG`
   798→when you want to flip both layers at once.
   799→
   800→To tail logs from Terminal:
   801→
   802→```bash
   803→log stream --level debug --predicate 'subsystem == "SharingInstant"'
   804→```
   805→
   806→#### InstantLogger (application-level observability)
   807→
   808→SharingInstant includes `InstantLogger` for application-level logging (optionally syncable to
   809→InstantDB). By default it prints to stdout, but you can tune it at app launch:
   810→
   811→```swift
   812→InstantLoggerConfig.printToStdout = false
   813→InstantLoggerConfig.logToOSLog = true
   814→```
   815→
   816→### Troubleshooting: linked entities resolve to `nil` (e.g. "Unknown Author")
   817→
   818→If a linked entity appears correctly in the optimistic UI but later resolves to `nil` after a
   819→server refresh, the most common cause is **server-side schema corruption** for the link attribute:
   820→
   821→- The attribute exists but has `value-type: blob` instead of `ref`, or
   822→- The attribute is a `ref` but is missing `reverse-identity` metadata.
   823→
   824→#### Why this happens
   825→
   826→SharingInstant (and the underlying Swift SDK) rely on InstantDB schema metadata to perform
   827→client-side joins. `reverse-identity` is the piece that tells the client which namespace + label
   828→represent “the other side” of a link. Without it, the client can’t safely resolve the relationship
   829→after a refresh, and your UI falls back to `nil`.
   830→
   831→#### How to fix it
   832→
   833→1. **Prefer fixing the schema at the source**: push a correct schema (TypeScript or Swift DSL)
   834→   so the server stores the link as a real `ref` with forward + reverse identities.
   835→2. **Lazy repair exists as a safety net**: the Swift SDK can piggyback an attribute update when it
   836→   detects a broken `ref` during a link operation, and then it applies refreshed schema from
   837→   `refresh-ok` before recomputing query results.
   838→
   839→## Testing
   840→
   841→SharingInstant includes both deterministic unit tests and end-to-end integration tests.
   842→
   843→### Why integration tests are opt-in
   844→
   845→Tests that create real apps / data on the InstantDB backend are inherently “louder”:
   846→
   847→- They require network access and backend credentials.
   848→- They need isolation to avoid flaking due to shared state.
   849→- They can be slow compared to local-only tests.
   850→
   851→For that reason, ephemeral backend round-trip tests are **skipped by default** and enabled only
   852→when explicitly requested.
   853→
   854→### Running ephemeral backend round-trip tests
   855→
   856→```bash
   857→INSTANT_RUN_EPHEMERAL_INTEGRATION_TESTS=1 \
   858→  swift test --package-path sharing-instant --filter EphemeralMicroblogRoundTripTests
   859→```
   860→
   861→## Installation
   862→
   863→You can add `sharing-instant` to your project using **either** Swift Package Manager **or** Xcode's 
   864→package manager UI. Choose whichever method you prefer – you only need to do one.
   865→
   866→### Option A: Swift Package Manager
   867→
   868→Add `sharing-instant` to your `Package.swift`:
   869→
   870→```swift
   871→dependencies: [
   872→  .package(url: "https://github.com/instantdb/sharing-instant", from: "0.1.0")
   873→]
   874→```
   875→
   876→Then add the product to your target:
   877→
   878→```swift
   879→.target(
   880→  name: "MyApp",
   881→  dependencies: [
   882→    .product(name: "SharingInstant", package: "sharing-instant"),
   883→  ]
   884→)
   885→```
   886→
   887→### Option B: Xcode
   888→
   889→1. File → Add Package Dependencies...
   890→2. Enter: `https://github.com/instantdb/sharing-instant`
   891→3. Add `SharingInstant` to your target
   892→

   894→
   895→- iOS 15+ / macOS 12+ / tvOS 15+ / watchOS 8+
   896→- Swift 6.0+
   897→- Xcode 16+

   299→  /// A type defining a user defaults persistence strategy.
   300→  public struct AppStorageKey<Value: Sendable>: SharedKey {
   301→    private let lookup: any Lookup<Value>
   302→    private let key: String
   303→    private let store: UncheckedSendable<UserDefaults>
   304→
   305→    public var id: AppStorageKeyID {
   306→      AppStorageKeyID(key: key, store: store.wrappedValue)
   307→    }
   308→
   309→    private init(lookup: some Lookup<Value>, key: String, store: UserDefaults?) {
   310→      @Dependency(\.defaultAppStorage) var defaultStore
   311→      self.lookup = lookup
   312→      self.key = key
   313→      let store = store ?? defaultStore
   314→      self.store = UncheckedSendable(store)
   315→      #if DEBUG
   316→        if store.responds(to: Selector(("_identifier"))),
   317→          let suiteName = store.perform(Selector(("_identifier"))).takeUnretainedValue() as? String
   318→        {
   319→          let objectID = ObjectIdentifier(store)
   320→          suites.withLock { suites in
   321→            defer { suites[suiteName] = objectID }
   322→            if let id = suites[suiteName], id != objectID {
   323→              reportIssue(
   324→                """
   325→                '@Shared(\(self))' was given a new store object for an existing suite name \
   326→                (\(suiteName.debugDescription)).
   327→
   328→                Shared app storage for a given suite should all share the same store object to \
   329→                ensure synchronization and observation. For example, define a store as a \
   330→                'static let' and refer to this single instance when creating shared app storage:
   331→
   332→                    extension UserDefaults {
   333→                      nonisolated(unsafe) static let mySuite = UserDefaults(
   334→                        suiteName: \(suiteName.debugDescription)
   335→                      )!
   336→                    }
   337→
   338→                    @Shared(.appStorage(\(key.debugDescription), store: .mySuite) var myProperty
   339→                """
   340→              )
   341→            }
   342→          }
   343→        }
   344→      #endif
   345→    }

   450→    public func load(context: LoadContext<Value>, continuation: LoadContinuation<Value>) {
   451→      continuation.resume(with: .success(lookupValue(default: context.initialValue)))
   452→    }
   453→
   454→    public func subscribe(
   455→      context: LoadContext<Value>, subscriber: SharedSubscriber<Value>
   456→    ) -> SharedSubscription {
   457→      let removeObserver: @Sendable () -> Void
   458→      let keyContainsPeriod = key.contains(".")
   459→      if keyContainsPeriod || key.hasPrefix("@") {
   460→        @Dependency(\.appStorageKeyFormatWarningEnabled) var appStorageKeyFormatWarningEnabled
   461→        if appStorageKeyFormatWarningEnabled {
   462→          let character = keyContainsPeriod ? "." : "@"
   463→          reportIssue(
   464→            """
   465→            A Shared app storage key (\(key.debugDescription)) contains an invalid character \
   466→            (\(character.debugDescription)) for key-value observation. External updates will be \
   467→            observed less efficiently and accurately via notification center, instead.
   468→
   469→            Please reformat this key by removing invalid characters in order to ensure efficient, \
   470→            cross-process observation.
   471→
   472→            If you cannot control the format of this key and would like to silence this warning, \
   473→            override the '\\.appStorageKeyFormatWarningEnabled' dependency at the entry point of \
   474→            your application. For example:
   475→
   476→                import Dependencies
   477→
   478→                @main
   479→                struct MyApp: App {
   480→                  init() {
   481→                    prepareDependencies {
   482→                      $0.appStorageKeyFormatWarningEnabled = false
   483→                    }
   484→                    // ...
   485→                  }
   486→                  // ...
   487→                }
   488→            """
   489→          )
   490→        }
   491→        let previousValue = Mutex(context.initialValue)
   492→        let userDefaultsDidChange = NotificationCenter.default.addObserver(
   493→          forName: UserDefaults.didChangeNotification,
   494→          object: store.wrappedValue,
   495→          queue: nil
   496→        ) { _ in
   497→          let newValue = lookupValue(default: context.initialValue)
   498→          defer { previousValue.withLock { $0 = newValue } }
   499→          func isEqual<T>(_ lhs: T, _ rhs: T) -> Bool? {
   500→            func open<U: Equatable>(_ lhs: U) -> Bool {
   501→              lhs == rhs as? U
   502→            }
   503→            guard let lhs = lhs as? any Equatable else { return nil }
   504→            return open(lhs)
   505→          }
   506→          guard
   507→            !(isEqual(newValue, previousValue.withLock { $0 }) ?? false)
   508→              || (isEqual(newValue, context.initialValue) ?? true)
   509→          else {
   510→            return
   511→          }
   512→          guard !SharedAppStorageLocals.isSetting
   513→          else { return }
   514→          DispatchQueue.main.async {
   515→            subscriber.yield(with: .success(newValue))
   516→          }
   517→        }
   518→        removeObserver = { NotificationCenter.default.removeObserver(userDefaultsDidChange) }
   519→      } else {
   520→        let observer = Observer {
   521→          guard !SharedAppStorageLocals.isSetting
   522→          else { return }
   523→          subscriber.yield(with: .success(lookupValue(default: context.initialValue)))
   524→        }
   525→        store.wrappedValue.addObserver(observer, forKeyPath: key, context: nil)
   526→        removeObserver = { store.wrappedValue.removeObserver(observer, forKeyPath: key) }
   527→      }
   528→      return SharedSubscription(removeObserver)
   529→    }
   530→
   531→    public func save(_ value: Value, context _: SaveContext, continuation: SaveContinuation) {
   532→      lookup.saveValue(value, to: store.wrappedValue, at: key)
   533→      continuation.resume()
   534→    }
   535→
   536→    private func lookupValue(default initialValue: Value?) -> Value? {
   537→      lookup.loadValue(from: store.wrappedValue, at: key, default: initialValue)
   538→    }
   539→
   540→    private final class Observer: NSObject, Sendable {
   541→      let didChange: @Sendable () -> Void
   542→      init(didChange: @escaping @Sendable () -> Void) {
   543→        self.didChange = didChange
   544→        super.init()
   545→      }
   546→      override func observeValue(
   547→        forKeyPath keyPath: String?,
   548→        of object: Any?,
   549→        change: [NSKeyValueChangeKey: Any]?,
   550→        context: UnsafeMutableRawPointer?
   551→      ) {
   552→        self.didChange()
   553→      }
   554→    }
   555→  }

   558→    public var description: String {
   559→      ".appStorage(\(String(reflecting: key)))"
   560→    }
   561→  }

   563→  public struct AppStorageKeyID: Hashable {
   564→    fileprivate let key: String
   565→    fileprivate let store: UserDefaults
   566→  }
   567→
   568→  extension DependencyValues {
   569→    /// Default file storage used by ``SharedReaderKey/appStorage(_:)``.
   570→    ///
   571→    /// Use this dependency to override the manner in which
   572→    /// ``SharedReaderKey/appStorage(_:)`` interacts with UserDefaults. For
   573→    /// example, while your app is running for UI tests you probably do not want your features writing
   574→    /// changes to your actual UserDefaults suite, which would cause that data to bleed over from test to test.
   575→    ///
   576→    /// So, for that situation you can use the ``inMemory`` value so that each
   577→    /// run of the app starts with a fresh suite that will never interfere with other tests:
   578→    ///
   579→    /// ```swift
   580→    /// import Dependencies
   581→    /// import Sharing
   582→    /// import SwiftUI
   583→    ///
   584→    /// @main
   585→    /// struct MyApp: App {
   586→    ///   init() {
   587→    ///     if ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["UITesting"] == "true"
   588→    ///       prepareDependencies {

   644→  private protocol Lookup<Value>: Sendable {

   671→
   672→    func saveValue(_ newValue: Value, to store: UserDefaults, at key: String) {

   704→      }

   711→    func loadValue(from store: UserDefaults, at key: String, default defaultValue: URL?) -> URL? {

   723→
   724→    func saveValue(_ newValue: URL, to store: UserDefaults, at key: String) {

   731→  private struct RawRepresentableLookup<Value: RawRepresentable & Sendable, Base: Lookup>: Lookup
   732→  where Value.RawValue == Base.Value {
   733→    let base: Base
   734→    func loadValue(
   735→      from store: UserDefaults, at key: String, default defaultValue: Value?
   736→    ) -> Value? {
   737→      base.loadValue(from: store, at: key, default: defaultValue?.rawValue)
   738→        .flatMap(Value.init(rawValue:))
   739→    }
   740→    func saveValue(_ newValue: Value, to store: UserDefaults, at key: String) {
   741→      base.saveValue(newValue.rawValue, to: store, at: key)

   743→  }

   745→  private struct OptionalLookup<Base: Lookup>: Lookup {

   747→    func loadValue(
   748→      from store: UserDefaults, at key: String, default defaultValue: Base.Value??
   749→    ) -> Base.Value?? {
   750→      base.loadValue(from: store, at: key, default: defaultValue ?? nil)
   751→        .flatMap(Optional.some)
   752→        ?? .none
   753→    }
   754→    func saveValue(_ newValue: Base.Value?, to store: UserDefaults, at key: String) {
   755→      if let newValue {

     1→(ns instant.reactive.session
     2→  "Manager for the lifecycle of a user session.
     3→
     4→   When a user connects over a socket, they can authenticate,
     5→   subscribe/unsubscribe from queries, make transsactions, and receive updates.
     6→
     7→   Each connection has their own `session` worker, that can understand these
     8→   commands."

    68→  ([session pending-handler handler-id]

    98→(defn get-supported-features [versions]

   102→        (cond-> #{}

   150→(defn- handle-init! [store sess-id event]
   151→  (let [{:keys [refresh-token client-event-id versions]
   152→         admin-token :__admin-token} event
   153→        prev-auth   (:session/auth (rs/session store sess-id))
   154→        _           (when prev-auth

   156→        app-id      (ex/get-param! event [:app-id] uuid-util/coerce)

   161→                       {:app-id app-id :refresh-token refresh-token}))

   163→        admin?      (and admin-token

   166→                                                         :token admin-token})))
   167→        auth        {:app    app

   169→                     :admin? admin?}
   170→        features (get-supported-features versions)]
   171→    (tracer/add-data! {:attributes (auth-and-creator-attrs auth creator versions)})
   172→    (apply rs/assoc-session! store sess-id
   173→           :session/auth auth
   174→           :session/creator creator
   175→           :session/features features
   176→           (concat

   179→            (when (supports-skip-attrs? features)

   182→                                          :session-id      sess-id
   183→                                          :client-event-id client-event-id
   184→                                          :auth            auth
   185→                                          :attrs           attrs})))

   356→                             pending-handler-id)))))

   358→(defn- handle-remove-sync! [store sess-id {:keys [keep-subscription] :as event}]
   359→  (let [subscription-id (ex/get-param! event [:subscription-id] uuid-util/coerce)
   360→        app-id (-> (get-auth! store sess-id) :app :id)
   361→        sync-ent (rs/get-sync-query store app-id sess-id subscription-id)]
   362→    (when sync-ent
   363→      (rs/remove-sync-query store app-id sess-id subscription-id)
   364→      (when-not keep-subscription
   365→        (sync-sub-model/delete! {:id (:sync/subscription-id sync-ent)
   366→                                 :app-id app-id})))))
   367→
   368→(defn- handle-refresh-sync-table! [store sess-id {:keys [subscription-id] :as _event}]
   369→  (let [{:keys [app]} (get-auth! store sess-id)
   370→        {app-id :id} app
   371→        ent (rs/get-sync-query store app-id sess-id subscription-id)]
   372→    (when ent
   373→      (let [unread-txes (rs/sync-query-unread-txes app-id ent)]
   374→        (when (seq unread-txes)
   375→          (let [max-txes 100
   376→                txes-to-send (take max-txes unread-txes)]
   377→            (rs/send-event! store app-id sess-id
   378→                            {:op :sync-update-triples
   379→                             :subscription-id subscription-id
   380→                             :txes txes-to-send})
   381→            (rs/sync-query-update-sent-tx store app-id (:db/id ent) (:tx-id (last txes-to-send)))
   382→
   383→            ;; There are still more txes to process, but we don't want to send too many in a single
   384→            ;; websocket packet, so requeue
   385→            (when (< max-txes (count unread-txes))
   386→              (receive-queue/put! (-> (rs/session store sess-id) :session/socket :receive-q)
   387→                                  {:op :refresh-sync-table
   388→                                   :subscription-id subscription-id
   389→                                   :app-id app-id
   390→                                   :session-id sess-id}))))))))
   391→
   392→(defn- handle-resync-table! [store sess-id event]
   393→  (let [{:keys [app user admin?]} (get-auth! store sess-id)
   394→        {app-id :id} app
   395→        tx-id (ex/get-param! event [:tx-id] (fn [v] (try (long v) (catch Throwable _ nil))))
   396→        subscription-id (ex/get-param! event [:subscription-id] uuid-util/coerce)
   397→        token (ex/get-param! event [:token] uuid-util/coerce)
   398→        record (sync-sub-model/get-by-id-with-topics! {:id subscription-id
   399→                                                       :token token
   400→                                                       :admin? admin?
   401→                                                       :user-id (:id user)})]
   402→
   403→    ;; TODO(sync-table): This will be replaced by a check that the tx is still in the db
   404→    ;;                   when we have stable storage for the tx-data
   405→    ;; Commenting it out for now so that we don't get a bunch of reconnects while testing
   406→    #_(when-not (ucoll/seek (fn [x]
   407→                              (= (:tx-id x) tx-id))
   408→                            @rs/sync-table-txes)
   409→        (ex/throw-validation-err! :subscription
   410→                                  {:subscription-id subscription-id
   411→                                   :tx-id tx-id}
   412→                                  [{:message "transactions for the subscription are no longer available"}]))
   413→    (rs/sync-query-resync store app-id sess-id
   414→                          (:id record) tx-id (:topics record))
   415→    (receive-queue/put! (-> (rs/session store sess-id) :session/socket :receive-q)
   416→                        {:op :refresh-sync-table
   417→                         :subscription-id subscription-id
   418→                         :app-id app-id
   419→                         :session-id sess-id})))
   420→
   421→(defn- handle-remove-query! [store sess-id {:keys [q client-event-id] :as _event}]
   422→  (let [{:keys [app]} (get-auth! store sess-id)]
   423→    (rs/remove-query! store (:id app) sess-id q)
   424→    (rs/send-event! store (:id app) sess-id {:op :remove-query-ok :q q
   425→                                             :client-event-id client-event-id})))
   426→
   427→(defn- recompute-instaql-query!
   428→  [{:keys [store current-user app-id sess-id attrs table-info admin?]}
   429→   {:keys [instaql-query/query instaql-query/return-type instaql-query/inference?
   430→           instaql-query/forms-hash]}]
   431→  (let [ctx {:db {:conn-pool (aurora/conn-pool (db-read-level app-id))}
   432→             :session-id sess-id
   433→             :app-id app-id
   434→             :attrs attrs
   435→             ;; Will only be present for byop apps
   436→             :table-info table-info
   437→             :current-user current-user
   438→             :admin? admin?}
   439→        start-ms (System/currentTimeMillis)
   440→        {:keys [instaql-result result-meta result-changed? instaql-topic?]}
   441→        (rq/instaql-query-reactive! store ctx query return-type inference?)
   442→        end-ms (System/currentTimeMillis)]
   443→    {:instaql-query query
   444→     :instaql-query-hash forms-hash
   445→     :instaql-result instaql-result
   446→     :result-meta result-meta
   447→     :result-changed? result-changed?
   448→     :duration-ms (- end-ms start-ms)
   449→     :instaql-topic? instaql-topic?}))
   450→
   451→(defn- handle-refresh! [store sess-id event debug-info]
   452→  (e2e-tracer/invalidator-tracking-step! {:tx-id (:tx-id event)
   453→                                          :tx-created-at (:tx-created-at event)
   454→                                          :name "start-refresh"
   455→                                          :attributes {:session-id sess-id}})
   456→  (let [auth (get-auth! store sess-id)
   457→        app-id (-> auth :app :id)
   458→        current-user (-> auth :user)
   459→        admin? (-> auth :admin?)
   460→        {:keys [attrs table-info]} (get-attrs (:app auth))
   461→        stale-queries (rs/get-stale-instaql-queries store app-id sess-id)
   462→        opts {:store store
   463→              :app-id app-id
   464→              :current-user current-user
   465→              :sess-id sess-id
   466→              :attrs attrs
   467→              :table-info table-info
   468→              :admin? admin?}
   469→        processed-tx-id (rs/get-processed-tx-id store app-id)
   470→        _ (reset! debug-info {:processed-tx-id processed-tx-id
   471→                              :instaql-queries (map :instaql-query/query stale-queries)})
   472→        recompute-results (->> stale-queries
   473→                               (ua/pmap (partial recompute-instaql-query! opts)))
   474→        {computations true spam false} (group-by :result-changed? recompute-results)
   475→        num-spam (count spam)
   476→        num-computations (count computations)
   477→        num-recomputations (count recompute-results)
   478→        tracer-attrs {:num-recomputations num-recomputations
   479→                      :num-spam num-spam
   480→                      :num-computations num-computations
   481→                      :dropped-spam? true
   482→                      :tx-latency-ms (e2e-tracer/tx-latency-ms (:tx-created-at event))}
   483→        {prev-attrs-hash :session/attrs-hash
   484→         features :session/features} (rs/session store sess-id)
   485→        can-skip-attrs? (supports-skip-attrs? features)
   486→        attrs-hash      (hash attrs)
   487→        attrs-changed?  (not= prev-attrs-hash attrs-hash)]
   488→    (doseq [{:keys [instaql-query instaql-query-hash duration-ms instaql-topic?]} spam]
   489→      (tracer/record-info! {:name "handle-refresh/spam"
   490→                            :attributes {:app-id app-id
   491→                                         :wal-log-enabled (flags/enable-wal-entity-log? app-id)
   492→                                         :instaql-query instaql-query
   493→                                         :instaql-query-hash instaql-query-hash
   494→                                         :instaql-query-normalized (instaql-util/normalized-forms instaql-query)
   495→                                         :duration-ms duration-ms
   496→                                         :instaql-topic? instaql-topic?}}))
   497→
   498→    (when (and can-skip-attrs? attrs-changed?)
   499→      (rs/assoc-session! store sess-id :session/attrs-hash attrs-hash))
   500→    (e2e-tracer/invalidator-tracking-step! {:tx-id (:tx-id event)
   501→                                            :tx-created-at (:tx-created-at event)
   502→                                            :name "finish-refresh-queries"
   503→                                            :attributes (assoc tracer-attrs
   504→                                                               :session-id sess-id)})
   505→    (tracer/with-span! {:name "handle-refresh/send-event!"
   506→                        :attributes tracer-attrs}
   507→      (when (seq computations)
   508→        (rs/send-event! store app-id sess-id (with-meta
   509→                                               (cond->
   510→                                                {:op :refresh-ok
   511→                                                 :processed-tx-id processed-tx-id
   512→                                                 :computations computations}
   513→                                                 (or (not can-skip-attrs?) attrs-changed?)
   514→                                                 (assoc :attrs attrs))
   515→                                               {:tx-id (:tx-id event)
   516→                                                :tx-created-at (:tx-created-at event)
   517→                                                :session-id sess-id}))))))
   518→
   519→;; -----
   520→;; transact
   521→
   522→(defn handle-transact!
   523→  [store sess-id {:keys [tx-steps client-event-id] :as _event}]
   524→  (let [auth (get-auth! store sess-id)
   525→        app-id (-> auth :app :id)
   526→        coerced (tx/coerce! tx-steps)
   527→        ctx {:db {:conn-pool (aurora/conn-pool :write)}
   528→             :rules (rule-model/get-by-app-id {:app-id app-id})
   529→             :app-id app-id
   530→             :current-user (:user auth)
   531→             :admin? (:admin? auth)
   532→             :datalog-query-fn d/query
   533→             :attrs (attr-model/get-by-app-id app-id)}
   534→        _ (tx/validate! ctx coerced)
   535→        {tx-id :id}
   536→        (permissioned-tx/transact! ctx coerced)]
   537→    (rs/send-event! store app-id sess-id
   538→                    {:op :transact-ok
   539→                     :tx-id tx-id
   540→                     :client-event-id client-event-id})))
   541→
   542→;; -----
   543→;; error
   544→
   545→(defn handle-error! [store sess-id {:keys [status
   546→                                           app-id
   547→                                           client-event-id
   548→                                           original-event
   549→                                           type
   550→                                           message
   551→                                           hint]}]
   552→  (rs/send-event! store
   553→                  app-id
   554→                  sess-id
   555→                  {:op :error
   556→                   :status status
   557→                   :client-event-id client-event-id
   558→                   :original-event original-event
   559→                   :type type
   560→                   :message message
   561→                   :hint hint}))
