   160→// MARK: - Explicit Mutation Methods for Shared Collections
   161→
   162→extension Shared {
   163→  
   164→  // MARK: - Create
   165→  
   166→  /// Create a new entity and sync to InstantDB.
   167→  ///
   168→  /// This method follows the TypeScript InstantDB SDK pattern:
   169→  /// 1. Sends transaction to Reactor which applies optimistic update
   170→  /// 2. Reactor notifies subscriptions to update @Shared value
   171→  /// 3. Server transaction is sent
   172→  ///
   173→  /// Unlike `withLock { $0.append(entity) }`, this does NOT compute diffs.
   174→  /// It sends exactly one transaction for the new entity.
   175→  ///
   176→  /// ## Example
   177→  ///
   178→  /// ```swift
   179→  /// @Shared(.instantSync(Schema.goals)) var goals: [Goal]
   180→  ///
   181→  /// let newGoal = Goal(id: UUID().uuidString, title: "Learn Swift")
   182→  /// try await $goals.create(newGoal)
   183→  /// ```
   184→  ///
   185→  /// - Parameter entity: The entity to create
   186→  /// - Throws: If the transaction fails
   187→  @MainActor
   188→  public func create<Element: EntityIdentifiable & Encodable & Sendable>(
   189→    _ entity: Element
   190→  ) async throws where Value: RangeReplaceableCollection, Value.Element == Element {
   191→    @Dependency(\.instantReactor) var reactor
   192→    @Dependency(\.instantAppID) var appID
   193→    
   194→    // Generate explicit transaction chunk
   195→    let namespace = Element.namespace
   196→    let attrs = try encodeEntityAttributes(entity)
   197→    
   198→    let chunk = TransactionChunk(
   199→      namespace: namespace,
   200→      id: entity.id,
   201→      ops: [["update", namespace, entity.id, attrs]]
   202→    )
   203→    
   204→    // Send to Reactor which handles optimistic update + server transaction
   205→    try await reactor.transact(appID: appID, chunks: [chunk])
   206→  }
   207→  
   208→  // MARK: - Delete
   209→  
   210→  /// Delete an entity by ID and sync to InstantDB.
   211→  ///
   212→  /// This method follows the TypeScript InstantDB SDK pattern:
   213→  /// 1. Sends transaction to Reactor which applies optimistic update
   214→  /// 2. Reactor notifies subscriptions to update @Shared value
   215→  /// 3. Server transaction is sent
   216→  ///
   217→  /// Unlike `withLock { $0.remove(id:) }`, this does NOT compute diffs.
   218→  /// It sends exactly one delete transaction.
   219→  ///
   220→  /// ## Example
   221→  ///
   222→  /// ```swift
   223→  /// @Shared(.instantSync(Schema.goals)) var goals: [Goal]
   224→  ///
   225→  /// try await $goals.delete(id: goal.id)
   226→  /// ```
   227→  ///
   228→  /// - Parameter id: The ID of the entity to delete
   229→  /// - Throws: If the transaction fails
   230→  @MainActor
   231→  public func delete<Element: EntityIdentifiable & Sendable>(
   232→    id: String
   233→  ) async throws where Value: RangeReplaceableCollection, Value.Element == Element {
   234→    @Dependency(\.instantReactor) var reactor
   235→    @Dependency(\.instantAppID) var appID
   236→    
   237→    // Generate explicit delete chunk
   238→    let namespace = Element.namespace
   239→    
   240→    let chunk = TransactionChunk(
   241→      namespace: namespace,
   242→      id: id,
   243→      ops: [["delete", namespace, id]]
   244→    )
   245→    
   246→    // Send to Reactor which handles optimistic update + server transaction
   247→    try await reactor.transact(appID: appID, chunks: [chunk])
   248→  }
   249→  
   250→  // MARK: - Update
   251→  
   252→  /// Update an entity's fields and sync to InstantDB.
   253→  ///
   254→  /// This method follows the TypeScript InstantDB SDK pattern:
   255→  /// 1. Reads current entity, applies modification
   256→  /// 2. Sends transaction to Reactor which applies optimistic update
   257→  /// 3. Reactor notifies subscriptions to update @Shared value
   258→  /// 4. Server transaction is sent
   259→  ///
   260→  /// **Important**: This method sends only the CHANGED fields, not the entire entity.
   261→  /// This prevents concurrent updates from clobbering each other (e.g., updating
   262→  /// `text` and `words` simultaneously on a transcription segment).
   263→  ///
   264→  /// ## Example
   265→  ///
   266→  /// ```swift
   267→  /// @Shared(.instantSync(Schema.goals)) var goals: [Goal]
   268→  ///
   269→  /// try await $goals.update(id: goal.id) { goal in
   270→  ///   goal.title = "Updated Title"
   271→  ///   goal.completed = true
   272→  /// }
   273→  /// ```
   274→  ///
   275→  /// - Parameters:
   276→  ///   - id: The ID of the entity to update
   277→  ///   - modify: A closure that modifies the entity
   278→  /// - Throws: If the entity is not found or the transaction fails
   279→  ///
   280→  /// ## Why We Read From TripleStore
   281→  /// See the IdentifiedArrayOf version for detailed explanation. In short:
   282→  /// we read from TripleStore to get optimistic updates that may not have
   283→  /// propagated to wrappedValue yet due to AsyncStream timing.
   284→  @MainActor
   285→  public func update<Element: EntityIdentifiable & Encodable & Sendable>(
   286→    id: String,
   287→    _ modify: (inout Element) -> Void
   288→  ) async throws where Value: RangeReplaceableCollection, Value.Element == Element {
   289→    @Dependency(\.instantReactor) var reactor
   290→    @Dependency(\.instantAppID) var appID
   291→
   292→    // Read from TripleStore directly to get optimistic updates that may not have
   293→    // propagated to wrappedValue yet. Fall back to wrappedValue for backward compat.
   294→    var entity: Element
   295→    if let storeEntity: Element = await reactor.getEntity(id: id) {
   296→      entity = storeEntity
   297→    } else if let wrappedEntity = wrappedValue.first(where: { $0.id == id }) {
   298→      entity = wrappedEntity
   299→    } else {
   300→      throw InstantMutationError.entityNotFound(id: id, namespace: Element.namespace)
   301→    }
   302→
   303→    // Encode BEFORE modification to compare
   304→    let beforeAttrs = try encodeEntityAttributes(entity)
   305→
   306→    // Apply modification locally
   307→    modify(&entity)
   308→
   309→    // Encode AFTER modification
   310→    let afterAttrs = try encodeEntityAttributes(entity)
   311→
   312→    // Compute only the changed fields (field-level update)
   313→    // This prevents concurrent updates from clobbering each other
   314→    let changedAttrs = computeChangedFields(before: beforeAttrs, after: afterAttrs)
   315→
   316→    guard !changedAttrs.isEmpty else {
   317→      // No actual changes - nothing to do
   318→      return
   319→    }
   320→
   321→    // Generate explicit update chunk with ONLY changed fields
   322→    let namespace = Element.namespace
   323→
   324→    let chunk = TransactionChunk(
   325→      namespace: namespace,
   326→      id: id,
   327→      ops: [["update", namespace, id, changedAttrs]]
   328→    )
   329→
   330→    // Send to Reactor which handles optimistic update + server transaction
   331→    try await reactor.transact(appID: appID, chunks: [chunk])
   332→  }
   333→  
   334→  // MARK: - Link
   335→  
   336→  /// Link an entity to another entity.
   337→  ///
   338→  /// This method sends an explicit "link" transaction to the server.
   339→  /// It does NOT modify local state (the link will be reflected when
   340→  /// the subscription receives the updated data).
   341→  ///
   342→  /// ## Example
   343→  ///
   344→  /// ```swift
   345→  /// @Shared(.instantSync(Schema.posts.with(\.author))) var posts: [Post]
   346→  ///
   347→  /// // Link a post to its author
   348→  /// try await $posts.link(post.id, "author", to: profile.id, namespace: "profiles")
   349→  /// ```
   350→  ///
   351→  /// - Parameters:
   352→  ///   - id: The ID of the entity to link from
   353→  ///   - label: The link label (e.g., "author", "creator")
   354→  ///   - targetId: The ID of the entity to link to
   355→  ///   - namespace: The namespace of the target entity
   356→  /// - Throws: If the transaction fails
   357→  @MainActor
   358→  public func link<Element: EntityIdentifiable & Sendable>(
   359→    _ id: String,
   360→    _ label: String,
   361→    to targetId: String,
   362→    namespace targetNamespace: String
   363→  ) async throws where Value: RangeReplaceableCollection, Value.Element == Element {
   364→    @Dependency(\.instantReactor) var reactor
   365→    @Dependency(\.instantAppID) var appID
   366→    
   367→    let namespace = Element.namespace
   368→    
   369→    let chunk = TransactionChunk(
   370→      namespace: namespace,
   371→      id: id,
   372→      ops: [["link", namespace, id, [label: ["id": targetId, "namespace": targetNamespace]] as [String: Any]]]
   373→    )
   374→    
   375→    try await reactor.transact(appID: appID, chunks: [chunk])
   376→  }
   377→  
   378→  /// Link an entity to another entity using the target entity directly.
   379→  ///
   380→  /// This is a convenience method that extracts the ID and namespace from the target entity.
   381→  ///
   382→  /// ## Example
   383→  ///
   384→  /// ```swift

   386→  ///
   387→  /// // Link a post to its author
   388→  /// try await $posts.link(post.id, "author", to: profile)
   389→  /// ```
   390→  ///
   391→  /// - Parameters:
   392→  ///   - id: The ID of the entity to link from
   393→  ///   - label: The link label (e.g., "author", "creator")
   394→  ///   - target: The entity to link to
   395→  /// - Throws: If the transaction fails
   396→  @MainActor
   397→  public func link<Element: EntityIdentifiable & Sendable, Target: EntityIdentifiable & Sendable>(
   398→    _ id: String,
   399→    _ label: String,
   400→    to target: Target
   401→  ) async throws where Value: RangeReplaceableCollection, Value.Element == Element {
   402→    try await link(id, label, to: target.id, namespace: Target.namespace)
   403→  }
   404→

   475→// MARK: - IdentifiedArray Support
   476→
   477→extension Shared {
   478→  
   479→  /// Create a new entity and sync to InstantDB (IdentifiedArray version).
   480→  ///
   481→  /// ## How This Works (TypeScript SDK Pattern)
   482→  ///
   483→  /// Following the TypeScript InstantDB SDK architecture:
   484→  /// 1. Generate a transaction chunk with the entity data
   485→  /// 2. Send to Reactor.transact() which:
   486→  ///    - Applies optimistic update to triple store
   487→  ///    - Notifies subscriptions via handleOptimisticUpsert()
   488→  ///    - Sends transaction to server
   489→  /// 3. The subscription's AsyncStream yields the new value
   490→  /// 4. InstantSyncKey.subscribe() updates the @Shared value
   491→  ///
   492→  /// We do NOT use withLock here because:
   493→  /// - withLock triggers save() which computes diffs
   494→  /// - Diff computation can race with other mutations and generate incorrect deletes
   495→  /// - The TypeScript SDK never uses diff-based saves for explicit mutations
   496→  @MainActor
   497→  public func create<Element: EntityIdentifiable & Encodable & Sendable>(
   498→    _ entity: Element
   499→  ) async throws where Value == IdentifiedArrayOf<Element> {
   500→    @Dependency(\.instantReactor) var reactor
   501→    @Dependency(\.instantAppID) var appID
   502→
   503→    // 1. Generate explicit transaction chunk
   504→    let namespace = Element.namespace
   505→    let attrs = try encodeEntityAttributes(entity)
   506→
   507→    let chunk = TransactionChunk(
   508→      namespace: namespace,
   509→      id: entity.id,
   510→      ops: [["update", namespace, entity.id, attrs]]
   511→    )
   512→
   513→    // 2. Send to Reactor which handles:
   514→    //    - Optimistic update to triple store
   515→    //    - Subscription notification (updates @Shared value)
   516→    //    - Server transaction
   517→    try await reactor.transact(appID: appID, chunks: [chunk])
   518→  }
   519→  
   520→  /// Delete an entity by ID and sync to InstantDB (IdentifiedArray version).
   521→  ///
   522→  /// Following TypeScript SDK pattern - no withLock to avoid triggering diff-based save.
   523→  @MainActor
   524→  public func delete<Element: EntityIdentifiable & Sendable>(
   525→    id: String
   526→  ) async throws where Value == IdentifiedArrayOf<Element> {
   527→    @Dependency(\.instantReactor) var reactor
   528→    @Dependency(\.instantAppID) var appID
   529→    
   530→    // Generate explicit delete chunk
   531→    let namespace = Element.namespace
   532→    
   533→    let chunk = TransactionChunk(
   534→      namespace: namespace,
   535→      id: id,
   536→      ops: [["delete", namespace, id]]
   537→    )
   538→    
   539→    // Send to Reactor which handles optimistic update + server transaction
   540→    try await reactor.transact(appID: appID, chunks: [chunk])
   541→  }
   542→  
   543→  /// Update an entity's fields and sync to InstantDB (IdentifiedArray version).
   544→  ///
   545→  /// Following TypeScript SDK pattern - we need to read the current entity to apply
   546→  /// the modification, but we don't use withLock to avoid triggering diff-based save.
   547→  ///
   548→  /// **Important**: This method sends only the CHANGED fields, not the entire entity.
   549→  /// This prevents concurrent updates from clobbering each other (e.g., updating
   550→  /// `text` and `words` simultaneously on a transcription segment).
   551→  ///
   552→  /// ## Why We Read From TripleStore
   553→  /// The `wrappedValue` is updated asynchronously via AsyncStream. When `create()`
   554→  /// and `update()` are called in rapid succession:
   555→  /// 1. `create()` applies optimistic update to TripleStore (synchronous)
   556→  /// 2. `create()` yields to AsyncStream (asynchronous delivery)
   557→  /// 3. `update()` reads `wrappedValue` → entity not found (stream not consumed yet)
   558→  ///
   559→  /// By reading from the TripleStore directly, we get the latest state including
   560→  /// optimistic updates that haven't yet flowed through to `wrappedValue`.
   561→  @MainActor
   562→  public func update<Element: EntityIdentifiable & Encodable & Sendable>(
   563→    id: String,
   564→    _ modify: (inout Element) -> Void
   565→  ) async throws where Value == IdentifiedArrayOf<Element> {
   566→    @Dependency(\.instantReactor) var reactor
   567→    @Dependency(\.instantAppID) var appID
   568→
   569→    // Read from TripleStore directly to get optimistic updates that may not have
   570→    // propagated to wrappedValue yet. Fall back to wrappedValue for backward compat.
   571→    var entity: Element
   572→    if let storeEntity: Element = await reactor.getEntity(id: id) {
   573→      entity = storeEntity
   574→    } else if let wrappedEntity = wrappedValue[id: id] {
   575→      entity = wrappedEntity
   576→    } else {
   577→      throw InstantMutationError.entityNotFound(id: id, namespace: Element.namespace)
   578→    }
   579→
   580→    // Encode BEFORE modification to compare
   581→    let beforeAttrs = try encodeEntityAttributes(entity)
   582→
   583→    // Apply modification locally
   584→    modify(&entity)
   585→
   586→    // Encode AFTER modification
   587→    let afterAttrs = try encodeEntityAttributes(entity)
   588→
   589→    // Compute only the changed fields (field-level update)
   590→    // This prevents concurrent updates from clobbering each other
   591→    let changedAttrs = computeChangedFields(before: beforeAttrs, after: afterAttrs)
   592→
   593→    guard !changedAttrs.isEmpty else {
   594→      // No actual changes - nothing to do
   595→      return
   596→    }
   597→
   598→    // Generate explicit update chunk with ONLY changed fields
   599→    let namespace = Element.namespace
   600→
   601→    let chunk = TransactionChunk(
   602→      namespace: namespace,
   603→      id: id,
   604→      ops: [["update", namespace, id, changedAttrs]]
   605→    )
   606→
   607→    // Send to Reactor which handles optimistic update + server transaction
   608→    try await reactor.transact(appID: appID, chunks: [chunk])
   609→  }
   610→
   611→  /// Update a single field of an entity without reading the full entity first.
   612→  ///
   613→  /// This is the safest method for concurrent updates because it:
   614→  /// 1. Does NOT read the current entity (avoids stale snapshots)
   615→  /// 2. Sends ONLY the specified field to the server
   616→  /// 3. Cannot clobber other fields being updated concurrently
   617→  ///
   618→  /// ## Example
   619→  ///
   620→  /// ```swift
   621→  /// // Update just the text field - safe even if words is being updated concurrently
   622→  /// try await $segments.updateField(id: segmentId, field: "text", value: "New text")
   623→  /// ```
   624→  ///
   625→  /// - Parameters:
   626→  ///   - id: The ID of the entity to update
   627→  ///   - field: The field name to update
   628→  ///   - value: The new value for the field
   629→  /// - Throws: If the transaction fails
   630→  @MainActor
   631→  public func updateField<Element: EntityIdentifiable & Sendable>(
   632→    id: String,
   633→    field: String,
   634→    value: Any
   635→  ) async throws where Value == IdentifiedArrayOf<Element> {
   636→    @Dependency(\.instantReactor) var reactor
   637→    @Dependency(\.instantAppID) var appID
   638→
   639→    let namespace = Element.namespace
   640→
   641→    let chunk = TransactionChunk(
   642→      namespace: namespace,
   643→      id: id,
   644→      ops: [["update", namespace, id, [field: value]]]
   645→    )
   646→
   647→    try await reactor.transact(appID: appID, chunks: [chunk])
   648→  }
   649→
   650→  /// Update multiple fields of an entity without reading the full entity first.
   651→  ///
   652→  /// This method sends ONLY the specified fields, preventing concurrent updates
   653→  /// from clobbering each other.
   654→  ///
   655→  /// ## Example
   656→  ///
   657→  /// ```swift
   658→  /// try await $segments.updateFields(id: segmentId, fields: [
   659→  ///   "text": "New text",
   660→  ///   "endTime": 1.5
   661→  /// ])
   662→  /// ```
   663→  @MainActor
   664→  public func updateFields<Element: EntityIdentifiable & Sendable>(
   665→    id: String,
   666→    fields: [String: Any]
   667→  ) async throws where Value == IdentifiedArrayOf<Element> {
   668→    @Dependency(\.instantReactor) var reactor
   669→    @Dependency(\.instantAppID) var appID
   670→
   671→    guard !fields.isEmpty else { return }
   672→
   673→    let namespace = Element.namespace
   674→
   675→    let chunk = TransactionChunk(
   676→      namespace: namespace,
   677→      id: id,
   678→      ops: [["update", namespace, id, fields]]
   679→    )
   680→
   681→    try await reactor.transact(appID: appID, chunks: [chunk])
   682→  }
   683→  
   684→  /// Link an entity to another entity (IdentifiedArray version).
   685→  @MainActor

   687→    _ id: String,
   688→    _ label: String,
   689→    to targetId: String,
   690→    namespace targetNamespace: String
   691→  ) async throws where Value == IdentifiedArrayOf<Element> {
   692→    @Dependency(\.instantReactor) var reactor
   693→    @Dependency(\.instantAppID) var appID
   694→    
   695→    let namespace = Element.namespace
   696→
   697→    let chunk = TransactionChunk(
   698→      namespace: namespace,

   700→      ops: [["link", namespace, id, [label: ["id": targetId, "namespace": targetNamespace]] as [String: Any]]]
   701→    )
   702→    
   703→    try await reactor.transact(appID: appID, chunks: [chunk])

   705→

   707→  @MainActor
   708→  public func link<Element: EntityIdentifiable & Sendable, Target: EntityIdentifiable & Sendable>(
   709→    _ id: String,

   711→    to target: Target
   712→  ) async throws where Value == IdentifiedArrayOf<Element> {

   748→
   749→// MARK: - Errors
   750→
   751→/// Errors that can occur during explicit mutations.
   752→public enum InstantMutationError: Error, LocalizedError {
   753→  case entityNotFound(id: String, namespace: String)
   754→  case encodingFailed(Error)
   755→  
   756→  public var errorDescription: String? {
   757→    switch self {
   758→    case .entityNotFound(let id, let namespace):
   759→      return "Entity not found: \(namespace)/\(id)"
   760→    case .encodingFailed(let error):
   761→      return "Failed to encode entity: \(error.localizedDescription)"
   762→    }
   763→  }
   764→}
   765→
   766→// MARK: - Helpers
   767→
   768→/// Compute only the fields that changed between two encoded attribute dictionaries.
   769→///
   770→/// This is critical for preventing concurrent update clobbering. When two updates
   771→/// run simultaneously:
   772→/// - Update A reads entity, modifies `text`, encodes all attrs including stale `words`
   773→/// - Update B reads entity, modifies `words`, encodes all attrs including stale `text`
   774→///
   775→/// Without field-level diffing, whichever update arrives at the server last
   776→/// clobbers the other's changes.
   777→///
   778→/// With field-level diffing:
   779→/// - Update A sends only `{text: "new text"}`
   780→/// - Update B sends only `{words: [...]}`
   781→/// - Both updates succeed without clobbering
   782→private func computeChangedFields(
   783→  before: [String: Any],
   784→  after: [String: Any]
   785→) -> [String: Any] {
   786→  var changed: [String: Any] = [:]
   787→
   788→  for (key, afterValue) in after {
   789→    if let beforeValue = before[key] {
   790→      // Field existed before - check if it changed
   791→      if !valuesAreEqual(beforeValue, afterValue) {
   792→        changed[key] = afterValue
   793→      }
   794→    } else {
   795→      // New field
   796→      changed[key] = afterValue
   797→    }
   798→  }
   799→
   800→  // Also check for removed fields (set to nil)
   801→  for key in before.keys {
   802→    if after[key] == nil {
   803→      changed[key] = NSNull()
   804→    }
   805→  }
   806→
   807→  return changed
   808→}
   809→
   810→/// Compare two values for equality.
   811→///
   812→/// This handles the various types that can appear in encoded entity attributes.
   813→private func valuesAreEqual(_ lhs: Any, _ rhs: Any) -> Bool {
   814→  // Handle NSNull
   815→  if lhs is NSNull && rhs is NSNull {
   816→    return true
   817→  }
   818→
   819→  // Handle primitives
   820→  if let l = lhs as? String, let r = rhs as? String {
   821→    return l == r
   822→  }
   823→  if let l = lhs as? Double, let r = rhs as? Double {
   824→    return l == r
   825→  }
   826→  if let l = lhs as? Int, let r = rhs as? Int {
   827→    return l == r
   828→  }
   829→  if let l = lhs as? Bool, let r = rhs as? Bool {
   830→    return l == r
   831→  }
   832→
   833→  // Handle arrays (JSON fields like `words`)
   834→  if let l = lhs as? [Any], let r = rhs as? [Any] {
   835→    guard l.count == r.count else { return false }
   836→    for (i, lVal) in l.enumerated() {
   837→      if !valuesAreEqual(lVal, r[i]) {
   838→        return false
   839→      }
   840→    }
   841→    return true
   842→  }
   843→
   844→  // Handle dictionaries (nested objects)
   845→  if let l = lhs as? [String: Any], let r = rhs as? [String: Any] {
   846→    guard l.count == r.count else { return false }
   847→    for (key, lVal) in l {
   848→      guard let rVal = r[key], valuesAreEqual(lVal, rVal) else {

   850→      }
   851→    }
   852→    return true
   853→  }

   856→  return false

   859→/// Encode an entity's attributes to a dictionary for the transaction.

   861→/// This extracts all properties except `id` and link properties (which are
   862→/// handled separately via link operations).

   864→/// ## Why We Use a Custom Encoder

   866→/// The naive approach of `JSONEncoder` + `JSONSerialization.jsonObject()` has a critical bug:
   867→/// `JSONSerialization` uses `NSNumber` for both numbers and booleans, and Swift's bridging
   868→/// can interpret `0`/`1` as `false`/`true`. This causes InstantDB server errors like:
   869→/// "Invalid value type for tiles.x. Value must be a number but the provided value type is boolean."
   870→///
   871→/// Instead, we use a custom `DictionaryEncoder` that preserves type information.
   872→private func encodeEntityAttributes<E: Encodable>(_ entity: E) throws -> [String: Any] {

   878→  // The TypeScript SDK sends JSON arrays (like `words: [{text, startTime, endTime}]`)
   879→  // as regular attributes, not as links.
   880→  var attrs: [String: Any] = [:]
   881→  for (key, value) in dict {
   882→    // Skip id - it's handled separately
   883→    if key == "id" { continue }
   884→
   885→    // Skip nil values
   886→    if case Optional<Any>.none = value { continue }
   887→    if value is NSNull { continue }
   888→
   889→    attrs[key] = value

   892→  return attrs

   210→private final class ContinuationBox<Value>: Sendable {

   234→  func resume(with result: Result<Value?, any Error>) {

   236→      defer { callback = nil }

   238→    }

   241→        """
   242→        \(description()) tried to resume its continuation more than once.
   243→        """
   244→      )
   245→      return
   246→    }

    56→async function upgradeQuerySubs5To6(
    57→  hash: string,
    58→  value: any,
    59→  querySubStore: IDBObjectStore,

    61→  const subs =
    62→    // Backwards compatibility for older versions where we JSON.stringified before storing
    63→    typeof value === 'string' ? JSON.parse(value) : value;
    64→  if (!subs) {

    68→  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {

    71→      const value = typeof v === 'string' ? JSON.parse(v) : v;
    72→      if (value.lastAccessed) {
    73→        const objectMeta: ObjectMeta = {
    74→          createdAt: value.lastAccessed,
    75→          updatedAt: value.lastAccessed,
    76→          size: value.result?.store?.triples?.length ?? 0,
    77→        };
    78→        objects[hash] = objectMeta;

    81→      putReqs.add(putReq);

    84→    const metaPutReq = querySubStore.put(meta, META_KEY);
    85→    putReqs.add(metaPutReq);

    87→      r.onsuccess = () => {
    88→        putReqs.delete(r);

    91→        }

    97→    }
    98→  });

   113→async function upgrade5To6(appId: string, v6Db: IDBDatabase): Promise<void> {

   136→      }

   186→export default class IndexedDBStorage extends StorageInterface {

   193→  constructor(appId: string, storeName: StorageInterfaceStoreName) {

   200→
   201→  _init(): Promise<IDBDatabase> {
   202→    return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
   203→      let requiresUpgrade = false;
   204→      const request = indexedDB.open(this.dbName, 1);
   205→
   206→      request.onerror = (event) => {
   207→        reject(event);
   208→      };
   209→
   210→      request.onsuccess = (event) => {

   238→  try {
   239→    const json = JSON.parse(body);
   240→    return rejectFn(new InstantAPIError({ status: res.status, body: json }));
   241→  } catch (_e) {
   242→    return rejectFn(
   243→      new InstantAPIError({
   244→        status: res.status,
   245→        body: { type: undefined, message: body },
   246→      }),
   247→    );
   248→  }
   249→}
   250→
   251→async function jsonFetch(
   252→  input: RequestInfo,
   253→  init: RequestInit | undefined,
   254→): Promise<any> {
   255→  const defaultFetchOpts = getDefaultFetchOpts();
   256→  const headers = {
   257→    ...(init?.headers || {}),
   258→    'Instant-Admin-Version': version,
   259→    'Instant-Core-Version': coreVersion,
   260→  };
   261→  const res = await fetch(input, { ...defaultFetchOpts, ...init, headers });
   262→  if (res.status === 200) {
   263→    const json = await res.json();
   264→    return Promise.resolve(json);
   265→  }
   266→
   267→  return jsonReject((x) => Promise.reject(x), res);
   268→}
   269→
   270→/**
   271→ *
   272→ * The first step: init your application!
   273→ *
   274→ * Visit https://instantdb.com/dash to get your `appId` :)
   275→ *
   276→ * @example
   277→ *  import { init } from "@instantdb/admin"
   278→ *
   279→ *  const db = init({
   280→ *    appId: process.env.INSTANT_APP_ID!,
   281→ *    adminToken: process.env.INSTANT_APP_ADMIN_TOKEN
   282→ *  })
   283→ *
   284→ *  // You can also provide a schema for type safety and editor autocomplete!
   285→ *
   286→ *  import { init } from "@instantdb/admin"
   287→ *  import schema from ""../instant.schema.ts";
   288→ *
   289→ *  const db = init({
   290→ *    appId: process.env.INSTANT_APP_ID!,
   291→ *    adminToken: process.env.INSTANT_APP_ADMIN_TOKEN,
   292→ *    schema,
   293→ *  })
   294→ *  // To learn more: https://instantdb.com/docs/modeling-data
   295→ */
   296→function init<
   297→  Schema extends InstantSchemaDef<any, any, any> = InstantUnknownSchema,
   298→  UseDates extends boolean = false,
   299→>(
   300→  // Allows config with missing `useDateObjects`, but keeps `UseDates`
   301→  // as a non-nullable in the InstantConfig type.
   302→  config: Omit<InstantConfig<Schema, UseDates>, 'useDateObjects'> & {
   303→    useDateObjects?: UseDates;
   304→  },
   305→): InstantAdminDatabase<Schema, UseDates, InstantConfig<Schema, UseDates>> {
   306→  const configStrict = {
   307→    ...config,
   308→    useDateObjects: (config.useDateObjects ?? false) as UseDates,
   309→  };
   310→
   311→  return new InstantAdminDatabase<
   312→    Schema,
   313→    UseDates,
   314→    InstantConfig<Schema, UseDates>
   315→  >(configStrict);
   316→}
   317→
   318→/**
   319→ * @deprecated
   320→ * `init_experimental` is deprecated. You can replace it with `init`.
   321→ *
   322→ * @example
   323→ *
   324→ * // Before
   325→ * import { init_experimental } from "@instantdb/admin"
   326→ * const db = init_experimental({  ...  });
   327→ *
   328→ * // After
   329→ * import { init } from "@instantdb/admin"
   330→ * const db = init({ ...  });
   331→ */
   332→const init_experimental = init;
   333→
   334→function steps(inputChunks) {
   335→  const chunks = Array.isArray(inputChunks) ? inputChunks : [inputChunks];
   336→  return chunks.flatMap(getOps);
   337→}

   339→type PresenceResult<Data> = {
   340→  [peerId: string]: { data: Data; 'peer-id': string; user: User | null };
   341→};
   342→
   343→class Rooms<Schema extends InstantSchemaDef<any, any, any>> {
   344→  config: FilledConfig;
   345→
   346→  constructor(config: FilledConfig) {
   347→    this.config = config;
   348→  }
   349→
   350→  async getPresence<RoomType extends keyof RoomsOf<Schema>>(
   351→    roomType: RoomType,
   352→    roomId: string,
   353→  ): Promise<PresenceResult<PresenceOf<Schema, RoomType>>> {
   354→    const res = await jsonFetch(
   355→      `${this.config.apiURI}/admin/rooms/presence?room-type=${String(roomType)}&room-id=${roomId}`,
   356→      {
   357→        method: 'GET',
   358→        headers: authorizedHeaders(this.config),
   359→      },
   360→    );
   361→
   362→    return res.sessions || {};
   363→  }
   364→}

   366→class Auth {
   367→  config: FilledConfig;
   368→
   369→  constructor(config: FilledConfig) {
   370→    this.config = config;
   371→    this.createToken = this.createToken.bind(this);
   372→  }
   373→
   374→  /**
   375→   * Generates a magic code for the user with the given email.
   376→   * This is useful if you want to use your own email provider
   377→   * to send magic codes.
   378→   *
   379→   * @example
   380→   *   // Generate a magic code
   381→   *   const { code } = await db.auth.generateMagicCode({ email })
   382→   *   // Send the magic code to the user with your own email provider
   383→   *   await customEmailProvider.sendMagicCode(email, code)
   384→   *
   385→   * @see https://instantdb.com/docs/backend#custom-magic-codes
   386→   */
   387→  generateMagicCode = async (email: string): Promise<{ code: string }> => {
   388→    return jsonFetch(`${this.config.apiURI}/admin/magic_code`, {
   389→      method: 'POST',
   390→      headers: authorizedHeaders(this.config),
   391→      body: JSON.stringify({ email }),
   392→    });
   393→  };
   394→
   395→  /**
   396→   * Sends a magic code to the user with the given email.
   397→   * This uses Instant's built-in email provider.
   398→   *
   399→   * @example
   400→   *   // Send an email to user with magic code
   401→   *   await db.auth.sendMagicCode({ email })
   402→   *
   403→   * @see https://instantdb.com/docs/backend#custom-magic-codes
   404→   */
   405→  sendMagicCode = async (email: string): Promise<{ code: string }> => {
   406→    return jsonFetch(`${this.config.apiURI}/admin/send_magic_code`, {
   407→      method: 'POST',
   408→      headers: authorizedHeaders(this.config),
   409→      body: JSON.stringify({ email }),
   410→    });
   411→  };
   412→
   413→  /**
   414→   * Verifies a magic code for the user with the given email.
   415→   *
   416→   * @example
   417→   *   const user = await db.auth.verifyMagicCode({ email, code })
   418→   *   console.log("Verified user:", user)
   419→   *
   420→   * @see https://instantdb.com/docs/backend#custom-magic-codes
   421→   */
   422→  verifyMagicCode = async (email: string, code: string): Promise<User> => {
   423→    const { user } = await jsonFetch(
   424→      `${this.config.apiURI}/admin/verify_magic_code`,
   425→      {
   426→        method: 'POST',
   427→        headers: authorizedHeaders(this.config),
   428→        body: JSON.stringify({ email, code }),
   429→      },
   430→    );
   431→    return user;
   432→  };
   433→
   434→  /**
   435→   * Creates a login token for the user with the given email.
   436→   * If that user does not exist, we create one.
   437→   *
   438→   * This is often useful for writing custom auth flows.
   439→   *
   440→   * @example
   441→   *   app.post('/custom_sign_in', async (req, res) => {
   442→   *     // ... your custom flow for users
   443→   *     const token = await db.auth.createToken({ email })
   444→   *     return res.status(200).send({ token })
   445→   *   })
   446→   *
   447→   * @see https://instantdb.com/docs/backend#custom-auth
   448→   */
   449→  createToken(email: { email: string } | { id: string }): Promise<AuthToken>;
   450→
   451→  /**
   452→   *
   453→   * @deprecated Passing an email string directly is deprecated.
   454→   *
   455→   * Use an object with the `email` key instead.
   456→   *
   457→   * @example
   458→   * // Before
   459→   * const token = await auth.createToken(email)
   460→   * // After
   461→   * const token = await auth.createToken({ email })
   462→   */
   463→  createToken(email: string): Promise<AuthToken>;
   464→
   465→  async createToken(
   466→    input: string | { email: string } | { id: string },
   467→  ): Promise<AuthToken> {
   468→    const body = typeof input === 'string' ? { email: input } : input;
   469→    const ret: { user: { refresh_token: string } } = await jsonFetch(
   470→      `${this.config.apiURI}/admin/refresh_tokens`,
   471→      {
   472→        method: 'POST',
   473→        headers: authorizedHeaders(this.config),
   474→        body: JSON.stringify(body),
   475→      },
   476→    );
   477→    return ret.user.refresh_token;
   478→  }
   479→
   480→  /**
   481→   * Verifies a given token and returns the associated user.
   482→   *
   483→   * This is often useful for writing custom endpoints, where you need
   484→   * to authenticate users.
   485→   *
   486→   * @example
   487→   *   app.post('/custom_endpoint', async (req, res) => {
   488→   *     const user = await db.auth.verifyToken(req.headers['token'])
   489→   *     if (!user) {
   490→   *       return res.status(401).send('Uh oh, you are not authenticated')
   491→   *     }
   492→   *     // ...
   493→   *   })
   494→   * @see https://instantdb.com/docs/backend#custom-endpoints
   495→   */
   496→  verifyToken = async (token: AuthToken): Promise<User> => {
   497→    const res = await jsonFetch(
   498→      `${this.config.apiURI}/runtime/auth/verify_refresh_token`,
   499→      {
   500→        method: 'POST',
   501→        headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' },
   502→        body: JSON.stringify({
   503→          'app-id': this.config.appId,
   504→          'refresh-token': token,
   505→        }),
   506→      },
   507→    );
   508→    return res.user;
   509→  };
   510→
   511→  /**
   512→   * Retrieves an app user by id, email, or refresh token.
   513→   *
   514→   * @example
   515→   *   try {
   516→   *     const user = await db.auth.getUser({ email })
   517→   *     console.log("Found user:", user)
   518→   *   } catch (err) {
   519→   *     console.error("Failed to retrieve user:", err.message);
   520→   *   }
   521→   *
   522→   * @see https://instantdb.com/docs/backend#retrieve-a-user
   523→   */
   524→  getUser = async (
   525→    params: { email: string } | { id: string } | { refresh_token: string },
   526→  ): Promise<Omit<User, 'refresh_token'>> => {
   527→    const qs = Object.entries(params)
   528→      .map(([k, v]) => `${k}=${encodeURIComponent(v)}`)
   529→      .join('&');
   530→
   531→    const response: { user: User } = await jsonFetch(
   532→      `${this.config.apiURI}/admin/users?${qs}`,
   533→      {
   534→        method: 'GET',
   535→        headers: authorizedHeaders(this.config),
   536→      },
   537→    );
   538→
   539→    return response.user;
   540→  };
   541→
   542→  /**
   543→   * Deletes an app user by id, email, or refresh token.
   544→   *
   545→   * NB: This _only_ deletes the user; it does not delete all user data.
   546→   * You will need to handle this manually.
   547→   *
   548→   * @example
   549→   *   try {
   550→   *     const deletedUser = await db.auth.deleteUser({ email })
   551→   *     console.log("Deleted user:", deletedUser)
   552→   *   } catch (err) {
   553→   *     console.error("Failed to delete user:", err.message);
   554→   *   }
   555→   *
   556→   * @see https://instantdb.com/docs/backend#delete-a-user
   557→   */
   558→  deleteUser = async (
   559→    params: { email: string } | { id: string } | { refresh_token: string },
   560→  ): Promise<User> => {
   561→    const qs = Object.entries(params).map(([k, v]) => `${k}=${v}`);
   562→    const response: { deleted: User } = await jsonFetch(
   563→      `${this.config.apiURI}/admin/users?${qs}`,
   564→      {
   565→        method: 'DELETE',
   566→        headers: authorizedHeaders(this.config),
   567→      },
   568→    );
   569→
   570→    return response.deleted;
   571→  };
   572→
   573→  /**
   574→   * Signs out the user with the given email.
   575→   * This invalidates any tokens associated with the user.
   576→   * If the user is not found, an error will be thrown.
   577→   *
   578→   * @example
   579→   *   try {
   580→   *     await auth.signOut({ email: "alyssa_p_hacker@instantdb.com" });
   581→   *     console.log("Successfully signed out");
   582→   *   } catch (err) {
   583→   *     console.error("Sign out failed:", err.message);
   584→   *   }
   585→   *
   586→   * @see https://instantdb.com/docs/backend#sign-out
   587→   */
   588→  async signOut(
   589→    params: { email: string } | { id: string } | { refresh_token: string },
   590→  ): Promise<void>;
   591→
   592→  /**
   593→   * @deprecated Passing an email string directly is deprecated.
   594→   * Use an object with the `email` key instead.
   595→   *
   596→   * @example
   597→   * // Before
   598→   * auth.signOut(email)
   599→   *
   600→   * // After
   601→   * auth.signOut({ email })
   602→   */
   603→  async signOut(email: string): Promise<void>;
   604→
   605→  async signOut(
   606→    input:
   607→      | string
   608→      | { email: string }
   609→      | { id: string }
   610→      | { refresh_token: string },
   611→  ): Promise<void> {
   612→    // If input is a string, we assume it's an email.
   613→    // This is because of backwards compatibility: we used to only
   614→    // accept email strings. Eventually we can remove this
   615→    const params = typeof input === 'string' ? { email: input } : input;
   616→    const config = this.config;
   617→    await jsonFetch(`${config.apiURI}/admin/sign_out`, {
   618→      method: 'POST',
   619→      headers: authorizedHeaders(config),
   620→      body: JSON.stringify(params),
   621→    });
   622→  }
   623→}

   625→type StorageFile = {
   626→  key: string;
   627→  name: string;
   628→  size: number;
   629→  etag: string;
   630→  last_modified: number;
   631→};
   632→
   633→type DeleteManyFileResponse = {
   634→  data: {
   635→    ids: string[] | null;
   636→  };
   637→};
   638→
   639→const isNodeReadable = (v: any): v is Readable =>
   640→  v &&
   641→  typeof v === 'object' &&
   642→  typeof v.pipe === 'function' &&
   643→  typeof v.read === 'function';
   644→
   645→const isWebReadable = (v: any): v is ReadableStream =>
   646→  v && typeof v.getReader === 'function';
   647→
   648→/**
   649→ * Functions to manage file storage.
   650→ */
   651→class Storage {
   652→  config: FilledConfig;
   653→  impersonationOpts?: ImpersonationOpts;
   654→
   655→  constructor(config: FilledConfig, impersonationOpts?: ImpersonationOpts) {
   656→    this.config = config;
   657→    this.impersonationOpts = impersonationOpts;
   658→  }
   659→
   660→  /**
   661→   * Uploads file at the provided path. Accepts a Buffer or a Readable stream.
   662→   *
   663→   * @see https://instantdb.com/docs/storage
   664→   * @example
   665→   *   const buffer = fs.readFileSync('demo.png');
   666→   *   const isSuccess = await db.storage.uploadFile('photos/demo.png', buffer);
   667→   */
   668→  uploadFile = async (
   669→    path: string,
   670→    file: Buffer | Readable | ReadableStream | Uint8Array,
   671→    metadata: FileOpts = {},
   672→  ): Promise<UploadFileResponse> => {
   673→    const headers = {
   674→      ...authorizedHeaders(this.config, this.impersonationOpts),
   675→      path,
   676→    };
   677→    if (metadata.contentDisposition) {
   678→      headers['content-disposition'] = metadata.contentDisposition;
   679→    }
   680→
   681→    // headers.content-type will become "undefined" (string)
   682→    // if not removed from the object
   683→    delete headers['content-type'];
   684→
   685→    if (metadata.contentType) {
   686→      headers['content-type'] = metadata.contentType;
   687→    }
   688→
   689→    let duplex: 'half' | undefined;
   690→    if (isNodeReadable(file)) {
   691→      duplex = 'half'; // one-way stream
   692→    }
   693→    if (isNodeReadable(file) || isWebReadable(file)) {
   694→      if (!metadata.fileSize) {
   695→        throw new Error(
   696→          'fileSize is required in metadata when uploading streams',
   697→        );
   698→      }
   699→      headers['content-length'] = metadata.fileSize.toString();
   700→    }
   701→
   702→    let options = {
   703→      method: 'PUT',
   704→      headers,
   705→      body: file as unknown as BodyInit,
   706→      ...(duplex && { duplex }),
   707→    };
   708→
   709→    return jsonFetch(`${this.config.apiURI}/admin/storage/upload`, options);
   710→  };
   711→
   712→  /**
   713→   * Deletes a file by its path name (e.g. "photos/demo.png").
   714→   *
   715→   * @see https://instantdb.com/docs/storage
   716→   * @example
   717→   *   await db.storage.delete("photos/demo.png");
   718→   */
   719→  delete = async (pathname: string): Promise<DeleteFileResponse> => {
   720→    return jsonFetch(
   721→      `${this.config.apiURI}/admin/storage/files?filename=${encodeURIComponent(
   722→        pathname,
   723→      )}`,
   724→      {
   725→        method: 'DELETE',
   726→        headers: authorizedHeaders(this.config, this.impersonationOpts),
   727→      },
   728→    );
   729→  };
   730→
   731→  /**
   732→   * Deletes multiple files by their path names (e.g. "photos/demo.png", "essays/demo.txt").
   733→   *
   734→   * @see https://instantdb.com/docs/storage
   735→   * @example
   736→   *   await db.storage.deleteMany(["images/1.png", "images/2.png", "images/3.png"]);
   737→   */
   738→  deleteMany = async (pathnames: string[]): Promise<DeleteManyFileResponse> => {
   739→    return jsonFetch(`${this.config.apiURI}/admin/storage/files/delete`, {
   740→      method: 'POST',
   741→      headers: authorizedHeaders(this.config, this.impersonationOpts),
   742→      body: JSON.stringify({ filenames: pathnames }),
   743→    });
   744→  };
   745→
   746→  /**
   747→   * @deprecated. This method will be removed in the future. Use `uploadFile`
   748→   * instead
   749→   */
   750→  upload = async (
   751→    pathname: string,
   752→    file: Buffer,
   753→    metadata: FileOpts = {},
   754→  ): Promise<boolean> => {
   755→    const { data: presignedUrl } = await jsonFetch(
   756→      `${this.config.apiURI}/admin/storage/signed-upload-url`,
   757→      {
   758→        method: 'POST',
   759→        headers: authorizedHeaders(this.config),
   760→        body: JSON.stringify({
   761→          app_id: this.config.appId,
   762→          filename: pathname,
   763→        }),
   764→      },
   765→    );
   766→    const headers = {};
   767→    const contentType = metadata.contentType;
   768→    if (contentType) {
   769→      headers['Content-Type'] = contentType;
   770→    }
   771→    const { ok } = await fetch(presignedUrl, {
   772→      method: 'PUT',
   773→      body: file as unknown as BodyInit,
   774→      headers,
   775→    });
   776→
   777→    return ok;
   778→  };
   779→
   780→  /**
   781→   * @deprecated. This method will be removed in the future. Use `query` instead
   782→   * @example
   783→   * const files = await db.query({ $files: {}})
   784→   */
   785→  list = async (): Promise<StorageFile[]> => {
   786→    const { data } = await jsonFetch(
   787→      `${this.config.apiURI}/admin/storage/files`,
   788→      {
   789→        method: 'GET',
   790→        headers: authorizedHeaders(this.config),
   791→      },
   792→    );
   793→
   794→    return data;
   795→  };
   796→
   797→  /**
   798→   * @deprecated. getDownloadUrl will be removed in the future.
   799→   * Use `query` instead to query and fetch for valid urls
   800→   *
   801→   * db.useQuery({
   802→   *   $files: {
   803→   *     $: {
   804→   *       where: {
   805→   *         path: "moop.png"
   806→   *       }
   807→   *     }
   808→   *   }
   809→   * })
   810→   */
   811→  getDownloadUrl = async (pathname: string): Promise<string> => {
   812→    const { data } = await jsonFetch(
   813→      `${this.config.apiURI}/admin/storage/signed-download-url?app_id=${this.config.appId}&filename=${encodeURIComponent(pathname)}`,
   814→      {
   815→        method: 'GET',
   816→        headers: authorizedHeaders(this.config),
   817→      },
   818→    );
   819→
   820→    return data;
   821→  };
   822→}
   823→
   824→type AdminQueryOpts = {
   825→  ruleParams?: RuleParams;
   826→  fetchOpts?: RequestInit;
   827→};
   828→
   829→/**
   830→ *
   831→ * The first step: init your application!
   832→ *
   833→ * Visit https://instantdb.com/dash to get your `appId` and `adminToken` :)
   834→ *
   835→ * @example
   836→ *  const db = init({ appId: "my-app-id", adminToken: "my-admin-token" })
   837→ */
   838→class InstantAdminDatabase<
   839→  Schema extends InstantSchemaDef<any, any, any>,
   840→  UseDates extends boolean = false,
   841→  Config extends InstantConfig<Schema, UseDates> = InstantConfig<
   842→    Schema,
   843→    UseDates
   844→  >,
   845→> {
   846→  config: InstantConfigFilled<Schema, UseDates>;
   847→  auth: Auth;
   848→  storage: Storage;
   849→  rooms: Rooms<Schema>;
   850→  impersonationOpts?: ImpersonationOpts;
   851→
   852→  public tx = txInit<NonNullable<Schema>>();
   853→
   854→  constructor(_config: Config) {
   855→    this.config = instantConfigWithDefaults(_config);
   856→    this.auth = new Auth(this.config);
   857→    this.storage = new Storage(this.config, this.impersonationOpts);
   858→    this.rooms = new Rooms<Schema>(this.config);
   859→  }
   860→
   861→  /**
   862→   * Sometimes you want to scope queries to a specific user.
   863→   *
   864→   * You can provide a user's auth token, email, or impersonate a guest.
   865→   *
   866→   * @see https://instantdb.com/docs/backend#impersonating-users
   867→   * @example
   868→   *  await db.asUser({email: "stopa@instantdb.com"}).query({ goals: {} })
   869→   */
   870→  asUser = (
   871→    opts: ImpersonationOpts,
   872→  ): InstantAdminDatabase<Schema, UseDates, Config> => {

     5→///
     6→/// A wrapper around InstantDB.TripleStore that adds Observation capabilities.
     7→public final class SharedTripleStore: @unchecked Sendable {
     8→    // Backing SDK Store
     9→    public let inner: InstantDB.TripleStore = InstantDB.TripleStore()
    10→    public let attrsStore: AttrsStore = AttrsStore()
    11→    
    12→    // Observers [EntityID: [Token: Callback]]
    13→    private var observers: [String: [UUID: @Sendable () -> Void]] = [:]
    14→    private let lock = NSRecursiveLock()
    15→
    16→    public init() {}
    17→    
    18→    // MARK: - Primitives
    19→    
    20→    public func updateAttributes(_ attributes: [Attribute]) {
    21→        for attr in attributes {
    22→            attrsStore.addAttr(attr)
    23→        }
    24→    }
    25→    
    26→    public func addTriple(_ triple: Triple, hasCardinalityOne: Bool, isRef: Bool) {
    27→        inner.addTriple(triple, hasCardinalityOne: hasCardinalityOne, isRef: isRef)
    28→        var changedIDs: Set<String> = [triple.entityId]
    29→        // For ref triples, also notify the target entity so reverse link views update.
    30→        if isRef, case .ref(let targetId) = triple.value {
    31→            changedIDs.insert(targetId)
    32→        }
    33→        notifyObservers(for: changedIDs)
    34→    }
    35→    
    36→    public func addTriples(_ triples: [Triple]) {
    37→        var changedIDs: Set<String> = []
    38→        for triple in triples {
    39→            let attr = attrsStore.getAttr(triple.attributeId)
    40→            let hasCardinalityOne = attr?.cardinality == .one
    41→            let isRef = attr?.valueType == .ref
    42→            inner.addTriple(triple, hasCardinalityOne: hasCardinalityOne, isRef: isRef)
    43→            changedIDs.insert(triple.entityId)
    44→
    45→            // For ref triples, also notify the target entity so reverse link views update.
    46→            // When a ref triple [subject, refAttr, target] is added, the target entity's
    47→            // "resolved view" changes (it now has an inbound link from subject).
    48→            // Without this, subscriptions driven by reverse links (e.g., media.transcriptionRuns)
    49→            // won't see new links until a server refresh.
    50→            if isRef, case .ref(let targetId) = triple.value {
    51→                changedIDs.insert(targetId)
    52→            }
    53→        }
    54→        notifyObservers(for: changedIDs)
    55→    }
    56→    
    57→    public func retractTriple(_ triple: Triple, isRef: Bool) {
    58→        inner.retractTriple(triple, isRef: isRef)
    59→        var changedIDs: Set<String> = [triple.entityId]
    60→        // For ref triples, also notify the target entity so reverse link views update.
    61→        if isRef, case .ref(let targetId) = triple.value {
    62→            changedIDs.insert(targetId)
    63→        }
    64→        notifyObservers(for: changedIDs)
    65→    }
    66→    
    67→    public func deleteEntity(id: String) {
    68→        var idsChanged: Set<String> = [id]
    69→        
    70→        // 1. Delete forward attributes and links (triples where this entity is the subject)
    71→        let triples = inner.getTriples(entity: id)
    72→        for triple in triples {
    73→             let attr = attrsStore.getAttr(triple.attributeId)
    74→             let isRef = attr?.valueType == .ref
    75→             inner.retractTriple(triple, isRef: isRef)
    76→        }
    77→        
    78→        // 2. Delete reverse links (triples where this entity is the VALUE/target of a ref)
    79→        // This matches the TypeScript SDK behavior in store.ts deleteEntity()
    80→        // Without this, the VAE index retains stale references to the deleted entity,
    81→        // causing "ghost" entities to appear when resolving reverse links.
    82→        let reverseTriples = inner.getReverseRefs(entityId: id)
    83→        for triple in reverseTriples {
    84→            let attr = attrsStore.getAttr(triple.attributeId)
    85→            let isRef = attr?.valueType == .ref
    86→            inner.retractTriple(triple, isRef: isRef)
    87→            // Also notify the entity that had the forward link
    88→            idsChanged.insert(triple.entityId)
    89→        }
    90→        
    91→        notifyObservers(for: idsChanged)
    92→    }
    93→

    95→    
    96→    /// Merges dictionaries (from Server Tree).
    97→    /// Used by legacy Reactor calls or if manual merging is needed.
    98→    func merge(dictionaries: [[String: Any]]) {
    99→        var changedIDs: Set<String> = []
   100→        for dict in dictionaries {
   101→            guard let id = dict["id"] as? String else { continue }
   102→            changedIDs.insert(id)
   103→        }
   104→        notifyObservers(for: changedIDs)
   105→    }

   109→    public func get<T: Decodable>(id: String, includedLinks: Set<String>? = nil) -> T? {

   111→    }
   112→
   113→    // MARK: - Observation
   114→
   115→    @discardableResult
   116→    func addObserver(id: String, onChange: @escaping @Sendable () -> Void) -> UUID {
   117→        lock.withLock {
   118→            let token = UUID()
   119→            if observers[id] == nil {
   120→                observers[id] = [:]
   121→            }
   122→            observers[id]?[token] = onChange
   123→            return token
   124→        }
   125→    }
   126→
   127→    func removeObserver(id: String, token: UUID) {
   128→        lock.withLock {
   129→            observers[id]?.removeValue(forKey: token)
   130→            if observers[id]?.isEmpty == true {
   131→                observers[id] = nil
   132→            }
   133→        }
   134→    }
   135→
   136→    private func notifyObservers(for ids: Set<String>) {
   137→        if ids.isEmpty { return }
   138→        
   139→        // Snapshot callbacks synchronously to avoid data races
   140→        let snapshot: [@Sendable () -> Void] = lock.withLock {
   141→            var callbacks: [@Sendable () -> Void] = []
   142→            for id in ids {
   143→                if let tokens = observers[id] {
   144→                    callbacks.append(contentsOf: tokens.values)
   145→                }
   146→            }
   147→            return callbacks
   148→        }
   149→        
   150→        if snapshot.isEmpty { return }
   151→
   152→        // Execute callbacks asynchronously
   153→        Task {
   154→            for callback in snapshot {
   155→                callback()
   156→            }
   157→        }
   158→    }
   159→}

Based on the search results, here's information about Swift fire-and-forget Task patterns for calling async code from synchronous functions:

## Swift Fire-and-Forget Task Patterns

### Basic Concept

The "fire and forget" approach allows you to create a task without storing it, and Swift will ensure it runs until completion correctly. Sometimes you don't care about the result of the task, or sometimes the task automatically updates some external value when it completes, so you can just use them as "fire and forget" operations. This makes them a great way to run async code from a synchronous function.

### Using Task as a Bridge

Swift's new Task type enables us to encapsulate, observe, and control a unit of asynchronous work — which in turn lets us call async-marked APIs, and perform background work, even within code that's otherwise completely synchronous. That way, we can gradually introduce async functions and the rest of Swift's new concurrency system, even within applications that weren't designed with those new features in mind.(no content)Perhaps the most common way to use a Task within UI-based apps is to have it act as a bridge between our synchronous, main thread-bound UI code, and any background operations that are used to fetch or process the data that our UI is rendering.

### Key Behavior

Asynchronous tasks are not automatically cancelled when their corresponding Task handle is deallocated — they just keep executing in the background.(no content)The lifetime of the task is not bound by the button's action closure. So, even though the closure will finish immediately, the task it created will carry on running to completion.

### Mutation Challenges

Developers often face challenges doing complex operations asynchronously in background threads and bringing results back to the main thread, with errors like "Mutation of captured var 'personName' in concurrently-executing code."

### Using Actors for Thread-Safe Mutation

By using an actor for a management object, you can be confident that operations performed on that object will be executed safely and consistently. Swift automatically handles synchronization of access to the actor, avoiding race conditions and conflicts in reading and writing properties or method calls. This ensures that even in scenarios with multiple threads working simultaneously, the object's state will remain intact and consistent.

### Common Issue with Cascading Async

When adopting structured concurrency, developers run into the issue of the entire call stack needing to be updated to async functions, even when they are void returning. Many want to make a "fire and forget" type async call from a synchronous method and break this chain.

Here's what I found:

## TanStack Query Mutation Pattern

TanStack Query, formerly known as React Query, has two main functions: useQuery and useMutation.

### Core Callbacks

The `onSuccess` callback fires when the mutation is successful and will be passed the mutation's result.(no content)The `onError` function will fire if the mutation encounters an error and will be passed the error.(no content)`onSettled` allows you to carry out operations regardless of the outcome - it fires when the mutation is either successful or encounters an error and receives either the data or error.(no content)`onMutate` is an optional callback for optimistic updates that fires before the mutation function. The value returned from this function will be passed to both the onError and onSettled functions in the event of a mutation failure and can be useful for rolling back optimistic updates.

### Usage Pattern

Supported callback options include: onSuccess, onError and onSettled.(no content)There is a slight difference in handling onSuccess, onError and onSettled callbacks when it comes to consecutive mutations. When passed to the mutate function, they will be fired up only once and only if the component is still mounted. This is due to the fact that mutation observer is removed and resubscribed every time when the mutate function is called. On the contrary, useMutation handlers execute for each mutate call.

### Awaiting Callbacks

Only callbacks on useMutation are awaited - the ones on .mutate are not. The reason is that .mutate can be called multiple times. Invalidation should usually happen on the callbacks of useMutation.

---

The TanStack Query library is primarily designed for JavaScript/TypeScript ecosystems (React, Vue, Solid, Svelte). Based on the search results, here's what I found about Swift WebSocket URLSessionWebSocketTask with actors and threading:

## URLSessionWebSocketTask Overview

URLSessionWebSocketTask is a URL session task that communicates over the WebSockets protocol standard.(no content)Unlike other tasks, the URLSessionWebSocketTask class does not use the HTTP protocol but the WebSocket protocol. Unlike HTTP, WebSocket keeps an open connection between a client and a server, allowing the server to send content to the client without being requested. While WebSocket is primarily used in interactive web applications, it's also useful for iOS apps that require low latency, such as live chats, collaboration on shared documents, and data broadcasts like stock prices and sports scores.(no content)URLSession does not have an asynchronous API to create a URLSessionWebSocketTask as it happened for the tasks above. Instead, you must create one explicitly calling the webSocketTask(with:) method on a session and then start it using the task's resume() method.

## Using WebSocket with Swift Concurrency

With a generic WebSocketConnection class and some simple SwiftUI magic, it's not a big task to create a simple real-time iOS application powered by WebSocket technology and Swift Concurrency. Wrapping the URLSessionWebSocketTask's receive method in an AsyncThrowingStream even makes it possible to asynchronously iterate over incoming messages.

## MainActor and Background Thread Behavior

MainActor is a new attribute introduced in Swift 5.5 as a global actor providing an executor that performs its tasks on the main thread.(no content)Calling async functions from a Task on the main actor will perform the async work on background threads. The Task begins on the main thread, but the URLSession data task jumps to a background thread to wait for the network response.(no content)When using a Task from the main actor, it can still jump between various threads to perform async work and avoid blocking the UI thread with waits.

## Key Threading Considerations

@MainActor is really helpful to make code run on the main actor, but it's not foolproof. For example, if you have a @MainActor class then in theory all its methods will run on the main actor, but one of those methods could trigger code to run on a background task. For example, if you're using Face ID and call evaluatePolicy() to authenticate the user, the completion handler will be called on a background thread even though that code is still within the @MainActor class.(no content)If you do need to spontaneously run some code on the main actor, you can do that by calling MainActor.run() and providing your work. This allows you to safely push work onto the main actor no matter where your code is currently running.

## Detached Tasks for Background Execution

In practical terms, a detached task will always run on a background thread. You can create a detached task as follows: `Task.detached { // this runs on the global executor }`(no content)Detached tasks are added to the global executor—a little like the global queue in Grand Central Dispatch. While they don't block the UI thread, the workload might not be run immediately—we can set priority level (e.g. .low, .medium, or .high) to nudge the system in the right direction.

## Actor Isolation for WebSocket Connections

A WebSocketConnection class can be implemented as `final class WebSocketConnection<Incoming: Decodable & Sendable, Outgoing: Encodable & Sendable>: NSObject, Sendable` with the webSocketTask, encoder, and decoder as private properties.

This pattern ensures thread-safe handling of WebSocket communications while properly managing actor isolation.
