    11→   [instant.reactive.receive-queue :as receive-queue]
    12→   [instant.reactive.store :as rs]
    13→   [instant.reactive.topics :as topics]
    14→   [instant.util.async :as ua]
    15→   [instant.util.e2e-tracer :as e2e-tracer]
    16→   [instant.util.tracer :as tracer])
    17→  (:import
    18→   (java.sql Timestamp)
    19→   (java.time Instant)
    20→   (java.time.temporal ChronoUnit)
    21→   (java.util Map Queue)
    22→   (java.util.concurrent ConcurrentHashMap)
    23→   (org.postgresql.replication LogSequenceNumber)))
    24→
    25→(declare wal-opts)
    26→
    27→(declare invalidator-q)
    28→
    29→(defn- invalidate!
    30→  "Given a collection of changes, stales all relevant queries and returns
    31→  sockets to be refreshed."
    32→  ;; process-id used for tests
    33→  [_process-id store {:keys [app-id tx-id] :as wal-record}]
    34→  (let [topics      (topics/topics-for-changes wal-record)
    35→        session-ids (rs/mark-stale-topics! store app-id tx-id topics wal-record)
    36→        sockets     (keep #(:session/socket (rs/session store %)) session-ids)
    37→        sync-subs (rs/get-stale-sync-subs store app-id topics)]
    38→    {:sockets sockets
    39→     :sync-subs sync-subs}))
    40→
    41→(defn- invalidate-byop!
    42→  "Given a collection of changes, stales all relevant queries and returns
    43→  sockets to be refreshed."
    44→  [table-info app-id store {:keys [tx-id] :as record}]
    45→  (let [topics      (topics/topics-for-byop-changes table-info record)
    46→        session-ids (rs/mark-stale-topics! store app-id tx-id topics record)
    47→        sockets     (keep #(:session/socket (rs/session store %)) session-ids)]
    48→    sockets))
    49→
    50→;; ------
    51→;; wal record xf
    52→
    53→(defn app-id-from-columns [columns]
    54→  (some-> columns
    55→          (topics/get-column "app_id")
    56→          (parse-uuid)))
    57→
    58→(defn extract-app-id
    59→  [{:keys [columns] :as _change}]
    60→  (app-id-from-columns columns))
    61→
    62→(defn id-from-columns [columns]
    63→  (some-> columns
    64→          (topics/get-column "id")
    65→          (parse-uuid)))
    66→
    67→(defn extract-id
    68→  [{:keys [columns] :as _change}]
    69→  (id-from-columns columns))
    70→
    71→(defn extract-tx-id [{:keys [columns] :as _change}]
    72→  (topics/get-column columns "id"))
    73→
    74→(defn extract-tx-created-at [{:keys [columns] :as _change}]
    75→  (when-let [^String created-at (topics/get-column columns "created_at")]
    76→    (.toInstant (Timestamp/valueOf created-at))))
    77→
    78→(defn transform-wal-record [{:keys [changes messages tx-bytes] :as _record}]
    79→  ;; n.b. Add the table to the `add-tables` setting in create-replication-stream
    80→  ;;      or else we will never be notified about it.
    81→  (let [{:strs [idents triples attrs transactions
    82→                wal_logs wal_logs_0 wal_logs_1 wal_logs_2 wal_logs_3 wal_logs_4 wal_logs_5 wal_logs_6 wal_logs_7]}
    83→        (group-by :table changes)
    84→
    85→        some-changes (or (seq idents)
    86→                         (seq triples)
    87→                         (seq attrs))
    88→        transactions-change (first transactions)
    89→        app-id (extract-app-id transactions-change)]
    90→
    91→
    92→    (when (and some-changes app-id)
    93→      (let [tx-id (extract-tx-id transactions-change)
    94→            tx-created-at (extract-tx-created-at transactions-change)]
    95→        (e2e-tracer/invalidator-tracking-step! {:tx-id tx-id
    96→                                                :tx-created-at tx-created-at
    97→                                                :name "transform-wal-record"})
    98→        ;; n.b. make sure to update combine-wal-records below if new
    99→        ;;      items are added to this map
   100→        {:attr-changes attrs
   101→         :ident-changes idents
   102→         :triple-changes triples
   103→         :app-id app-id
   104→         :tx-created-at tx-created-at
   105→         :tx-id tx-id
   106→         :tx-bytes tx-bytes
   107→         :messages messages
   108→         :wal-logs (concat wal_logs wal_logs_0 wal_logs_1 wal_logs_2 wal_logs_3
   109→                           wal_logs_4 wal_logs_5 wal_logs_6 wal_logs_7)}))))
   110→
   111→(defn wal-record-xf
   112→  "Filters wal records for supported changes. Returns [app-id changes]"
   113→  []
   114→  (keep #'transform-wal-record))
   115→
   116→(defn combine-wal-records
   117→  "Combines a list of wal-records into a single wal-record.
   118→   We combine all of the change lists and advance the tx-id to the
   119→   latest tx-id in the list."
   120→  [r1 r2]
   121→  (when (< (::grouped-queue/combined r1 1) (flags/flag :invalidator-batch-limit 500))
   122→    ;; Complain loudly if we accidently mix wal-records from multiple apps
   123→    (when (not= (:app-id r1) (:app-id r2))
   124→      (throw (ex-info "app-id mismatch in combine-wal-records" {:r1 r1 :r2 r2})))
   125→    (e2e-tracer/invalidator-tracking-step! {:tx-id (:tx-id r1)
   126→                                            :name "skipped-in-combined-wal-record"})
   127→
   128→    ;; Keep the old tx-created-at so that we see the worst case wal-latency-ms
   129→    (-> r1
   130→        (update :attr-changes   (fnil into []) (:attr-changes r2))
   131→        (update :ident-changes  (fnil into []) (:ident-changes r2))
   132→        (update :triple-changes (fnil into []) (:triple-changes r2))
   133→        (update :messages       (fnil into []) (:messages r2))
   134→        (update :wal-logs       (fnil into []) (:wal-logs r2))
   135→        (update :tx-bytes       (fnil + 0) (:tx-bytes r2))
   136→        (assoc :tx-id           (:tx-id r2)))))
   137→
   138→(defn transform-byop-wal-record [{:keys [changes nextlsn]}]
   139→  ;; TODO(byop): if change is empty, then there might be changes to the schema
   140→  (let [triple-changes (filter (fn [c]
   141→                                 (#{:update :insert :delete} (:action c)))
   142→                               changes)]
   143→    (when triple-changes
   144→      {:triple-changes triple-changes
   145→       :tx-id (LogSequenceNumber/.asLong nextlsn)})))
   146→
   147→(defn byop-wal-record-xf
   148→  []
   149→  (keep #'transform-byop-wal-record))
   150→
   151→;; ------
   152→;; invalidator
   153→
   154→(defn- store-snapshot [store app-id]
   155→  (rs/->ReactiveStore
   156→   (ds/conn-from-db @(:sessions store))
   157→   (^[Map] ConcurrentHashMap/new
   158→    (if-let [conn (some-> store
   159→                          :conns
   160→                          (Map/.get app-id)
   161→                          deref
   162→                          ds/conn-from-db)]
   163→      {app-id conn}
   164→      {}))))
   165→
   166→(defn wal-latency-ms [{:keys [tx-created-at]}]
   167→  (when tx-created-at
   168→    (.between ChronoUnit/MILLIS tx-created-at (Instant/now))))
   169→
   170→(defn process-wal-record [process-id store record-count wal-record]
   171→  (let [{:keys [app-id tx-id tx-created-at tx-bytes]} wal-record]
   172→    (tracer/with-span! {:name "invalidator/work"
   173→                        :attributes {:app-id app-id
   174→                                     :tx-id tx-id
   175→                                     :wal-record-count record-count
   176→                                     :wal-latency-ms (wal-latency-ms wal-record)
   177→                                     :tx-bytes tx-bytes}}
   178→
   179→      (try
   180→        (let [{:keys [sockets sync-subs]} (invalidate! process-id store wal-record)]
   181→          (tracer/add-data! {:attributes {:num-sockets (count sockets)
   182→                                          :num-sync-subs (count sync-subs)
   183→                                          :tx-latency-ms (e2e-tracer/tx-latency-ms tx-created-at)}})
   184→          (e2e-tracer/invalidator-tracking-step! {:tx-id tx-id
   185→                                                  :tx-created-at tx-created-at
   186→                                                  :name "send-refreshes"
   187→                                                  :attributes {:num-sockets (count sockets)}})
   188→          (when (or (config/dev?) (seq sync-subs))
   189→            (rs/add-transaction-to-sync-table-txes wal-record))
   190→          (tracer/with-span! {:name "invalidator/send-refreshes"}
   191→            (doseq [{:keys [id]} sockets]
   192→              (receive-queue/put! {:op :refresh
   193→                                   :session-id id
   194→                                   :tx-id tx-id
   195→                                   :tx-created-at tx-created-at}))
   196→            (doseq [{:sync/keys [session-id id]} sync-subs]
   197→              (receive-queue/put! {:op :refresh-sync-table
   198→                                   :app-id app-id
   199→                                   :session-id session-id
   200→                                   :subscription-id id}))))
   201→        (catch Throwable t
   202→          (def -wal-record wal-record)
   203→          (def -store-value (store-snapshot store app-id))
   204→          (tracer/add-exception! t {:escaping? false}))))))
   205→
   206→(defn drop-backpressure? [queue wal-record]
   207→  (let [app-id (:app-id wal-record)
   208→        group (get (:groups queue) app-id)
   209→        head (when group (Queue/.peek group))
   210→        put-at (some-> head :instant.grouped-queue/put-at)
   211→        latency (if put-at (- (System/currentTimeMillis) put-at) 0)]
   212→    (when (and (flags/invalidator-drop-backpressure? app-id)
   213→               (> latency (flags/invalidator-drop-tx-latency-ms)))
   214→      (tracer/record-info! {:name "invalidator/drop-backpressure"
   215→                            :attributes {:app-id app-id
   216→                                         :latency latency}})
   217→      true)))
   218→
   219→(defn start-worker [process-id store wal-chan]
   220→  (tracer/record-info! {:name "invalidation-worker/start"})
   221→  (let [queue
   222→        (grouped-queue/start
   223→         {:group-key-fn :app-id
   224→          :combine-fn   combine-wal-records
   225→          :process-fn   (fn [_key wal-record]
   226→                          (process-wal-record process-id
   227→                                              store
   228→                                              (::grouped-queue/combined wal-record 1)
   229→                                              wal-record))
   230→          :metrics-path "instant.reactive.invalidator.q"
   231→          :max-workers  8})]
   232→    (a/go
   233→      (loop []
   234→        (when-some [wal-record (a/<! wal-chan)]
   235→          (when-not (drop-backpressure? queue wal-record)
   236→            (grouped-queue/put! queue wal-record))
   237→          (recur)))
   238→      (grouped-queue/stop queue)
   239→      (tracer/record-info! {:name "invalidation-worker/shutdown"}))
   240→    queue))
   241→
   242→(defn handle-byop-record [table-info app-id store wal-record]
   243→  (when-let [record (transform-byop-wal-record wal-record)]
   244→    (try
   245→      (let [sockets (invalidate-byop! table-info app-id store record)]
   246→        (tracer/add-data! {:attributes {:num-sockets (count sockets)}})
   247→        (tracer/with-span! {:name "invalidator/send-refreshes"}
   248→          (doseq [{:keys [id]} sockets]
   249→            (receive-queue/put! {:op :refresh
   250→                                 :session-id id}))))
   251→      (catch Throwable t
   252→        (def -wal-record wal-record)
   253→        (def -store-value (store-snapshot store app-id))
   254→        (tracer/add-exception! t {:escaping? false})))))
   255→
   256→(defn start-byop-worker [store wal-chan]
   257→  (tracer/record-info! {:name "invalidation-worker/start-byop"})
   258→  (let [app-id config/instant-on-instant-app-id
   259→        {:keys [table-info]} (pg-introspect/introspect (aurora/conn-pool :read)
   260→                                                       "public")]
   261→    (loop []
   262→      (let [wal-record (a/<!! wal-chan)]
   263→        (if-not wal-record
   264→          (tracer/record-info! {:name "invalidation-worker/shutdown-byop"})
   265→          (do
   266→            (try
   267→              (handle-byop-record table-info
   268→                                  app-id
   269→                                  store
   270→                                  wal-record)
   271→              (catch Throwable t
   272→                (def -wal-record wal-record)
   273→                (def -store-value store)
   274→                (tracer/add-exception! t {:escaping? false})))
   275→            (recur)))))))
   276→
   277→;; ------
   278→;; orchestration
   279→
   280→(defn wal-ex-handler [e]
   281→  (tracer/record-exception-span! e {:name "invalidator/wal-ex-handler"
   282→                                    :escaping? false})
   283→  (wal/shutdown! wal-opts))
   284→
   285→(defn create-wal-chans []
   286→  (if-not config/instant-on-instant-app-id
   287→    (let [chan (a/chan 1 (wal-record-xf))]
   288→      {:wal-chan chan
   289→       :close-signal-chan (a/chan)
   290→       :worker-chan chan})
   291→    (let [wal-chan (a/chan 1)
   292→          mult (a/mult wal-chan)
   293→          worker-chan (a/chan 1 (wal-record-xf))
   294→          byop-chan (a/chan 1)]
   295→      (a/tap mult worker-chan)
   296→      (a/tap mult byop-chan)
   297→      {:wal-chan wal-chan
   298→       ;; Nothing will ever be put on this chan,
   299→       ;; it will be closed when the wal-chan is closed
   300→       ;; so that the consumer can know to stop waiting for
   301→       ;; its puts to complete
   302→       :close-signal-chan (a/chan)
   303→       :worker-chan worker-chan
   304→       :byop-chan byop-chan})))
   305→
   306→(defn start
   307→  "Entry point for invalidator. Starts a WAL listener and pipes WAL records to
   308→  our partition router. Partition router dispatches records to app workers who run `go-work`"
   309→  ([]
   310→   (start @config/process-id))
   311→  ([process-id]
   312→   (let [{:keys [wal-chan worker-chan byop-chan close-signal-chan]}
   313→         (create-wal-chans)
   314→
   315→         wal-opts (wal/make-wal-opts {:wal-chan wal-chan
   316→                                      :worker-chan worker-chan
   317→                                      :close-signal-chan close-signal-chan
   318→                                      :ex-handler wal-ex-handler
   319→                                      :get-conn-config (fn []
   320→                                                         (or (config/get-next-aurora-config)
   321→                                                             ;; Use the next db so that we don't
   322→                                                             ;; have to worry about restarting the
   323→                                                             ;; invalidator when failing over to a
   324→                                                             ;; new blue/green deployment
   325→                                                             (config/get-aurora-config)))
   326→                                      :slot-suffix process-id
   327→                                      :slot-type :invalidator})]
   328→     (ua/fut-bg
   329→      (wal/start-worker wal-opts))
   330→
   331→     @(:started-promise wal-opts)
   332→
   333→     (def invalidator-q
   334→       (start-worker process-id rs/store worker-chan))
   335→
   336→     (when byop-chan
   337→       (ua/fut-bg
   338→        (start-byop-worker rs/store byop-chan)))
   339→
   340→     wal-opts)))
   341→
   342→(defn start-global []
   343→  (def wal-opts (start)))
   344→
   345→(defn stop [wal-opts]
   346→  (let [shutdown-future (future (wal/shutdown! wal-opts))]
   347→    (loop []
   348→      (when-not (realized? shutdown-future)
   349→        (wal/kick-wal (aurora/conn-pool :write))
   350→        (Thread/sleep 100)
   351→        (recur))))
   352→  (a/close! (:to wal-opts))
   353→  (a/close! (:close-signal-chan wal-opts))
   354→  (a/close! (:worker-chan wal-opts)))
   355→
   356→(defn stop-global []
   357→  (when (bound? #'wal-opts)
   358→    (stop wal-opts)))
   359→
   360→(defn restart []
   361→  (stop-global)
   362→  (start-global))
   363→

    54→      }
    55→    }

    57→

    63→  #endif

   357→  final class Box: @unchecked Sendable {
   358→    private let lock = NSRecursiveLock()
   359→    private var _reference: any MutableReference<Value>
   360→    #if canImport(Combine)
   361→      let subject = PassthroughRelay<Value>()
   362→      private var subjectCancellable: AnyCancellable
   363→    #endif
   364→    #if canImport(SwiftUI)
   365→      private var swiftUICancellable: AnyCancellable?
   366→    #endif
   367→    var reference: any MutableReference<Value> {
   368→      _read {
   369→        lock.lock()
   370→        defer { lock.unlock() }
   371→        yield _reference
   372→      }
   373→      _modify {
   374→        lock.lock()
   375→        defer { lock.unlock() }
   376→        yield &_reference
   377→        #if canImport(Combine)
   378→          subjectCancellable = _reference.publisher.subscribe(subject)
   379→        #endif
   380→      }
   381→      set {
   382→        lock.withLock {
   383→          _reference = newValue
   384→          #if canImport(Combine)
   385→            subjectCancellable = _reference.publisher.subscribe(subject)
   386→          #endif
   387→        }
   388→      }
   389→    }
   390→    init(_ reference: any MutableReference<Value>) {
   391→      self._reference = reference
   392→      #if canImport(Combine)
   393→        subjectCancellable = _reference.publisher.subscribe(subject)
   394→      #endif
   395→    }
   396→    deinit {
   397→      #if canImport(Combine)
   398→        subjectCancellable.cancel()
   399→      #endif
   400→      #if canImport(SwiftUI)
   401→        swiftUICancellable?.cancel()
   402→      #endif
   403→    }
   404→    #if canImport(SwiftUI)
   405→      func subscribe(state: State<Int>) {
   406→        guard #unavailable(iOS 17, macOS 14, tvOS 17, watchOS 10) else { return }
   407→        _ = state.wrappedValue
   408→        let cancellable = subject.sink { _ in state.wrappedValue &+= 1 }
   409→        lock.withLock { swiftUICancellable = cancellable }
   410→      }
   411→    #endif
   412→  }
   413→}

   427→extension Shared: Equatable where Value: Equatable {
   428→  public static func == (lhs: Self, rhs: Self) -> Bool {
   429→    // TODO: Explore 'isTesting ? (check snapshot against value) : lhs.reference == rhs.reference
   430→    func isEqual() -> Bool {

    55→    stateForResult(_core._reactor.getPreviousResult(query)),
    56→  );

    59→  // if `subscribe` changes, so we use `useCallback` to memoize the function.
    60→  const subscribe = useCallback(

     1→// PersistedObjects save data outside of memory.
     2→//
     3→// When we load a persisted object, it's possible we call `set`
     4→// before we finish loading. To address we handle set in two ways:
     5→//
     6→// 1. Before load
     7→// We simply update currentValue in memory
     8→//
     9→// 2. After load
    10→// We update currentValue in memory and in storage
    11→//
    12→// Each PersistedObject provides it's own `onMerge`
    13→// function to handle the merge of data from storage and memory
    14→// on load

    17→// callback immediately

    19→import { create } from 'mutative';
    20→import type { Logger } from './log.ts';

    22→function safeIdleCallback(cb, timeout: number) {
    23→  if (typeof requestIdleCallback === 'undefined') {
    24→    cb();
    25→  } else {
    26→    requestIdleCallback(cb, { timeout });
    27→  }
    28→}

   474→  // Schedules a GC to run in one minute (unless it is already scheduled)

   517→  public updateInPlace(f: (prev: Record<string, T>) => void) {

   233→    // Helper function to collect types recursively from a generic type
   234→    func collectAndGenerateTypes(from genericType: GenericTypeIR, fieldName: String, entityName: String) {

     3→//
     4→// Intermediate Representation (IR) for InstantDB schemas.
     5→// This is the canonical representation that both TypeScript and Swift parsers produce,
     6→// and that both TypeScript and Swift generators consume.
     7→//
     8→// ## Generic Type Support
     9→//
    10→// This IR supports TypeScript generics on field types:
    11→// - String unions: i.string<"a" | "b" | "c">() → GenericTypeIR.stringUnion
    12→// - Object types: i.json<{ field: type }>() → GenericTypeIR.object
    13→// - Arrays: i.json<Type[]>() → GenericTypeIR.array
    14→// - Type references: i.string<MyType>() → resolved via SymbolTable
    15→
    16→import Foundation
    17→
    18→// MARK: - Schema IR
    19→
    20→/// The complete schema intermediate representation.
    21→///
    22→/// This is the canonical format that enables bidirectional codegen:
    23→/// - TypeScript parser → SchemaIR → Swift generator
    24→/// - Swift parser → SchemaIR → TypeScript generator
    25→///
    26→/// ## Example
    27→///
    28→/// ```swift
    29→/// let schema = SchemaIR(
    30→///   entities: [
    31→///     EntityIR(name: "todos", fields: [...]),
    32→///     EntityIR(name: "users", fields: [...])
    33→///   ],
    34→///   links: [
    35→///     LinkIR(name: "userTodos", ...)
    36→///   ]
    37→/// )
    38→/// ```
    39→public struct SchemaIR: Codable, Sendable, Equatable {
    40→  /// All entities defined in the schema
    41→  public var entities: [EntityIR]
    42→  
    43→  /// All links (relationships) between entities
    44→  public var links: [LinkIR]
    45→  
    46→  /// All rooms for presence and topics
    47→  public var rooms: [RoomIR]
    48→  
    49→  /// Type aliases defined in the schema file
    50→  public var typeAliases: [TypeAliasIR]
    51→  
    52→  /// Import declarations from the schema file
    53→  public var imports: [ImportDeclaration]
    54→  
    55→  /// Schema-level documentation comment
    56→  public var documentation: String?
    57→  
    58→  /// Source file this schema was parsed from (for error messages)
    59→  public var sourceFile: String?
    60→  
    61→  public init(
    62→    entities: [EntityIR] = [],
    63→    links: [LinkIR] = [],
    64→    rooms: [RoomIR] = [],
    65→    typeAliases: [TypeAliasIR] = [],
    66→    imports: [ImportDeclaration] = [],
    67→    documentation: String? = nil,
    68→    sourceFile: String? = nil
    69→  ) {
    70→    self.entities = entities
    71→    self.links = links
    72→    self.rooms = rooms
    73→    self.typeAliases = typeAliases
    74→    self.imports = imports
    75→    self.documentation = documentation
    76→    self.sourceFile = sourceFile
    77→  }
    78→  
    79→  /// Find an entity by name
    80→  public func entity(named name: String) -> EntityIR? {
    81→    entities.first { $0.name == name }
    82→  }
    83→  
    84→  /// Find all links where this entity is the "from" side
    85→  public func linksFrom(entity name: String) -> [LinkIR] {
    86→    links.filter { $0.forward.entityName == name }
    87→  }
    88→  
    89→  /// Find all links where this entity is the "to" side
    90→  public func linksTo(entity name: String) -> [LinkIR] {
    91→    links.filter { $0.reverse.entityName == name }
    92→  }
    93→  
    94→  /// Find a room by name
    95→  public func room(named name: String) -> RoomIR? {
    96→    rooms.first { $0.name == name }
    97→  }
    98→}

   100→// MARK: - Entity IR
   101→
   102→/// An entity (table/collection) in the schema.
   103→///
   104→/// ## Example
   105→///
   106→/// For this TypeScript:
   107→/// ```typescript
   108→/// todos: i.entity({
   109→///   title: i.string(),
   110→///   done: i.boolean(),
   111→/// })
   112→/// ```
   113→///
   114→/// The IR is:
   115→/// ```swift
   116→/// EntityIR(
   117→///   name: "todos",
   118→///   fields: [
   119→///     FieldIR(name: "title", type: .string, isOptional: false),
   120→///     FieldIR(name: "done", type: .boolean, isOptional: false)
   121→///   ]
   122→/// )
   123→/// ```
   124→public struct EntityIR: Codable, Sendable, Equatable, Identifiable {
   125→  public var id: String { name }
   126→  
   127→  /// The entity name (namespace), e.g., "todos", "users"
   128→  /// This is the key in the `entities` object in TypeScript
   129→  public var name: String
   130→  
   131→  /// The fields (attributes) of this entity
   132→  /// Does NOT include `id` - that's implicit for all entities
   133→  public var fields: [FieldIR]
   134→  
   135→  /// Documentation comment for this entity
   136→  public var documentation: String?
   137→  
   138→  public init(
   139→    name: String,
   140→    fields: [FieldIR] = [],
   141→    documentation: String? = nil
   142→  ) {
   143→    self.name = name
   144→    self.fields = fields
   145→    self.documentation = documentation
   146→  }
   147→  
   148→  /// The Swift struct name (PascalCase singular)
   149→  /// "todos" → "Todo", "users" → "User", "people" → "Person"
   150→  ///
   151→  /// ## System Entities
   152→  ///
   153→  /// InstantDB has system entities prefixed with `$` (e.g., `$files`, `$users`).
   154→  /// These are converted to Swift-safe names:
   155→  /// - `$files` → `InstantFile`
   156→  /// - `$users` → `InstantUser`
   157→  ///
   158→  /// The `$` prefix is reserved in Swift for compiler-synthesized declarations
   159→  /// (like property wrapper projections), so we use the `Instant` prefix instead.
   160→  public var swiftTypeName: String {
   161→    // Handle InstantDB system entities (prefixed with $)
   162→    // The $ prefix is reserved in Swift for compiler-synthesized declarations
   163→    // like $foo for @State property wrappers, so we convert to Instant prefix
   164→    if name.hasPrefix("$") {
   165→      let baseName = String(name.dropFirst()) // Remove $
   166→      // Convert "$files" → "InstantFile", "$users" → "InstantUser"
   167→      let singular = singularize(baseName)
   168→      return "Instant" + singular.prefix(1).uppercased() + singular.dropFirst()
   169→    }
   170→    
   171→    // Handle irregular plurals
   172→    let irregularPlurals: [String: String] = [
   173→      "people": "Person",
   174→      "children": "Child",
   175→      "men": "Man",
   176→      "women": "Woman",
   177→      "mice": "Mouse",
   178→      "geese": "Goose",
   179→      "teeth": "Tooth",
   180→      "feet": "Foot",
   181→      "data": "Data",
   182→      "media": "Media",
   183→      "criteria": "Criterion",
   184→      "phenomena": "Phenomenon",
   185→    ]
   186→    
   187→    if let irregular = irregularPlurals[name.lowercased()] {
   188→      return irregular
   189→    }
   190→    
   191→    // Handle regular plurals
   192→    let singular = singularize(name)
   193→    
   194→    return singular.prefix(1).uppercased() + singular.dropFirst()
   195→  }
   196→  
   197→  /// Whether this entity is a system entity (prefixed with $)
   198→  ///
   199→  /// System entities like `$files` and `$users` are managed by InstantDB
   200→  /// and have special behavior. They are rarely used directly in app code.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about how the SwiftData `@Model` macro works internally:

## Overview of the @Model Macro

The `@Model` macro converts a Swift class into a stored model that's managed by SwiftData.(no content)It's part of Swift's new macro system, introduced to help developers write more efficient and cleaner code.

## How It Works Internally

### Property Transformation
The macro automatically converts stored properties into getters and setters that read/write the underlying SwiftData information.(no content)By examining the complete expanded code, properties like `timestamp` are transformed into computed properties with constructors by the macro code.

### Protocol Conformances
It automatically makes your class load and store from SwiftData, adds support for observing changes, and also adds conformances for Hashable, Identifiable, Observable, and PersistentModel.

### Backing Data
Since `backingData` (`_DefaultBackingData`) does not have a public constructor, we cannot construct that data through a managed object instance. Another constructor in PersistentModel is provided for SwiftData internally to convert a managed object into a PersistentModel.

### Core Data Foundation
Although Apple rarely emphasizes the relationship between SwiftData and Core Data, it is undeniable that the SwiftData framework is built on top of Core Data. The database file format is compatible, allowing existing data to be directly operated with the new framework.

### Schema Generation
SwiftData schemas are standard Swift code, but you can annotate properties with additional metadata when necessary. This simple act of class decoration with @Model triggers schema generation, transforming your classes' stored properties into persisted ones.

### Automatic CRUD and Observation
@Model automatically adds code to load and store instances of your model from SwiftData. You don't need to write manual CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) operations.

### Macro Expansion
If we ignore the @Model macro flag, the code is exactly the same as defining a standard Swift class. However, with SwiftData and the @Model macro, we can extend it to become a data model with a complete description. In Xcode, when expanding macros, we will be able to see the complete code after macro expansion (@_PersistedProperty can be expanded twice).

## 2024 Updates

In 2024, there is a new schema macro that allows you to construct a compound constraint on persistent models. You can use the new #Unique macro to tell SwiftData which combinations of your model's properties must always remain unique in the model data. When two model instances share the same unique values, SwiftData will perform an upsert on collision with an existing model.(no content)Custom data stores let you use familiar SwiftData APIs, like the @Model and @Query macros, no matter what format the data needs to be persisted with.

Based on the search results, here's a comprehensive guide on Swift attached macros, including member macros and peer macros:

## Swift Attached Macros Overview

Attached macros are so-called because they are attached to a particular declaration. They are written using the custom attribute syntax (e.g., `@AddCompletionHandler`) that already provides extensibility for declarations through property wrappers, result builders, and global actors.(no content)There are two roles that create freestanding macros: Expression and declaration. And there are five roles that create attached macros: Peer, accessor, member attribute, member, and conformance.

## Attached Macro Roles

### Peer Macros

Peer macros expand new declarations on the same scope as the declaration it was attached to.(no content)A peer macro can be attached to any declaration, not only variables, and functions, and types, but even things like import and operator declarations, and can insert new declarations alongside it. So if you use it on a method or property, you'll end up creating members of the type, but if you use it on a top-level function or type, you'll end up creating new top-level declarations.(no content)@attached(peer) (Peer Macros): These add new declarations alongside the declaration they are attached to. They are "peers" in the same scope. Example: A macro that automatically generates an equatable conformance or a hashable conformance for a struct or class.

**Example Implementation:**
To implement a peer macro, you declare the signature like: `@attached(peer, names: overloaded) public macro AddAsync() = #externalMacro(module: "AddAsyncMacros", type: "AddAsyncMacro")`(no content)The struct must conform to `PeerMacro` and implement the expansion function. In this case, the Macro can only be attached to a function, so that we will cast it to `FunctionDeclSyntax`.

### Member Macros

Member declaration macros allow one to introduce new member declarations within the type or extension to which they apply.(no content)Member macros simply add new declarations inside the type they are applied to.(no content)A Member Macro named CustomCodable generates CodingKeys enum cases for properties within Codable conformant types. The macro is adorned with the "member" attribute, indicating its role in producing new declarations within the same scope. The definition looks like: `@attached(member, names: named(CodingKeys)) public macro CustomCodable() = #externalMacro(module: "MacroExamplesImplementation", type: "CustomCodable")`

### Member Attribute Macros

A member attribute macro cannot create new members to an existing declaration. It can, however, change the attributes of members, by e.g. marking them @objc or @nonobjc or adding property wrappers.(no content)Member attribute macros allow one to modify the member declarations that were explicitly written within the type or extension by adding new attributes to them. Those new attributes could then refer to other macros, such as peer or accessor macros, or builtin attributes.

## Implementation Structure

When the compiler sees a macro being used, it starts a plug-in in a separate process and asks it to expand the macro. "#externalMacro" is what defines that relationship. It specifies the plug-in the compiler should launch and the name of a type inside that plug-in. So when Swift expands this macro, it will launch a plug-in called "MyLibMacros" and ask a type called "StringifyMacro" to expand it.(no content)Macros must be created in a special Package that depends on the swift-syntax library. To create a new Macro, go to New -> Package and select Swift Macro. Inside the newly created Package, you will find auto-generated files for macro signature declaration, testing, and implementation.

## Declaring Macro Names

Peer macros, member macros, and declaration macros basically exist entirely to introduce new names that non-macro code can access. But when they do, they need to declare the names they're adding, so the compiler knows about them. And they do that inside their role attribute.(no content)Whenever a macro produces declarations that are visible to other Swift code, it is required to declare the names in advance. All of the names need to be specified within the attribute declaring the macro role, using forms like `named(<declaration-name>)` for specific fixed names.

## Combining Multiple Roles

Each role has a specific purpose, such as adding members, creating accessors, or adding peers alongside the declaration. A given attached macro can inhabit several different roles, and as such will be expanded multiple times corresponding to the different roles, which allows the various roles to be composed.(no content)One macro can be with multiple types as long as we implement the corresponding protocol. The Attached macro is an enabler for many new features in Swift. For example, the Swift Data and Observable features are built on top of this.

Based on my search, here's what I found about Swift macro expansion, code generation, and type-safe query builders:

## Swift Macros Overview

Macros in Swift are compile-time code transformations. They act like annotations that inject or manipulate code before compilation. This provides powerful ways to reduce boilerplate and enforce conventions across large codebases. Unlike C macros, Swift macros are type-safe, scoped, and operate with the Swift compiler's knowledge, ensuring they're reliable and integrated with tooling like autocompletion and refactoring.

## Code Generation Examples

### Expression Macro (URL Example)
What's harder is the actual macro itself, which needs to read the "https://swift.org" string that was passed in and convert it into a URL. The macro implementation uses SwiftSyntax to parse arguments and validate them at compile time.

### Freestanding Declaration Macro
You can use SwiftSyntax's string literal conversions to generate multiple declarations. For example, generating an EnvironmentKey enum along with a property accessor by returning an array of `DeclSyntax` elements.

### Member Macro Example
A member attribute macro, when applied to a type such as a class, lets us apply an attribute to every member in a class. This is identical in concept to the older @objcMembers attribute. For example, if you have an observable object that uses @Published on every one of its properties, you could write a simple @AllPublished macro.

## Type-Safe Query Builder with Macros

StructuredQueries is a Swift package that provides a very type-safe API for building SQL in Swift. It leverages a ton of advanced Swift features—including macros, parameter packs, dynamic member lookup with metatype key paths, result builders, and more—to achieve things not seen in other languages and libraries. For example, applying the library's @Table macro to Swift data types enables type-safe query building.

## Tools for Building Macros

SwiftSyntax gives you several different tools to create expansions. Syntax nodes are immutable, but they have lots of APIs that either create new nodes or return modified versions of existing nodes. The SwiftSyntaxBuilder library adds SwiftUI-style syntax builders where some of the child nodes are specified by a trailing closure.

## Testing Macros

The `assertMacro` function provides an alternative to Apple's `assertMacroExpansion` that automatically snapshots macro expansions. It also provides string-based matching for diagnostics and fix-its instead of manually specifying line and column numbers.

## Additional Resources

- Apple provides an official step-by-step guide to using macros for compile-time code generation in Swift, along with real-world examples like @AddCompletionHandler and @AddAsync.

- SwiftRequest is a lightweight, type-safe HTTP client for Swift that streamlines HTTP request construction using macros. Papyrus is also a type-safe, protocol-based HTTP client that turns APIs into Swift protocols.

   184→(defn oauth-start [{{:keys [state code_challenge code_challenge_method]} :params :as req}]

   194→                                                            :client-name client-name})
   195→

   203→                                    :let [value (get-in req [:params param])]
   204→                                    :when value]
   205→                                [param value]))

   207→                            {:app-id (:app_id client)})
   208→        matched-origin (app-authorized-redirect-origin-model/find-match
   209→                        authorized-origins
   210→                        redirect-uri)
   211→        _ (when-not matched-origin
   212→            (ex/throw-validation-err!

   214→             redirect-uri
   215→             [{:message "Invalid redirect_uri. If you're the developer, make sure to add your website to the list of approved domains from the Dashboard."}]))

   232→                      extra-params)]

     5→extension SharedReaderKey where Self == FactKey {
     6→  static func fact(_ number: Int?) -> Self {
     7→    Self(number: number)

    10→
    11→// NB: This 'SharedReaderKey` conformance is designed to allow one to hold onto a 'fact: String?'
    12→//     in their features, while secretly it is powered by a network request to fetch the fact.
    13→//     Conformances to 'SharedReaderKey' must be Sendable, and so this is why the 'loadTask'
    14→//     variable is held in a mutex.
    15→final class FactKey: SharedReaderKey {
    16→  let id = UUID()
    17→  let number: Int?
    18→  let loadTask = Mutex<Task<Void, Never>?>(nil)
    19→
    20→  init(number: Int?) {
    21→    self.number = number
    22→  }
    23→
    24→  func load(context _: LoadContext<String?>, continuation: LoadContinuation<String?>) {
    25→    guard let number else {
    26→      continuation.resume(returning: nil)
    27→      return
    28→    }
    29→    loadTask.withLock { task in
    30→      task?.cancel()
    31→      task = Task {
    32→        do {
    33→          // NB: This dependence on 'URLSession.shared' should be hidden behind a dependency
    34→          //     so that features that use this shared state are still testable.
    35→          let (data, _) = try await URLSession.shared.data(
    36→            from: URL(string: "http://numbersapi.com/\(number)")!
    37→          )
    38→          // NB: The Numbers API can be quite fast. Let's simulate a slower connection.
    39→          try await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(1))
    40→          // NB: Simulate errors from the API for negative numbers.
    41→          guard number >= 0 else {
    42→            struct BoringNumber: LocalizedError {
    43→              let number: Int
    44→              var errorDescription: String? { "\(number) is a boring number." }
    45→            }
    46→            throw BoringNumber(number: number)
    47→          }
    48→          continuation.resume(returning: String(decoding: data, as: UTF8.self))
    49→        } catch {
    50→          continuation.resume(throwing: error)
    51→        }
    52→      }
    53→    }
    54→  }
    55→
    56→  func subscribe(
    57→    context _: LoadContext<String?>, subscriber _: SharedSubscriber<String?>
    58→  ) -> SharedSubscription {
    59→    SharedSubscription {}
    60→  }
    61→}

     1→import Foundation
     2→import JavaScriptKit
     3→import Sharing
     4→
     5→extension SharedKey {
     6→  static func localStorage<Value>(_ key: String) -> Self where Self == LocalStorageKey<Value> {
     7→    LocalStorageKey(key: key)
     8→  }
     9→}
    10→
    11→struct LocalStorageKey<Value: Codable & Sendable>: SharedKey {
    12→  let key: String
    13→
    14→  var id: some Hashable { key }
    15→
    16→  func load(context _: LoadContext<Value>, continuation: LoadContinuation<Value>) {
    17→    continuation.resume(with: Result { try getAndDecodeItem() })
    18→  }
    19→
    20→  func subscribe(
    21→    context _: LoadContext<Value>, subscriber: SharedSubscriber<Value>
    22→  ) -> SharedSubscription {
    23→    nonisolated(unsafe) let listener = JSClosure { _ in
    24→      subscriber.yield(with: Result { try getAndDecodeItem() })
    25→      return .undefined
    26→    }
    27→    _ = JSObject.global.window.addEventListener("storage", listener)
    28→    return SharedSubscription {
    29→      _ = JSObject.global.window.removeEventListener("storage", listener)
    30→    }
    31→  }
    32→
    33→  func save(_ value: Value, context _: SaveContext, continuation: SaveContinuation) {
    34→    continuation.resume(
    35→      with: Result {
    36→        _ = try JSObject.global.window.localStorage.setItem(
    37→          key,
    38→          String(decoding: JSONEncoder().encode(value), as: UTF8.self)
    39→        )
    40→      }
    41→    )
    42→  }
    43→
    44→  private func getAndDecodeItem() throws -> Value? {
    45→    guard let string = JSObject.global.window.localStorage.getItem(key).string
    46→    else { return nil }
    47→    return try JSONDecoder().decode(Value.self, from: Data(string.utf8))
    48→  }
    49→}
    50→

    19→/// A type-safe key for syncing an entity collection with InstantDB.
    20→///
    21→/// `EntityKey` enables zero-configuration sync with type safety:
    22→///
    23→/// ```swift
    24→/// // Define your schema (usually generated from instant.schema.ts)
    25→/// enum Schema {
    26→///   static let todos = EntityKey<Todo>(namespace: "todos")
    27→///   static let users = EntityKey<User>(namespace: "users")
    28→/// }
    29→///
    30→/// // Use in SwiftUI views
    31→/// @Shared(Schema.todos)
    32→/// private var todos: IdentifiedArrayOf<Todo> = []
    33→///
    34→/// // With ordering
    35→/// @Shared(Schema.todos.orderBy(\.createdAt, .desc))
    36→/// private var todos: IdentifiedArrayOf<Todo> = []
    37→/// ```
    38→///
    39→/// ## Query Modifiers
    40→///
    41→/// Chain modifiers to customize the query:
    42→///
    43→/// ```swift
    44→/// Schema.todos
    45→///   .orderBy(\.createdAt, .desc)  // Type-safe ordering
    46→///   .limit(10)                     // Limit results

    48→///

    50→///
    51→/// Typically, `EntityKey` instances are generated from your `instant.schema.ts`

    53→/// Internal node for recursive query structure (using indirect enum to allow nesting)
    54→public indirect enum EntityQueryNode: Hashable, Sendable {
    55→  case link(
    56→    name: String,
    57→    limit: Int? = nil,
    58→    orderBy: String? = nil,
    59→    orderDirection: EntityKeyOrderDirection? = nil,
    60→    whereClauses: [String: EntityKeyPredicate] = [:],
    61→    children: [EntityQueryNode] = []
    62→  )
    63→}

    97→  public init(

   183→  transact = (
   184→    chunks: TransactionChunk<any, any> | TransactionChunk<any, any>[],
   185→  ) => {
   186→    return this.core.transact(chunks);
   187→  };
   188→
   189→  /**
   190→   * Use this to query your data!
   191→   *
   192→   * @see https://instantdb.com/docs/instaql
   193→   *

   195→   *   // listen to all goals
   196→   *   const { isLoading, error, data } = db.useQuery({ goals: {} });
   197→   *
   198→   *   // goals where the title is "Get Fit"

   200→   *     goals: { $: { where: { title: 'Get Fit' } } },
   201→   *   });
   202→   *
   203→   *   // all goals, _alongside_ their todos
   204→   *   const { isLoading, error, data } = db.useQuery({

   208→   *   // skip if `user` is not logged in

   213→  useQuery = <Q extends ValidQuery<Q, Schema>>(
   214→    query: null | Q,
   215→    opts?: InstaQLOptions,
   216→  ): InstaQLLifecycleState<Schema, Q, UseDates> => {
   217→    return useQueryInternal<Q, Schema, UseDates>(this.core, query, opts).state;

   220→  /**

   226→   * @see https://instantdb.com/docs/auth
   227→   * @example
   228→   *  function App() {
   229→   *    const { isLoading, user, error } = db.useAuth()
   230→   *    if (isLoading) {
   231→   *      return <div>Loading...</div>

   262→    }, []);

   265→      subscribe,

   267→      () => defaultAuthState,
   268→    );

   270→  };

   272→  /**

   275→   * You will want to protect any calls of this hook with a
   276→   * <db.SignedIn> component, or your own logic based on db.useAuth()

   280→   * @example
   281→   *  function UserDisplay() {
   282→   *    const user = db.useUser()
   283→   *    return <div>Logged in as: {user.email}</div>
   284→   *  }
   285→   *
   286→   *  <db.SignedIn>
   287→   *    <UserDisplay />
   288→   *  </db.SignedIn>
   289→   *
   290→   */
   291→  useUser = (): User => {
   292→    const { user } = this.useAuth();
   293→    if (!user) {
   294→      throw new InstantError(
   295→        'useUser must be used within an auth-protected route',
   296→      );
   297→    }
   298→    return user;
   299→  };

   301→  /**

   303→   * for scenarios where you want to know the current auth
   304→   * state without subscribing to changes.
   305→   *
   306→   * @see https://instantdb.com/docs/auth
   307→   * @example
   308→   *   const user = await db.getAuth();
   309→   *   console.log('logged in as', user.email)
   310→   */
   311→  getAuth(): Promise<User | null> {
   312→    return this.core.getAuth();
   313→  }
   314→
   315→  /**
   316→   * Listen for connection status changes to Instant. Use this for things like
   317→   * showing connection state to users
   318→   *
   319→   * @see https://www.instantdb.com/docs/patterns#connection-status
   320→   * @example
   321→   *  function App() {
   322→   *    const status = db.useConnectionStatus()
   323→   *    const connectionState =
   324→   *      status === 'connecting' || status === 'opened'
   325→   *        ? 'authenticating'
   326→   *      : status === 'authenticated'
   327→   *        ? 'connected'
   328→   *      : status === 'closed'
   329→   *        ? 'closed'
   330→   *      : status === 'errored'
   331→   *        ? 'errored'
   332→   *      : 'unexpected state';
   333→   *
   334→   *    return <div>Connection state: {connectionState}</div>
   335→   *  }
   336→   */
   337→  useConnectionStatus = (): ConnectionStatus => {
   338→    const statusRef = useRef<ConnectionStatus>(
   339→      this.core._reactor.status as ConnectionStatus,
   340→    );
   341→
   342→    const subscribe = useCallback((cb: Function) => {
   343→      const unsubscribe = this.core.subscribeConnectionStatus((newStatus) => {
   344→        if (newStatus !== statusRef.current) {
   345→          statusRef.current = newStatus;
   346→          cb();
   347→        }
   348→      });
   349→
   350→      return unsubscribe;
   351→    }, []);

   353→    const status = useSyncExternalStore<ConnectionStatus>(
   354→      subscribe,
   355→      () => statusRef.current,

   357→      () => 'connecting',
   358→    );

   360→    return status;
   361→  };
   362→
   363→  /**
   364→   * Use this for one-off queries.
   365→   * Returns local data if available, otherwise fetches from the server.
   366→   * Because we want to avoid stale data, this method will throw an error
   367→   * if the user is offline or there is no active connection to the server.
   368→   *

   370→   *
   371→   * @example
   372→   *
   373→   *  const resp = await db.queryOnce({ goals: {} });
   374→   *  console.log(resp.data.goals)
   375→   */
   376→  queryOnce = <Q extends ValidQuery<Q, Schema>>(
   377→    query: Q,
   378→    opts?: InstaQLOptions,
   379→  ): Promise<{
   380→    data: InstaQLResponse<Schema, Q, UseDates>;
   381→    pageInfo: PageInfoResponse<Q>;
   382→  }> => {
   383→    return this.core.queryOnce(query, opts);

   386→  /**

   389→   *
   390→   * @example

   395→   */
   396→  SignedIn: React.FC<{

   402→    return <>{children}</>;

   413→   *
   414→   */
   415→  SignedOut: React.FC<{

   417→  }> = ({ children }) => {

     5→  final class PassthroughRelay<Output>: Subject {
     6→    typealias Failure = Never
     7→
     8→    private let lock: os_unfair_lock_t
     9→    private var _upstreams: [any Combine.Subscription] = []
    10→    private var _downstreams = ContiguousArray<Subscription>()
    11→
    12→    init() {
    13→      self.lock = os_unfair_lock_t.allocate(capacity: 1)
    14→      self.lock.initialize(to: os_unfair_lock())
    15→    }
    16→
    17→    deinit {
    18→      for subscription in _upstreams {
    19→        subscription.cancel()
    20→      }
    21→      lock.deinitialize(count: 1)
    22→      lock.deallocate()
    23→    }
    24→
    25→    func receive(subscriber: some Subscriber<Output, Never>) {
    26→      let subscription = Subscription(upstream: self, downstream: subscriber)
    27→      lock.withLock { _downstreams.append(subscription) }
    28→      subscriber.receive(subscription: subscription)
    29→    }
    30→
    31→    func send(_ value: Output) {

    33→        subscription.receive(value)
    34→      }
    35→    }
    36→
    37→    func send(completion: Subscribers.Completion<Never>) {
    38→      let subscriptions = lock.withLock {
    39→        let subscriptions = _downstreams
    40→        _downstreams.removeAll()
    41→        return subscriptions
    42→      }
    43→      for subscription in subscriptions {
    44→        subscription.receive(completion: completion)
    45→      }
    46→    }
    47→
    48→    func send(subscription: any Combine.Subscription) {

    50→      subscription.request(.unlimited)
    51→    }
    52→
    53→    private func remove(_ subscription: Subscription) {
    54→      lock.withLock {
    55→        guard let index = _downstreams.firstIndex(of: subscription)
    56→        else { return }
    57→        _downstreams.remove(at: index)

    59→    }

    61→    fileprivate final class Subscription: Combine.Subscription, Equatable {
    62→      private var demand = Subscribers.Demand.none
    63→      private var downstream: (any Subscriber<Output, Never>)?
    64→      private let lock: os_unfair_lock_t
    65→      private var upstream: PassthroughRelay?
    66→
    67→      init(upstream: PassthroughRelay, downstream: any Subscriber<Output, Never>) {
    68→        self.upstream = upstream
    69→        self.downstream = downstream
    70→        self.lock = os_unfair_lock_t.allocate(capacity: 1)
    71→        self.lock.initialize(to: os_unfair_lock())
    72→      }
    73→
    74→      deinit {

    89→
    90→        guard let downstream else {
    91→          lock.unlock()
    92→          return
    93→        }
    94→
    95→        switch demand {
    96→        case .unlimited:
    97→          lock.unlock()
    98→          // NB: Adding to unlimited demand has no effect and can be ignored.
    99→          _ = downstream.receive(value)
   100→
   101→        case .none:
   102→          lock.unlock()
   103→
   104→        default:
   105→          demand -= 1
   106→          lock.unlock()
   107→          let moreDemand = downstream.receive(value)
   108→          lock.withLock { demand += moreDemand }
   109→        }
   110→      }
   111→
   112→      func receive(completion: Subscribers.Completion<Never>) {

   115→          downstream = nil
   116→          upstream = nil

   121→        precondition(demand > 0, "Demand must be greater than zero")
   122→        lock.lock()
   123→        defer { lock.unlock() }
   124→        guard case .some = downstream else { return }
   125→        self.demand += demand
   126→        guard let upstream else { return }
   127→        let subscriptions = upstream.lock.withLock { upstream._upstreams }
   128→        for subscription in subscriptions {

   130→        }
   131→      }

     4→  /// A synchronization primitive that protects shared mutable state via mutual exclusion.
     5→  ///
     6→  /// A back-port of Swift's `Mutex` type for wider platform availability.
     7→  #if hasFeature(StaticExclusiveOnly)
     8→    @_staticExclusiveOnly
     9→  #endif
    10→  package struct Mutex<Value: ~Copyable>: ~Copyable {
    11→    private let _lock = NSLock()
    12→    private let _box: Box
    13→
    14→    /// Initializes a value of this mutex with the given initial state.
    15→    ///
    16→    /// - Parameter initialValue: The initial value to give to the mutex.
    17→    package init(_ initialValue: consuming sending Value) {
    18→      _box = Box(initialValue)
    19→    }
    20→
    21→    private final class Box {
    22→      var value: Value
    23→      init(_ initialValue: consuming sending Value) {
    24→        value = initialValue
    25→      }
    26→    }
    27→  }
    28→
    29→  extension Mutex: @unchecked Sendable where Value: ~Copyable {}
    30→
    31→  extension Mutex where Value: ~Copyable {
    32→    /// Calls the given closure after acquiring the lock and then releases ownership.
    33→    borrowing package func withLock<Result: ~Copyable, E: Error>(
    34→      _ body: (inout sending Value) throws(E) -> sending Result
    35→    ) throws(E) -> sending Result {
    36→      _lock.lock()
    37→      defer { _lock.unlock() }
    38→      return try body(&_box.value)
    39→    }
    40→
    41→    /// Attempts to acquire the lock and then calls the given closure if successful.
    42→    borrowing package func withLockIfAvailable<Result: ~Copyable, E: Error>(
    43→      _ body: (inout sending Value) throws(E) -> sending Result
    44→    ) throws(E) -> sending Result? {
    45→      guard _lock.try() else { return nil }
    46→      defer { _lock.unlock() }
    47→      return try body(&_box.value)
    48→    }
    49→  }
    50→#else
    51→  package struct Mutex<Value> {
    52→    private let _lock = NSLock()
    53→    private let _box: Box
    54→
    55→    package init(_ initialValue: consuming Value) {
    56→      _box = Box(initialValue)
    57→    }

    63→      }
    64→    }
    65→  }

   119→   119→(defn supports-batch-messages? [features]
   120→   120→  (contains? features :batch-messages))
   121→   121→
   122→   122→(defn auth-and-creator-attrs [auth creator versions]
   123→   123→  (cond-> {:app-id (-> auth :app :id)
   124→   124→           :app-title (-> auth :app :title)
   125→   125→           :app-user-email (-> auth :user :email)
   126→   126→           :creator-id (-> creator :id)
   127→   127→           :creator-email (-> creator :email)}
   128→   128→    (get versions react-version-key)
   129→   129→    (assoc "@instantdb/react" (get versions react-version-key))
   130→   130→
   131→   131→    (get versions react-native-version-key)
   132→   132→    (assoc "@instantdb/react-native" (get versions react-native-version-key))
   133→   133→
   134→   134→    (get versions core-version-key)
   135→   135→    (assoc "@instantdb/core" (get versions core-version-key))))
   136→   136→
