## TypeScript SDK Reference (Source of Truth)

Always refer to the TypeScript SDK for behavior decisions. Key files:

### Reactor.js

**File:** `/Users/mlustig/Development/personal/instantdb/instant/client/packages/core/src/Reactor.js`

The Reactor (Lines 205-2466) is the central orchestrator:

\```javascript
export default class Reactor {
    attrs;                        // Schema attributes from server
    _isOnline = true;            // Network status
    status = STATUS.CONNECTING;  // connecting|opened|authenticated|closed|errored

    querySubs;     // PersistedObject<string, QuerySub> - Query subscriptions
    kv;            // PersistedObject - pendingMutations, currentUser
    queryCbs = {}; // Record<hash, Array<{q, cb}>> - Active callbacks

    mutationDeferredStore = new Map();  // Tracks pending mutation promises
}
\```

### Optimistic Updates

**File:** `Reactor.js` (Lines 1263-1272):

\```javascript
_applyOptimisticUpdates(store, attrsStore, mutations, processedTxId) {
    for (const [_, mut] of mutations) {
        // Only apply mutations not yet confirmed by server
        if (!mut['tx-id'] || (processedTxId && mut['tx-id'] > processedTxId)) {
            const result = s.transact(store, attrsStore, mut['tx-steps']);
            store = result.store;
            attrsStore = result.attrsStore;
        }
    }
    return { store, attrsStore };
}
\```

### Store Structure

**File:** `/Users/mlustig/Development/personal/instantdb/instant/client/packages/core/src/store.ts` (Lines 17-23):

\```typescript
type Store = {
    eav: Map<string, Map<string, Map<any, Triple>>>;  // Entity-Attribute-Value
    aev: Map<string, Map<string, Map<any, Triple>>>;  // Attribute-Entity-Value
    vae: Map<any, Map<string, Map<string, Triple>>>;  // Value-Attribute-Entity (refs)
};

type Triple = [entityId, attrId, value, timestamp];
\```

### Transaction Steps (tx-steps)

Format for mutations sent to server:

\```javascript
['add-triple', eid, attrId, value, { mode: 'upsert' }]  // Add/update data
['retract-triple', eid, attrId, value]                   // Remove data
['delete-entity', eid, etype]                            // Delete entity
['deep-merge-triple', eid, attrId, { nested: 'obj' }]   // Deep merge JSON
['add-attr', { id, forward-identity, value-type }]       // Create attribute
\```

## WebSocket Protocol

### Client → Server Messages

| Operation | Purpose |
|-----------|---------|
| `init` | Initialize session with app-id, refresh-token |
| `add-query` | Subscribe to InstaQL query |
| `remove-query` | Unsubscribe from query |
| `transact` | Execute mutation (tx-steps) |
| `join-room` | Join ephemeral room for presence |
| `set-presence` | Set presence data in room |
| `client-broadcast` | Broadcast to room peers |

### Server → Client Messages

| Operation | Purpose |
|-----------|---------|
| `init-ok` | Session initialized, includes attrs |
| `add-query-ok` | Query results (triples + page-info) |
| `refresh-ok` | Updated query results after invalidation |
| `transact-ok` | Mutation confirmed with tx-id |
| `error` | Error with type, message, hint |
| `patch-presence` | Incremental presence update |
| `server-broadcast` | Broadcast from peer |

### Example Messages

**Add Query:**
\```json
{
    "op": "add-query",
    "q": { "todos": { "$": { "where": { "done": false } } } },
    "client-event-id": "uuid"
}
\```

**Transact:**
\```json
{
    "op": "transact",
    "tx-steps": [
        ["add-triple", "entity-uuid", "attr-uuid", "value", { "mode": "upsert" }]
    ],
    "client-event-id": "uuid"
}
\```

**Error Response:**
\```json
{
    "op": "error",
    "status": 400,
    "type": "validation-failed",
    "message": "Invalid entity reference",
    "hint": { "entity-id": "invalid-uuid" }
}
\```

## Swift Concurrency Patterns

### Design Principle: Synchronous Call Sites

The user-facing API is synchronous. Async work happens internally via `Task {}`:

\```swift
// User code - NO async/await needed
$todos.createTodo(title: "Buy milk")

// Internal implementation
func createTodo(title: String, callbacks: MutationCallbacks<Todo>) {
    // 1. Optimistic update (synchronous)
    applyOptimisticUpdate(...)

    // 2. Fire-and-forget async sync
    Task {
        do {
            try await reactor.transact(...)
            await MainActor.run { callbacks.onSuccess?(result) }
        } catch {
            rollbackOptimisticUpdate(...)
            await MainActor.run { callbacks.onError?(error) }
        }
    }
}
\```

### TanStack Query-Style Callbacks

**File:** `Sources/SharingInstant/SharedMutations.swift`

\```swift
public struct MutationCallbacks<T: Sendable>: Sendable {
    public var onMutate: (@Sendable () -> Void)?      // Before mutation
    public var onSuccess: (@Sendable (T) -> Void)?    // On success
    public var onError: (@Sendable (Error) -> Void)?  // On error
    public var onSettled: (@Sendable () -> Void)?     // Always called
}
\```

### Actor Isolation

The Reactor is an actor for thread-safe state:

\```swift
// Sources/SharingInstant/Internal/Reactor.swift (Line 153)
public actor Reactor {
    private let store: SharedTripleStore
    private var activeSubscriptions: [UUID: SubscriptionHandle] = [:]

    // All methods run on actor's serial executor (background)
    func transact(_ mutation: Mutation) async throws { ... }
}
\```

### MainActor for UI Updates

\```swift
// Bridge from actor to MainActor for UI callbacks
Task {
    let result = await reactor.transact(mutation)
    await MainActor.run {
        self.updateUIState(result)
    }
}
\```

## Current State & Known Issues

### What Works Well

1. **Type-safe queries with KeyPaths:**
   \```swift
   @Shared(.instantSync(Schema.todos.where(\.done, .eq(false)).orderBy(\.createdAt, .desc)))
   \```

2. **Link queries with `.with()`:**
   \```swift
   @Shared(.instantSync(Schema.posts.with(\.author)))
   \```

3. **Generated semantic mutations:**
   \```swift
   $todos.toggleDone(id)
   $todos.markDone(id)
   \```

4. **TanStack-style callbacks**

5. **Offline persistence of pending mutations**

### Known Issues

**ISSUE: save() does not track deletions**
- File: `ISSUE-save-does-not-track-deletions.md`
- `$todos.withLock { $0.remove(id:) }` does NOT sync to server
- Must use explicit `$todos.delete(id:)` instead
- This is intentional - matches TypeScript SDK

**StateTracker Removed:**
- Previously tried to detect changes via "50% heuristic"
- Too fragile, caused phantom deletions
- Now: all mutations must be explicit

### Rough Edges to Address

1. **Multi-app support** - Untested, deprecation warnings in code
2. **Flaky demos** - Some examples need reliability improvements
3. **Complex transcription schema** - Current SpeechRecorderApp schema is overly complex
4. **Async at call site** - Some APIs still require async/await

- IDE autocomplete for relationships
- Schema defined alongside model

## Case Study: Rapid Transcription

### Use Case

Real-time speech transcription with:
- **Volatile segments** - Rapidly updated with partial text
- **Finalized segments** - Complete with word-level timestamps

### Schema Design (from `instant.schema.ts`)

\```typescript
transcriptionSegments: i.entity({
    startTime: i.number().indexed(),
    endTime: i.number().indexed(),
    text: i.string(),
    segmentIndex: i.number().indexed(),
    isFinalized: i.boolean().indexed(),
    words: i.json<{ text: string; startTime: number; endTime: number }[]>().optional(),
}),
\```

### Pattern

1. Create segment with `isFinalized: false`
2. Rapidly update `text` as transcription streams
3. When finalized, update `isFinalized: true` and add `words`
4. Create new segment for next utterance

### Key Implementation

- Use `updateFields()` for field-level updates (prevents clobbering)
- Debounce rapid updates in UI layer
- Server handles ordering via tx-id

## Code Style

### Comments
- NEVER place comments to the right of code
- ALWAYS place comments on the line ABOVE
- Use `///` doc comments for public APIs

### MARK Sections
\```swift
// MARK: - Properties
// MARK: - Initialization
// MARK: - Public API
// MARK: - Private Helpers
\```

### Documentation
Always explain the "why", not just the "what":

\```swift
/// Returns active queries for re-registration after reconnection.
///
/// ## Why This Exists
/// When WebSocket reconnects, the server loses our subscriptions.
/// Without re-sending, UI would show stale data.
///
/// ## Discovery
/// Found during VPN testing - connection recovered but queries weren't re-sent.
func getActiveQueries() -> [(eventId: String, query: [String: Any])]
\```

## SharingInstant Swift SDK - Git History Analysis

### Timeline of Key Changes (December 2025 - January 2026)

---

### **RECURSIVE ENTITY RESOLUTION FIXES**

#### 1. `d393412` - December 22, 2025 - **Fix reverse-link hydration in TripleStore decoding**
**Critical Bug Fix**

**Problem:** When resolving entities like `Post.author`, the TripleStore resolver only walked forward refs. Reverse relationships (like `posts.author` which is stored as `profiles.posts` forward triple) were dropped during store re-emit, causing UI to flip from optimistic author to "Unknown Author" after refresh.

**Solution:** Added `TripleStore+Extensions.swift` with `resolve(id:attrsStore:depth:maxDepth:)` method that:
- Materializes reverse link properties using `AttrsStore.revIdents` + `TripleStore.getReverseRefs()`
- Keeps nested entities shallow (depth limit) to avoid infinite cycles
- Added test `TripleStoreReverseLinkResolutionTests.testDecodingReverseLinkAuthorFromProfilePosts`

**Files:** 
- `/Users/mlustig/Development/personal/instantdb/sharing-instant/Sources/SharingInstant/Extensions/TripleStore+Extensions.swift` (new file, 139 lines)

---

#### 2. `842efc3` - December 25, 2025 - **Add IndirectLink property wrapper for recursive has-one links**

**Problem:** Swift `struct`s cannot contain themselves (directly or indirectly) through `Optional` because it stores payload inline. Schemas with has-one cycles like `Segment.parent -> Segment` fail to compile.

**Solution:** 
- Created `@IndirectLink` property wrapper using `indirect enum` storage to break cycles
- Added Tarjan's SCC algorithm in `SwiftGenerator.swift` to detect has-one cycles
- Automatically applies `@IndirectLink` to has-one link properties in cycles during codegen

**Files:**
- `/Users/mlustig/Development/personal/instantdb/sharing-instant/Sources/SharingInstant/IndirectLink.swift` (new file, 95 lines)
- `/Users/mlustig/Development/personal/instantdb/sharing-instant/Sources/InstantSchemaCodegen/SwiftGenerator.swift` (+144 lines)

#### 9. `99b4c69` - January 9, 2026 - **Apply pending mutations at query time (TypeScript SDK pattern)**

**Critical fix for offline mode:**
**Problem:** Offline todos disappear when navigating away and back to a screen.

**Solution:** Now matches TypeScript SDK's `dataForQuery() -> _applyOptimisticUpdates()` pattern:
- `SubscriptionState.handleStoreUpdate()` fetches pending mutations from SQLite and merges on-the-fly before yielding results
- Fixed attribute ID resolution: UUIDs looked up via `attrsStore.getAttr()` then namespace/field extracted from `forwardIdentity`

**Key insight:** Pending mutations are source of truth for unconfirmed changes and must be applied at query evaluation time, not persisted to the store.

# Memory Leak Analysis Report: SharingInstant Swift SDK

## Executive Summary

After thorough analysis of the SharingInstant SDK codebase, I have identified several potential memory leak patterns and memory ballooning issues. The issues range from critical retain cycles to unbounded data growth in the TripleStore.

---

## 1. Retain Cycles in Closures

### Issue 1.1: Missing `[weak self]` in Reactor.subscribe() closures

**File:** `/Users/mlustig/Development/personal/instantdb/sharing-instant/Sources/SharingInstant/Internal/Reactor.swift`

**Lines 524-567:** The `subscribe` methods create `AsyncStream` with closures that capture `self` (the Reactor actor):

```swift
// Lines 524-542
public func subscribe<Value: EntityIdentifiable & Codable & Sendable>(
  appID: String,
  configuration: SharingInstantSync.CollectionConfiguration<Value>
) -> AsyncStream<[Value]> {
  AsyncStream { continuation in
    let task = Task {
      // Start subscription immediately so cached results can be delivered
      // even when offline (JS core semantics).
      await self.startSubscription(  // <-- Strong capture of `self`
        appID: appID,
        namespace: configuration.namespace,
        // ...
      )
    }
    // ...
  }
}
```

**Impact:** If the `AsyncStream` is retained by a subscription but the Reactor should be deallocated, the strong capture of `self` prevents deallocation.

**Severity:** Medium - The Reactor is typically a singleton via dependency injection, but this pattern is problematic.

---

### Issue 1.2: Closure in InstantDB subscribe callback without `[weak subscriptionState]` consistency

**File:** `/Users/mlustig/Development/personal/instantdb/sharing-instant/Sources/SharingInstant/Internal/Reactor.swift`

**Lines 972-1052:** The InstantDB subscription callback correctly uses `[weak subscriptionState]` on line 972, which is good:

```swift
// Line 972
return try? client.subscribe(q) { [weak subscriptionState] result in
```

However, the `sharedStore` is captured strongly on line 901 and used on line 1012:

```swift
// Line 901
let sharedStore = store  // Strong reference

// Line 1012 inside callback
sharedStore.updateAttributes(client.attributes)
```

**Impact:** The `store` reference (SharedTripleStore) is kept alive as long as the subscription callback exists.

**Severity:** Medium - This can prevent the TripleStore from being deallocated when subscriptions are active.

---

### Issue 1.3: Connection state `.sink` closure captures

**File:** `/Users/mlustig/Development/personal/instantdb/sharing-instant/Sources/SharingInstant/Internal/Reactor.swift`

**Lines 1077-1117:** The connection state sink properly uses `[weak subscriptionState]`:

```swift
// Line 1081
.sink { [weak subscriptionState] newState in
```

This is correctly implemented. However, the cancellable is stored in an unsafe mutable pointer:

```swift
// Lines 1068-1069
let connectionCancellableBox = UnsafeMutablePointer<AnyCancellable?>.allocate(capacity: 1)
connectionCancellableBox.initialize(to: nil)
```

**Impact:** If the Task is cancelled before reaching the cleanup code (lines 1147-1149), the pointer may leak.

**Severity:** Low-Medium - Memory leak in edge case scenarios.

---

## 2. Actor Reference Holding

### Issue 2.1: Singleton Reactor with SharedTripleStore

**File:** `/Users/mlustig/Development/personal/instantdb/sharing-instant/Sources/SharingInstant/InstantDependency.swift`

```swift
// Lines 4-6
private enum InstantReactorKey: DependencyKey {
  static let liveValue = Reactor(store: SharedTripleStore())
}
```

**Impact:** The Reactor is created as a singleton with its own SharedTripleStore. This means:
1. The TripleStore lives for the entire app lifetime
2. Data is never garbage collected unless explicitly deleted
3. All subscription data accumulates indefinitely

**Severity:** High - This is the primary cause of memory ballooning.

---

### Issue 2.2: activeSubscriptions Dictionary Never Shrinks

**File:** `/Users/mlustig/Development/personal/instantdb/sharing-instant/Sources/SharingInstant/Internal/Reactor.swift`

**Lines 159 and 1169-1171:**

```swift
// Line 159
private var activeSubscriptions: [UUID: SubscriptionHandle] = [:]

// Lines 1169-1171
private func removeSubscriptionHandle(id: UUID) {
  activeSubscriptions.removeValue(forKey: id)
}
```

The `removeSubscriptionHandle` is called on line 1157 when the subscription Task is cancelled. However, if the cancellation doesn't complete cleanly (e.g., due to a crash or force quit), the SubscriptionHandle remains in memory.

**Severity:** Low - Cleanup generally works, but edge cases exist.

---

## 3. Subscription Management Issues

### Issue 3.1: SubscriptionState holds strong references

**File:** `/Users/mlustig/Development/personal/instantdb/sharing-instant/Sources/SharingInstant/Internal/Reactor.swift`

**Lines 1185-1232:** The `SubscriptionState` actor holds:

```swift
private actor SubscriptionState<Value: EntityIdentifiable & Codable & Sendable> {
    private var currentIDs: [String] = []           // Unbounded growth
    private let continuation: AsyncStream<[Value]>.Continuation  // Strong ref
    private let store: SharedTripleStore            // Strong ref to singleton
    private let namespace: String
    private let orderByIsDescending: Bool
    private let includedLinks: Set<String>
    private let appID: String
    private let clientInstanceID: String
    private var optimisticIDs: [String] = []        // Unbounded growth
```

**Impact:**
- `currentIDs` and `optimisticIDs` grow unboundedly as entities are added
- The `store` reference keeps the SharedTripleStore alive
- The `continuation` keeps the AsyncStream alive

**Severity:** Medium - `currentIDs` accumulates all entity IDs seen during the subscription lifetime.

---

### Issue 3.2: cleanup() method is a no-op

**File:** `/Users/mlustig/Development/personal/instantdb/sharing-instant/Sources/SharingInstant/Internal/Reactor.swift`

**Lines 1446-1448:**

```swift
func cleanup() async {
    // No observers to clean up - query-level reactivity doesn't use per-entity observers
}
```

**Impact:** The cleanup method does nothing. While the comment suggests observers aren't used, the actor still holds references to `currentIDs`, `optimisticIDs`, `continuation`, and `store`.

**Severity:** Medium - Resources aren't actually cleaned up.

---

## 4. TripleStore Growth Issues

### Issue 4.1: No Garbage Collection for Old Data

**File:** `/Users/mlustig/Development/personal/instantdb/instant-ios-sdk/Sources/InstantDB/Store/TripleStore.swift`

The `TripleStore` class has three indexes (EAV, AEV, VAE) that grow unboundedly:

```swift
// Lines 41-51
private var eav: [String: [String: [AnyHashable: Triple]]] = [:]
private var aev: [String: [String: [AnyHashable: Triple]]] = [:]
private var vae: [AnyHashable: [String: [String: Triple]]] = [:]
```

**There is no mechanism to:**
- Evict old/unused triples
- Limit the size of any index
- Garbage collect unreferenced entities

**Impact:** The TripleStore grows indefinitely as more data is fetched from InstantDB.

## Recommendations

1. **Add TripleStore eviction**: Implement an LRU cache or time-based eviction for triples that haven't been accessed recently.

2. **Use `[weak self]` consistently**: Audit all closures in the Reactor actor for proper weak captures.

3. **Implement proper SubscriptionState cleanup**: Clear `currentIDs` and `optimisticIDs` when the subscription ends.

4. **Cache pending mutations**: Instead of re-fetching on every `handleStoreUpdate()`, cache them and update incrementally.

5. **Add memory monitoring**: Implement instrumentation to track TripleStore size, active subscriptions count, and observer count.

6. **Consider subscription scoping**: Allow subscriptions to scope their TripleStore view to only the entities they need.

# Detailed Comparison: SharingInstant (Swift) vs InstantDB (TypeScript)

## 1. Reactor/Core Coordinator

### TypeScript (`Reactor.js`)

**Key Data Structures:**
```javascript
// Lines 212-268
querySubs: PersistedObject<string, QuerySub, QuerySubInStorage>
kv: PersistedObject (includes pendingMutations Map)
queryCbs = {}  // callbacks per query hash
queryOnceDfds = {}  // deferred promises for one-shot queries
_dataForQueryCache = {}  // query result caching
_inFlightMutationEventIds = new Set()  // track sent mutations
```

**Key Methods in TS NOT in Swift:**
1. **`_cleanupPendingMutationsQueries()`** (lines 1461-1476) - Removes confirmed mutations after all queries have processed them
2. **`_cleanupPendingMutationsTimeout()`** (lines 1483-1499) - Timeout-based cleanup for mutations that don't affect queries
3. **`_cleanupQuery()`** (lines 1066-1074) - Removes query subscriptions and cache entries when no listeners remain
4. **`_rewriteMutations()`** (lines 1094-1172) - Rewrites mutations when attrs change, updates attr IDs
5. **`dataForQuery()`** with caching (lines 1224-1261) - Caches results by version to avoid recomputation
6. **`optimisticAttrs()`** (lines 1184-1221) - Merges pending attr changes into current attrs

### Swift (`Reactor.swift`)

**Key Data Structures:**
```swift
// Lines 157-161
private let store: SharedTripleStore
private var activeSubscriptions: [UUID: SubscriptionHandle] = [:]
private var hasRestoredPendingMutations: Bool = false
```

**Notable Differences:**

| Feature | TypeScript | Swift |
|---------|-----------|-------|
| Query caching | `_dataForQueryCache` with version checking | No caching layer |
| Mutation cleanup | Two cleanup mechanisms (query-based + timeout) | No explicit cleanup |
| Pending mutation storage | `PersistedObject` with IndexedDB | Relies on `InstantClient.getUnconfirmedPendingMutations()` |
| Query subscription tracking | Hash-based with callbacks | UUID-based `SubscriptionHandle` |
| Attr rewriting | `_rewriteMutations()` fixes attr IDs | Not implemented |

**Swift Missing Methods:**
- `_cleanupPendingMutationsQueries()` - No mechanism to clear confirmed mutations
- `_cleanupPendingMutationsTimeout()` - No timeout-based cleanup
- `_cleanupQuery()` - No cleanup when subscriptions end (though `removeSubscriptionHandle()` exists)
- Query result caching with version tracking

## 2. Store/TripleStore Data Indexing

### TypeScript (`store.ts`)

**Triple Indexes (lines 17-23):**
```typescript
export type Store = {
  eav: Map<string, Map<string, Map<any, Triple>>>;  // Entity -> Attr -> Value -> Triple
  aev: Map<string, Map<string, Map<any, Triple>>>;  // Attr -> Entity -> Value -> Triple
  vae: Map<any, Map<string, Map<string, Triple>>>;  // Value -> Attr -> Entity -> Triple (refs only)
  useDateObjects: boolean | null | undefined;
  cardinalityInference: boolean | null | undefined;
};
```

**Attr Indexing (lines 63-165 AttrsStoreClass):**
```typescript
blobAttrs: Map<string, Map<string, InstantDBAttr>>  // etype -> label -> attr
primaryKeys: Map<string, InstantDBAttr>              // etype -> primary key attr
forwardIdents: Map<string, Map<string, InstantDBAttr>>  // etype -> label -> attr
revIdents: Map<string, Map<string, InstantDBAttr>>      // etype -> label -> attr
```

**Garbage Collection (lines 525-592 `deleteEntity`):**
```typescript
function deleteEntity(store: Store, attrsStore: AttrsStore, args: any[]) {
  // Delete forward links and attributes
  // Handle cascade deletes via `on-delete-reverse` and `on-delete`
  // Delete reverse links from VAE index
}
```

### Swift (`TripleStore.swift`)

**Triple Indexes (from InstantDB SDK `TripleStore`):**
- Uses the InstantDB SDK's internal `TripleStore` which maintains EAV, AEV, VAE indexes
- Wrapped by `SharedTripleStore` for thread-safe observation

**Attr Indexing (`AttrsStore` - referenced but simplified):**
```swift
// attrsStore.getAttr(attrId)
// attrsStore.getAttrByForwardIdent()
// attrsStore.getAttrByReverseIdent()
// attrsStore.revIdents[entityType]  // reverse identity lookup
```

**Key Differences:**

| Feature | TypeScript | Swift |
|---------|-----------|-------|
| Triple storage | Nested Maps (EAV/AEV/VAE) | Delegated to SDK's TripleStore |
| Cascade deletes | Full support via `on-delete`, `on-delete-reverse` | Not implemented (lines 67-92 only delete direct refs) |
| Cardinality inference | `store.cardinalityInference` flag | Relies on attr schema |
| Date coercion | `useDateObjects` for Date objects | ISO8601 string via JSONDecoder |

**Swift Missing Features:**
- No cascade delete support (`on-delete`, `on-delete-reverse`)
- No GC configuration options for store size management

## 3. Optimistic Updates

### TypeScript (`_applyOptimisticUpdates`, lines 1263-1272)

```javascript
_applyOptimisticUpdates(store, attrsStore, mutations, processedTxId) {
  for (const [_, mut] of mutations) {
    // Only apply mutations that:
    // 1. Have no tx-id (not yet confirmed by server), OR
    // 2. Have tx-id greater than processedTxId (newer than what server has processed)
    if (!mut['tx-id'] || (processedTxId && mut['tx-id'] > processedTxId)) {
      const result = s.transact(store, attrsStore, mut['tx-steps']);
      store = result.store;
      attrsStore = result.attrsStore;
    }
  }
  return { store, attrsStore };
}
```

**Key Pattern:** Creates a NEW store with optimistic updates applied, does NOT mutate the base store.

### Swift (`applyOptimisticUpdate`, lines 681-761)

```swift
private func applyOptimisticUpdate(chunks: [TransactionChunk]) async {
  let timestamp = ConflictResolution.optimisticTimestamp()
  for chunk in chunks {
    for op in chunk.ops {
      switch action {
      case "create", "update":
        let triples = Normalization.normalize(...)
        store.addTriples(triples)  // Mutates store directly
      case "delete":
        store.deleteEntity(id: id)
      // ...
      }
    }
  }
  // Notify subscriptions
  await notifyAll()
}
```

**Key Differences:**

| Feature | TypeScript | Swift |
|---------|-----------|-------|
| Store mutation | Creates new store (immutable) | Mutates existing store directly |
| tx-id tracking | Tracks `tx-id` for each mutation | No tx-id tracking |
| processedTxId filtering | Skips already-processed mutations | No filtering mechanism |
| Clearing optimistic updates | Via `_cleanupPendingMutationsQueries()` | No explicit clearing |

**When Optimistic Updates Are Cleared:**

**TypeScript:**
1. When server returns `transact-ok`, mutation gets a `tx-id` (line 732-737)
2. `_cleanupPendingMutationsQueries()` removes mutations where `tx-id <= minProcessedTxId` across all queries
3. `_cleanupPendingMutationsTimeout()` removes old confirmed mutations after 30 seconds

**Swift:**
- **No explicit clearing mechanism found**
- `SubscriptionState.optimisticIDs` is cleared when server returns matching IDs (line 1251), but this only affects the ID tracking, not the actual mutations in the store

## 4. Query Subscription Lifecycle

### TypeScript

**Subscription Flow:**
```
subscribeQuery() -> _startQuerySub() -> add to querySubs + queryCbs -> send add-query to server
              ↓
         unsubscribe callback
              ↓
_unsubQuery() -> remove from queryCbs -> _cleanupQuery() -> querySubs.unloadKey(hash) + send remove-query
```

**Cleanup (`_cleanupQuery`, lines 1066-1074):**
```javascript
_cleanupQuery(q, hash) {
  const hasListeners = this._hasQueryListeners(hash);
  if (hasListeners) return;
  delete this.queryCbs[hash];
  delete this.queryOnceDfds[hash];
  delete this._dataForQueryCache[hash];
  this.querySubs.unloadKey(hash);  // Allows GC of persisted query data
  this._trySendAuthed(uuid(), { op: 'remove-query', q });  // Tell server to stop sending updates
}
```

### Swift

**Subscription Flow:**
```
subscribe() -> AsyncStream -> startSubscription() -> register SubscriptionHandle -> client.subscribe()
          ↓
    continuation.onTermination
          ↓
removeSubscriptionHandle() + subscriptionState.cleanup()
```

**Cleanup (`removeSubscriptionHandle`, line 1169-1171 + `cleanup`, line 1446-1448):**
```swift
private func removeSubscriptionHandle(id: UUID) {
  activeSubscriptions.removeValue(forKey: id)
}

func cleanup() async {
  // No observers to clean up - query-level reactivity doesn't use per-entity observers
}
```

**Key Differences:**

| Feature | TypeScript | Swift |
|---------|-----------|-------|
| Query hash storage | `PersistedObject` with unloadKey | In-memory only |
| Server notification | Sends `remove-query` message | No explicit message |
| Cache cleanup | Deletes from `_dataForQueryCache` | No cache to clean |
| GC integration | querySubs has GC options | No GC |

**Swift Missing:**
- No `remove-query` message sent to server when subscription ends
- No persistence layer cleanup
- No query result cache cleanup

## 5. Memory Management Patterns

### TypeScript

**WeakMap Usage (only for schema hashing):**
```typescript
// index.ts lines 252-254
function initSchemaHashStore(): WeakMap<any, string> {
  globalThis.__instantDbSchemaHashStore ?? new WeakMap<any, string>();
}
```

**PersistedObject GC (`utils/PersistedObject.ts`, lines 350-472):**
```typescript
gc: {
  maxSize: 1_000_000,  // max triples across all cached queries
  maxAgeMs: 1000 * 60 * 60 * 24 * 7 * 52,  // 1 year
  maxEntries: 1000,  // max number of cached queries
}

private async _gc() {
  // Remove keys not in meta
  // Remove entries over maxAge
  // Remove entries over maxEntries limit
  // Remove oldest entries until under maxSize
}
```

**Avoiding Stale Data:**
1. `querySubs.unloadKey(hash)` removes from memory when no listeners
2. `_dataForQueryCache` cleared on user change (line 1995)
3. Version tracking (`querySubs.version()`, `kv.version()`) for cache invalidation
4. GC runs periodically to clean old persisted data

### Swift

**Memory Management:**
```swift
// SharedTripleStore uses NSRecursiveLock for thread safety
// Observers stored in [String: [UUID: callback]] dictionary
// No WeakMap/WeakRef equivalents used
```

**No GC Implementation:**
- No max size limits
- No age-based cleanup
- No entry count limits
- Store grows unbounded

## 6. Recursive Entity Resolution

### TypeScript (`instaql.ts`)

**Resolution Flow:**
1. `queryOne()` -> `resolveObjects()` -> `extendObjects()`
2. `extendObjects()` iterates child queries (non-`$` keys in form)
3. For each child, calls `makeJoin()` to create pattern, then recursively calls `queryOne()`
4. Uses `level` parameter to track recursion depth

**Key Code (lines 527-577):**
```typescript
function extendObjects(makeVar, store, attrsStore, { etype, level, form }, objects) {
  const childQueries = Object.keys(form).filter((c) => c !== '$');
  if (!childQueries.length) {
    return Object.values(objects);
  }
  return Object.entries(objects).map(function extendChildren([eid, parent]) {
    const childResults = childQueries.map(function getChildResult(label) {
      // Create join pattern for this relationship
      const [nextEtype, nextLevel, join] = makeJoin(makeVar, attrsStore, etype, level, label, eid);
      // Recursively query children
      const childrenArray = queryOne(store, attrsStore, {
        etype: nextEtype,
        level: nextLevel,
        form: form[label],
        join,
      });
      return { [label]: isSingular ? childrenArray[0] : childrenArray };
    });
    return childResults.reduce((parent, child) => ({ ...parent, ...child }), parent);
  });
}
```

### Swift (`TripleStore+Extensions.swift`)

**Resolution Flow:**
1. `get<T>()` -> `resolve()`
2. `resolve()` iterates triples for entity, groups by attribute
3. For ref attributes, recursively calls `resolve()` on target entity
4. For reverse links, looks up `revIdents` and resolves parent entities
5. Uses `depth`/`maxDepth` for recursion control
6. `includedLinks` parameter limits which links to resolve

**Key Code (lines 19-172):**
```swift
public func resolve(id: String, attrsStore: AttrsStore, depth: Int = 0, maxDepth: Int = 10, includedLinks: Set<String>? = nil) -> [String: Any] {
  if depth > maxDepth { return ["id": id] }
  
  let triples = self.getTriples(entity: id)
  // Group by attribute, then resolve each
  for (attrId, attrTriples) in triplesByAttr {
    if attr.valueType == .ref {
      // Skip if not in includedLinks
      if let includedLinks = includedLinks, !includedLinks.contains(label) { continue }
      
      for triple in attrTriples {
        let childObj = resolve(id: targetId, attrsStore: attrsStore, depth: depth + 1, maxDepth: maxDepth, includedLinks: includedLinks)
        // Skip ghost entities (only have "id")
        if childObj.count <= 1 { continue }
        resolvedRefs.append(childObj)
      }
    }
  }
  
  // Resolve reverse links
  if depth < maxDepth, let entityType {
    for (reverseLabel, attr) in reverseAttrs {
      if let includedLinks = includedLinks, !includedLinks.contains(reverseLabel) { continue }
      // Get and resolve reverse refs
    }
  }
}
```

**Key Differences:**

| Feature | TypeScript | Swift |
|---------|-----------|-------|
| Query-driven | Uses query form to determine what to fetch | Uses `includedLinks` parameter |
| Index usage | Uses store's Map indexes directly | Uses `getTriples()` helper |
| Reverse links | Handled via schema's forward/reverse identity | Uses `revIdents` lookup |
| Ghost entity filtering | Not shown in instaql (handled at store level?) | Explicit check `childObj.count <= 1` |
| Cardinality | Determined by `linkIndex` from schema | Determined by `attr.cardinality` and `attr.unique` |

---

## Summary: Gaps in Swift Implementation

### Critical Missing Features:
1. **Pending mutation cleanup** - Mutations accumulate indefinitely
2. **Query result caching** - Every subscription re-computes from scratch
3. **Subscription cleanup notification** - Server not told when subscriptions end
4. **Cascade deletes** - `on-delete` and `on-delete-reverse` not supported
5. **Attr rewriting** - When attrs change, old mutations may have stale attr IDs

### Memory Management Gaps:
1. No GC configuration or implementation
2. No max size/age/entry limits
3. Store and subscriptions grow unbounded
4. No `unloadKey` equivalent for freeing memory

### Minor Differences:
1. No `_dataForQueryCache` for avoiding duplicate work
2. No version tracking for cache invalidation
3. No `processedTxId` filtering for optimistic updates
4. No `remove-query` message to server

### 1. Segment Creation Pattern

**Location:** `/Users/mlustig/Development/personal/instantdb/sharing-instant/Examples/CaseStudies/RapidTranscriptionDemo.swift`

**Findings:**

- **No debouncing**: There's no throttling of rapid updates - every update goes through the full mutation pipeline.

## Summary of Memory Growth Causes

1. **Rapid Task Creation**: Each update creates new `Task` instances without debouncing.

2. **JSON Serialization Overhead**: Every `handleStoreUpdate()` call involves JSON encode/decode for all entities.

3. **Multiple Subscription Notifications**: `notifyAll()` triggers work on ALL subscriptions, not just affected ones.

4. **No Cleanup of Old Segments**: The demo doesn't show segment cleanup; segments accumulate in memory.

5. **SQLite Queries on Every Update**: `getUnconfirmedPendingMutations()` is called on every `handleStoreUpdate()`.

6. **Computed Property Re-evaluation**: `testSegments` filter/sort runs on every state change.

7. **Full Entity Resolution**: Without explicit `includedLinks`, link resolution may traverse more of the graph than needed.

---

## Recommendations for Investigation

1. **Profile with Instruments**: Use Allocations and Time Profiler to identify hotspots.

2. **Add Debouncing**: Consider batching rapid updates before sending to server.

3. **Optimize handleStoreUpdate()**: Cache pending mutations instead of fetching from SQLite every call.

4. **Explicit includedLinks**: Ensure all queries explicitly specify which links to resolve.

5. **Lazy Word Resolution**: Consider not storing words in memory until needed for display.

# Swift Memory Leak Patterns for Real-Time Sync Libraries

This research covers memory leak patterns and fixes for Swift applications using actors, observation, and async streams - particularly relevant for real-time sync libraries with WebSocket connections and reactive state.

---

## 1. Actor Retain Cycles

### The Problem

Actors can cause retain cycles when:
1. A `Task` is stored as a property on the actor/class
2. The task's closure captures `self` strongly
3. The task runs indefinitely or for a long time

### Problematic Pattern

```swift
actor SyncManager {
    private var syncTask: Task<Void, Never>?
    
    func startSync() {
        // PROBLEM: Task captures self strongly, stored as property
        syncTask = Task {
            while true {  // Infinite loop
                await self.processUpdates()  // Strong capture of self
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(1))
            }
        }
    }
}
```

### Fixed Pattern

```swift
actor SyncManager {
    private var syncTask: Task<Void, Never>?
    
    func startSync() {
        syncTask = Task { [weak self] in
            while !Task.isCancelled {
                // Only grab strong reference briefly, inside the loop
                guard let self else { return }
                await self.processUpdates()
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(1))
            }
        }
    }
    
    func stopSync() {
        syncTask?.cancel()
        syncTask = nil
    }
    
    deinit {
        syncTask?.cancel()
    }
}
```

### Important Nuance

As noted by [Swift by Sundell](https://www.swiftbysundell.com/articles/memory-management-when-using-async-await/), Tasks don't create retain cycles by default - the issue arises specifically when you store the task as a property while the task also captures self strongly, and the task runs indefinitely.

### Best Practice for Weak Self in Tasks

According to [Donny Wals](https://www.donnywals.com/how-to-use-weak-self-in-swift-concurrency-tasks/):

```swift
// WRONG - captures strong reference immediately
Task { [weak self] in
    guard let self else { return }  // Strong ref grabbed at start
    // ... long running work with self captured
}

// CORRECT - unwrap only when needed, briefly
Task { [weak self] in
    for await event in stream {
        guard let self else { return }
        await self.handleEvent(event)  // Brief strong ref
    }
}

// ALSO CORRECT - use optional chaining
Task { [weak self] in
    await self?.handleEvent()  // Never grabs strong ref
}
```

---

## 2. @Observable Memory Leaks

### iOS 17 Regression Issue

According to [Apple Developer Forums](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/736110), iOS 17 introduced a regression where `@Observable` objects stored as `@State` can leak:

```swift
// PROBLEMATIC on iOS 17.0-17.1
struct SheetView: View {
    @State private var viewModel = ViewModel()  // Leaks!
    
    var body: some View {
        Button("Show") { showSheet = true }
            .sheet(isPresented: $showSheet) {
                DetailView(vm: viewModel)
            }
    }
}

@Observable
class ViewModel {
    // Never deallocates when sheet dismissed on iOS 17.0-17.1
}
```

### Workaround (for iOS 17.0-17.1)

According to [John Bafford](https://bafford.com/2023/10/12/swiftui-memory-leak-workaround/):

```swift
// Revert to ObservableObject pattern
class ViewModel: ObservableObject {
    @Published var data: String = ""
}

struct SheetView: View {
    @StateObject private var viewModel = ViewModel()  // Fixed
}
```

**Note**: This was fixed after iOS 17.1 per Apple forums.

### Point-Free Perception Library

The [Perception library](https://github.com/pointfreeco/swift-perception) backports `@Observable` to iOS 13+ but had its own memory issues. According to [Point-Free's blog](https://www.pointfree.co/blog/posts/180-perception-2-0-an-updated-back-port-of-swift-s-observation-framework):

> "Since Observation's first release in Swift 5.9 there has been a subtle way to accidentally introduce a memory leak into your app. Due to how withObservationTracking works, subscriptions cannot be cleaned up unless a final mutation is made to state."

Perception 2.0 fixes this by listening for observer deallocation.

---

## 3. AsyncStream Memory Issues

### The Core Problem

[Wesley Matlock on Medium](https://medium.com/@wesleymatlock/modern-swift-concurrency-in-the-wild-asyncstream-asyncsequence-cancelation-headaches-60722d779ccf) explains:

> "When the task is cancelled, the consuming side of the stream stops receiving values... However, the producing side doesn't automatically stop. It will keep running unless we handle cleanup explicitly."

### Problematic Pattern

```swift
class QuerySubscription {
    private var stream: AsyncStream<[Entity]>?
    
    func subscribe() -> AsyncStream<[Entity]> {
        AsyncStream { continuation in
            // PROBLEM: Timer never stopped, continuation never finished
            let timer = Timer.scheduledTimer(withTimeInterval: 1, repeats: true) { _ in
                continuation.yield(self.fetchData())  // Strong capture of self
            }
        }
    }
}
```

### Fixed Pattern

```swift
class QuerySubscription {
    func subscribe() -> AsyncStream<[Entity]> {
        AsyncStream { continuation in
            let timer = Timer.scheduledTimer(withTimeInterval: 1, repeats: true) { [weak self] _ in
                guard let self else {
                    continuation.finish()
                    return
                }
                continuation.yield(self.fetchData())
            }
            
            // CRITICAL: Handle termination
            continuation.onTermination = { @Sendable _ in
                timer.invalidate()
            }
        }
    }
}
```

### Using AsyncStream.makeStream

Per [Donny Wals](https://www.donnywals.com/building-an-asyncsequence-with-asyncstream-makestream/):

```swift
actor WebSocketManager {
    private var continuation: AsyncStream<Message>.Continuation?
    
    func messages() -> AsyncStream<Message> {
        let (stream, continuation) = AsyncStream<Message>.makeStream()
        self.continuation = continuation
        
        continuation.onTermination = { [weak self] _ in
            Task { await self?.cleanup() }
        }
        
        return stream
    }
    
    func cleanup() {
        continuation?.finish()
        continuation = nil
    }
}
```

---

## 4. Closure Capture in Swift Concurrency

### Sendable Closures Don't Prevent Retain Cycles

According to [Waheed Afolabi on Medium](https://medium.com/@afolabiwaheed/mastering-swift-closures-6f1fe2ab1ff2):

> "Sendable closures help avoid concurrency issues but don't inherently solve retain-cycles. It would be best to use `[weak self]` or `[unowned self]` to avoid retain-cycles."

### Swift 6 Non-Sendable Captures

[Donny Wals](https://www.donnywals.com/solving-capture-of-non-sendable-type-in-sendable-closure-in-swift/) explains solutions:

```swift
// PROBLEM: Non-Sendable type captured
class DataManager {  // Not Sendable
    func load() {
        Task {
            await fetchData()  // Warning: Capture of non-sendable type
        }
    }
}

// SOLUTION 1: Make it Sendable via actor
actor DataManager {
    func load() {
        Task {
            await fetchData()  // Fine - actors are Sendable
        }
    }
}

// SOLUTION 2: MainActor isolation
@MainActor
class DataManager {
    func load() {
        Task {
            await fetchData()  // Fine - isolated to MainActor
        }
    }
}

// SOLUTION 3: Copy data out
class DataManager {
    func load() {
        let endpoint = self.endpoint  // Copy Sendable data
        Task {
            await fetch(from: endpoint)  // Only Sendable data crosses boundary
        }
    }
}
```

---

## 5. Combine/Observation Cleanup

### AnyCancellable Basics

Per [Donny Wals](https://www.donnywals.com/what-exactly-is-a-combine-anycancellable/):

> "An AnyCancellable instance automatically calls cancel() when deinitialized."

### Proper Subscription Management

```swift
class QueryManager {
    private var cancellables = Set<AnyCancellable>()
    
    func observe(_ query: Query) {
        query.publisher
            .sink { [weak self] result in
                self?.handleResult(result)
            }
            .store(in: &cancellables)
    }
    
    func cleanup() {
        cancellables.removeAll()  // Cancels all subscriptions
    }
    
    deinit {
        // AnyCancellables auto-cancel on dealloc, but explicit is clearer
        cancellables.removeAll()
    }
}
```

### Avoid Retain Cycles in sink

From [Swift by Sundell](https://www.swiftbysundell.com/articles/combine-self-cancellable-memory-management/):

```swift
// PROBLEM: Retain cycle
publisher
    .assign(to: \.value, on: self)  // Strong reference to self
    .store(in: &cancellables)  // self holds cancellables

// SOLUTION 1: Use sink with weak self
publisher
    .sink { [weak self] value in
        self?.value = value
    }
    .store(in: &cancellables)

// SOLUTION 2: Assign to @Published property (Combine manages lifetime)
publisher
    .assign(to: &$value)  // No AnyCancellable returned
```

---

## 6. Actor Deinit Isolation (Swift 6.2+)

### The Problem

Per [Anton Gubarenko](https://antongubarenko.substack.com/p/understanding-swift-6-concurrency):

> "Even if a type has actor isolation, deinitializers are always non-isolated. This creates potential race conditions and crashes."

### Swift 6.2 Solution: `isolated deinit`

From [Hacking with Swift](https://www.hackingwithswift.com/articles/277/whats-new-in-swift-6-2):

```swift
@MainActor 
class ConnectionManager {
    private var connection: WebSocketConnection?
    
    func cleanup() {
        connection?.close()
        connection = nil
    }
    
    // Swift 6.2+: isolated deinit runs on MainActor
    isolated deinit {
        cleanup()  // Safe to call MainActor-isolated method
    }
}
```

### Pre-Swift 6.2 Workaround

```swift
@MainActor
class ConnectionManager {
    private var connection: WebSocketConnection?
    
    // Use a non-isolated helper
    private final class DeinitHelper {
        var onDeinit: (() -> Void)?
        deinit { onDeinit?() }
    }
    
    private let deinitHelper = DeinitHelper()
    
    init() {
        deinitHelper.onDeinit = { [weak self] in
            Task { @MainActor in
                self?.cleanup()
            }
        }
    }
}
```

---

## 7. WebSocket Memory Leaks

### URLSessionWebSocketTask Issues

According to [Apple Developer Forums](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/725039):

> "Calling disconnect which triggers the cancel method on URLSessionWebSocketTask triggers memory leaks."

### Proper Cleanup

From [Kristaps Grinbergs](https://dev.to/fassko/clearing-up-after-subscribing-to-swift-websockets-56o4):

```swift
class WebSocketManager {
    private var session: URLSession?
    private var task: URLSessionWebSocketTask?
    
    func connect(to url: URL) {
        session = URLSession(configuration: .default)
        task = session?.webSocketTask(with: url)
        task?.resume()
    }
    
    func disconnect() {
        // Use WebSocket-specific close
        task?.cancel(with: .goingAway, reason: nil)
        task = nil
        
        // CRITICAL: Invalidate session to prevent leaks
        session?.invalidateAndCancel()
        session = nil
    }
    
    deinit {
        disconnect()
    }
}
```

### Consider Alternatives

Apple recommends using Network framework (NWConnection) for WebSocket per [TN3151](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/725039). Some developers report that [SwiftNIO](https://github.com/apple/swift-nio) eliminates WebSocket memory issues.

## 8. Profiling with Instruments

### Finding Memory Leaks

Per [DEV Community](https://dev.to/raphacmartin/debugging-memory-leaks-with-instruments-in-xcode-56hk):

1. **Open Instruments**: Product > Profile (Cmd+I)
2. **Choose Leaks template**
3. **Run and interact with your app**
4. **Look for red markers** in the timeline
5. **Inspect "Cycles & Roots"** to see retain cycles

### Memory Graph Debugger

From [Donny Wals](https://www.donnywals.com/using-xcodes-memory-graph-to-find-memory-leaks/):

1. Run app with Xcode
2. Click memory debugger icon (between code and console)
3. Look for objects with **"Leaked allocation" badges**
4. Inspect reference chains to find the cycle

### Unit Testing for Leaks

Per [Swift by Sundell](https://www.swiftbysundell.com/articles/using-unit-tests-to-identify-avoid-memory-leaks-in-swift/):

```swift
extension XCTestCase {
    func trackForMemoryLeaks(
        _ instance: AnyObject,
        file: StaticString = #filePath,
        line: UInt = #line
    ) {
        addTeardownBlock { [weak instance] in
            XCTAssertNil(
                instance,
                "Instance should have been deallocated. Potential memory leak.",
                file: file,
                line: line
            )
        }
    }
}

// Usage
func testQuerySubscriptionDeallocates() {
    var subscription: QuerySubscription? = QuerySubscription()
    trackForMemoryLeaks(subscription!)
    
    subscription?.start()
    subscription?.stop()
    subscription = nil
    // Test will fail if subscription is still alive
}
```

### LifetimeTracker

From [GitHub - LifetimeTracker](https://github.com/krzysztofzablocki/LifetimeTracker):

```swift
class QueryManager: LifetimeTrackable {
    static var lifetimeConfiguration = LifetimeConfiguration(
        maxCount: 1,  // Expected max instances
        groupName: "QueryManager"
    )
    
    init() {
        trackLifetime()
    }
}
```

This surfaces leaks immediately during development, not just when you remember to check Instruments.

## 9. Real-Time Sync Library Patterns

### Complete Example: Safe Query Subscription

```swift
@MainActor
final class InstantDBClient {
    private var subscriptionTasks: [String: Task<Void, Never>] = [:]
    private var cancellables = Set<AnyCancellable>()
    private var webSocketManager: WebSocketManager?
    
    func subscribe<T: Entity>(
        to query: Query<T>
    ) -> AsyncStream<QueryResult<T>> {
        let queryId = query.id
        
        return AsyncStream { [weak self] continuation in
            guard let self else {
                continuation.finish()
                return
            }
            
            let task = Task { [weak self] in
                guard let self else {
                    continuation.finish()
                    return
                }
                
                do {
                    for try await result in await self.webSocketManager!.results(for: query) {
                        if Task.isCancelled { break }
                        continuation.yield(result)
                    }
                } catch {
                    continuation.finish()
                }
            }
            
            self.subscriptionTasks[queryId] = task
            
            continuation.onTermination = { @Sendable [weak self] _ in
                Task { @MainActor [weak self] in
                    self?.subscriptionTasks[queryId]?.cancel()
                    self?.subscriptionTasks.removeValue(forKey: queryId)
                }
            }
        }
    }
    
    func disconnect() {
        // Cancel all subscription tasks
        for task in subscriptionTasks.values {
            task.cancel()
        }
        subscriptionTasks.removeAll()
        
        // Clear Combine subscriptions
        cancellables.removeAll()
        
        // Properly close WebSocket
        webSocketManager?.disconnect()
        webSocketManager = nil
    }
    
    deinit {
        // For Swift < 6.2, schedule cleanup on MainActor
        // For Swift 6.2+, use `isolated deinit`
    }
}
```

---

## Summary of Key Patterns

| Issue | Solution |
|-------|----------|
| Task retaining self | Use `[weak self]`, unwrap briefly inside loops |
| AsyncStream not cleaning up | Always use `onTermination` handler |
| Actor deinit isolation | Use `isolated deinit` (Swift 6.2+) or dispatch to actor |
| @Observable leaks (iOS 17.0-17.1) | Use ObservableObject or update to iOS 17.2+ |
| WebSocket leaks | Call `session.invalidateAndCancel()` on disconnect |
| Combine sink cycles | Use `[weak self]` in sink closures |
| Unfinished continuations | Always call `continuation.finish()` |
| Long-running Tasks | Store and cancel tasks, check `Task.isCancelled` |

## Summary: Recursive Entity Resolution Analysis in SharingInstant

### Overview

I have analyzed the SharingInstant codebase to identify potential memory issues and infinite loops in the recursive entity resolution code. Here are my findings:

---

### 1. TripleStore Entity Resolution

**Key File**: `/Users/mlustig/Development/personal/instantdb/sharing-instant/Sources/SharingInstant/Extensions/TripleStore+Extensions.swift`

#### Depth Limit Protection
The `resolve()` function has a **depth limit** to prevent infinite recursion:

- **Default maxDepth**: 10 (line 23)
- **Early return**: `if depth > maxDepth { return ["id": id] }` (line 26)

```swift
// Lines 19-26:
public func resolve(
    id: String,
    attrsStore: AttrsStore,
    depth: Int = 0,
    maxDepth: Int = 10,
    includedLinks: Set<String>? = nil
) -> [String: Any] {
    if depth > maxDepth { return ["id": id] }
```

#### NO Cycle Detection (Potential Issue)
**CRITICAL**: There is **no visited set** to detect cycles. The code relies solely on depth limiting. This means:

- If Entity A links to Entity B links to Entity A, both will be resolved until `maxDepth` is hit
- With the default `maxDepth = 10`, a circular A→B→A reference will resolve **5 complete A-B cycles** before stopping
- Each cycle doubles the amount of data being processed

**Code paths that recurse without cycle detection**:

1. **Forward links** (lines 67-79):
```swift
for triple in attrTriples {
    if case .ref(let targetId) = triple.value {
        let childObj = resolve(id: targetId, attrsStore: attrsStore, depth: depth + 1, maxDepth: maxDepth, includedLinks: includedLinks)
        // ...
    }
}
```

2. **Reverse links** (lines 131-138):
```swift
let parentObj = resolve(
    id: triple.entityId,
    attrsStore: attrsStore,
    depth: depth + 1,
    maxDepth: maxDepth,
    includedLinks: includedLinks
)
```

---

### 2. `includedLinks` Parameter - Memory Safety Feature

The `includedLinks` parameter (lines 15-17, 24) provides **opt-in link resolution**:

- `nil` → resolves ALL links (default, potentially dangerous)
- `[]` (empty set) → resolves NO links (safest)
- `["posts", "author"]` → resolves only specified links

**This is the primary memory protection mechanism** beyond depth limiting.

**Code path** (lines 59-61):
```swift
if let includedLinks = includedLinks, !includedLinks.contains(label) {
    continue
}
```

---

### 3. InstaQL/Query Processing

**Key Files**:
- `/Users/mlustig/Development/personal/instantdb/sharing-instant/Sources/SharingInstant/EntityKey.swift`
- `/Users/mlustig/Development/personal/instantdb/sharing-instant/Sources/SharingInstant/InstantSyncKey+Helpers.swift`

#### Query Structure (`EntityQueryNode`)
The `EntityQueryNode` enum (EntityKey.swift lines 54-63) is an `indirect enum` that supports recursive nesting:

```swift
public indirect enum EntityQueryNode: Hashable, Sendable {
  case link(
    name: String,
    limit: Int? = nil,
    orderBy: String? = nil,
    orderDirection: EntityKeyOrderDirection? = nil,
    whereClauses: [String: EntityKeyPredicate] = [:],
    children: [EntityQueryNode] = []  // Recursive children
  )
}
```

**The `.with()` builder methods** allow unlimited nesting:
```swift
Schema.users.with(\.posts) { posts in
  posts.with(\.comments) { comments in
    comments.with(\.author)  // Can nest indefinitely
  }
}
```

**No limit on query depth** - the query tree can be arbitrarily deep.

#### `convertLinkTreeToInstaQL` (InstantSyncKey+Helpers.swift lines 4-46)
This function recursively converts the link tree:
```swift
func convertLinkTreeToInstaQL(_ tree: [EntityQueryNode]) -> [String: Any] {
    // ...
    if !children.isEmpty {
       let childDict = convertLinkTreeToInstaQL(children)  // Recursive call
       linkDef = childDict
    }
    // ...
}
```

---

### 4. Entity Decoding

**Key File**: `/Users/mlustig/Development/personal/instantdb/sharing-instant/Sources/SharingInstant/Extensions/TripleStore+Extensions.swift` (lines 174-197)

The `get<T: Decodable>()` method:
1. Calls `resolve()` to build a dictionary
2. Serializes to JSON
3. Decodes via `JSONDecoder`

```swift
public func get<T: Decodable>(id: String, attrsStore: AttrsStore, includedLinks: Set<String>? = nil) -> T? {
    let dict = resolve(id: id, attrsStore: attrsStore, includedLinks: includedLinks)
    // JSON encode/decode
}
```

**Memory concern**: The entire resolved dictionary is JSON serialized, which doubles memory usage during decoding.

---

### 5. Normalization (Reverse Direction)

**Key File**: `/Users/mlustig/Development/personal/instantdb/sharing-instant/Sources/SharingInstant/Internal/Normalization.swift`

The `normalize()` function also recurses when processing linked entities (lines 56-64, 103-108):

```swift
// Recursive normalize child
triples.append(contentsOf: normalize(
    data: childDict,
    namespace: targetNamespace,
    attrsStore: attrsStore,
    createdAt: createdAt
))
```

**No depth limit in normalization** - unlike `resolve()`, the `normalize()` function has NO `maxDepth` parameter. If incoming data contains circular references, this could theoretically cause stack overflow.

---

### 6. IndirectLink Property Wrapper

**Key File**: `/Users/mlustig/Development/personal/instantdb/sharing-instant/Sources/SharingInstant/IndirectLink.swift`

The `@IndirectLink` property wrapper breaks **compile-time** cycles in generated struct types:

```swift
@propertyWrapper
public struct IndirectLink<Value> {
  private var storage: IndirectLinkStorage<Value>?
  // Uses indirect enum for storage
}
```

This is used by code generation (SwiftGenerator.swift lines 568-659) to detect and break has-one cycles at compile time. However, **this does not prevent runtime circular resolution** - it only prevents compiler errors from self-referential structs.

---

### 7. Subscription State Memory

**Key File**: `/Users/mlustig/Development/personal/instantdb/sharing-instant/Sources/SharingInstant/Internal/Reactor.swift`

The `SubscriptionState` actor (lines 1185-1449) maintains:
- `currentIDs: [String]` - List of entity IDs being tracked
- `optimisticIDs: [String]` - Local optimistic writes

In `handleStoreUpdate()` (lines 1274-1397), entities are resolved from the store:

```swift
// Line 1369:
if let val: Value = store.get(id: id, includedLinks: includedLinks) {
```

**Good**: `includedLinks` is passed to limit resolution scope.

---

### Specific Code Paths That Could Cause Memory Growth

| Location | File | Lines | Issue |
|----------|------|-------|-------|
| Circular A→B→A resolution | TripleStore+Extensions.swift | 67-79 | No visited set, resolves until maxDepth |
| Reverse link circular resolution | TripleStore+Extensions.swift | 131-138 | Same issue with reverse links |
| `nil` includedLinks default | TripleStore+Extensions.swift | 24, 183 | Resolves ALL links by default |
| Normalization recursion | Normalization.swift | 56-64, 103-108 | No depth limit at all |
| JSON serialization doubling | TripleStore+Extensions.swift | 186 | Full dictionary serialized to JSON |
| Unlimited query nesting | EntityKey.swift | 278-301, 315-337 | `.with()` allows infinite depth |

---

### Recommendations Summary

1. **Add cycle detection** to `resolve()` using a `visited: Set<String>` parameter
2. **Add depth limit** to `Normalization.normalize()` 
3. **Consider lowering default maxDepth** from 10 to something like 5
4. **Document the memory implications** of using `nil` for `includedLinks`
5. **Add telemetry/warnings** when resolution depth exceeds a threshold

    16→// #region agent log
    17→/// Debug logging helper for Cursor debug mode - sends via HTTP to Mac
    18→/// Logs are queued and persisted to disk, then sent when network is available.
    19→///
    20→/// To use:
    21→/// 1. Run: python3 Scripts/debug-log-server.py 7248
    22→/// 2. Update the IP below to your Mac's local IP
    23→private let debugLogServerURL = "http://192.168.68.111:7248/ingest/debug"
    24→
    25→/// Actor to manage thread-safe debug log queue with persistence
    26→private actor DebugLogQueue {
    27→    static let shared = DebugLogQueue()
    28→
    29→    private let fileURL: URL
    30→    private var isFlushing = false
    31→
    32→    init() {
    33→        let docs = FileManager.default.urls(for: .documentDirectory, in: .userDomainMask).first!
    34→        self.fileURL = docs.appendingPathComponent("debug-logs-queue.jsonl")
    35→    }
    36→
    37→    func enqueue(_ jsonData: Data) {
    38→        // Append to file (JSONL format - one JSON object per line)
    39→        if let line = String(data: jsonData, encoding: .utf8) {
    40→            let lineWithNewline = line + "\n"
    41→            if let lineData = lineWithNewline.data(using: .utf8) {
    42→                if FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: fileURL.path) {
    43→                    if let handle = try? FileHandle(forWritingTo: fileURL) {
    44→                        handle.seekToEndOfFile()
    45→                        handle.write(lineData)
    46→                        try? handle.close()
    47→                    }
    48→                } else {
    49→                    try? lineData.write(to: fileURL)
    50→                }
    51→            }
    52→        }
    53→
    54→        // Try to flush immediately
    55→        Task {
    56→            await flush()
    57→        }
    58→    }
    59→
    60→    func flush() async {
    61→        guard !isFlushing else { return }
    62→        isFlushing = true
    63→        defer { isFlushing = false }
    64→
    65→        guard FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: fileURL.path),
    66→              let content = try? String(contentsOf: fileURL, encoding: .utf8) else {
    67→            return
    68→        }
    69→
    70→        let lines = content.components(separatedBy: "\n").filter { !$0.isEmpty }
    71→        guard !lines.isEmpty else { return }
    72→
    73→        guard let ingestURL = URL(string: debugLogServerURL) else { return }
    74→
    75→        var successCount = 0
    76→
    77→        for line in lines {
    78→            guard let jsonData = line.data(using: .utf8) else {
    79→                successCount += 1 // Skip malformed
    80→                continue
    81→            }
    82→
    83→            var request = URLRequest(url: ingestURL)
    84→            request.httpMethod = "POST"
    85→            request.setValue("application/json", forHTTPHeaderField: "Content-Type")
    86→            request.httpBody = jsonData
    87→            request.timeoutInterval = 5
    88→
    89→            do {
    90→                let (_, response) = try await URLSession.shared.data(for: request)
    91→                if let httpResponse = response as? HTTPURLResponse, httpResponse.statusCode == 200 {
    92→                    successCount += 1
    93→                } else {
    94→                    break // Server error, stop
    95→                }
    96→            } catch {
    97→                // Network error - stop trying, will retry later
    98→                break
    99→            }
   100→        }
   101→
   102→        // Remove successfully sent logs by rewriting file with remaining lines
   103→        if successCount > 0 {
   104→            let remainingLines = Array(lines.dropFirst(successCount))
   105→            if remainingLines.isEmpty {
   106→                try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: fileURL)
   107→            } else {
   108→                let remainingContent = remainingLines.joined(separator: "\n") + "\n"
   109→                try? remainingContent.write(to: fileURL, atomically: true, encoding: .utf8)
   110→            }
   111→        }
   112→    }
   113→}

   153→public actor Reactor {
   154→  // public static let shared = Reactor() // Removed for DI
   155→
   156→
   157→  private let store: SharedTripleStore
   158→  private let clientInstanceID: String
   159→  private var activeSubscriptions: [UUID: SubscriptionHandle] = [:]
   160→
   161→  /// Tracks whether we've restored pending mutations from SQLite.
   162→  ///
   163→  /// ## Why This Exists
   164→  /// When the app restarts, pending mutations (optimistic updates that haven't been
   165→  /// confirmed by the server) are persisted in SQLite but not in the in-memory
   166→  /// SharedTripleStore. Without restoring them, the UI would show stale data until
   167→  /// the server confirms the mutations (which requires network connectivity).
   168→  ///
   169→  /// This flag ensures we only restore once per app launch to avoid duplicate
   170→  /// application of the same mutations.
   171→  private var hasRestoredPendingMutations: Bool = false
   172→
   173→  public init(store: SharedTripleStore, clientInstanceID: String = "default") {
   174→    self.store = store
   175→    self.clientInstanceID = clientInstanceID
   176→  }
   177→
   178→  // MARK: - Pending Mutation Restoration
   179→
   180→  /// Restores pending mutations from SQLite to the in-memory SharedTripleStore.
   181→  ///
   182→  /// ## Why This Exists
   183→  /// When the app restarts, pending mutations are persisted in SQLite but not in
   184→  /// the in-memory SharedTripleStore. This method re-applies those mutations so
   185→  /// users see their changes immediately, even before the server confirms them.
   186→  ///
   187→  /// This matches the TypeScript SDK behavior where `pendingMutations` are merged
   188→  /// into query results via `_applyOptimisticUpdates()`.
   189→  ///
   190→  /// - Parameter client: The InstantClient to load pending mutations from
   191→  private func restorePendingMutationsIfNeeded(client: InstantClient, appID: String) async {
   192→    guard !hasRestoredPendingMutations else {
   193→      reactorDebugLog("restorePendingMutations: SKIPPED - already restored")
   194→      return
   195→    }
   196→    hasRestoredPendingMutations = true
   197→
   198→    reactorDebugLog("restorePendingMutations: START", data: [
   199→      "activeSubscriptionCount": activeSubscriptions.count,
   200→      "subscriptionNamespaces": activeSubscriptions.values.map { $0.namespace }
   201→    ])
   202→
   203→    let pending = await client.getUnconfirmedPendingMutations()
   204→    guard !pending.isEmpty else {
   205→      reactorDebugLog("restorePendingMutations: no pending mutations to restore")
   206→      return
   207→    }
   208→
   209→    reactorDebugLog("restorePendingMutations: found \(pending.count) pending mutations", data: [
   210→      "mutationEventIds": pending.map { $0.eventId }
   211→    ])
   212→
   213→    // Get current attributes for cardinality information
   214→    let attrs = await MainActor.run { client.attributes }
   215→    reactorDebugLog("restorePendingMutations: got attributes", data: [
   216→      "attrCount": attrs.count
   217→    ])
   218→    if !attrs.isEmpty {
   219→      store.updateAttributes(attrs)
   220→    }
   221→
   222→    // Track all entity IDs we're restoring so we can notify subscriptions properly
   223→    var restoredEntityIds: [(namespace: String, id: String)] = []
   224→
   225→    // Apply each pending mutation to the local store
   226→    for mutation in pending {
   227→      let entityIds = applyPendingMutationToStore(mutation)
   228→      restoredEntityIds.append(contentsOf: entityIds)
   229→    }
   230→
   231→    reactorDebugLog("restorePendingMutations: applied to store", data: [
   232→      "restoredEntityCount": restoredEntityIds.count,
   233→      "restoredEntityIds": restoredEntityIds.map { "\($0.namespace):\($0.id)" }
   234→    ])
   235→
   236→    // CRITICAL: We must notify with specific entity IDs, not just notifyAll()
   237→    // because notifyAll() uses "__notifyAll__" sentinel which doesn't add to currentIDs.
   238→    // If currentIDs is empty (no server data yet), the subscription yields nothing.
   239→    for (namespace, id) in restoredEntityIds {
   240→      await notifyOptimisticUpsert(namespace: namespace, id: id)
   241→    }
   242→
   243→    reactorDebugLog("restorePendingMutations: notified subscriptions", data: [
   244→      "notifiedCount": restoredEntityIds.count
   245→    ])
   246→
   247→    // Also do a full notifyAll to ensure any complex queries recompute
   248→    await notifyAll()
   249→
   250→    reactorDebugLog("restorePendingMutations: COMPLETE", data: [
   251→      "restoredCount": pending.count,
   252→      "entityIds": restoredEntityIds.map { $0.id }
   253→    ])
   254→  }
   255→
   256→  /// Applies a single pending mutation's tx-steps to the local TripleStore.
   257→  ///
   258→  /// This parses the raw tx-steps format and applies creates/updates/deletes
   259→  /// to the SharedTripleStore, making the data immediately visible to subscriptions.
   260→  ///
   261→  /// - Returns: Array of (namespace, entityId) tuples for entities that were modified
   262→  private func applyPendingMutationToStore(_ mutation: PendingMutation) -> [(namespace: String, id: String)] {
   263→    let timestamp = ConflictResolution.optimisticTimestamp()
   264→    var modifiedEntities: [(namespace: String, id: String)] = []
   265→
   266→    for step in mutation.txSteps {
   267→      // CRITICAL FIX: step is [AnyCodableValue], not [Any].
   268→      // We must access .value on each element to get the underlying value.
   269→      guard step.count >= 1,
   270→            let action = step[0].value as? String else {
   271→        continue
   272→      }
   273→
   274→      switch action {
   275→      case "add-triple":
   276→        // Format: ["add-triple", entityId, attrId, value, ...]
   277→        guard step.count >= 4,
   278→              let entityId = step[1].value as? String,
   279→              let attrId = step[2].value as? String else {
   280→          continue
   281→        }
   282→        let rawValue = step[3].value
   283→        let value = convertToTripleValue(rawValue)
   284→
   285→        let triple = Triple(
   286→          entityId: entityId,
   287→          attributeId: attrId,
   288→          value: value,
   289→          createdAt: timestamp
   290→        )
   291→        let attr = store.attrsStore.getAttr(attrId)
   292→        let hasCardinalityOne = attr?.cardinality == .one
   293→        let isRef = attr?.valueType == .ref
   294→        store.addTriple(triple, hasCardinalityOne: hasCardinalityOne, isRef: isRef)
   295→
   296→        // Extract namespace from attrId (format: "namespace/field")
   297→        let namespace = attrId.components(separatedBy: "/").first ?? "unknown"
   298→        if !modifiedEntities.contains(where: { $0.id == entityId }) {
   299→          modifiedEntities.append((namespace: namespace, id: entityId))
   300→        }
   301→
   302→      case "retract-triple":
   303→        // Format: ["retract-triple", entityId, attrId, value, ...]
   304→        guard step.count >= 4,
   305→              let entityId = step[1].value as? String,
   306→              let attrId = step[2].value as? String else {
   307→          continue
   308→        }
   309→        let rawValue = step[3].value
   310→        let value = convertToTripleValue(rawValue)
   311→
   312→        let triple = Triple(
   313→          entityId: entityId,
   314→          attributeId: attrId,
   315→          value: value,
   316→          createdAt: timestamp
   317→        )
   318→        let attr = store.attrsStore.getAttr(attrId)
   319→        let isRef = attr?.valueType == .ref
   320→        store.retractTriple(triple, isRef: isRef)
   321→
   322→        let namespace = attrId.components(separatedBy: "/").first ?? "unknown"
   323→        if !modifiedEntities.contains(where: { $0.id == entityId }) {
   324→          modifiedEntities.append((namespace: namespace, id: entityId))
   325→        }
   326→
   327→      case "delete-entity":
   328→        // Format: ["delete-entity", namespace, entityId]
   329→        guard step.count >= 3,
   330→              let namespace = step[1].value as? String,
   331→              let entityId = step[2].value as? String else {
   332→          continue
   333→        }
   334→        store.deleteEntity(id: entityId)
   335→        // Don't add to modifiedEntities since it's deleted
   336→
   337→      default:
   338→        // Skip add-attr, update-attr, etc. - they're handled by the server
   339→        break
   340→      }
   341→    }
   342→
   343→    reactorDebugLog("applyPendingMutationToStore: processed mutation", data: [
   344→      "eventId": mutation.eventId,
   345→      "stepCount": mutation.txSteps.count,
   346→      "modifiedEntities": modifiedEntities.map { "\($0.namespace):\($0.id)" }
   347→    ])
   348→
   349→    return modifiedEntities
   350→  }
   351→
   352→  /// Converts a raw value from tx-steps to a TripleValue.
   353→  private func convertToTripleValue(_ rawValue: Any) -> TripleValue {
   354→    switch rawValue {
   355→    case let s as String:
   356→      return .string(s)
   357→    case let i as Int:
   358→      return .double(Double(i))
   359→    case let i as Int64:
   360→      return .double(Double(i))
   361→    case let d as Double:
   362→      return .double(d)
   363→    case let b as Bool:
   364→      return .bool(b)
   365→    case is NSNull:
   366→      return .null
   367→    default:
   368→      // For complex types, try to represent as string
   369→      return .string(String(describing: rawValue))
   370→    }
   371→  }

   388→  private func waitForAttributes(
   389→    client: InstantClient,
   390→    timeoutSeconds: TimeInterval,
   391→    logContext: [String: Any]
   392→  ) async -> [Attribute] {
   393→    let deadline = Date().addingTimeInterval(timeoutSeconds)
   394→
   395→    while Date() < deadline {
   396→      let attrs = await MainActor.run { client.attributes }
   397→      if !attrs.isEmpty { return attrs }
   398→      try? await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: 50_000_000)
   399→    }
   400→
   401→    let attrs = await MainActor.run { client.attributes }
   402→    if attrs.isEmpty {
   403→      let contextDescription = logContext
   404→        .map { "\($0.key): \(String(describing: $0.value))" }
   405→        .sorted()
   406→        .joined(separator: ", ")
   407→
   408→      await MainActor.run {
   409→        InstantLogger.warning(
   410→          """
   411→          Reactor timed out waiting for schema attributes.
   412→
   413→          WHAT HAPPENED:
   414→            The client reported an authenticated WebSocket connection, but the schema
   415→            attributes were not available yet. Without attributes, we cannot normalize
   416→            InstaQL trees into triples reliably.
   417→
   418→          WHY THIS MATTERS:
   419→            Without schema, the triple store drops unknown fields, which can lead to
   420→            missing required fields when decoding entities from the store.
   421→
   422→          HOW TO FIX:
   423→            • Ensure the server's `init-ok` includes `attrs`.
   424→            • If this is a race, increase the wait window or refactor to await the
   425→              SDK's init processing before subscribing/transacting.
   426→
   427→          CONTEXT:
   428→            \(contextDescription)
   429→          """,
   430→          json: nil
   431→        )
   432→      }
   433→    }
   434→
   435→    return attrs
   436→  }

   438→  private func subscriptionFilter(whereClause: [String: Any]?) -> SubscriptionFilter {
   439→    guard let whereClause else { return .matchAll }
   440→    
   441→    if let id = whereClause["id"] as? String {
   442→      return .idEquals(id)
   443→    }
   444→    
   445→    if let dict = whereClause["id"] as? [String: Any],
   446→       let eq = dict["$eq"] as? String {
   447→      return .idEquals(eq)
   448→    }
   449→    
   450→    return .unsupported
   451→  }
   452→  
   453→  /// Notifies ALL active subscriptions to recompute their data from the store.
   454→  ///
   455→  /// ## Why This Exists (TypeScript Parity)
   456→  /// The TypeScript SDK's `notifyAll()` (Reactor.js lines 1303-1310) recomputes ALL
   457→  /// subscriptions after any mutation. This ensures:
   458→  /// - Cross-namespace consistency (e.g., a link mutation affects both sides)
   459→  /// - Correct filtering (subscriptions with complex WHERE clauses recompute)
   460→  /// - No missed updates (even if we can't predict which subscriptions are affected)
   461→  ///
   462→  /// ## Performance Note
   463→  /// This is intentionally aggressive. The TypeScript SDK does the same because
   464→  /// correctness trumps optimization. Each subscription reads from the normalized
   465→  /// store which is fast, and deduplication happens at the UI layer.
   466→  private func notifyAll() async {
   467→    for (_, handle) in activeSubscriptions {
   468→      // Trigger a recompute by calling upsert with a sentinel ID.
   469→      // The SubscriptionState will re-read from the store and yield new values.
   470→      await handle.upsert("__notifyAll__")
   471→    }
   472→  }
   473→
   474→  private func notifyOptimisticUpsert(namespace: String, id: String) async {
   475→    let matchingHandles = activeSubscriptions.values.filter { $0.namespace == namespace }
   476→    reactorDebugLog("notifyOptimisticUpsert", data: [
   477→      "namespace": namespace,
   478→      "id": id,
   479→      "totalSubscriptions": activeSubscriptions.count,
   480→      "matchingSubscriptions": matchingHandles.count,
   481→      "allNamespaces": activeSubscriptions.values.map { $0.namespace }
   482→    ])
   483→
   484→    for (_, handle) in activeSubscriptions where handle.namespace == namespace {
   485→      switch handle.filter {
   486→      case .matchAll:
   487→        reactorDebugLog("notifyOptimisticUpsert: calling upsert (matchAll)", data: [
   488→          "namespace": namespace,
   489→          "id": id
   490→        ])
   491→        await handle.upsert(id)
   492→      case .idEquals(let expectedId):
   493→        guard expectedId == id else { continue }
   494→        reactorDebugLog("notifyOptimisticUpsert: calling upsert (idEquals)", data: [
   495→          "namespace": namespace,
   496→          "id": id
   497→        ])
   498→        await handle.upsert(id)
   499→      case .unsupported:
   500→        continue
   501→      }
   502→    }
   503→  }
   504→
   505→  private func notifyOptimisticDelete(namespace: String, id: String) async {
   506→    for handle in activeSubscriptions.values where handle.namespace == namespace {
   507→      switch handle.filter {
   508→      case .matchAll:
   509→        await handle.delete(id)
   510→      case .idEquals(let expectedId):
   511→        guard expectedId == id else { continue }
   512→        await handle.delete(id)
   513→      case .unsupported:
   514→        continue
   515→      }
   516→    }
   517→  }
