   160→// MARK: - Explicit Mutation Methods for Shared Collections
   161→
   162→extension Shared {
   163→  
   164→  // MARK: - Create
   165→  
   166→  /// Create a new entity and sync to InstantDB.
   167→  ///
   168→  /// This method follows the TypeScript InstantDB SDK pattern:
   169→  /// 1. Sends transaction to Reactor which applies optimistic update
   170→  /// 2. Reactor notifies subscriptions to update @Shared value
   171→  /// 3. Server transaction is sent
   172→  ///
   173→  /// Unlike `withLock { $0.append(entity) }`, this does NOT compute diffs.
   174→  /// It sends exactly one transaction for the new entity.
   175→  ///
   176→  /// ## Example
   177→  ///
   178→  /// ```swift
   179→  /// @Shared(.instantSync(Schema.goals)) var goals: [Goal]
   180→  ///
   181→  /// let newGoal = Goal(id: UUID().uuidString, title: "Learn Swift")
   182→  /// try await $goals.create(newGoal)
   183→  /// ```
   184→  ///
   185→  /// - Parameter entity: The entity to create
   186→  /// - Throws: If the transaction fails
   187→  @MainActor
   188→  public func create<Element: EntityIdentifiable & Encodable & Sendable>(
   189→    _ entity: Element
   190→  ) async throws where Value: RangeReplaceableCollection, Value.Element == Element {
   191→    @Dependency(\.instantReactor) var reactor
   192→    @Dependency(\.instantAppID) var appID
   193→    
   194→    // Generate explicit transaction chunk
   195→    let namespace = Element.namespace
   196→    let attrs = try encodeEntityAttributes(entity)
   197→    
   198→    let chunk = TransactionChunk(
   199→      namespace: namespace,
   200→      id: entity.id,
   201→      ops: [["update", namespace, entity.id, attrs]]
   202→    )
   203→    
   204→    // Send to Reactor which handles optimistic update + server transaction
   205→    try await reactor.transact(appID: appID, chunks: [chunk])
   206→  }
   207→  
   208→  // MARK: - Delete
   209→  
   210→  /// Delete an entity by ID and sync to InstantDB.
   211→  ///
   212→  /// This method follows the TypeScript InstantDB SDK pattern:
   213→  /// 1. Sends transaction to Reactor which applies optimistic update
   214→  /// 2. Reactor notifies subscriptions to update @Shared value
   215→  /// 3. Server transaction is sent
   216→  ///
   217→  /// Unlike `withLock { $0.remove(id:) }`, this does NOT compute diffs.
   218→  /// It sends exactly one delete transaction.
   219→  ///
   220→  /// ## Example
   221→  ///
   222→  /// ```swift
   223→  /// @Shared(.instantSync(Schema.goals)) var goals: [Goal]
   224→  ///
   225→  /// try await $goals.delete(id: goal.id)
   226→  /// ```
   227→  ///
   228→  /// - Parameter id: The ID of the entity to delete
   229→  /// - Throws: If the transaction fails
   230→  @MainActor
   231→  public func delete<Element: EntityIdentifiable & Sendable>(
   232→    id: String
   233→  ) async throws where Value: RangeReplaceableCollection, Value.Element == Element {
   234→    @Dependency(\.instantReactor) var reactor
   235→    @Dependency(\.instantAppID) var appID
   236→    
   237→    // Generate explicit delete chunk
   238→    let namespace = Element.namespace
   239→    
   240→    let chunk = TransactionChunk(
   241→      namespace: namespace,
   242→      id: id,
   243→      ops: [["delete", namespace, id]]
   244→    )
   245→    
   246→    // Send to Reactor which handles optimistic update + server transaction
   247→    try await reactor.transact(appID: appID, chunks: [chunk])
   248→  }
   249→  
   250→  // MARK: - Update
   251→  
   252→  /// Update an entity's fields and sync to InstantDB.
   253→  ///
   254→  /// This method follows the TypeScript InstantDB SDK pattern:
   255→  /// 1. Reads current entity, applies modification
   256→  /// 2. Sends transaction to Reactor which applies optimistic update
   257→  /// 3. Reactor notifies subscriptions to update @Shared value
   258→  /// 4. Server transaction is sent
   259→  ///
   260→  /// **Important**: This method sends only the CHANGED fields, not the entire entity.
   261→  /// This prevents concurrent updates from clobbering each other (e.g., updating
   262→  /// `text` and `words` simultaneously on a transcription segment).
   263→  ///
   264→  /// ## Example
   265→  ///
   266→  /// ```swift
   267→  /// @Shared(.instantSync(Schema.goals)) var goals: [Goal]
   268→  ///
   269→  /// try await $goals.update(id: goal.id) { goal in
   270→  ///   goal.title = "Updated Title"
   271→  ///   goal.completed = true
   272→  /// }
   273→  /// ```
   274→  ///
   275→  /// - Parameters:
   276→  ///   - id: The ID of the entity to update
   277→  ///   - modify: A closure that modifies the entity
   278→  /// - Throws: If the entity is not found or the transaction fails
   279→  ///
   280→  /// ## Why We Read From TripleStore
   281→  /// See the IdentifiedArrayOf version for detailed explanation. In short:
   282→  /// we read from TripleStore to get optimistic updates that may not have
   283→  /// propagated to wrappedValue yet due to AsyncStream timing.
   284→  @MainActor
   285→  public func update<Element: EntityIdentifiable & Encodable & Sendable>(
   286→    id: String,
   287→    _ modify: (inout Element) -> Void
   288→  ) async throws where Value: RangeReplaceableCollection, Value.Element == Element {
   289→    @Dependency(\.instantReactor) var reactor
   290→    @Dependency(\.instantAppID) var appID
   291→
   292→    // Read from TripleStore directly to get optimistic updates that may not have
   293→    // propagated to wrappedValue yet. Fall back to wrappedValue for backward compat.
   294→    var entity: Element
   295→    if let storeEntity: Element = await reactor.getEntity(id: id) {
   296→      entity = storeEntity
   297→    } else if let wrappedEntity = wrappedValue.first(where: { $0.id == id }) {
   298→      entity = wrappedEntity
   299→    } else {
   300→      throw InstantMutationError.entityNotFound(id: id, namespace: Element.namespace)
   301→    }
   302→
   303→    // Encode BEFORE modification to compare
   304→    let beforeAttrs = try encodeEntityAttributes(entity)
   305→
   306→    // Apply modification locally
   307→    modify(&entity)
   308→
   309→    // Encode AFTER modification
   310→    let afterAttrs = try encodeEntityAttributes(entity)
   311→
   312→    // Compute only the changed fields (field-level update)
   313→    // This prevents concurrent updates from clobbering each other
   314→    let changedAttrs = computeChangedFields(before: beforeAttrs, after: afterAttrs)
   315→
   316→    guard !changedAttrs.isEmpty else {
   317→      // No actual changes - nothing to do
   318→      return
   319→    }
   320→
   321→    // Generate explicit update chunk with ONLY changed fields
   322→    let namespace = Element.namespace
   323→
   324→    let chunk = TransactionChunk(
   325→      namespace: namespace,
   326→      id: id,
   327→      ops: [["update", namespace, id, changedAttrs]]
   328→    )
   329→
   330→    // Send to Reactor which handles optimistic update + server transaction
   331→    try await reactor.transact(appID: appID, chunks: [chunk])
   332→  }
   333→  
   334→  // MARK: - Link
   335→  
   336→  /// Link an entity to another entity.
   337→  ///
   338→  /// This method sends an explicit "link" transaction to the server.
   339→  /// It does NOT modify local state (the link will be reflected when
   340→  /// the subscription receives the updated data).
   341→  ///
   342→  /// ## Example
   343→  ///
   344→  /// ```swift
   345→  /// @Shared(.instantSync(Schema.posts.with(\.author))) var posts: [Post]
   346→  ///
   347→  /// // Link a post to its author
   348→  /// try await $posts.link(post.id, "author", to: profile.id, namespace: "profiles")
   349→  /// ```
   350→  ///
   351→  /// - Parameters:
   352→  ///   - id: The ID of the entity to link from
   353→  ///   - label: The link label (e.g., "author", "creator")
   354→  ///   - targetId: The ID of the entity to link to
   355→  ///   - namespace: The namespace of the target entity
   356→  /// - Throws: If the transaction fails
   357→  @MainActor
   358→  public func link<Element: EntityIdentifiable & Sendable>(
   359→    _ id: String,
   360→    _ label: String,
   361→    to targetId: String,
   362→    namespace targetNamespace: String
   363→  ) async throws where Value: RangeReplaceableCollection, Value.Element == Element {
   364→    @Dependency(\.instantReactor) var reactor
   365→    @Dependency(\.instantAppID) var appID
   366→    
   367→    let namespace = Element.namespace
   368→    
   369→    let chunk = TransactionChunk(
   370→      namespace: namespace,
   371→      id: id,
   372→      ops: [["link", namespace, id, [label: ["id": targetId, "namespace": targetNamespace]] as [String: Any]]]
   373→    )
   374→    
   375→    try await reactor.transact(appID: appID, chunks: [chunk])
   376→  }
   377→  
   378→  /// Link an entity to another entity using the target entity directly.

   389→  /// ```
   390→  ///
   391→  /// - Parameters:

   394→  ///   - target: The entity to link to

   398→    _ id: String,

   401→  ) async throws where Value: RangeReplaceableCollection, Value.Element == Element {
   402→    try await link(id, label, to: target.id, namespace: Target.namespace)
   403→  }

   475→// MARK: - IdentifiedArray Support
   476→
   477→extension Shared {
   478→  
   479→  /// Create a new entity and sync to InstantDB (IdentifiedArray version).
   480→  ///
   481→  /// ## How This Works (TypeScript SDK Pattern)
   482→  ///
   483→  /// Following the TypeScript InstantDB SDK architecture:
   484→  /// 1. Generate a transaction chunk with the entity data
   485→  /// 2. Send to Reactor.transact() which:
   486→  ///    - Applies optimistic update to triple store
   487→  ///    - Notifies subscriptions via handleOptimisticUpsert()
   488→  ///    - Sends transaction to server
   489→  /// 3. The subscription's AsyncStream yields the new value
   490→  /// 4. InstantSyncKey.subscribe() updates the @Shared value
   491→  ///
   492→  /// We do NOT use withLock here because:
   493→  /// - withLock triggers save() which computes diffs
   494→  /// - Diff computation can race with other mutations and generate incorrect deletes
   495→  /// - The TypeScript SDK never uses diff-based saves for explicit mutations
   496→  @MainActor
   497→  public func create<Element: EntityIdentifiable & Encodable & Sendable>(
   498→    _ entity: Element
   499→  ) async throws where Value == IdentifiedArrayOf<Element> {
   500→    @Dependency(\.instantReactor) var reactor
   501→    @Dependency(\.instantAppID) var appID
   502→
   503→    // 1. Generate explicit transaction chunk
   504→    let namespace = Element.namespace
   505→    let attrs = try encodeEntityAttributes(entity)
   506→
   507→    let chunk = TransactionChunk(
   508→      namespace: namespace,
   509→      id: entity.id,
   510→      ops: [["update", namespace, entity.id, attrs]]
   511→    )
   512→
   513→    // 2. Send to Reactor which handles:
   514→    //    - Optimistic update to triple store
   515→    //    - Subscription notification (updates @Shared value)
   516→    //    - Server transaction
   517→    try await reactor.transact(appID: appID, chunks: [chunk])
   518→  }
   519→  
   520→  /// Delete an entity by ID and sync to InstantDB (IdentifiedArray version).
   521→  ///
   522→  /// Following TypeScript SDK pattern - no withLock to avoid triggering diff-based save.
   523→  @MainActor
   524→  public func delete<Element: EntityIdentifiable & Sendable>(
   525→    id: String
   526→  ) async throws where Value == IdentifiedArrayOf<Element> {
   527→    @Dependency(\.instantReactor) var reactor
   528→    @Dependency(\.instantAppID) var appID
   529→    
   530→    // Generate explicit delete chunk
   531→    let namespace = Element.namespace
   532→    
   533→    let chunk = TransactionChunk(
   534→      namespace: namespace,
   535→      id: id,
   536→      ops: [["delete", namespace, id]]
   537→    )
   538→    
   539→    // Send to Reactor which handles optimistic update + server transaction
   540→    try await reactor.transact(appID: appID, chunks: [chunk])
   541→  }
   542→  
   543→  /// Update an entity's fields and sync to InstantDB (IdentifiedArray version).
   544→  ///
   545→  /// Following TypeScript SDK pattern - we need to read the current entity to apply
   546→  /// the modification, but we don't use withLock to avoid triggering diff-based save.
   547→  ///
   548→  /// **Important**: This method sends only the CHANGED fields, not the entire entity.
   549→  /// This prevents concurrent updates from clobbering each other (e.g., updating
   550→  /// `text` and `words` simultaneously on a transcription segment).
   551→  ///
   552→  /// ## Why We Read From TripleStore
   553→  /// The `wrappedValue` is updated asynchronously via AsyncStream. When `create()`
   554→  /// and `update()` are called in rapid succession:
   555→  /// 1. `create()` applies optimistic update to TripleStore (synchronous)
   556→  /// 2. `create()` yields to AsyncStream (asynchronous delivery)
   557→  /// 3. `update()` reads `wrappedValue` → entity not found (stream not consumed yet)
   558→  ///
   559→  /// By reading from the TripleStore directly, we get the latest state including
   560→  /// optimistic updates that haven't yet flowed through to `wrappedValue`.
   561→  @MainActor
   562→  public func update<Element: EntityIdentifiable & Encodable & Sendable>(
   563→    id: String,
   564→    _ modify: (inout Element) -> Void
   565→  ) async throws where Value == IdentifiedArrayOf<Element> {
   566→    @Dependency(\.instantReactor) var reactor
   567→    @Dependency(\.instantAppID) var appID
   568→
   569→    // Read from TripleStore directly to get optimistic updates that may not have
   570→    // propagated to wrappedValue yet. Fall back to wrappedValue for backward compat.
   571→    var entity: Element
   572→    if let storeEntity: Element = await reactor.getEntity(id: id) {
   573→      entity = storeEntity
   574→    } else if let wrappedEntity = wrappedValue[id: id] {
   575→      entity = wrappedEntity
   576→    } else {
   577→      throw InstantMutationError.entityNotFound(id: id, namespace: Element.namespace)
   578→    }
   579→
   580→    // Encode BEFORE modification to compare
   581→    let beforeAttrs = try encodeEntityAttributes(entity)
   582→
   583→    // Apply modification locally
   584→    modify(&entity)
   585→
   586→    // Encode AFTER modification
   587→    let afterAttrs = try encodeEntityAttributes(entity)
   588→
   589→    // Compute only the changed fields (field-level update)
   590→    // This prevents concurrent updates from clobbering each other
   591→    let changedAttrs = computeChangedFields(before: beforeAttrs, after: afterAttrs)
   592→
   593→    guard !changedAttrs.isEmpty else {
   594→      // No actual changes - nothing to do
   595→      return
   596→    }
   597→
   598→    // Generate explicit update chunk with ONLY changed fields
   599→    let namespace = Element.namespace
   600→
   601→    let chunk = TransactionChunk(
   602→      namespace: namespace,
   603→      id: id,
   604→      ops: [["update", namespace, id, changedAttrs]]
   605→    )
   606→
   607→    // Send to Reactor which handles optimistic update + server transaction
   608→    try await reactor.transact(appID: appID, chunks: [chunk])
   609→  }
   610→
   611→  /// Update a single field of an entity without reading the full entity first.
   612→  ///
   613→  /// This is the safest method for concurrent updates because it:
   614→  /// 1. Does NOT read the current entity (avoids stale snapshots)
   615→  /// 2. Sends ONLY the specified field to the server
   616→  /// 3. Cannot clobber other fields being updated concurrently
   617→  ///
   618→  /// ## Example
   619→  ///
   620→  /// ```swift
   621→  /// // Update just the text field - safe even if words is being updated concurrently
   622→  /// try await $segments.updateField(id: segmentId, field: "text", value: "New text")
   623→  /// ```
   624→  ///
   625→  /// - Parameters:
   626→  ///   - id: The ID of the entity to update
   627→  ///   - field: The field name to update
   628→  ///   - value: The new value for the field
   629→  /// - Throws: If the transaction fails
   630→  @MainActor
   631→  public func updateField<Element: EntityIdentifiable & Sendable>(
   632→    id: String,
   633→    field: String,
   634→    value: Any
   635→  ) async throws where Value == IdentifiedArrayOf<Element> {
   636→    @Dependency(\.instantReactor) var reactor
   637→    @Dependency(\.instantAppID) var appID
   638→
   639→    let namespace = Element.namespace
   640→
   641→    let chunk = TransactionChunk(
   642→      namespace: namespace,
   643→      id: id,
   644→      ops: [["update", namespace, id, [field: value]]]
   645→    )
   646→
   647→    try await reactor.transact(appID: appID, chunks: [chunk])
   648→  }
   649→
   650→  /// Update multiple fields of an entity without reading the full entity first.
   651→  ///
   652→  /// This method sends ONLY the specified fields, preventing concurrent updates
   653→  /// from clobbering each other.
   654→  ///
   655→  /// ## Example
   656→  ///
   657→  /// ```swift
   658→  /// try await $segments.updateFields(id: segmentId, fields: [
   659→  ///   "text": "New text",
   660→  ///   "endTime": 1.5
   661→  /// ])
   662→  /// ```
   663→  @MainActor
   664→  public func updateFields<Element: EntityIdentifiable & Sendable>(
   665→    id: String,
   666→    fields: [String: Any]
   667→  ) async throws where Value == IdentifiedArrayOf<Element> {
   668→    @Dependency(\.instantReactor) var reactor
   669→    @Dependency(\.instantAppID) var appID
   670→
   671→    guard !fields.isEmpty else { return }
   672→
   673→    let namespace = Element.namespace
   674→
   675→    let chunk = TransactionChunk(
   676→      namespace: namespace,
   677→      id: id,
   678→      ops: [["update", namespace, id, fields]]
   679→    )
   680→
   681→    try await reactor.transact(appID: appID, chunks: [chunk])
   682→  }
   683→  
   684→  /// Link an entity to another entity (IdentifiedArray version).
   685→  @MainActor

   687→    _ id: String,

   689→    to targetId: String,
   690→    namespace targetNamespace: String

   701→    )

   748→
   749→// MARK: - Errors
   750→
   751→/// Errors that can occur during explicit mutations.
   752→public enum InstantMutationError: Error, LocalizedError {
   753→  case entityNotFound(id: String, namespace: String)
   754→  case encodingFailed(Error)
   755→  
   756→  public var errorDescription: String? {
   757→    switch self {
   758→    case .entityNotFound(let id, let namespace):
   759→      return "Entity not found: \(namespace)/\(id)"
   760→    case .encodingFailed(let error):
   761→      return "Failed to encode entity: \(error.localizedDescription)"
   762→    }
   763→  }
   764→}
   765→
   766→// MARK: - Helpers
   767→
   768→/// Compute only the fields that changed between two encoded attribute dictionaries.
   769→///
   770→/// This is critical for preventing concurrent update clobbering. When two updates
   771→/// run simultaneously:
   772→/// - Update A reads entity, modifies `text`, encodes all attrs including stale `words`
   773→/// - Update B reads entity, modifies `words`, encodes all attrs including stale `text`
   774→///
   775→/// Without field-level diffing, whichever update arrives at the server last
   776→/// clobbers the other's changes.
   777→///
   778→/// With field-level diffing:
   779→/// - Update A sends only `{text: "new text"}`
   780→/// - Update B sends only `{words: [...]}`
   781→/// - Both updates succeed without clobbering
   782→private func computeChangedFields(
   783→  before: [String: Any],
   784→  after: [String: Any]
   785→) -> [String: Any] {
   786→  var changed: [String: Any] = [:]
   787→
   788→  for (key, afterValue) in after {
   789→    if let beforeValue = before[key] {
   790→      // Field existed before - check if it changed
   791→      if !valuesAreEqual(beforeValue, afterValue) {
   792→        changed[key] = afterValue
   793→      }
   794→    } else {
   795→      // New field
   796→      changed[key] = afterValue
   797→    }
   798→  }
   799→
   800→  // Also check for removed fields (set to nil)
   801→  for key in before.keys {
   802→    if after[key] == nil {
   803→      changed[key] = NSNull()
   804→    }
   805→  }
   806→
   807→  return changed
   808→}
   809→
   810→/// Compare two values for equality.
   811→///
   812→/// This handles the various types that can appear in encoded entity attributes.
   813→private func valuesAreEqual(_ lhs: Any, _ rhs: Any) -> Bool {
   814→  // Handle NSNull
   815→  if lhs is NSNull && rhs is NSNull {
   816→    return true
   817→  }
   818→
   819→  // Handle primitives
   820→  if let l = lhs as? String, let r = rhs as? String {
   821→    return l == r
   822→  }
   823→  if let l = lhs as? Double, let r = rhs as? Double {
   824→    return l == r
   825→  }
   826→  if let l = lhs as? Int, let r = rhs as? Int {
   827→    return l == r
   828→  }
   829→  if let l = lhs as? Bool, let r = rhs as? Bool {
   830→    return l == r
   831→  }
   832→
   833→  // Handle arrays (JSON fields like `words`)
   834→  if let l = lhs as? [Any], let r = rhs as? [Any] {
   835→    guard l.count == r.count else { return false }
   836→    for (i, lVal) in l.enumerated() {
   837→      if !valuesAreEqual(lVal, r[i]) {
   838→        return false
   839→      }
   840→    }
   841→    return true
   842→  }
   843→
   844→  // Handle dictionaries (nested objects)
   845→  if let l = lhs as? [String: Any], let r = rhs as? [String: Any] {
   846→    guard l.count == r.count else { return false }
   847→    for (key, lVal) in l {
   848→      guard let rVal = r[key], valuesAreEqual(lVal, rVal) else {
   849→        return false
   850→      }
   851→    }
   852→    return true
   853→  }
   854→
   855→  // Different types = not equal
   856→  return false
   857→}
   858→
   859→/// Encode an entity's attributes to a dictionary for the transaction.
   860→///
   861→/// This extracts all properties except `id` and link properties (which are
   862→/// handled separately via link operations).
   863→///
   864→/// ## Why We Use a Custom Encoder
   865→///
   866→/// The naive approach of `JSONEncoder` + `JSONSerialization.jsonObject()` has a critical bug:
   867→/// `JSONSerialization` uses `NSNumber` for both numbers and booleans, and Swift's bridging
   868→/// can interpret `0`/`1` as `false`/`true`. This causes InstantDB server errors like:
   869→/// "Invalid value type for tiles.x. Value must be a number but the provided value type is boolean."
   870→///
   871→/// Instead, we use a custom `DictionaryEncoder` that preserves type information.
   872→private func encodeEntityAttributes<E: Encodable>(_ entity: E) throws -> [String: Any] {
   873→  let encoder = DictionaryEncoder()
   874→  let dict = try encoder.encode(entity)
   875→
   876→  // Filter out id (handled separately)
   877→  // Note: We NO LONGER filter out arrays/objects - they can be JSON fields!
   878→  // The TypeScript SDK sends JSON arrays (like `words: [{text, startTime, endTime}]`)
   879→  // as regular attributes, not as links.
   880→  var attrs: [String: Any] = [:]
   881→  for (key, value) in dict {
   882→    // Skip id - it's handled separately
   883→    if key == "id" { continue }
   884→
   885→    // Skip nil values
   886→    if case Optional<Any>.none = value { continue }
   887→    if value is NSNull { continue }
   888→
   889→    attrs[key] = value
   890→  }
   891→
   892→  return attrs
   893→}

   897→/// A custom encoder that encodes `Encodable` values directly to `[String: Any]` dictionaries.
   898→///

   900→/// - `Double` values stay as `Double` (not converted to `NSNumber` which might be interpreted as `Bool`)
   901→/// - `Bool` values stay as `Bool`
   902→/// - `Int` values stay as `Int`

   905→private class DictionaryEncoder {
   906→  func encode<T: Encodable>(_ value: T) throws -> [String: Any] {
   907→    let encoder = _DictionaryEncoder()

   910→      throw InstantMutationError.encodingFailed(
   911→        NSError(domain: "SharingInstant", code: -1, userInfo: [
   912→          NSLocalizedDescriptionKey: "Failed to encode entity to dictionary"
   913→        ])
   914→      )
   915→    }
   916→    return dict
   917→  }
   918→}

    15→// MARK: - InstantStorage
    16→
    17→/// A coordinator for InstantDB file storage with an ergonomic SwiftUI API.
    18→///
    19→/// `InstantStorage` is designed to feel like a TanStack Query `useMutation`:
    20→/// you can trigger storage actions imperatively while also observing a
    21→/// first-class status enum to drive loading/error UI.
    22→///
    23→/// ## Why This Exists
    24→/// InstantDB's JS clients expose `db.storage.*` helpers for upload/delete/linking.
    25→/// The Swift core SDK (`instant-ios-sdk`) provides those HTTP endpoints on
    26→/// `InstantClient.storage`, but callers would otherwise need to keep track of
    27→/// local UI state such as "upload in flight", "last error", and "last result".
    28→///
    29→/// This wrapper centralizes that state so app code stays small and consistent.
    30→///
    31→/// ## Permissions
    32→/// Storage operations are gated by InstantDB's permissions system via `$files`.
    33→/// If your app has no `$files` rules, the server denies access by default.
    34→///
    35→/// - SeeAlso: https://www.instantdb.com/docs/storage
    36→/// - SeeAlso: https://www.instantdb.com/docs/permissions
    37→@MainActor
    38→public final class InstantStorage: ObservableObject {
    39→
    40→  // MARK: - Operation State
    41→
    42→  /// State for an in-flight or completed storage operation.
    43→  ///
    44→  /// This is intentionally "mutation-shaped": it models a single operation at a time,
    45→  /// which matches how SwiftUI screens typically present upload/delete actions.
    46→  public enum OperationState<Success> {
    47→    case idle
    48→    case inFlight(startedAt: Date)
    49→    case success(Success, finishedAt: Date)
    50→    case failure(any Error, finishedAt: Date)
    51→
    52→    public var isInFlight: Bool {
    53→      if case .inFlight = self { return true }
    54→      return false
    55→    }
    56→
    57→    public var value: Success? {
    58→      if case .success(let value, _) = self { return value }
    59→      return nil
    60→    }
    61→
    62→    public var error: (any Error)? {
    63→      if case .failure(let error, _) = self { return error }
    64→      return nil
    65→    }
    66→  }
    67→

   123→
   124→  /// Creates a convenience wrapper for performing operations on a specific storage path.
   125→  ///
   126→  /// ## Example
   127→  ///
   128→  /// ```swift
   129→  /// let avatar = storage.file("\(user.id)/avatar.png")
   130→  /// try await avatar.upload(data: pngData, options: .init(contentType: "image/png"))
   131→  /// let url = try await avatar.link()
   132→  /// ```
   133→  public func file(_ path: String) -> FileHandle {
   134→    FileHandle(storage: self, path: path)

   160→    }

   173→  // MARK: - Upload
   174→
   175→  /// Uploads a file to InstantDB storage at `path`.
   176→  ///
   177→  /// ## Overwrite Semantics
   178→  /// Uploading to an existing path overwrites the previous contents (JS parity).
   179→  ///
   180→  /// - Parameters:
   181→  ///   - path: Storage path, e.g. `"photos/demo.png"`.
   182→  ///   - data: File data.
   183→  ///   - options: Metadata such as content type / disposition.
   184→  /// - Returns: The created/updated `$files` id plus the requested path.
   185→  @discardableResult
   186→  public func uploadFile(
   187→    path: String,
   188→    data: Data,
   189→    options: StorageAPI.UploadOptions = .init()
   190→  ) async throws -> UploadedFile {
   191→    uploadTask?.cancel()
   192→
   193→    let startedAt = Date()
   194→    uploadState = .inFlight(startedAt: startedAt)
   195→
   196→    let task = Task { @MainActor in
   197→      let client = InstantClientFactory.makeClient(appID: appID)
   198→
   199→      let id = try await client.storage.uploadFile(path: path, data: data, options: options)
   200→      return UploadedFile(id: id, path: path)
   201→    }
   202→    uploadTask = task
   203→
   204→    do {
   205→      let uploaded = try await task.value
   206→      uploadState = .success(uploaded, finishedAt: Date())
   207→      logger.info("Uploaded file (appID=\(self.appID), path=\(path), id=\(uploaded.id))")
   208→      return uploaded
   209→    } catch {
   210→      uploadState = .failure(error, finishedAt: Date())
   211→      logger.error("Upload failed (appID=\(self.appID), path=\(path)): \(error.localizedDescription)")
   212→      throw error
   213→    }
   214→  }
   215→
   216→  /// Uploads a file from disk to InstantDB storage at `path`.
   217→  ///
   218→  /// - Note: This reads the file into memory. For very large files, prefer streaming
   219→  /// uploads from trusted server-side tooling.
   220→  @discardableResult
   221→  public func uploadFile(
   222→    path: String,
   223→    fileURL: URL,
   224→    options: StorageAPI.UploadOptions = .init()
   225→  ) async throws -> UploadedFile {
   226→    let data = try Data(contentsOf: fileURL)
   227→    return try await uploadFile(path: path, data: data, options: options)
   228→  }

   230→  /// Callback-style upload for use from synchronous contexts (e.g. SwiftUI button actions).
   231→  @discardableResult
   232→  public func uploadFile(
   233→    path: String,
   234→    data: Data,
   235→    options: StorageAPI.UploadOptions = .init(),
   236→    completion: @escaping @MainActor (Result<UploadedFile, any Error>) -> Void
   237→  ) -> Task<UploadedFile, Error> {
   238→    let task = Task { @MainActor in
   239→      do {
   240→        let value = try await self.uploadFile(path: path, data: data, options: options)
   241→        completion(.success(value))
   242→        return value
   243→      } catch {
   244→        completion(.failure(error))
   245→        throw error
   246→      }
   247→    }
   248→
   249→    return task
   250→  }

   603→  public func transact(
   604→    appID: String,
   605→    chunks: [TransactionChunk]
   606→  ) async throws {
   607→    // #region agent log - H10: Trace transact timing
   608→    let transactStart = Date()
   609→    let chunkIds = chunks.map { $0.id }
   610→    reactorDebugLog("transact START", data: ["chunkIds": chunkIds])
   611→    // #endregion
   612→    
   613→    let client = await MainActor.run { InstantClientFactory.makeClient(appID: appID, instanceID: self.clientInstanceID) }
   614→    // #region agent log
   615→    reactorDebugLog("transact: got client", data: ["elapsed_ms": Date().timeIntervalSince(transactStart) * 1000])
   616→    // #endregion
   617→
   618→    // Ensure connected
   619→    let isDisconnected = await MainActor.run { client.connectionState == .disconnected }
   620→    if isDisconnected {
   621→      await MainActor.run { client.connect() }
   622→    }
   623→    // #region agent log
   624→    reactorDebugLog("transact: checked connection", data: ["elapsed_ms": Date().timeIntervalSince(transactStart) * 1000, "wasDisconnected": isDisconnected])
   625→    // #endregion
   626→
   627→    let initialAttrs = await MainActor.run { client.attributes }
   628→    if !initialAttrs.isEmpty {
   629→      store.updateAttributes(initialAttrs)
   630→    }
   631→    // #region agent log
   632→    reactorDebugLog("transact: got attrs", data: ["elapsed_ms": Date().timeIntervalSince(transactStart) * 1000, "attrCount": initialAttrs.count])
   633→    // #endregion
   634→
   635→    // Optimistic Update
   636→    // We apply the changes to the triple store immediately so callers can read their
   637→    // writes locally while the server transaction is in-flight.
   638→    await applyOptimisticUpdate(chunks: chunks)
   639→    // #region agent log
   640→    reactorDebugLog("transact: applied optimistic", data: ["elapsed_ms": Date().timeIntervalSince(transactStart) * 1000])
   641→    // #endregion
   642→
   643→    // Persist + enqueue mutations while offline, and flush automatically on reconnect.
   644→    _ = try await client.transactLocalFirst(chunks)
   645→    // #region agent log
   646→    reactorDebugLog("transact END", data: ["elapsed_ms": Date().timeIntervalSince(transactStart) * 1000, "chunkIds": chunkIds])
   647→    // #endregion
   648→  }

   650→  /// Explicitly sign in as a guest.
   651→  /// Useful for testing or anonymous usage.
   652→  public func signInAsGuest(appID: String) async throws {
   653→      let client = await MainActor.run { InstantClientFactory.makeClient(appID: appID, instanceID: self.clientInstanceID) }
   654→      
   655→      // Perform sign in on MainActor
   656→      // Perform sign in (AuthManager is @MainActor, so this hops automatically)
   657→      let authManager = await client.authManager
   658→      _ = try await authManager.signInAsGuest()
   659→      
   660→      // Loop until authenticated (or error)
   661→      var authenticated = false
   662→      let deadline = Date().addingTimeInterval(10)
   663→      while !authenticated && Date() < deadline {
   664→          let isAuthenticated = await MainActor.run { client.connectionState == .authenticated }
   665→          if isAuthenticated {
   666→              authenticated = true
   667→          } else {
   668→             let isError = await MainActor.run { 
   669→                 if case .error = client.connectionState { return true }
   670→                 return false
   671→             }
   672→             if isError {
   673→                  throw InstantError.connectionFailed(NSError(domain: "Reactor", code: -1, userInfo: [NSLocalizedDescriptionKey: "Connection failed"]))
   674→             }
   675→          }
   676→          if !authenticated { try? await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: 100_000_000) }
   677→      }
   678→      guard authenticated else { throw InstantError.notAuthenticated }
   679→  }

   681→  private func applyOptimisticUpdate(chunks: [TransactionChunk]) async {
   682→    let timestamp = ConflictResolution.optimisticTimestamp()
   683→
   684→    // Track affected entities for targeted notifications
   685→    var affectedNamespaces: Set<String> = []
   686→    var upsertedIds: [(namespace: String, id: String)] = []
   687→    var deletedIds: [(namespace: String, id: String)] = []
   688→
   689→    for chunk in chunks {
   690→      for op in chunk.ops {
   691→        guard let action = op.first as? String else { continue }
   692→
   693→        let namespace = (op.count > 1 ? op[1] as? String : nil) ?? chunk.namespace
   694→        let id = (op.count > 2 ? op[2] as? String : nil) ?? chunk.id
   695→        affectedNamespaces.insert(namespace)
   696→
   697→        switch action {
   698→        case "create", "update":
   699→          guard op.count > 3, let payload = op[3] as? [String: Any] else { continue }
   700→          var entity = payload
   701→          entity["id"] = id
   702→
   703→          let triples = Normalization.normalize(
   704→            data: entity,
   705→            namespace: namespace,
   706→            attrsStore: store.attrsStore,
   707→            createdAt: timestamp
   708→          )
   709→          store.addTriples(triples)
   710→          upsertedIds.append((namespace: namespace, id: id))
   711→
   712→        case "link":
   713→          guard op.count > 3, let payload = op[3] as? [String: Any] else { continue }
   714→          var entity: [String: Any] = ["id": id]
   715→          for (key, value) in payload {
   716→            entity[key] = value
   717→          }
   718→
   719→          let triples = Normalization.normalize(
   720→            data: entity,
   721→            namespace: namespace,
   722→            attrsStore: store.attrsStore,
   723→            createdAt: timestamp
   724→          )
   725→          store.addTriples(triples)
   726→          upsertedIds.append((namespace: namespace, id: id))
   727→
   728→        case "unlink":
   729→          guard op.count > 3, let payload = op[3] as? [String: Any] else { continue }
   730→          applyOptimisticUnlink(
   731→            namespace: namespace,
   732→            entityId: id,
   733→            payload: payload,
   734→            timestamp: timestamp
   735→          )
   736→          upsertedIds.append((namespace: namespace, id: id))
   737→
   738→        case "delete":
   739→          store.deleteEntity(id: id)
   740→          deletedIds.append((namespace: namespace, id: id))
   741→
   742→        default:
   743→          continue
   744→        }
   745→      }
   746→    }
   747→
   748→    // Notify subscriptions of the specific changes
   749→    // This ensures currentIDs gets updated with the new entity IDs
   750→    for (namespace, id) in upsertedIds {
   751→      await notifyOptimisticUpsert(namespace: namespace, id: id)
   752→    }
   753→    for (namespace, id) in deletedIds {
   754→      await notifyOptimisticDelete(namespace: namespace, id: id)
   755→    }
   756→
   757→    // Also notify all subscriptions to ensure cross-namespace consistency
   758→    // (e.g., a link mutation affects both sides of the relationship)
   759→    // See Reactor.js pushOps() line 1367: this.notifyAll()
   760→    await notifyAll()
   761→  }
   762→
   763→  private func applyOptimisticUnlink(
   764→    namespace: String,
   765→    entityId: String,
   766→    payload: [String: Any],
   767→    timestamp: Int64
   768→  ) {
   769→    for (label, rawValue) in payload {
   770→      if let attr = store.attrsStore.getAttrByForwardIdent(entityType: namespace, label: label) {
   771→        guard attr.valueType == .ref else { continue }
   772→
   773→        for targetId in referencedEntityIDs(from: rawValue) {
   774→          let triple = Triple(entityId: entityId, attributeId: attr.id, value: .ref(targetId), createdAt: timestamp)
   775→          store.retractTriple(triple, isRef: true)
   776→        }
   777→        continue
   778→      }
   779→
   780→      if let attr = store.attrsStore.getAttrByReverseIdent(entityType: namespace, label: label) {
   781→        guard attr.valueType == .ref else { continue }
   782→
   783→        for sourceId in referencedEntityIDs(from: rawValue) {
   784→          let triple = Triple(entityId: sourceId, attributeId: attr.id, value: .ref(entityId), createdAt: timestamp)
   785→          store.retractTriple(triple, isRef: true)

Perfect! Now I have all the information I need. Let me provide a comprehensive analysis of the differences between the TypeScript and Swift query-driven approaches.

## Analysis: TypeScript Query-Driven vs Swift's resolve() Implementation

I've analyzed both implementations. Here's what I found:

### TypeScript Reactor.js - Query-Driven Approach

**Key function: `dataForQuery()` (lines 1269-1317)**

```javascript
dataForQuery(hash, applyOptimistic = true) {
  // ... validation ...
  
  let store = result.store;
  let attrsStore = result.attrsStore;
  const { pageInfo, aggregate, processedTxId } = result;
  
  // Runs the QUERY against the store
  const resp = instaql(
    { store: store, attrsStore: attrsStore, pageInfo, aggregate },
    q,  // <-- THE QUERY OBJECT
  );
  
  return { data: resp, querySubVersion, pendingMutationsVersion };
}
```

**How it works:**

In `instaql.ts`, the query determines what gets resolved:

1. **`extendObjects()` (lines 527-577)** - Only traverses links that exist in the query form:
```typescript
function extendObjects(...) {
  const childQueries = Object.keys(form).filter((c) => c !== '$');
  if (!childQueries.length) {
    return Object.values(objects);  // No child queries = no links resolved
  }
  return Object.entries(objects).map(function extendChildren([eid, parent]) {
    const childResults = childQueries.map(function getChildResult(label) {
      // Only resolves labels that are KEYS in the query form
      // ...
    });
  });
}
```

2. **The query itself defines scope:**
```javascript
// Query like this:
{
  users: { 
    $: { where: { ... } },
    posts: {},      // <-- This key triggers resolution of "posts" link
    // comments NOT included = NOT resolved
  }
}
```

**Result:** Only `posts` links are resolved. Any links not explicitly named in the query are ignored entirely.

---

### Swift TripleStore+Extensions.swift - Issue: Resolves ALL Links When includedLinks is nil

**Key function: `resolve()` (lines 19-172)**

```swift
public func resolve(
    id: String,
    attrsStore: AttrsStore,
    depth: Int = 0,
    maxDepth: Int = 10,
    includedLinks: Set<String>? = nil  // <-- THE PROBLEM
) -> [String: Any] {
    // ...
    for (attrId, attrTriples) in triplesByAttr {
        guard let attr = attrsStore.getAttr(attrId) else { continue }
        
        if attr.valueType == .ref {
            // Skip links not in includedLinks (if specified)
            // THIS ONLY WORKS IF includedLinks IS NOT NIL
            if let includedLinks = includedLinks, !includedLinks.contains(label) {
                continue  // <-- ONLY SKIPS IF includedLinks WAS PROVIDED
            }
            
            // If includedLinks is nil, ALL links are resolved!
            // ...
        }
    }
}
```

**Problem:** When `includedLinks = nil`:
- The guard passes through
- ALL ref attributes are resolved recursively
- Matches neither TypeScript's query-driven approach nor the stated design goal

**Example mismatch:**
```swift
// TypeScript query (resolves ONLY users AND posts):
{
  users: { posts: {} }
}

// Swift call (resolves users + ALL their links):
store.resolve(id: userId, attrsStore: attrs, includedLinks: nil)
// Returns: users with posts, comments, media, followers, following, ...
```

---

### The Design Choice Analysis

**TypeScript's Query-Driven Approach (Better):**
- Scope is defined by the query shape
- N+1 queries aren't possible - you only fetch what you ask for
- Memory efficient - no unintended hydration
- Predictable: same query always returns same data structure
- Cache-friendly: query hash determines what's cached

**Swift's All-Links Behavior (Current Issue):**
- `includedLinks = nil` means "resolve everything"
- Violates the stated design goal (see line 15-17 in Swift):
  ```swift
  /// If nil, all links are resolved.
  ///                    If empty set, no links are resolved. This matches the TypeScript SDK's
  ///                    query-driven link resolution behavior.
  ```
- Causes performance problems with large nested graphs
- Can OOM with circular references (though maxDepth helps)

---

### Why This Difference Exists

**Platform Limitation:** Swift lacks the query-as-data capability that JavaScript has:
- TypeScript uses query object structure to determine traversal
- Swift can't introspect the caller's `.with()` chain at resolution time
- The Swift SDK would need to pass query information down to `resolve()`

**Current Workaround:** The code has a comment acknowledging this (lines 15-17):
```swift
/// If nil, all links are resolved.
/// If empty set, no links are resolved. This matches the TypeScript SDK's
/// query-driven link resolution behavior.
```

But this is **aspirational**, not accurate. The actual behavior is:
- `nil` = resolve ALL links (doesn't match TypeScript)
- `Set<String>()` = resolve zero links (matches TypeScript)

---

### Recommended Fix

The Swift SDK should:

1. **Make `includedLinks` required** (no nil default):
```swift
public func resolve(
    id: String,
    attrsStore: AttrsStore,
    includedLinks: Set<String>  // No default nil
) -> [String: Any]
```

2. **Pass query structure from higher-level API** (similar to TypeScript):
```swift
// In the reactive query subscription:
let includedLinks = extractLinksFromQuery(queryForm)
let resolved = store.resolve(id: eid, attrsStore: attrs, includedLinks: includedLinks)
```

3. **Update documentation** to clarify the behavior matches TypeScript only when `includedLinks` is explicitly provided.

This would achieve true query-driven resolution matching the TypeScript implementation.

## Pending Mutation Persistence: TypeScript vs Swift

Based on my analysis of the codebases, here's how TypeScript and Swift handle pending mutation persistence:

### 1. **WHEN ARE MUTATIONS SAVED TO DISK?**

#### TypeScript (PersistedObject + Reactor.js)

**Timing: Asynchronous, throttled fire-and-forget**

```typescript
// Reactor.js, line 1359-1361
_updatePendingMutations((prev) => {
  prev.set(eventId, mutation);
});
```

- When `_updatePendingMutations()` is called, it updates the in-memory `Map` via `updateInPlace()`
- This triggers `PersistedObject.updateInPlace()` (PersistedObject.ts:517-538)
- The persistence is **throttled** (default 100ms):
  ```typescript
  // PersistedObject.ts:501-506
  this._nextSave = setTimeout(() => {
    safeIdleCallback(() => {
      this._nextSave = null;
      this._writeToStorage(opts).then(resolve).catch(reject);
    }, this._idleCallbackMaxWaitMs);  // 100ms idle callback max wait
  }, this._saveThrottleMs);  // 100ms throttle
  ```

- Uses `requestIdleCallback` if available, falls back to synchronous callback
- **Fire-and-forget**: Returns immediately, doesn't wait for persistence to complete
- Serializes `Map` to array of entries for storage: `[...x.entries()]` (line 174)

#### Swift (InstantDB SDK + Reactor)

**Timing: Synchronous, embedded in transaction flow**

```swift
// SharedMutations.swift, lines 193-206
try await reactor.transact(appID: appID, chunks: [chunk])
```

- Calls `reactor.transact()` which immediately calls:
  ```swift
  // Reactor.swift:644
  _ = try await client.transactLocalFirst(chunks)
  ```

- `transactLocalFirst()` is implemented in InstantDB SDK and:
  1. **Immediately persists to SQLite** (synchronous)
  2. Enqueues for server transmission
  3. Returns after both operations complete

- **NOT fire-and-forget**: The `await` blocks until persistence is confirmed
- Mutations stored in SQLite `pending_mutations` table with full transaction data

### 2. **WHEN ARE MUTATIONS LOADED FROM DISK?**

#### TypeScript

**Timing: App startup, lazy loaded on first access**

```typescript
// Reactor.js, lines 450-452
this.kv.waitForKeyToLoad('pendingMutations');
this.kv.waitForKeyToLoad(currentUserKey);
this._beforeUnloadCbs.push(() => {
  this.kv.flush();
  this.querySubs.flush();
});
```

- Initiates load at startup via `waitForKeyToLoad()` but doesn't block
- `PersistedObject._loadKey()` loads asynchronously in background (line 221-236)
- On `transact-ok` message from server, mutations are rewritten/cleaned up (line 730-737):
  ```typescript
  this._updatePendingMutations((prev) => {
    prev.set(eventId, {
      ...prev.get(eventId),
      'tx-id': txId,
      confirmed: Date.now(),
    });
  });
  ```

#### Swift

**Timing: App startup, explicitly restored before first subscription**

```swift
// Reactor.swift, lines 191-254
private func restorePendingMutationsIfNeeded(client: InstantClient, appID: String) async {
  guard !hasRestoredPendingMutations else {
    reactorDebugLog("restorePendingMutations: SKIPPED - already restored")
    return
  }
  hasRestoredPendingMutations = true

  let pending = await client.getUnconfirmedPendingMutations()
  // ... apply each mutation to TripleStore
  for mutation in pending {
    let entityIds = applyPendingMutationToStore(mutation)
    restoredEntityIds.append(contentsOf: entityIds)
  }
}
```

- Loads from SQLite via `client.getUnconfirmedPendingMutations()`
- Applied to in-memory TripleStore **synchronously** via `applyPendingMutationToStore()` (lines 262-349)
- Only happens **once per app launch** (tracked by `hasRestoredPendingMutations` flag)
- Called when subscriptions are created (before first data delivery)

### 3. **WHAT HAPPENS IF APP CLOSES BEFORE SERVER ACK?**

#### TypeScript

**Strategy: Automatic recovery on reconnect**

```typescript
// Reactor.js, lines 1445-1453 (_flushPendingMessages)
const muts = this._rewriteMutationsSorted(
  this.ensureAttrs(),
  this._pendingMutations(),
);
muts.forEach(([eventId, mut]) => {
  if (!mut['tx-id']) {
    this._sendMutation(eventId, mut);
  }
});
```

**Lifecycle:**
1. Mutation persisted to IndexedDB while in-flight
2. App closes → pendingMutations preserved in storage
3. App reopens → pendingMutations loaded from storage
4. On reconnect → `_flushPendingMessages()` resends mutations without `tx-id`
5. Server responds with `transact-ok` → mutation marked with `tx-id` and `confirmed` timestamp
6. Cleanup after 30 seconds per query update (line 1483-1500):
   ```typescript
   if (
     mut.confirmed &&
     mut.confirmed + this._pendingTxCleanupTimeout < now
   ) {
     prev.delete(eventId);
   }
   ```

**Key insight:** Mutations are cleaned up based on **server confirmation**, not just receipt

#### Swift

**Strategy: Persistent retry queue in SQLite**

```swift
// Reactor.swift, lines 203-254
let pending = await client.getUnconfirmedPendingMutations()
// Apply to store
for mutation in pending {
  let entityIds = applyPendingMutationToStore(mutation)
}
```

**Lifecycle:**
1. Mutation persisted to SQLite via `transactLocalFirst()`
2. App closes → mutations remain in SQLite
3. App reopens → `restorePendingMutationsIfNeeded()` loads mutations
4. Mutations reapplied to TripleStore **immediately** (synchronous)
5. Server processes mutations and sends confirmation
6. SDK removes from SQLite upon server confirmation

**Key difference:** Swift applies mutations immediately on reload (restores optimistic state), TypeScript loads but applies on next notification.

### 4. **PERSISTENCE COMPARISON SUMMARY**

| Aspect | TypeScript | Swift |
|--------|-----------|-------|
| **Save Timing** | Async, throttled (100ms) | Sync, immediate |
| **Save Blocking** | No (fire-and-forget) | Yes (await completes) |
| **Storage** | IndexedDB | SQLite |
| **Load Timing** | App startup (lazy) | App startup (explicit) |
| **Load Blocking** | No (background) | Yes (before subscriptions) |
| **Restoration** | On-demand (during notification flow) | Explicit phase (`restorePendingMutationsIfNeeded`) |
| **Mutation Lifecycle** | Map in memory, periodic flush | SQLite table, explicit query |
| **Cleanup Trigger** | Server confirmation + timeout | Server confirmation only |

### 5. **KEY ARCHITECTURAL DIFFERENCE**

**TypeScript:**
- Loose coupling: Mutations persisted independently of queries
- Optimistic updates applied via `_applyOptimisticUpdates()` **on every query computation** (Reactor.js:1263)
- "Load when needed" approach to persistence

**Swift:**
- Tight coupling: Mutations bound to subscription lifecycle
- Optimistic updates restored **once at app startup**, then live in TripleStore
- "Load once and keep warm" approach - keeps all restored mutations alive in memory

**Critical insight from Swift code (Reactor.swift:186-188):**
```swift
/// This matches the TypeScript SDK behavior where `pendingMutations` are merged
/// into query results via `_applyOptimisticUpdates()`.
```

Swift is **explicitly designed to match TypeScript's behavior**, but implements it differently due to language/platform constraints (no IndexedDB equivalent, must use SQLite).

## TypeScript Garbage Collection in PersistedObject.ts - Complete Investigation

Based on my analysis of the codebase, here are the answers to your three questions:

### 1. DEFAULT VALUES FOR GC CONFIGURATION

The exact default values are defined in **Reactor.js (lines 433-437)** for the `querySubs` PersistedObject:

```typescript
gc: {
  maxAgeMs: 1000 * 60 * 60 * 24 * 7 * 52,  // 1 year (31,536,000,000 ms)
  maxEntries: 1000,
  maxSize: 1_000_000,                       // 1 million triples
}
```

**For the `kv` store**, GC is **completely disabled** (line 451):
```typescript
gc: null,  // Don't GC the kv store
```

**Key type definitions** (PersistedObject.ts, lines 48-52):
```typescript
export type GCOpts = {
  maxSize: number;        // Measured in application-specific units (triples for queries)
  maxAgeMs: number;       // Milliseconds since last update
  maxEntries: number;     // Maximum number of entries to keep
};
```

---

### 2. ORPHANED KEYS: "GC IN STORAGE BUT NOT IN META"

**What causes orphaned keys:**

Orphaned keys are entries that physically exist in storage but are **NOT tracked in the metadata (`__meta`)** object. These occur when:

**A. Crash During Save** (Most Common)
- A key is written to storage via `removeItem()` or `multiSet()` 
- The process crashes/disconnects before the `__meta` object is updated
- Result: Key exists in storage, but `meta.objects` doesn't have it registered

**B. Metadata Synchronization Failure**
- A GC operation deletes keys from storage but fails before persisting updated metadata
- Multiple tabs are active and one crashes after deleting but before flushing meta

**C. Manual Storage Corruption**
- IndexedDB gets corrupted or manually edited
- Keys are added to storage without corresponding meta entries

**Where orphan detection occurs** (PersistedObject.ts, lines 388-397):

```typescript
// First, remove all keys we don't know about
for (const key of keys) {
  if (sacredKeys.has(key) || key in meta.objects) {
    continue;
  }
  this._log.info('Lost track of key in meta', key);  // ORPHAN DETECTED
  promises.push(this._persister.removeItem(key));
  deets.removed.push(key);
  deets.removedMissingCount++;  // Increments when orphans found
}
```

**Recovery mechanism:**
- When `_gc()` runs, it fetches ALL keys from storage via `getAllKeys()`
- It compares against `meta.objects` and `sacredKeys`
- Any key in storage but not in meta is deleted immediately
- This maintains consistency across tabs via meta refresh (line 368)

---

### 3. THE "SACRED" TERMINOLOGY - EVICTION PREVENTION

**"Sacred" keys are entities that MUST NOT be garbage collected:**

Sacred keys are determined by combining three sets (PersistedObject.ts, lines 358-364):

```typescript
// Keys we can't delete
const sacredKeys = new Set(Object.keys(this.currentValue));  // Currently loaded values
for (const k of Object.keys(this._loadingKeys)) {
  sacredKeys.add(k);  // Keys actively being loaded
}
for (const k of this._loadedKeys) {
  sacredKeys.add(k);  // Keys that were loaded into memory
}
```

**Sacred keys include:**
1. **`this.currentValue[key]`** - Any entry currently in memory and being accessed
2. **`this._loadingKeys[key]`** - Any entry in the process of being fetched from storage
3. **`this._loadedKeys`** - Any entry that was loaded but not yet evicted

**How Sacred Status Prevents Eviction:**

Every eviction check verifies sacred status before deletion:

```typescript
// Age-based eviction (line 403):
if (!sacredKeys.has(k) && (m as ObjectMeta).updatedAt < now - this._gcOpts.maxAgeMs) {
  // Delete only if NOT sacred
}

// Entry count eviction (line 419):
const deletableMaxEntries = maxEntries.filter(([x]) => !sacredKeys.has(x));

// Size-based eviction (line 437):
const deletableDelEntries = delEntries.filter(([x]) => !sacredKeys.has(x));
```

**Why This Matters:**
- Prevents premature eviction of actively-used queries
- Protects keys that are being loaded (race condition safety)
- Ensures cross-tab consistency (via multi-tab safe refresh at line 368)

---

### GC EXECUTION FLOW

The garbage collection is scheduled with exponential backoff to reduce contention:

```typescript
// Schedules a GC to run in one minute (unless it is already scheduled)
gc() {
  if (this._nextGc) {
    return;  // Don't reschedule if already pending
  }
  this._nextGc = setTimeout(
    () => {
      safeIdleCallback(() => {
        this._nextGc = null;
        this._gc();  // Run GC during idle time
      }, 30 * 1000);  // Max wait 30 seconds
    },
    1000 * 60 + Math.random() * 500,  // 1 minute + jitter (prevents multi-tab race)
  );
}
```

The jitter (randomized 0-500ms) prevents multiple browser tabs from running GC simultaneously.

---

### REAL-WORLD EXAMPLE FROM TESTS

The test at line 219 in PersistedObject.test.ts demonstrates orphan cleanup:

After storing keys `{a, b, c, d, e}` and then unloading `e`, a page reload triggers GC which removes the oldest entries beyond the `maxEntries: 3` limit. The orphan detection fires if any keys existed in storage but weren't in the reloaded meta.

---

**Summary Table:**

| Aspect | Value/Detail |
|--------|--------------|
| **maxAgeMs default** | 1 year (31,536,000,000 ms) |
| **maxEntries default** | 1,000 |
| **maxSize default** | 1,000,000 triples |
| **Orphan cause** | Storage key exists, not in `meta.objects` |
| **Orphan detection** | During `_gc()` via `getAllKeys()` comparison |
| **Sacred keys** | Items in `currentValue`, `_loadingKeys`, `_loadedKeys` |
| **GC schedule** | ~1 minute with 0-500ms jitter, runs on idle |
| **kv store GC** | Disabled (gc: null) |

   195→// MARK: - Main Demo View

   197→struct RapidTranscriptionDemo: SwiftUICaseStudy {
   198→  let readMe = """
   199→    This demo simulates rapid real-time speech transcription updates to verify \
   200→    that SharingInstant handles high-frequency mutations correctly.
   201→
   202→    Real speech transcription emits updates at irregular intervals:
   203→    • Multiple updates within milliseconds (7-8ms apart)
   204→    • Longer gaps between words (800-1000ms)
   205→    • Final segment with word-level timing data
   206→
   207→    The demo creates multiple segments with rapid text updates, then finalizes \
   208→    them with word timing data. This tests concurrent field updates (text vs words) \
   209→    and verifies optimistic updates work correctly under load.
   210→    """
   211→  let caseStudyTitle = "Rapid Transcription"
   212→
   213→  @Shared(.instantSync(Schema.transcriptionSegments))
   214→  private var segments: IdentifiedArrayOf<TranscriptionSegment> = []
   215→
   216→  @Shared(.instantSync(Schema.transcriptionRuns))
   217→  private var runs: IdentifiedArrayOf<TranscriptionRun> = []
   218→
   219→  @Shared(.instantSync(Schema.media))
   220→  private var mediaItems: IdentifiedArrayOf<Media> = []
   221→
   222→  @State private var logs: [String] = []
   223→  @State private var isRunning = false
   224→  @State private var testResult: String?
   225→  @State private var testIds: TestIds?
   226→
   227→  struct TestIds {
   228→    let mediaId: String
   229→    let runId: String
   230→    let segmentIds: [String]
   231→  }
   232→
   233→  /// Filter segments to only show those created by this test
   234→  private var testSegments: [TranscriptionSegment] {
   235→    guard let ids = testIds else { return [] }
   236→    return segments.filter { ids.segmentIds.contains($0.id) }
   237→      .sorted { $0.segmentIndex < $1.segmentIndex }
   238→  }
   239→
   240→  var body: some View {
   241→    VStack(spacing: 0) {
   242→      if let result = testResult {
   243→        Text(result)
   244→          .font(.headline)
   245→          .foregroundColor(result.contains("SUCCESS") ? .green : .red)
   246→          .padding(.vertical, 8)
   247→          .accessibilityIdentifier("rapid_test_result")
   248→      }
   249→
   250→      HStack {
   251→        Button("Run Test") {
   252→          Task {
   253→            await runTest()
   254→          }
   255→        }
   256→        .disabled(isRunning)
   257→        .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)
   258→        .accessibilityIdentifier("rapid_run_test_button")
   259→
   260→        if testIds != nil {
   261→          Button("Cleanup") {
   262→            Task {
   263→              await cleanup()
   264→            }
   265→          }
   266→          .disabled(isRunning)
   267→          .buttonStyle(.bordered)
   268→          .accessibilityIdentifier("rapid_cleanup_button")
   269→        }
   270→      }
   271→      .padding(.vertical, 8)
   272→
   273→      // MARK: - Live Segments Display
   274→      if !testSegments.isEmpty {
   275→        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 8) {
   276→          Text("Live Segments & Words")
   277→            .font(.headline)
   278→            .padding(.horizontal)
   279→
   280→          ScrollView(.horizontal, showsIndicators: false) {
   281→            HStack(alignment: .top, spacing: 12) {
   282→              ForEach(testSegments) { segment in
   283→                SegmentCardView(segment: segment)
   284→              }
   285→            }
   286→            .padding(.horizontal)
   287→          }
   288→          .frame(maxHeight: 200)
   289→        }
   290→        .padding(.vertical, 8)
   291→        .background(Color.gray.opacity(0.1))
   292→      }
   293→
   294→      Divider()
   295→
   296→      // MARK: - Logs
   297→      ScrollViewReader { proxy in
   298→        ScrollView {
   299→          LazyVStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 4) {
   300→            ForEach(Array(logs.enumerated()), id: \.offset) { index, log in
   301→              Text(log)
   302→                .font(.system(.caption, design: .monospaced))
   303→                .id(index)
   304→            }
   305→          }
   306→          .padding()
   307→        }
   308→        .onChange(of: logs.count) { _, _ in
   309→          if let lastIndex = logs.indices.last {
   310→            proxy.scrollTo(lastIndex, anchor: .bottom)
   311→          }
   312→        }
   313→      }
   314→    }
   315→    .navigationTitle("Rapid Transcription")
   316→  }
   317→
   318→  private func log(_ message: String) {
   319→    let timestamp = Date()
   320→    let formatter = DateFormatter()
   321→    formatter.dateFormat = "HH:mm:ss.SSS"
   322→    let timeStr = formatter.string(from: timestamp)

     1→# SharingInstant Memory & Performance Fixes - Implementation Plan
     2→
     3→## Executive Summary
     4→
     5→This plan addresses **CRITICAL** and **HIGH** priority memory issues in the SharingInstant Swift SDK identified through comprehensive analysis of:
     6→- TypeScript Reactor.js cleanup mechanisms
     7→- TypeScript Store/PersistedObject GC patterns
     8→- Swift Reactor current implementation gaps
     9→- Git history of related fixes
    10→
    11→**Priority Fixes:**
    12→1. Cycle detection in entity resolution (CRITICAL)
    13→2. TripleStore garbage collection (CRITICAL)
    14→3. Pending mutation cleanup (HIGH)
    15→4. Query result caching with version tracking (HIGH)
    16→5. Pending mutation caching in Reactor (HIGH)
    17→
    18→---
    19→
    20→## Priority 1: Cycle Detection in Entity Resolution
    21→
    22→### Problem
    23→
    24→**File:** `Sources/SharingInstant/Extensions/TripleStore+Extensions.swift` (Lines 19-172)
    25→
    26→Current `resolve()` uses depth limiting but NO cycle detection:
    27→
    28→```swift
    29→public func resolve(id: String, attrsStore: AttrsStore, depth: Int = 0, maxDepth: Int = 10, includedLinks: Set<String>? = nil) -> [String: Any] {
    30→    if depth > maxDepth { return ["id": id] }  // Only protection
    31→    // ...recursive calls without tracking visited entities
    32→}
    33→```
    34→
    35→**Impact:** If Entity A links to B links to A, both are resolved 5 complete cycles before stopping, causing exponential memory growth.
    36→
    37→### TypeScript Reference
    38→
    39→TypeScript's InstaQL (`instaql.ts`) doesn't explicitly track visited entities, but its query-driven approach naturally limits resolution scope. The Swift implementation needs explicit protection because it resolves ALL links when `includedLinks` is nil.
    40→
    41→### Proposed Implementation
    42→
    43→```swift
    44→// File: Sources/SharingInstant/Extensions/TripleStore+Extensions.swift
    45→
    46→/// Resolves an entity by ID from the TripleStore, with cycle detection.
    47→///
    48→/// - Parameters:
    49→///   - id: The entity ID to resolve
    50→///   - attrsStore: The attributes store for schema info
    51→///   - depth: Current recursion depth (internal use)
    52→///   - maxDepth: Maximum recursion depth (default: 5, reduced from 10)
    53→///   - includedLinks: Links to resolve (nil = all, empty = none)
    54→///   - visited: Set of already-visited entity IDs for cycle detection
    55→/// - Returns: Dictionary representation of the entity
    56→public func resolve(
    57→    id: String,
    58→    attrsStore: AttrsStore,
    59→    depth: Int = 0,
    60→    maxDepth: Int = 5,  // CHANGED: Reduced from 10 to 5
    61→    includedLinks: Set<String>? = nil,
    62→    visited: inout Set<String>  // NEW: Cycle detection
    63→) -> [String: Any] {
    64→    // Cycle detection
    65→    guard !visited.contains(id) else {
    66→        return ["id": id]  // Return minimal representation for cycles
    67→    }
    68→    visited.insert(id)
    69→    defer { visited.remove(id) }  // Allow revisiting in different branches
    70→
    71→    // Depth limit
    72→    if depth > maxDepth { return ["id": id] }
    73→
    74→    let triples = self.getTriples(entity: id)
    75→    guard !triples.isEmpty else { return ["id": id] }
    76→
    77→    var result: [String: Any] = ["id": id]
    78→
    79→    // Group triples by attribute
    80→    let triplesByAttr = Dictionary(grouping: triples) { $0.attributeId }
    81→
    82→    for (attrId, attrTriples) in triplesByAttr {
    83→        guard let attr = attrsStore.getAttr(attrId) else { continue }
    84→        let label = attr.forwardIdentity.count > 2 ? attr.forwardIdentity[2] : attrId
    85→
    86→        if attr.valueType == .ref {
    87→            // Skip links not in includedLinks (if specified)
    88→            if let includedLinks = includedLinks, !includedLinks.contains(label) {
    89→                continue
    90→            }
    91→
    92→            // Resolve linked entities with cycle detection
    93→            var resolvedRefs: [[String: Any]] = []
    94→            for triple in attrTriples {
    95→                if case .ref(let targetId) = triple.value {
    96→                    let childObj = resolve(
    97→                        id: targetId,
    98→                        attrsStore: attrsStore,
    99→                        depth: depth + 1,
   100→                        maxDepth: maxDepth,
   101→                        includedLinks: includedLinks,
   102→                        visited: &visited  // Pass visited set
   103→                    )
   104→                    // Skip ghost entities (only have "id")
   105→                    if childObj.count > 1 {
   106→                        resolvedRefs.append(childObj)
   107→                    }
   108→                }
   109→            }
   110→
   111→            // Handle cardinality
   112→            if attr.cardinality == .one || attr.isUnique == true {
   113→                result[label] = resolvedRefs.first
   114→            } else {
   115→                result[label] = resolvedRefs
   116→            }
   117→        } else {
   118→            // Non-ref attributes: take most recent value
   119→            if let latestTriple = attrTriples.max(by: { $0.createdAt < $1.createdAt }) {
   120→                result[label] = latestTriple.value.rawValue
   121→            }
   122→        }
   123→    }
   124→
   125→    // Resolve reverse links with cycle detection
   126→    if depth < maxDepth, let entityType = attrsStore.getEntityType(forEntityId: id) {
   127→        let reverseAttrs = attrsStore.revIdents[entityType] ?? [:]
   128→
   129→        for (reverseLabel, attr) in reverseAttrs {
   130→            if let includedLinks = includedLinks, !includedLinks.contains(reverseLabel) {
   131→                continue
   132→            }
   133→
   134→            let reverseTriples = getReverseRefs(entityId: id, attributeId: attr.id)
   135→            var resolvedParents: [[String: Any]] = []
   136→
   137→            for triple in reverseTriples {
   138→                let parentObj = resolve(
   139→                    id: triple.entityId,
   140→                    attrsStore: attrsStore,
   141→                    depth: depth + 1,
   142→                    maxDepth: maxDepth,
   143→                    includedLinks: includedLinks,
   144→                    visited: &visited  // Pass visited set
   145→                )
   146→                if parentObj.count > 1 {
   147→                    resolvedParents.append(parentObj)
   148→                }
   149→            }
   150→
   151→            if attr.cardinality == .one || attr.isUnique == true {
   152→                result[reverseLabel] = resolvedParents.first
   153→            } else {
   154→                result[reverseLabel] = resolvedParents
   155→            }
   156→        }
   157→    }
   158→
   159→    return result
   160→}
   161→
   162→// Convenience overload that creates the visited set
   163→public func resolve(
   164→    id: String,
   165→    attrsStore: AttrsStore,
   166→    depth: Int = 0,
   167→    maxDepth: Int = 5,
   168→    includedLinks: Set<String>? = nil
   169→) -> [String: Any] {
   170→    var visited = Set<String>()
   171→    return resolve(
   172→        id: id,
   173→        attrsStore: attrsStore,
   174→        depth: depth,
   175→        maxDepth: maxDepth,
   176→        includedLinks: includedLinks,
   177→        visited: &visited
   178→    )
   179→}
   180→```

   213→## Priority 2: TripleStore Garbage Collection
   214→
   215→### Problem

   227→### TypeScript Reference
   228→
   229→**File:** `instant/client/packages/core/src/utils/PersistedObject.ts` (Lines 350-472)
   230→
   231→```javascript
   232→// GC Configuration
   233→export type GCOpts = {
   234→  maxSize: number;     // Maximum total size in bytes
   235→  maxAgeMs: number;    // Maximum age before eligible for GC
   236→  maxEntries: number;  // Maximum number of entries
   237→};
   238→
   239→// GC Algorithm (4 phases)
   240→private async _gc() {
   241→  // Phase 1: Remove orphaned keys (in storage but not in meta)
   242→  for (const key of keys) {
   243→    if (sacredKeys.has(key) || key in meta.objects) continue;
   244→    promises.push(this._persister.removeItem(key));
   245→  }
   246→
   247→  // Phase 2: Remove entries older than maxAgeMs
   248→  for (const [k, m] of Object.entries(meta.objects)) {
   249→    if (!sacredKeys.has(k) && m.updatedAt < now - this._gcOpts.maxAgeMs) {
   250→      promises.push(this._persister.removeItem(k));
   251→      delete meta.objects[k];
   252→    }
   253→  }
   254→
   255→  // Phase 3: Enforce maxEntries limit (LRU by updatedAt)
   256→  const entries = Object.entries(meta.objects).sort((a, b) =>
   257→    a[1].updatedAt - b[1].updatedAt
   258→  );
   259→  const deletable = entries.filter(([x]) => !sacredKeys.has(x));
   260→  if (entries.length > this._gcOpts.maxEntries) {
   261→    for (const [k] of deletable.slice(0, entries.length - this._gcOpts.maxEntries)) {
   262→      promises.push(this._persister.removeItem(k));
   263→      delete meta.objects[k];
   264→    }
   265→  }
   266→
   267→  // Phase 4: Enforce maxSize limit (LRU by updatedAt)
   268→  let currentSize = entries.reduce((acc, [_, m]) => acc + m.size, 0);
   269→  while (currentSize > this._gcOpts.maxSize && deletable.length) {
   270→    const [[k, m]] = deletable.splice(0, 1);
   271→    currentSize -= m.size;
   272→    promises.push(this._persister.removeItem(k));
   273→    delete meta.objects[k];
   274→  }
   275→}
   276→```

   278→### Proposed Implementation
   279→
   280→```swift
   281→// File: Sources/SharingInstant/Internal/TripleStoreGC.swift (NEW FILE)
   282→
   283→import Foundation
   284→
   285→/// Configuration for TripleStore garbage collection
   286→public struct TripleStoreGCConfig: Sendable {
   287→    /// Maximum number of triples to keep in the store
   288→    public let maxTriples: Int
   289→
   290→    /// Maximum age in seconds before a triple is eligible for GC
   291→    public let maxAgeSeconds: TimeInterval
   292→
   293→    /// Maximum number of unique entities to track
   294→    public let maxEntities: Int
   295→
   296→    /// Interval between GC runs in seconds
   297→    public let gcIntervalSeconds: TimeInterval
   298→
   299→    public static let `default` = TripleStoreGCConfig(
   300→        maxTriples: 100_000,
   301→        maxAgeSeconds: 60 * 60 * 24 * 7,  // 1 week
   302→        maxEntities: 10_000,
   303→        gcIntervalSeconds: 60  // 1 minute
   304→    )
   305→
   306→    public static let aggressive = TripleStoreGCConfig(
   307→        maxTriples: 10_000,
   308→        maxAgeSeconds: 60 * 60,  // 1 hour
   309→        maxEntities: 1_000,
   310→        gcIntervalSeconds: 30
   311→    )
   312→}
   313→
   314→/// Tracks entity access for LRU eviction
   315→struct EntityAccessRecord: Sendable {
   316→    let entityId: String
   317→    var lastAccessedAt: TimeInterval
   318→    var tripleCount: Int
   319→}
   320→
   321→/// Garbage collector for TripleStore
   322→public actor TripleStoreGC {
   323→    private let store: SharedTripleStore
   324→    private let config: TripleStoreGCConfig
   325→    private var entityAccess: [String: EntityAccessRecord] = [:]
   326→    private var sacredEntities: Set<String> = []  // Entities in active subscriptions
   327→    private var gcTask: Task<Void, Never>?
   328→
   329→    public init(store: SharedTripleStore, config: TripleStoreGCConfig = .default) {
   330→        self.store = store
   331→        self.config = config
   332→    }
   333→
   334→    /// Start periodic garbage collection
   335→    public func start() {
   336→        guard gcTask == nil else { return }
   337→
   338→        gcTask = Task { [weak self] in
   339→            while !Task.isCancelled {
   340→                try? await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: UInt64(self?.config.gcIntervalSeconds ?? 60) * 1_000_000_000)
   341→                await self?.runGC()
   342→            }
   343→        }
   344→    }
   345→
   346→    /// Stop garbage collection
   347→    public func stop() {
   348→        gcTask?.cancel()
   349→        gcTask = nil
   350→    }
   351→
   352→    /// Mark entities as sacred (in active subscriptions, cannot be evicted)
   353→    public func markSacred(_ entityIds: Set<String>) {
   354→        sacredEntities.formUnion(entityIds)
   355→    }
   356→
   357→    /// Unmark entities as sacred
   358→    public func unmarkSacred(_ entityIds: Set<String>) {
   359→        sacredEntities.subtract(entityIds)
   360→    }
   361→
   362→    /// Record entity access for LRU tracking
   363→    public func recordAccess(entityId: String, tripleCount: Int = 1) {
   364→        let now = Date().timeIntervalSince1970
   365→        if var record = entityAccess[entityId] {
   366→            record.lastAccessedAt = now
   367→            record.tripleCount = tripleCount
   368→            entityAccess[entityId] = record
   369→        } else {
   370→            entityAccess[entityId] = EntityAccessRecord(
   371→                entityId: entityId,
   372→                lastAccessedAt: now,
   373→                tripleCount: tripleCount
   374→            )
   375→        }
   376→    }
   377→
   378→    /// Run garbage collection
   379→    public func runGC() async -> GCResult {
   380→        let now = Date().timeIntervalSince1970
   381→        var result = GCResult()
   382→
   383→        // Phase 1: Remove orphaned entity access records
   384→        let storeEntityIds = store.getAllEntityIds()
   385→        for entityId in entityAccess.keys where !storeEntityIds.contains(entityId) {
   386→            entityAccess.removeValue(forKey: entityId)
   387→            result.orphanedRecordsRemoved += 1
   388→        }
   389→
   390→        // Phase 2: Remove entities older than maxAgeSeconds
   391→        for (entityId, record) in entityAccess {
   392→            guard !sacredEntities.contains(entityId) else { continue }
   393→
   394→            if record.lastAccessedAt < now - config.maxAgeSeconds {
   395→                store.deleteEntity(id: entityId)
   396→                entityAccess.removeValue(forKey: entityId)
   397→                result.agedOutEntities += 1
   398→            }
   399→        }
   400→
   401→        // Phase 3: Enforce maxEntities limit (LRU)
   402→        if entityAccess.count > config.maxEntities {
   403→            let sortedByAccess = entityAccess.values
   404→                .filter { !sacredEntities.contains($0.entityId) }
   405→                .sorted { $0.lastAccessedAt < $1.lastAccessedAt }
   406→
   407→            let toRemove = sortedByAccess.prefix(entityAccess.count - config.maxEntities)
   408→            for record in toRemove {
   409→                store.deleteEntity(id: record.entityId)
   410→                entityAccess.removeValue(forKey: record.entityId)
   411→                result.lruEvictedEntities += 1
   412→            }
   413→        }
   414→
   415→        // Phase 4: Enforce maxTriples limit (LRU by entity)
   416→        let totalTriples = entityAccess.values.reduce(0) { $0 + $1.tripleCount }
   417→        if totalTriples > config.maxTriples {
   418→            let sortedByAccess = entityAccess.values
   419→                .filter { !sacredEntities.contains($0.entityId) }
   420→                .sorted { $0.lastAccessedAt < $1.lastAccessedAt }
   421→
   422→            var currentTotal = totalTriples
   423→            for record in sortedByAccess {
   424→                guard currentTotal > config.maxTriples else { break }
   425→                store.deleteEntity(id: record.entityId)
   426→                entityAccess.removeValue(forKey: record.entityId)
   427→                currentTotal -= record.tripleCount
   428→                result.sizeEvictedEntities += 1
   429→            }
   430→        }
   431→
   432→        return result
   433→    }
   434→}
   435→
   436→public struct GCResult: Sendable {
   437→    var orphanedRecordsRemoved: Int = 0
   438→    var agedOutEntities: Int = 0
   439→    var lruEvictedEntities: Int = 0
   440→    var sizeEvictedEntities: Int = 0
   441→
   442→    var totalEvicted: Int {
   443→        agedOutEntities + lruEvictedEntities + sizeEvictedEntities
   444→    }
   445→}
   446→```
