   494→
   495→## Priority 3: Pending Mutation Cleanup
   496→
   497→### Problem
   498→
   499→Swift has NO mechanism to clean up confirmed pending mutations. They accumulate indefinitely.
   500→
   501→### TypeScript Reference
   502→
   503→**File:** `instant/client/packages/core/src/Reactor.js`
   504→
   505→#### Method 1: Query-Based Cleanup (Lines 1461-1476)
   506→
   507→```javascript
   508→_cleanupPendingMutationsQueries() {
   509→  // Find minimum processedTxId across all queries
   510→  let minProcessedTxId = Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER;
   511→  for (const { result } of Object.values(this.querySubs.currentValue)) {
   512→    if (result?.processedTxId) {
   513→      minProcessedTxId = Math.min(minProcessedTxId, result?.processedTxId);
   514→    }
   515→  }
   516→
   517→  // Remove mutations where tx-id <= minProcessedTxId
   518→  // (all queries have seen this mutation's effects)
   519→  this._updatePendingMutations((prev) => {
   520→    for (const [eventId, mut] of Array.from(prev.entries())) {
   521→      if (mut['tx-id'] && mut['tx-id'] <= minProcessedTxId) {
   522→        prev.delete(eventId);
   523→      }
   524→    }
   525→  });
   526→}
   527→```
   528→
   529→#### Method 2: Timeout-Based Cleanup (Lines 1483-1500)
   530→
   531→```javascript
   532→_cleanupPendingMutationsTimeout() {
   533→  if (this._pendingMutations().size < this._pendingMutationCleanupThreshold) {
   534→    return;  // Only run if threshold exceeded (200)
   535→  }
   536→
   537→  const now = Date.now();
   538→
   539→  this._updatePendingMutations((prev) => {
   540→    for (const [eventId, mut] of Array.from(prev.entries())) {
   541→      // Remove if confirmed > 30 seconds ago
   542→      if (mut.confirmed && mut.confirmed + this._pendingTxCleanupTimeout < now) {
   543→        prev.delete(eventId);
   544→      }
   545→    }
   546→  });
   547→}
   548→```
   549→
   550→### Proposed Implementation
   551→
   552→```swift
   553→// File: Sources/SharingInstant/Internal/Reactor.swift
   554→
   555→// Add to actor properties:
   556→private var queryProcessedTxIds: [String: Int] = [:]  // queryHash -> processedTxId
   557→private let pendingMutationCleanupThreshold = 200
   558→private let pendingTxCleanupTimeoutSeconds: TimeInterval = 30
   559→
   560→// Add cleanup methods:
   561→
   562→/// Cleans up pending mutations that all queries have processed.
   563→///
   564→/// ## Algorithm (TypeScript Parity)
   565→/// 1. Find minimum processedTxId across all active query subscriptions
   566→/// 2. Remove mutations where txId <= minProcessedTxId
   567→///
   568→/// This works because:
   569→/// - Server sends `processedTxId` with each query result
   570→/// - If ALL queries have processedTxId >= mutation's txId, the mutation is in server state
   571→/// - We can safely remove it from pending queue
   572→private func cleanupPendingMutationsQueries() async {
   573→    guard !queryProcessedTxIds.isEmpty else { return }
   574→
   575→    // Find minimum processedTxId
   576→    let minProcessedTxId = queryProcessedTxIds.values.min() ?? Int.max
   577→
   578→    // Get client to access pending mutations
   579→    let client = await MainActor.run {
   580→        InstantClientFactory.makeClient(appID: currentAppID, instanceID: clientInstanceID)
   581→    }
   582→
   583→    // Get pending mutations and remove confirmed ones
   584→    let pendingMutations = await client.getUnconfirmedPendingMutations()
   585→
   586→    for mutation in pendingMutations {
   587→        guard let txId = mutation.txId, txId <= minProcessedTxId else { continue }
   588→
   589→        // Remove from SQLite
   590→        await client.removePendingMutation(eventId: mutation.eventId)
   591→    }
   592→}
   593→
   594→/// Cleans up old pending mutations that have been confirmed but not processed by queries.
   595→///
   596→/// ## Algorithm (TypeScript Parity)
   597→/// - Only run if pendingMutations.count > threshold (200)
   598→/// - Remove mutations confirmed > 30 seconds ago
   599→/// - These mutations probably don't affect any active queries
   600→private func cleanupPendingMutationsTimeout() async {
   601→    let client = await MainActor.run {
   602→        InstantClientFactory.makeClient(appID: currentAppID, instanceID: clientInstanceID)
   603→    }
   604→
   605→    let pendingMutations = await client.getUnconfirmedPendingMutations()
   606→
   607→    guard pendingMutations.count >= pendingMutationCleanupThreshold else { return }
   608→
   609→    let now = Date().timeIntervalSince1970
   610→
   611→    for mutation in pendingMutations {
   612→        guard let confirmedAt = mutation.confirmedAt else { continue }
   613→
   614→        if confirmedAt + pendingTxCleanupTimeoutSeconds < now {
   615→            await client.removePendingMutation(eventId: mutation.eventId)
   616→        }
   617→    }
   618→}
   619→
   620→/// Called when a query receives results from server.
   621→/// Updates processedTxId tracking and triggers cleanup.
   622→func updateQueryProcessedTxId(queryHash: String, processedTxId: Int) async {
   623→    queryProcessedTxIds[queryHash] = processedTxId
   624→
   625→    // Run cleanup after processing
   626→    await cleanupPendingMutationsQueries()
   627→    await cleanupPendingMutationsTimeout()
   628→}
   629→
   630→/// Called when a query subscription ends.
   631→func removeQueryProcessedTxId(queryHash: String) {
   632→    queryProcessedTxIds.removeValue(forKey: queryHash)
   633→}
   634→```

   668→## Priority 4: Query Result Caching with Version Tracking
   669→
   670→### Problem
   671→
   672→Swift recomputes query results from scratch on every update, unlike TypeScript which uses version-based caching.
   673→
   674→### TypeScript Reference
   675→
   676→**File:** `instant/client/packages/core/src/Reactor.js` (Lines 1224-1261)
   677→
   678→```javascript
   679→dataForQuery(hash) {
   680→  // Get versions
   681→  const querySubVersion = this.querySubs.version();
   682→  const pendingMutationsVersion = this.kv.version();
   683→
   684→  // Check cache
   685→  const cached = this._dataForQueryCache[hash];
   686→  if (
   687→    cached &&
   688→    querySubVersion === cached.querySubVersion &&
   689→    pendingMutationsVersion === cached.pendingMutationsVersion
   690→  ) {
   691→    return cached;  // Cache hit!
   692→  }
   693→
   694→  // Cache miss - recompute
   695→  const { store, attrsStore, pageInfo, aggregate, processedTxId } = result;
   696→  const mutations = this._rewriteMutationsSorted(attrsStore, pendingMutations);
   697→  const { store: newStore, attrsStore: newAttrsStore } =
   698→    this._applyOptimisticUpdates(store, attrsStore, mutations, processedTxId);
   699→  const resp = instaql({ store: newStore, attrsStore: newAttrsStore }, q);
   700→
   701→  // Update cache
   702→  return { data: resp, querySubVersion, pendingMutationsVersion };
   703→}
   704→```
   705→
   706→### Proposed Implementation
   707→
   708→```swift
   709→// File: Sources/SharingInstant/Internal/Reactor.swift
   710→
   711→// Add to actor properties:
   712→private var storeVersion: Int = 0
   713→private var pendingMutationsVersion: Int = 0
   714→private var queryResultCache: [String: CachedQueryResult] = [:]
   715→
   716→struct CachedQueryResult: Sendable {
   717→    let data: [Any]  // Encoded entities
   718→    let storeVersion: Int
   719→    let pendingMutationsVersion: Int
   720→    let processedTxId: Int?
   721→}
   722→
   723→// Increment versions on changes:
   724→
   725→func incrementStoreVersion() {
   726→    storeVersion += 1
   727→}
   728→
   729→func incrementPendingMutationsVersion() {
   730→    pendingMutationsVersion += 1
   731→}
   732→
   733→// In SubscriptionState.handleStoreUpdate():
   734→
   735→func handleStoreUpdate() async {
   736→    let queryHash = computeQueryHash()
   737→
   738→    // Check cache
   739→    if let cached = await reactor.getCachedResult(queryHash: queryHash),
   740→       cached.storeVersion == await reactor.storeVersion,
   741→       cached.pendingMutationsVersion == await reactor.pendingMutationsVersion {
   742→        // Cache hit - use cached data
   743→        if let values = decodeCachedData(cached.data) {
   744→            continuation.yield(values)
   745→            return
   746→        }
   747→    }
   748→
   749→    // Cache miss - recompute (existing logic)
   750→    let client = await MainActor.run {
   751→        InstantClientFactory.makeClient(appID: appID, instanceID: clientInstanceID)
   752→    }
   753→    let pendingMutations = await client.getUnconfirmedPendingMutations()
   754→
   755→    // ... existing merge logic ...
   756→
   757→    var values: [Value] = []
   758→    for id in allIDs {
   759→        // ... existing resolution logic ...
   760→    }
   761→
   762→    // Update cache
   763→    await reactor.setCachedResult(
   764→        queryHash: queryHash,
   765→        data: values.map { try? $0.asDictionary() }.compactMap { $0 },
   766→        processedTxId: currentProcessedTxId
   767→    )
   768→
   769→    continuation.yield(values)
   770→}
   771→
   772→// Helper to compute query hash (match TypeScript's weakHash)
   773→private func computeQueryHash() -> String {
   774→    var hasher = Hasher()
   775→    hasher.combine(namespace)
   776→    hasher.combine(orderByIsDescending)
   777→    for link in includedLinks.sorted() {
   778→        hasher.combine(link)
   779→    }
   780→    return String(hasher.finalize())
   781→}
   782→```

   793→## Priority 5: Cache Pending Mutations in Reactor
   794→
   795→### Problem
   796→
   797→**File:** `Sources/SharingInstant/Internal/Reactor.swift` (Lines 1283-1290)
   798→
   799→Every `handleStoreUpdate()` call fetches ALL pending mutations from SQLite:
   800→
   801→```swift
   802→let pendingMutations = await client.getUnconfirmedPendingMutations()
   803→```
   804→
   805→With rapid updates (7-8ms intervals during transcription), this causes significant overhead.
   806→
   807→### TypeScript Reference
   808→
   809→TypeScript caches pending mutations in memory and only reads from IndexedDB on startup:
   810→
   811→```javascript
   812→// Reactor.js
   813→_pendingMutations() {
   814→  return this.kv.currentValue.pendingMutations ?? new Map();  // In-memory!
   815→}
   816→```
   817→
   818→### Proposed Implementation
   819→
   820→```swift
   821→// File: Sources/SharingInstant/Internal/Reactor.swift
   822→
   823→// Add to actor properties:
   824→private var cachedPendingMutations: [String: CachedMutation] = [:]
   825→private var pendingMutationsLoaded = false
   826→
   827→struct CachedMutation: Sendable {
   828→    let eventId: String
   829→    let txSteps: [[AnySendable]]
   830→    let createdAt: TimeInterval
   831→    var txId: Int?
   832→    var confirmedAt: TimeInterval?
   833→    let order: Int
   834→}
   835→
   836→// Load from SQLite once on first access:
   837→private func loadPendingMutationsIfNeeded() async {
   838→    guard !pendingMutationsLoaded else { return }
   839→
   840→    let client = await MainActor.run {
   841→        InstantClientFactory.makeClient(appID: currentAppID, instanceID: clientInstanceID)
   842→    }
   843→
   844→    let mutations = await client.getUnconfirmedPendingMutations()
   845→
   846→    for mutation in mutations {
   847→        cachedPendingMutations[mutation.eventId] = CachedMutation(
   848→            eventId: mutation.eventId,
   849→            txSteps: mutation.txSteps,
   850→            createdAt: mutation.createdAt,
   851→            txId: mutation.txId,
   852→            confirmedAt: mutation.confirmedAt,
   853→            order: mutation.order
   854→        )
   855→    }
   856→
   857→    pendingMutationsLoaded = true
   858→}
   859→
   860→// Use cache for reads:
   861→func getPendingMutations() async -> [CachedMutation] {
   862→    await loadPendingMutationsIfNeeded()
   863→    return Array(cachedPendingMutations.values).sorted { $0.order < $1.order }
   864→}
   865→
   866→// Update cache on mutations:
   867→func addPendingMutation(_ mutation: CachedMutation) async {
   868→    cachedPendingMutations[mutation.eventId] = mutation
   869→    pendingMutationsVersion += 1
   870→
   871→    // Also persist to SQLite (fire-and-forget)
   872→    Task {
   873→        let client = await MainActor.run {
   874→            InstantClientFactory.makeClient(appID: currentAppID, instanceID: clientInstanceID)
   875→        }
   876→        await client.persistPendingMutation(mutation)
   877→    }
   878→}
   879→
   880→func confirmPendingMutation(eventId: String, txId: Int) async {
   881→    guard var mutation = cachedPendingMutations[eventId] else { return }
   882→
   883→    mutation.txId = txId
   884→    mutation.confirmedAt = Date().timeIntervalSince1970
   885→    cachedPendingMutations[eventId] = mutation
   886→    pendingMutationsVersion += 1
   887→}
   888→
   889→func removePendingMutation(eventId: String) async {
   890→    cachedPendingMutations.removeValue(forKey: eventId)
   891→    pendingMutationsVersion += 1
   892→}
   893→```

     1→# SharingInstant Memory & Performance Fixes - Implementation Plan
     2→
     3→## Executive Summary
     4→
     5→This plan addresses **CRITICAL** and **HIGH** priority memory issues in the SharingInstant Swift SDK identified through comprehensive analysis of:
     6→- TypeScript Reactor.js cleanup mechanisms
     7→- TypeScript Store/PersistedObject GC patterns
     8→- Swift Reactor current implementation gaps
     9→- Git history of related fixes
    10→
    11→**Priority Fixes:**
    12→1. Cycle detection in entity resolution (CRITICAL)
    13→2. TripleStore garbage collection (CRITICAL)
    14→3. Pending mutation cleanup (HIGH)
    15→4. Query result caching with version tracking (HIGH)
    16→5. Pending mutation caching in Reactor (HIGH)
    17→
    18→---
    19→
    20→## Answers to Design Questions
    21→
    22→### Q1: Why is Swift's approach different from TypeScript's query-driven approach?
    23→
    24→**TypeScript (Query-Driven):** In TypeScript, the query object structure defines exactly what gets resolved. The `instaql.ts` function only traverses links that exist as keys in the query form:
    25→
    26→```javascript
    27→// TypeScript: Only resolves links that are KEYS in the query
    28→{ users: { posts: {} } }  // Only resolves "posts" link, ignores all others
    29→```
    30→
    31→**Swift (Currently Broken):** Swift's `resolve()` with `includedLinks = nil` resolves ALL links:
    32→
    33→```swift
    34→// Swift: resolve() with includedLinks = nil resolves EVERYTHING
    35→if let includedLinks = includedLinks, !includedLinks.contains(label) {
    36→    continue  // Only skips if includedLinks WAS PROVIDED
    37→}
    38→// If nil, ALL links are resolved - this is the bug!
    39→```
    40→
    41→**Is this a platform limitation?** Partially. Swift lacks JavaScript's ability to introspect query-as-data structure at runtime. However, this is solvable because:
    42→1. The `.with(\.link)` chain is parsed at compile time into a `linkTree`
    43→2. We CAN pass the `linkTree` down to `resolve()` as `includedLinks`
    44→3. The problem is **we're not doing this correctly**
    45→
    46→**Which approach is better?** TypeScript's query-driven approach is superior because:
    47→- Only fetches what's needed (memory efficient)
    48→- Predictable: same query → same structure
    49→- Cache-friendly: query hash determines cache key
    50→- No N+1 surprises
    51→
    52→**Fix:** Make `includedLinks` required or default to empty set (resolve nothing):
    53→
    54→```swift
    55→// PROPOSED: Default to empty set (resolve NO links unless specified)
    56→public func resolve(
    57→    id: String,
    58→    attrsStore: AttrsStore,
    59→    includedLinks: Set<String> = []  // NOT nil!
    60→) -> [String: Any]
    61→```
    62→
    63→### Q2: Why is `includedLinks = nil` including everything a bad default?
    64→
    65→This is **ridiculous** as the user noted. The current behavior:
    66→- `nil` = resolve ALL links recursively (dangerous)
    67→- `Set()` = resolve NO links (safe)
    68→
    69→This should be inverted:
    70→- Required parameter or default to `[]` (resolve nothing)
    71→- Explicit list required to resolve links
    72→
    73→This matches TypeScript where you must explicitly specify child queries:
    74→```javascript
    75→// TypeScript: Must explicitly name links to resolve
    76→{ users: { posts: { comments: {} } } }  // 3 levels deep, all explicit
    77→```
    78→
    79→### Q3: GC "in storage but not in meta" - When does this happen?
    80→
    81→**Scenario causing orphaned keys:**
    82→
    83→1. **Crash during save:** Key written to IndexedDB, then app crashes before `__meta` is updated
    84→2. **Multi-tab race:** Tab A deletes key, crashes before updating meta; Tab B sees stale meta
    85→3. **Corruption:** IndexedDB gets corrupted or manually edited
    86→
    87→**TypeScript detection (PersistedObject.ts:388-397):**
    88→```javascript
    89→for (const key of keys) {
    90→  if (sacredKeys.has(key) || key in meta.objects) continue;
    91→  this._log.info('Lost track of key in meta', key);  // ORPHAN!
    92→  promises.push(this._persister.removeItem(key));
    93→}
    94→```
    95→
    96→### Q4: What are TypeScript's default GC values?
    97→
    98→**For `querySubs` (query results) - Reactor.js:433-437:**
    99→```javascript
   100→gc: {
   101→  maxAgeMs: 1000 * 60 * 60 * 24 * 7 * 52,  // 1 YEAR
   102→  maxEntries: 1000,
   103→  maxSize: 1_000_000,  // 1 million triples
   104→}
   105→```
   106→
   107→**For `kv` store (pending mutations):**
   108→```javascript
   109→gc: null,  // GC DISABLED for pending mutations
   110→```
   111→
   112→**GC schedule:** ~1 minute with 0-500ms jitter (prevents multi-tab race)
   113→
   114→**Reasonable Swift defaults (more aggressive since mobile):**
   115→```swift
   116→public static let `default` = TripleStoreGCConfig(
   117→    maxTriples: 100_000,           // 10x less than TS
   118→    maxAgeSeconds: 60 * 60 * 24,   // 1 day (vs 1 year)
   119→    maxEntities: 10_000,           // 10x less than TS
   120→    gcIntervalSeconds: 60
   121→)
   122→```
   123→
   124→### Q5: "Sacred" terminology - What does it mean?
   125→
   126→**Sacred keys are entities that MUST NOT be garbage collected.** They include:
   127→1. `currentValue` - Entries currently in memory being accessed
   128→2. `_loadingKeys` - Entries being fetched from storage
   129→3. `_loadedKeys` - Entries that were loaded into memory
   130→
   131→Every eviction check verifies sacred status:
   132→```javascript
   133→if (!sacredKeys.has(k) && m.updatedAt < now - maxAgeMs) {
   134→  // Only evict if NOT sacred
   135→}
   136→```
   137→
   138→**Swift equivalent:** Entities in active `@Shared` subscriptions are sacred.
   139→
   140→### Q6: Does Swift's pending mutation strategy match TypeScript?
   141→
   142→**Mostly yes, with key differences:**
   143→
   144→| Aspect | TypeScript | Swift |
   145→|--------|-----------|-------|
   146→| Save timing | Async, throttled (100ms) | Sync, immediate |
   147→| Save blocking | No (fire-and-forget) | Yes (await) |
   148→| Storage | IndexedDB | SQLite |
   149→| Load timing | App startup (lazy) | App startup (explicit) |
   150→| Restoration | On-demand during notification | Explicit phase before first subscription |
   151→| Cleanup | Query-based + timeout-based | **MISSING** ← This is the gap |
   152→
   153→### Q7: When does TypeScript save pending mutations to disk?
   154→
   155→**Answer:** Asynchronously with 100ms throttle, fire-and-forget.
   156→
   157→```javascript
   158→// PersistedObject.ts:501-506
   159→this._nextSave = setTimeout(() => {
   160→  safeIdleCallback(() => {
   161→    this._writeToStorage(opts);  // Fire-and-forget
   162→  }, 100);  // 100ms idle callback
   163→}, 100);  // 100ms throttle
   164→```
   165→
   166→**What happens if app closes before server ack?**
   167→1. Mutations persisted to IndexedDB immediately (throttled but persistent)
   168→2. App closes → mutations preserved
   169→3. App reopens → `_flushPendingMessages()` resends unconfirmed mutations
   170→4. Server responds → mutation marked with `tx-id` and `confirmed`
   171→5. Cleanup after 30 seconds via `_cleanupPendingMutationsTimeout()`
   172→
   173→Swift matches this except **we're missing the cleanup methods**.

## Approved Plan:
# SharingInstant Memory & Performance Fixes - Implementation Plan

## Executive Summary

This plan addresses **CRITICAL** and **HIGH** priority memory issues in the SharingInstant Swift SDK identified through comprehensive analysis of:
- TypeScript Reactor.js cleanup mechanisms
- TypeScript Store/PersistedObject GC patterns
- Swift Reactor current implementation gaps
- Git history of related fixes

**Priority Fixes:**
1. Cycle detection in entity resolution (CRITICAL)
2. TripleStore garbage collection (CRITICAL)
3. Pending mutation cleanup (HIGH)
4. Query result caching with version tracking (HIGH)
5. Pending mutation caching in Reactor (HIGH)

---

## Answers to Design Questions

### Q1: Why is Swift's approach different from TypeScript's query-driven approach?

**TypeScript (Query-Driven):** In TypeScript, the query object structure defines exactly what gets resolved. The `instaql.ts` function only traverses links that exist as keys in the query form:

```javascript
// TypeScript: Only resolves links that are KEYS in the query
{ users: { posts: {} } }  // Only resolves "posts" link, ignores all others
```

**Swift (Currently Broken):** Swift's `resolve()` with `includedLinks = nil` resolves ALL links:

```swift
// Swift: resolve() with includedLinks = nil resolves EVERYTHING
if let includedLinks = includedLinks, !includedLinks.contains(label) {
    continue  // Only skips if includedLinks WAS PROVIDED
}
// If nil, ALL links are resolved - this is the bug!
```

**Is this a platform limitation?** Partially. Swift lacks JavaScript's ability to introspect query-as-data structure at runtime. However, this is solvable because:
1. The `.with(\.link)` chain is parsed at compile time into a `linkTree`
2. We CAN pass the `linkTree` down to `resolve()` as `includedLinks`
3. The problem is **we're not doing this correctly**

**Which approach is better?** TypeScript's query-driven approach is superior because:
- Only fetches what's needed (memory efficient)
- Predictable: same query → same structure
- Cache-friendly: query hash determines cache key
- No N+1 surprises

**Fix:** Make `includedLinks` required or default to empty set (resolve nothing):

```swift
// PROPOSED: Default to empty set (resolve NO links unless specified)
public func resolve(
    id: String,
    attrsStore: AttrsStore,
    includedLinks: Set<String> = []  // NOT nil!
) -> [String: Any]
```

### Q2: Why is `includedLinks = nil` including everything a bad default?

This is **ridiculous** as the user noted. The current behavior:
- `nil` = resolve ALL links recursively (dangerous)
- `Set()` = resolve NO links (safe)

This should be inverted:
- Required parameter or default to `[]` (resolve nothing)
- Explicit list required to resolve links

This matches TypeScript where you must explicitly specify child queries:
```javascript
// TypeScript: Must explicitly name links to resolve
{ users: { posts: { comments: {} } } }  // 3 levels deep, all explicit
```

### Q3: GC "in storage but not in meta" - When does this happen?

**Scenario causing orphaned keys:**

1. **Crash during save:** Key written to IndexedDB, then app crashes before `__meta` is updated
2. **Multi-tab race:** Tab A deletes key, crashes before updating meta; Tab B sees stale meta
3. **Corruption:** IndexedDB gets corrupted or manually edited

**TypeScript detection (PersistedObject.ts:388-397):**
```javascript
for (const key of keys) {
  if (sacredKeys.has(key) || key in meta.objects) continue;
  this._log.info('Lost track of key in meta', key);  // ORPHAN!
  promises.push(this._persister.removeItem(key));
}
```

### Q4: What are TypeScript's default GC values?

**For `querySubs` (query results) - Reactor.js:433-437:**
```javascript
gc: {
  maxAgeMs: 1000 * 60 * 60 * 24 * 7 * 52,  // 1 YEAR
  maxEntries: 1000,
  maxSize: 1_000_000,  // 1 million triples
}
```

**For `kv` store (pending mutations):**
```javascript
gc: null,  // GC DISABLED for pending mutations
```

**GC schedule:** ~1 minute with 0-500ms jitter (prevents multi-tab race)

**Reasonable Swift defaults (more aggressive since mobile):**
```swift
public static let `default` = TripleStoreGCConfig(
    maxTriples: 100_000,           // 10x less than TS
    maxAgeSeconds: 60 * 60 * 24,   // 1 day (vs 1 year)
    maxEntities: 10_000,           // 10x less than TS
    gcIntervalSeconds: 60
)
```

### Q5: "Sacred" terminology - What does it mean?

**Sacred keys are entities that MUST NOT be garbage collected.** They include:
1. `currentValue` - Entries currently in memory being accessed
2. `_loadingKeys` - Entries being fetched from storage
3. `_loadedKeys` - Entries that were loaded into memory

Every eviction check verifies sacred status:
```javascript
if (!sacredKeys.has(k) && m.updatedAt < now - maxAgeMs) {
  // Only evict if NOT sacred
}
```

**Swift equivalent:** Entities in active `@Shared` subscriptions are sacred.

### Q6: Does Swift's pending mutation strategy match TypeScript?

**Mostly yes, with key differences:**

| Aspect | TypeScript | Swift |
|--------|-----------|-------|
| Save timing | Async, throttled (100ms) | Sync, immediate |
| Save blocking | No (fire-and-forget) | Yes (await) |
| Storage | IndexedDB | SQLite |
| Load timing | App startup (lazy) | App startup (explicit) |
| Restoration | On-demand during notification | Explicit phase before first subscription |
| Cleanup | Query-based + timeout-based | **MISSING** ← This is the gap |

### Q7: When does TypeScript save pending mutations to disk?

**Answer:** Asynchronously with 100ms throttle, fire-and-forget.

```javascript
// PersistedObject.ts:501-506
this._nextSave = setTimeout(() => {
  safeIdleCallback(() => {
    this._writeToStorage(opts);  // Fire-and-forget
  }, 100);  // 100ms idle callback
}, 100);  // 100ms throttle
```

**What happens if app closes before server ack?**
1. Mutations persisted to IndexedDB immediately (throttled but persistent)
2. App closes → mutations preserved
3. App reopens → `_flushPendingMessages()` resends unconfirmed mutations
4. Server responds → mutation marked with `tx-id` and `confirmed`
5. Cleanup after 30 seconds via `_cleanupPendingMutationsTimeout()`

Swift matches this except **we're missing the cleanup methods**.

## Priority 1: Cycle Detection in Entity Resolution

### Problem

**File:** `Sources/SharingInstant/Extensions/TripleStore+Extensions.swift` (Lines 19-172)

Current `resolve()` uses depth limiting but NO cycle detection:

```swift
public func resolve(id: String, attrsStore: AttrsStore, depth: Int = 0, maxDepth: Int = 10, includedLinks: Set<String>? = nil) -> [String: Any] {
    if depth > maxDepth { return ["id": id] }  // Only protection
    // ...recursive calls without tracking visited entities
}
```

**Impact:** If Entity A links to B links to A, both are resolved 5 complete cycles before stopping, causing exponential memory growth.

### TypeScript Reference

TypeScript's InstaQL (`instaql.ts`) doesn't explicitly track visited entities, but its query-driven approach naturally limits resolution scope. The Swift implementation needs explicit protection because it resolves ALL links when `includedLinks` is nil.

### Proposed Implementation

```swift
// File: Sources/SharingInstant/Extensions/TripleStore+Extensions.swift

/// Resolves an entity by ID from the TripleStore, with cycle detection.
///
/// - Parameters:
///   - id: The entity ID to resolve
///   - attrsStore: The attributes store for schema info
///   - depth: Current recursion depth (internal use)
///   - maxDepth: Maximum recursion depth (default: 5, reduced from 10)
///   - includedLinks: Links to resolve (nil = all, empty = none)
///   - visited: Set of already-visited entity IDs for cycle detection
/// - Returns: Dictionary representation of the entity
public func resolve(
    id: String,
    attrsStore: AttrsStore,
    depth: Int = 0,
    maxDepth: Int = 5,  // CHANGED: Reduced from 10 to 5
    includedLinks: Set<String>? = nil,
    visited: inout Set<String>  // NEW: Cycle detection
) -> [String: Any] {
    // Cycle detection
    guard !visited.contains(id) else {
        return ["id": id]  // Return minimal representation for cycles
    }
    visited.insert(id)
    defer { visited.remove(id) }  // Allow revisiting in different branches

    // Depth limit
    if depth > maxDepth { return ["id": id] }

    let triples = self.getTriples(entity: id)
    guard !triples.isEmpty else { return ["id": id] }

    var result: [String: Any] = ["id": id]

    // Group triples by attribute
    let triplesByAttr = Dictionary(grouping: triples) { $0.attributeId }

    for (attrId, attrTriples) in triplesByAttr {
        guard let attr = attrsStore.getAttr(attrId) else { continue }
        let label = attr.forwardIdentity.count > 2 ? attr.forwardIdentity[2] : attrId

        if attr.valueType == .ref {
            // Skip links not in includedLinks (if specified)
            if let includedLinks = includedLinks, !includedLinks.contains(label) {
                continue
            }

            // Resolve linked entities with cycle detection
            var resolvedRefs: [[String: Any]] = []
            for triple in attrTriples {
                if case .ref(let targetId) = triple.value {
                    let childObj = resolve(
                        id: targetId,
                        attrsStore: attrsStore,
                        depth: depth + 1,
                        maxDepth: maxDepth,
                        includedLinks: includedLinks,
                        visited: &visited  // Pass visited set
                    )
                    // Skip ghost entities (only have "id")
                    if childObj.count > 1 {
                        resolvedRefs.append(childObj)
                    }
                }
            }

            // Handle cardinality
            if attr.cardinality == .one || attr.isUnique == true {
                result[label] = resolvedRefs.first
            } else {
                result[label] = resolvedRefs
            }
        } else {
            // Non-ref attributes: take most recent value
            if let latestTriple = attrTriples.max(by: { $0.createdAt < $1.createdAt }) {
                result[label] = latestTriple.value.rawValue
            }
        }
    }

    // Resolve reverse links with cycle detection
    if depth < maxDepth, let entityType = attrsStore.getEntityType(forEntityId: id) {
        let reverseAttrs = attrsStore.revIdents[entityType] ?? [:]

        for (reverseLabel, attr) in reverseAttrs {
            if let includedLinks = includedLinks, !includedLinks.contains(reverseLabel) {
                continue
            }

            let reverseTriples = getReverseRefs(entityId: id, attributeId: attr.id)
            var resolvedParents: [[String: Any]] = []

            for triple in reverseTriples {
                let parentObj = resolve(
                    id: triple.entityId,
                    attrsStore: attrsStore,
                    depth: depth + 1,
                    maxDepth: maxDepth,
                    includedLinks: includedLinks,
                    visited: &visited  // Pass visited set
                )
                if parentObj.count > 1 {
                    resolvedParents.append(parentObj)
                }
            }

            if attr.cardinality == .one || attr.isUnique == true {
                result[reverseLabel] = resolvedParents.first
            } else {
                result[reverseLabel] = resolvedParents
            }
        }
    }

    return result
}

// Convenience overload that creates the visited set
public func resolve(
    id: String,
    attrsStore: AttrsStore,
    depth: Int = 0,
    maxDepth: Int = 5,
    includedLinks: Set<String>? = nil
) -> [String: Any] {
    var visited = Set<String>()
    return resolve(
        id: id,
        attrsStore: attrsStore,
        depth: depth,
        maxDepth: maxDepth,
        includedLinks: includedLinks,
        visited: &visited
    )
}
```

```swift
// Test case: A -> B -> A cycle
func testCycleDetection() {
    let store = TripleStore()
    let attrsStore = AttrsStore()

    // Setup: A links to B, B links to A
    store.addTriples([
        Triple(entityId: "a", attributeId: "link-to-b", value: .ref("b"), createdAt: 1),
        Triple(entityId: "b", attributeId: "link-to-a", value: .ref("a"), createdAt: 1),
```

## Priority 2: TripleStore Garbage Collection

### Problem

**File:** `Sources/SharingInstant/InstantDependency.swift`

```swift
private enum InstantReactorKey: DependencyKey {
    static let liveValue = Reactor(store: SharedTripleStore())  // Singleton - never GC'd
}
```

The TripleStore grows unboundedly with no eviction mechanism.

### TypeScript Reference

**File:** `instant/client/packages/core/src/utils/PersistedObject.ts` (Lines 350-472)

```javascript
// GC Configuration
export type GCOpts = {
  maxSize: number;     // Maximum total size in bytes
  maxAgeMs: number;    // Maximum age before eligible for GC
  maxEntries: number;  // Maximum number of entries
};

// GC Algorithm (4 phases)
private async _gc() {
  // Phase 1: Remove orphaned keys (in storage but not in meta)
  for (const key of keys) {
    if (sacredKeys.has(key) || key in meta.objects) continue;
    promises.push(this._persister.removeItem(key));
  }

  // Phase 2: Remove entries older than maxAgeMs
  for (const [k, m] of Object.entries(meta.objects)) {
    if (!sacredKeys.has(k) && m.updatedAt < now - this._gcOpts.maxAgeMs) {
      promises.push(this._persister.removeItem(k));
      delete meta.objects[k];
    }
  }

  // Phase 3: Enforce maxEntries limit (LRU by updatedAt)
  const entries = Object.entries(meta.objects).sort((a, b) =>
    a[1].updatedAt - b[1].updatedAt
  );
  const deletable = entries.filter(([x]) => !sacredKeys.has(x));
  if (entries.length > this._gcOpts.maxEntries) {
    for (const [k] of deletable.slice(0, entries.length - this._gcOpts.maxEntries)) {
      promises.push(this._persister.removeItem(k));
      delete meta.objects[k];
    }
  }

  // Phase 4: Enforce maxSize limit (LRU by updatedAt)
  let currentSize = entries.reduce((acc, [_, m]) => acc + m.size, 0);
  while (currentSize > this._gcOpts.maxSize && deletable.length) {
    const [[k, m]] = deletable.splice(0, 1);
    currentSize -= m.size;
    promises.push(this._persister.removeItem(k));
    delete meta.objects[k];
  }
}
```

### Proposed Implementation

```swift
// File: Sources/SharingInstant/Internal/TripleStoreGC.swift (NEW FILE)

import Foundation

/// Configuration for TripleStore garbage collection
public struct TripleStoreGCConfig: Sendable {
    /// Maximum number of triples to keep in the store
    public let maxTriples: Int

    /// Maximum age in seconds before a triple is eligible for GC
    public let maxAgeSeconds: TimeInterval

    /// Maximum number of unique entities to track
    public let maxEntities: Int

    /// Interval between GC runs in seconds
    public let gcIntervalSeconds: TimeInterval

    public static let `default` = TripleStoreGCConfig(
        maxTriples: 100_000,
        maxAgeSeconds: 60 * 60 * 24 * 7,  // 1 week
        maxEntities: 10_000,
        gcIntervalSeconds: 60  // 1 minute
    )

    public static let aggressive = TripleStoreGCConfig(
        maxTriples: 10_000,
        maxAgeSeconds: 60 * 60,  // 1 hour
        maxEntities: 1_000,
        gcIntervalSeconds: 30
    )
}

/// Tracks entity access for LRU eviction
struct EntityAccessRecord: Sendable {
    let entityId: String
    var lastAccessedAt: TimeInterval
    var tripleCount: Int
}

/// Garbage collector for TripleStore
public actor TripleStoreGC {
    private let store: SharedTripleStore
    private let config: TripleStoreGCConfig
    private var entityAccess: [String: EntityAccessRecord] = [:]
    private var sacredEntities: Set<String> = []  // Entities in active subscriptions
    private var gcTask: Task<Void, Never>?

    public init(store: SharedTripleStore, config: TripleStoreGCConfig = .default) {
        self.store = store
        self.config = config
    }

    /// Start periodic garbage collection
    public func start() {
        guard gcTask == nil else { return }

        gcTask = Task { [weak self] in
            while !Task.isCancelled {
                try? await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: UInt64(self?.config.gcIntervalSeconds ?? 60) * 1_000_000_000)
                await self?.runGC()
            }
        }
    }

    /// Stop garbage collection
    public func stop() {
        gcTask?.cancel()
        gcTask = nil
    }

    /// Mark entities as sacred (in active subscriptions, cannot be evicted)
    public func markSacred(_ entityIds: Set<String>) {
        sacredEntities.formUnion(entityIds)
    }

    /// Unmark entities as sacred
    public func unmarkSacred(_ entityIds: Set<String>) {
        sacredEntities.subtract(entityIds)
    }

    /// Record entity access for LRU tracking
    public func recordAccess(entityId: String, tripleCount: Int = 1) {
        let now = Date().timeIntervalSince1970
        if var record = entityAccess[entityId] {
            record.lastAccessedAt = now
            record.tripleCount = tripleCount
            entityAccess[entityId] = record
        } else {
            entityAccess[entityId] = EntityAccessRecord(
                entityId: entityId,
                lastAccessedAt: now,
                tripleCount: tripleCount
            )
        }
    }

    /// Run garbage collection
    public func runGC() async -> GCResult {
        let now = Date().timeIntervalSince1970
        var result = GCResult()

        // Phase 1: Remove orphaned entity access records
        let storeEntityIds = store.getAllEntityIds()
        for entityId in entityAccess.keys where !storeEntityIds.contains(entityId) {
            entityAccess.removeValue(forKey: entityId)
            result.orphanedRecordsRemoved += 1
        }

        // Phase 2: Remove entities older than maxAgeSeconds
        for (entityId, record) in entityAccess {
            guard !sacredEntities.contains(entityId) else { continue }

            if record.lastAccessedAt < now - config.maxAgeSeconds {
                store.deleteEntity(id: entityId)
                entityAccess.removeValue(forKey: entityId)
                result.agedOutEntities += 1
            }
        }

        // Phase 3: Enforce maxEntities limit (LRU)
        if entityAccess.count > config.maxEntities {
            let sortedByAccess = entityAccess.values
                .filter { !sacredEntities.contains($0.entityId) }
                .sorted { $0.lastAccessedAt < $1.lastAccessedAt }

            let toRemove = sortedByAccess.prefix(entityAccess.count - config.maxEntities)
            for record in toRemove {
                store.deleteEntity(id: record.entityId)
                entityAccess.removeValue(forKey: record.entityId)
                result.lruEvictedEntities += 1
            }
        }

        // Phase 4: Enforce maxTriples limit (LRU by entity)
        let totalTriples = entityAccess.values.reduce(0) { $0 + $1.tripleCount }
        if totalTriples > config.maxTriples {
            let sortedByAccess = entityAccess.values
                .filter { !sacredEntities.contains($0.entityId) }
                .sorted { $0.lastAccessedAt < $1.lastAccessedAt }

            var currentTotal = totalTriples
            for record in sortedByAccess {
                guard currentTotal > config.maxTriples else { break }
                store.deleteEntity(id: record.entityId)
                entityAccess.removeValue(forKey: record.entityId)
                currentTotal -= record.tripleCount
                result.sizeEvictedEntities += 1
            }
        }

        return result
    }
}

public struct GCResult: Sendable {
    var orphanedRecordsRemoved: Int = 0
    var agedOutEntities: Int = 0
    var lruEvictedEntities: Int = 0
    var sizeEvictedEntities: Int = 0

    var totalEvicted: Int {
        agedOutEntities + lruEvictedEntities + sizeEvictedEntities
    }
}
```

## Priority 3: Pending Mutation Cleanup

### Problem

Swift has NO mechanism to clean up confirmed pending mutations. They accumulate indefinitely.

### TypeScript Reference

**File:** `instant/client/packages/core/src/Reactor.js`

#### Method 1: Query-Based Cleanup (Lines 1461-1476)

```javascript
_cleanupPendingMutationsQueries() {
  // Find minimum processedTxId across all queries
  let minProcessedTxId = Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER;
  for (const { result } of Object.values(this.querySubs.currentValue)) {
    if (result?.processedTxId) {
      minProcessedTxId = Math.min(minProcessedTxId, result?.processedTxId);
    }
  }

  // Remove mutations where tx-id <= minProcessedTxId
  // (all queries have seen this mutation's effects)
  this._updatePendingMutations((prev) => {
    for (const [eventId, mut] of Array.from(prev.entries())) {
      if (mut['tx-id'] && mut['tx-id'] <= minProcessedTxId) {
        prev.delete(eventId);
      }
    }
  });
}
```

#### Method 2: Timeout-Based Cleanup (Lines 1483-1500)

```javascript
_cleanupPendingMutationsTimeout() {
  if (this._pendingMutations().size < this._pendingMutationCleanupThreshold) {
    return;  // Only run if threshold exceeded (200)
  }

  const now = Date.now();

  this._updatePendingMutations((prev) => {
    for (const [eventId, mut] of Array.from(prev.entries())) {
      // Remove if confirmed > 30 seconds ago
      if (mut.confirmed && mut.confirmed + this._pendingTxCleanupTimeout < now) {
        prev.delete(eventId);
      }
    }
  });
}
```

### Proposed Implementation

```swift
// File: Sources/SharingInstant/Internal/Reactor.swift

// Add to actor properties:
private var queryProcessedTxIds: [String: Int] = [:]  // queryHash -> processedTxId
private let pendingMutationCleanupThreshold = 200
private let pendingTxCleanupTimeoutSeconds: TimeInterval = 30

// Add cleanup methods:

/// Cleans up pending mutations that all queries have processed.
///
/// ## Algorithm (TypeScript Parity)
/// 1. Find minimum processedTxId across all active query subscriptions
/// 2. Remove mutations where txId <= minProcessedTxId
///
/// This works because:
/// - Server sends `processedTxId` with each query result
/// - If ALL queries have processedTxId >= mutation's txId, the mutation is in server state
/// - We can safely remove it from pending queue
private func cleanupPendingMutationsQueries() async {
    guard !queryProcessedTxIds.isEmpty else { return }

    // Find minimum processedTxId
    let minProcessedTxId = queryProcessedTxIds.values.min() ?? Int.max

    // Get client to access pending mutations
    let client = await MainActor.run {
        InstantClientFactory.makeClient(appID: currentAppID, instanceID: clientInstanceID)
    }

    // Get pending mutations and remove confirmed ones
    let pendingMutations = await client.getUnconfirmedPendingMutations()

    for mutation in pendingMutations {
        guard let txId = mutation.txId, txId <= minProcessedTxId else { continue }

        // Remove from SQLite
        await client.removePendingMutation(eventId: mutation.eventId)
    }
}

/// Cleans up old pending mutations that have been confirmed but not processed by queries.
///
/// ## Algorithm (TypeScript Parity)
/// - Only run if pendingMutations.count > threshold (200)
/// - Remove mutations confirmed > 30 seconds ago
/// - These mutations probably don't affect any active queries
private func cleanupPendingMutationsTimeout() async {
    let client = await MainActor.run {
        InstantClientFactory.makeClient(appID: currentAppID, instanceID: clientInstanceID)
    }

    let pendingMutations = await client.getUnconfirmedPendingMutations()

    guard pendingMutations.count >= pendingMutationCleanupThreshold else { return }

    let now = Date().timeIntervalSince1970

    for mutation in pendingMutations {
        guard let confirmedAt = mutation.confirmedAt else { continue }

        if confirmedAt + pendingTxCleanupTimeoutSeconds < now {
            await client.removePendingMutation(eventId: mutation.eventId)
        }
    }
}

/// Called when a query receives results from server.
/// Updates processedTxId tracking and triggers cleanup.
func updateQueryProcessedTxId(queryHash: String, processedTxId: Int) async {
    queryProcessedTxIds[queryHash] = processedTxId

    // Run cleanup after processing
    await cleanupPendingMutationsQueries()
    await cleanupPendingMutationsTimeout()
}

/// Called when a query subscription ends.
func removeQueryProcessedTxId(queryHash: String) {
    queryProcessedTxIds.removeValue(forKey: queryHash)
}
```

## Priority 4: Query Result Caching with Version Tracking

### Problem

Swift recomputes query results from scratch on every update, unlike TypeScript which uses version-based caching.

### TypeScript Reference

**File:** `instant/client/packages/core/src/Reactor.js` (Lines 1224-1261)

```javascript
dataForQuery(hash) {
  // Get versions
  const querySubVersion = this.querySubs.version();
  const pendingMutationsVersion = this.kv.version();

  // Check cache
  const cached = this._dataForQueryCache[hash];
  if (
    cached &&
    querySubVersion === cached.querySubVersion &&
    pendingMutationsVersion === cached.pendingMutationsVersion
  ) {
    return cached;  // Cache hit!
  }

  // Cache miss - recompute
  const { store, attrsStore, pageInfo, aggregate, processedTxId } = result;
  const mutations = this._rewriteMutationsSorted(attrsStore, pendingMutations);
  const { store: newStore, attrsStore: newAttrsStore } =
    this._applyOptimisticUpdates(store, attrsStore, mutations, processedTxId);
  const resp = instaql({ store: newStore, attrsStore: newAttrsStore }, q);

  // Update cache
  return { data: resp, querySubVersion, pendingMutationsVersion };
}
```

### Proposed Implementation

```swift
// File: Sources/SharingInstant/Internal/Reactor.swift

// Add to actor properties:
private var storeVersion: Int = 0
private var pendingMutationsVersion: Int = 0
private var queryResultCache: [String: CachedQueryResult] = [:]

struct CachedQueryResult: Sendable {
    let data: [Any]  // Encoded entities
    let storeVersion: Int
    let pendingMutationsVersion: Int
    let processedTxId: Int?
}

// Increment versions on changes:

func incrementStoreVersion() {
    storeVersion += 1
}

func incrementPendingMutationsVersion() {
    pendingMutationsVersion += 1
}

// In SubscriptionState.handleStoreUpdate():

func handleStoreUpdate() async {
    let queryHash = computeQueryHash()

    // Check cache
    if let cached = await reactor.getCachedResult(queryHash: queryHash),
       cached.storeVersion == await reactor.storeVersion,
       cached.pendingMutationsVersion == await reactor.pendingMutationsVersion {
        // Cache hit - use cached data
        if let values = decodeCachedData(cached.data) {
            continuation.yield(values)
            return
        }
    }

    // Cache miss - recompute (existing logic)
    let client = await MainActor.run {
        InstantClientFactory.makeClient(appID: appID, instanceID: clientInstanceID)
    }
    let pendingMutations = await client.getUnconfirmedPendingMutations()

    // ... existing merge logic ...

    var values: [Value] = []
    for id in allIDs {
        // ... existing resolution logic ...
    }

    // Update cache
    await reactor.setCachedResult(
        queryHash: queryHash,
        data: values.map { try? $0.asDictionary() }.compactMap { $0 },
        processedTxId: currentProcessedTxId
    )

    continuation.yield(values)
}

// Helper to compute query hash (match TypeScript's weakHash)
private func computeQueryHash() -> String {
    var hasher = Hasher()
    hasher.combine(namespace)
    hasher.combine(orderByIsDescending)
    for link in includedLinks.sorted() {
        hasher.combine(link)
    }
    return String(hasher.finalize())
}
```

## Priority 5: Cache Pending Mutations in Reactor

### Problem

**File:** `Sources/SharingInstant/Internal/Reactor.swift` (Lines 1283-1290)

Every `handleStoreUpdate()` call fetches ALL pending mutations from SQLite:

```swift
let pendingMutations = await client.getUnconfirmedPendingMutations()
```

With rapid updates (7-8ms intervals during transcription), this causes significant overhead.

### TypeScript Reference

TypeScript caches pending mutations in memory and only reads from IndexedDB on startup:

```javascript
// Reactor.js
_pendingMutations() {
  return this.kv.currentValue.pendingMutations ?? new Map();  // In-memory!
}
```

### Proposed Implementation

```swift
// File: Sources/SharingInstant/Internal/Reactor.swift

// Add to actor properties:
private var cachedPendingMutations: [String: CachedMutation] = [:]
private var pendingMutationsLoaded = false

struct CachedMutation: Sendable {
    let eventId: String
    let txSteps: [[AnySendable]]
    let createdAt: TimeInterval
    var txId: Int?
    var confirmedAt: TimeInterval?
    let order: Int
}

// Load from SQLite once on first access:
private func loadPendingMutationsIfNeeded() async {
    guard !pendingMutationsLoaded else { return }

    let client = await MainActor.run {
        InstantClientFactory.makeClient(appID: currentAppID, instanceID: clientInstanceID)
    }

    let mutations = await client.getUnconfirmedPendingMutations()

    for mutation in mutations {
        cachedPendingMutations[mutation.eventId] = CachedMutation(
            eventId: mutation.eventId,
            txSteps: mutation.txSteps,
            createdAt: mutation.createdAt,
            txId: mutation.txId,
            confirmedAt: mutation.confirmedAt,
            order: mutation.order
        )
    }

    pendingMutationsLoaded = true
}

// Use cache for reads:
func getPendingMutations() async -> [CachedMutation] {
    await loadPendingMutationsIfNeeded()
    return Array(cachedPendingMutations.values).sorted { $0.order < $1.order }
}

// Update cache on mutations:
func addPendingMutation(_ mutation: CachedMutation) async {
    cachedPendingMutations[mutation.eventId] = mutation
    pendingMutationsVersion += 1

    // Also persist to SQLite (fire-and-forget)
    Task {
        let client = await MainActor.run {
            InstantClientFactory.makeClient(appID: currentAppID, instanceID: clientInstanceID)
        }
        await client.persistPendingMutation(mutation)
    }
}

func confirmPendingMutation(eventId: String, txId: Int) async {
    guard var mutation = cachedPendingMutations[eventId] else { return }

    mutation.txId = txId
    mutation.confirmedAt = Date().timeIntervalSince1970
    cachedPendingMutations[eventId] = mutation
    pendingMutationsVersion += 1
}

func removePendingMutation(eventId: String) async {
    cachedPendingMutations.removeValue(forKey: eventId)
    pendingMutationsVersion += 1
}
```

```swift
// File: Tests/SharingInstantTests/CycleDetectionSharedTests.swift

import XCTest
import Sharing
@testable import SharingInstant

final class CycleDetectionSharedTests: XCTestCase {

    /// Test that circular entity references don't cause infinite loops
    /// Uses @Shared property wrapper to exercise the full API path
    func testCircularLinksWithSharedWrapper() async throws {
        // Create entities that reference each other
        @Shared(.instantSync(Schema.users)) var users: IdentifiedArrayOf<User> = []
        @Shared(.instantSync(Schema.posts)) var posts: IdentifiedArrayOf<Post> = []

        let userId = UUID().uuidString
        let postId = UUID().uuidString

        // Create user
        try await $users.create(User(id: userId, name: "Test"))

        // Create post by user (user -> posts link)
        try await $posts.create(Post(id: postId, title: "Test Post"))
        try await $posts.link(postId, "author", to: User(id: userId, name: ""))

        // Now query user.with(\.posts).with(\.author) - creates A -> B -> A
        @Shared(.instantSync(Schema.users.with(\.posts).with(\.author)))
        var usersWithCycle: IdentifiedArrayOf<User> = []

        // Wait for subscription to populate
        try await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(1))

        // Should complete without infinite loop
        XCTAssertFalse(usersWithCycle.isEmpty)

        // Verify cycle was broken (author shouldn't have posts again)
        if let user = usersWithCycle.first,
           let post = user.posts?.first,
           let author = post.author {
            XCTAssertNil(author.posts, "Cycle should be broken - author shouldn't have posts")
        }
    }

    /// Test memory doesn't grow unboundedly during rapid updates
    func testRapidUpdatesMemoryStable() async throws {
        @Shared(.instantSync(Schema.transcriptionSegments))
        var segments: IdentifiedArrayOf<TranscriptionSegment> = []

        let startMemory = getMemoryUsage()

        // Simulate 100 rapid updates (similar to RapidTranscriptionDemo)
        for i in 0..<100 {
            let segment = TranscriptionSegment(
                id: UUID().uuidString,
                startTime: Double(i) * 0.1,
                endTime: Double(i + 1) * 0.1,
                text: "Segment \(i)",
                segmentIndex: Double(i),
                isFinalized: false,
                ingestedAt: ISO8601DateFormatter().string(from: Date()),
                speaker: nil,
                words: nil
            )
            try await $segments.create(segment)

            // Brief delay to simulate real timing
            try await Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(10))
        }

        let endMemory = getMemoryUsage()
        let memoryGrowth = endMemory - startMemory

        // Memory should not grow more than 50MB for 100 segments
        XCTAssertLessThan(memoryGrowth, 50_000_000, "Memory grew excessively: \(memoryGrowth / 1_000_000)MB")
    }

    private func getMemoryUsage() -> Int {
        var info = mach_task_basic_info()
        var count = mach_msg_type_number_t(MemoryLayout<mach_task_basic_info>.size) / 4
        let result = withUnsafeMutablePointer(to: &info) {
            $0.withMemoryRebound(to: integer_t.self, capacity: Int(count)) {
                task_info(mach_task_self_, task_flavor_t(MACH_TASK_BASIC_INFO), $0, &count)
            }
        }
        return result == KERN_SUCCESS ? Int(info.resident_size) : 0
    }
}
```

## Summary

I implemented **Priority 1: Cycle Detection in Entity Resolution** by modifying `/Users/mlustig/Development/personal/instantdb/sharing-instant/Sources/SharingInstant/Extensions/TripleStore+Extensions.swift`.

### Changes Made

1. **Added `visited: inout Set<String>` parameter** to the main `resolve()` function to track entity IDs currently being resolved in the current resolution path.

2. **Cycle detection logic** at the start of `resolve()`:
   - Check if the ID is already in the visited set
   - If so, return `["id": id]` immediately to break the cycle
   - Add the ID to visited at the start
   - Use `defer { visited.remove(id) }` to remove it when exiting (this allows revisiting the same entity in different branches of the resolution tree)

3. **Reduced default maxDepth from 10 to 5** for additional safety on mobile devices with limited memory.

4. **Created a convenience overload** without the `visited` parameter that creates the visited set internally, ensuring backward compatibility for existing callers.

5. **Updated all recursive calls** (forward refs at line 90, string refs at line 102, and reverse links at lines 155-162) to pass the `visited` set through.

### Why This Matters

Without cycle detection, circular entity references like `A -> B -> A` would cause the resolver to traverse the cycle multiple times (up to maxDepth), leading to:
- Exponential memory growth
- Performance degradation
- Potential crashes on memory-constrained devices

The `defer { visited.remove(id) }` pattern is important because it allows the same entity to appear in different branches of the resolution tree. For example, if entities A and B both link to C, C should be fully resolved for both A and B independently.

## Summary

### Created `/Users/mlustig/Development/personal/instantdb/sharing-instant/Sources/SharingInstant/Internal/TripleStoreGC.swift`

The file contains:

1. **`TripleStoreGCConfig`** - Configuration struct with presets:
   - `default`: Conservative settings for most apps (100K triples, 10K entities, 24h age limit, 60s GC interval)
   - `aggressive`: For memory-constrained environments (10K triples, 1K entities, 1h age limit, 30s interval)
   - `disabled`: For testing or manual control (no automatic GC)

2. **`EntityAccessRecord`** - Tracks entity access times for LRU eviction with:
   - `entityId`: The entity being tracked
   - `lastAccessedAt`: Unix timestamp of last access
   - `tripleCount`: Number of triples for the entity

3. **`GCResult`** - Metrics from GC runs:
   - `orphanedRecordsRemoved`: Access records for deleted entities
   - `agedOutEntities`: Entities evicted due to age
   - `lruEvictedEntities`: Entities evicted due to entity count limit
   - `sizeEvictedEntities`: Entities evicted due to triple count limit

4. **`GCDiagnostics`** - Runtime state information

5. **`TripleStoreGC` actor** - Main implementation with 4-phase GC algorithm:
   - **Phase 1**: Remove orphaned access records (entities no longer in store)
   - **Phase 2**: Age-based eviction (entities older than maxAgeSeconds)
   - **Phase 3**: Entity count limit enforcement (LRU eviction)
   - **Phase 4**: Triple count limit enforcement (LRU eviction)

### Key Features:
- Sacred entities (in active subscriptions) are never evicted
- Background periodic GC with configurable interval
- Manual GC trigger via `runGC()`
- Sacred entity refresh callback for Reactor integration
- Thread-safe actor-based design matching Swift concurrency patterns

- `getTripleCount()` - Returns total triple count
- `getTripleCount(for:)` - Returns triple count for specific entity

The TripleStoreGC is designed to be integrated with the Reactor via a callback mechanism (`setSacredEntityRefreshCallback`). The Reactor integration code was prepared but due to concurrent file modifications, the Reactor changes should be applied in a separate commit to ensure stability. The GC can be integrated by:

2. Initializing GC in Reactor's init
3. Calling `gc.markSacred()` when subscriptions start
4. Calling `gc.unmarkSacred()` when subscriptions end
5. Calling `gc.recordAccess()` when entities are accessed

Implement Priority 5: Cache Pending Mutations in Reactor Memory

## Context
You are working on the SharingInstant Swift SDK. The plan is at /Users/mlustig/.claude/plans/groovy-kindling-whisper.md

## Task
Cache pending mutations in Reactor memory instead of querying SQLite on every handleStoreUpdate().

## Problem
Currently every `handleStoreUpdate()` calls:
```swift
let pendingMutations = await client.getUnconfirmedPendingMutations()
```

With rapid updates (7-8ms intervals during transcription), this causes significant SQLite overhead.

## Requirements

### 1. Add cache properties to Reactor

```swift
private var cachedPendingMutations: [String: CachedMutation] = [:]
private var pendingMutationsLoaded = false

struct CachedMutation: Sendable {
    let eventId: String
    let txSteps: [[String: Any]]
    let createdAt: TimeInterval
    var txId: Int?
    var confirmedAt: TimeInterval?
    let order: Int
}
```

### 2. Implement cache methods

**`loadPendingMutationsIfNeeded()`:**
- Only load from SQLite once on first access
- Set `pendingMutationsLoaded = true` after loading

**`getPendingMutations() -> [CachedMutation]`:**
- Call loadPendingMutationsIfNeeded()
- Return sorted array from cache

**`addPendingMutation(_ mutation: CachedMutation)`:**
- Add to cache
- Increment pendingMutationsVersion
- Persist to SQLite in fire-and-forget Task

**`confirmPendingMutation(eventId: String, txId: Int)`:**
- Update mutation in cache with txId and confirmedAt
- Increment pendingMutationsVersion

**`removePendingMutation(eventId: String)`:**
- Remove from cache
- Increment pendingMutationsVersion

### 3. Update handleStoreUpdate

Replace:
```swift
let pendingMutations = await client.getUnconfirmedPendingMutations()
```

With:
```swift
let pendingMutations = await reactor.getPendingMutations()
```

### 4. Update transact flow

When a mutation is created, call `addPendingMutation()`.
When server confirms, call `confirmPendingMutation()`.

## TypeScript Reference
TypeScript caches in memory (`this.kv.currentValue.pendingMutations`) and only reads from IndexedDB on startup.

```swift
    let data: [[String: Any]]  // Encoded entities as dictionaries
    let storeVersion: Int
    let pendingMutationsVersion: Int

}
```

### 3. Add cache methods to Reactor

- `incrementPendingMutationsVersion()` - call when mutations change
- `getCachedResult(queryHash: String) -> CachedQueryResult?`
- `setCachedResult(queryHash: String, data: [[String: Any]], processedTxId: Int?)`

### 4. Update SubscriptionState to use cache

In `Sources/SharingInstant/Internal/SubscriptionState.swift` or wherever `handleStoreUpdate()` is:

Before recomputing:
1. Compute query hash from namespace, orderBy, includedLinks
2. Check if cache has a valid result (matching store/mutation versions)
3. If cache hit, decode and yield cached data
4. If cache miss, recompute and update cache

### 5. Compute query hash

```swift
private func computeQueryHash() -> String {
    var hasher = Hasher()
    hasher.combine(namespace)
    hasher.combine(orderByIsDescending)
    for link in includedLinks.sorted() {
        hasher.combine(link)
    }
    return String(hasher.finalize())
}
```

- `pendingMutationsVersion === cached.pendingMutationsVersion`

     1→# SharingInstant Memory & Performance Fixes - Implementation Plan
     2→
     3→## Executive Summary
     4→
     5→This plan addresses **CRITICAL** and **HIGH** priority memory issues in the SharingInstant Swift SDK identified through comprehensive analysis of:
     6→- TypeScript Reactor.js cleanup mechanisms
     7→- TypeScript Store/PersistedObject GC patterns
     8→- Swift Reactor current implementation gaps

    19→
    20→## Answers to Design Questions
    21→
    22→### Q1: Why is Swift's approach different from TypeScript's query-driven approach?
    23→
    24→**TypeScript (Query-Driven):** In TypeScript, the query object structure defines exactly what gets resolved. The `instaql.ts` function only traverses links that exist as keys in the query form:
    25→
    26→```javascript
    27→// TypeScript: Only resolves links that are KEYS in the query
    28→{ users: { posts: {} } }  // Only resolves "posts" link, ignores all others
    29→```
    30→
    31→**Swift (Currently Broken):** Swift's `resolve()` with `includedLinks = nil` resolves ALL links:
    32→
    33→```swift
    34→// Swift: resolve() with includedLinks = nil resolves EVERYTHING
    35→if let includedLinks = includedLinks, !includedLinks.contains(label) {
    36→    continue  // Only skips if includedLinks WAS PROVIDED
    37→}
    38→// If nil, ALL links are resolved - this is the bug!
    39→```
    40→
    41→**Is this a platform limitation?** Partially. Swift lacks JavaScript's ability to introspect query-as-data structure at runtime. However, this is solvable because:
    42→1. The `.with(\.link)` chain is parsed at compile time into a `linkTree`
    43→2. We CAN pass the `linkTree` down to `resolve()` as `includedLinks`
    44→3. The problem is **we're not doing this correctly**
    45→
    46→**Which approach is better?** TypeScript's query-driven approach is superior because:
    47→- Only fetches what's needed (memory efficient)
    48→- Predictable: same query → same structure
    49→- Cache-friendly: query hash determines cache key
    50→- No N+1 surprises
    51→
    52→**Fix:** Make `includedLinks` required or default to empty set (resolve nothing):
    53→
    54→```swift
    55→// PROPOSED: Default to empty set (resolve NO links unless specified)
    56→public func resolve(
    57→    id: String,
    58→    attrsStore: AttrsStore,
    59→    includedLinks: Set<String> = []  // NOT nil!
    60→) -> [String: Any]
    61→```
    62→
    63→### Q2: Why is `includedLinks = nil` including everything a bad default?
    64→
    65→This is **ridiculous** as the user noted. The current behavior:
    66→- `nil` = resolve ALL links recursively (dangerous)
    67→- `Set()` = resolve NO links (safe)
    68→
    69→This should be inverted:
    70→- Required parameter or default to `[]` (resolve nothing)
    71→- Explicit list required to resolve links
    72→
    73→This matches TypeScript where you must explicitly specify child queries:
    74→```javascript
    75→// TypeScript: Must explicitly name links to resolve
    76→{ users: { posts: { comments: {} } } }  // 3 levels deep, all explicit
    77→```
    78→

    80→
    81→**Scenario causing orphaned keys:**
    82→
    83→1. **Crash during save:** Key written to IndexedDB, then app crashes before `__meta` is updated
    84→2. **Multi-tab race:** Tab A deletes key, crashes before updating meta; Tab B sees stale meta
    85→3. **Corruption:** IndexedDB gets corrupted or manually edited

    87→**TypeScript detection (PersistedObject.ts:388-397):**

    89→for (const key of keys) {
    90→  if (sacredKeys.has(key) || key in meta.objects) continue;
    91→  this._log.info('Lost track of key in meta', key);  // ORPHAN!
    92→  promises.push(this._persister.removeItem(key));
    93→}
    94→```

    96→### Q4: What are TypeScript's default GC values?
    97→
    98→**For `querySubs` (query results) - Reactor.js:433-437:**
    99→```javascript
   100→gc: {
   101→  maxAgeMs: 1000 * 60 * 60 * 24 * 7 * 52,  // 1 YEAR
   102→  maxEntries: 1000,
   103→  maxSize: 1_000_000,  // 1 million triples
   104→}
   105→```
   106→
   107→**For `kv` store (pending mutations):**

   111→
   112→**GC schedule:** ~1 minute with 0-500ms jitter (prevents multi-tab race)

   114→**Reasonable Swift defaults (more aggressive since mobile):**

   118→    maxAgeSeconds: 60 * 60 * 24,   // 1 day (vs 1 year)
   119→    maxEntities: 10_000,           // 10x less than TS
   120→    gcIntervalSeconds: 60

   122→```
   123→
   124→### Q5: "Sacred" terminology - What does it mean?
   125→
   126→**Sacred keys are entities that MUST NOT be garbage collected.** They include:
   127→1. `currentValue` - Entries currently in memory being accessed
   128→2. `_loadingKeys` - Entries being fetched from storage
   129→3. `_loadedKeys` - Entries that were loaded into memory
   130→
   131→Every eviction check verifies sacred status:
   132→```javascript
   133→if (!sacredKeys.has(k) && m.updatedAt < now - maxAgeMs) {
   134→  // Only evict if NOT sacred
   135→}
   136→```
   137→
   138→**Swift equivalent:** Entities in active `@Shared` subscriptions are sacred.
   139→
   140→### Q6: Does Swift's pending mutation strategy match TypeScript?
   141→
   142→**Mostly yes, with key differences:**
   143→
   144→| Aspect | TypeScript | Swift |
   145→|--------|-----------|-------|
   146→| Save timing | Async, throttled (100ms) | Sync, immediate |
   147→| Save blocking | No (fire-and-forget) | Yes (await) |
   148→| Storage | IndexedDB | SQLite |
   149→| Load timing | App startup (lazy) | App startup (explicit) |
   150→| Restoration | On-demand during notification | Explicit phase before first subscription |
   151→| Cleanup | Query-based + timeout-based | **MISSING** ← This is the gap |
   152→
   153→### Q7: When does TypeScript save pending mutations to disk?
   154→
   155→**Answer:** Asynchronously with 100ms throttle, fire-and-forget.

   157→```javascript
   158→// PersistedObject.ts:501-506
   159→this._nextSave = setTimeout(() => {

   162→  }, 100);  // 100ms idle callback
   163→}, 100);  // 100ms throttle

   167→1. Mutations persisted to IndexedDB immediately (throttled but persistent)
   168→2. App closes → mutations preserved
   169→3. App reopens → `_flushPendingMessages()` resends unconfirmed mutations
   170→4. Server responds → mutation marked with `tx-id` and `confirmed`
   171→5. Cleanup after 30 seconds via `_cleanupPendingMutationsTimeout()`
   172→
   173→Swift matches this except **we're missing the cleanup methods**.

   176→
   177→## Priority 1: Cycle Detection in Entity Resolution
   178→
   179→### Problem
   180→
   181→**File:** `Sources/SharingInstant/Extensions/TripleStore+Extensions.swift` (Lines 19-172)
   182→
   183→Current `resolve()` uses depth limiting but NO cycle detection:
   184→
   185→```swift
   186→public func resolve(id: String, attrsStore: AttrsStore, depth: Int = 0, maxDepth: Int = 10, includedLinks: Set<String>? = nil) -> [String: Any] {
   187→    if depth > maxDepth { return ["id": id] }  // Only protection
   188→    // ...recursive calls without tracking visited entities
   189→}
   190→```
   191→
   192→**Impact:** If Entity A links to B links to A, both are resolved 5 complete cycles before stopping, causing exponential memory growth.
   193→
   194→### TypeScript Reference
   195→
   196→TypeScript's InstaQL (`instaql.ts`) doesn't explicitly track visited entities, but its query-driven approach naturally limits resolution scope. The Swift implementation needs explicit protection because it resolves ALL links when `includedLinks` is nil.
   197→
   198→### Proposed Implementation
   199→
   200→```swift
   201→// File: Sources/SharingInstant/Extensions/TripleStore+Extensions.swift
   202→
   203→/// Resolves an entity by ID from the TripleStore, with cycle detection.
   204→///
   205→/// - Parameters:
   206→///   - id: The entity ID to resolve
   207→///   - attrsStore: The attributes store for schema info
   208→///   - depth: Current recursion depth (internal use)
   209→///   - maxDepth: Maximum recursion depth (default: 5, reduced from 10)
   210→///   - includedLinks: Links to resolve (nil = all, empty = none)
   211→///   - visited: Set of already-visited entity IDs for cycle detection
   212→/// - Returns: Dictionary representation of the entity
   213→public func resolve(
   214→    id: String,
   215→    attrsStore: AttrsStore,
   216→    depth: Int = 0,
   217→    maxDepth: Int = 5,  // CHANGED: Reduced from 10 to 5
   218→    includedLinks: Set<String>? = nil,
   219→    visited: inout Set<String>  // NEW: Cycle detection
   220→) -> [String: Any] {
   221→    // Cycle detection
   222→    guard !visited.contains(id) else {
   223→        return ["id": id]  // Return minimal representation for cycles
   224→    }
   225→    visited.insert(id)
   226→    defer { visited.remove(id) }  // Allow revisiting in different branches
   227→
   228→    // Depth limit
   229→    if depth > maxDepth { return ["id": id] }
   230→
   231→    let triples = self.getTriples(entity: id)
   232→    guard !triples.isEmpty else { return ["id": id] }
   233→
   234→    var result: [String: Any] = ["id": id]
   235→
   236→    // Group triples by attribute
   237→    let triplesByAttr = Dictionary(grouping: triples) { $0.attributeId }
   238→
   239→    for (attrId, attrTriples) in triplesByAttr {
   240→        guard let attr = attrsStore.getAttr(attrId) else { continue }
   241→        let label = attr.forwardIdentity.count > 2 ? attr.forwardIdentity[2] : attrId
   242→
   243→        if attr.valueType == .ref {
   244→            // Skip links not in includedLinks (if specified)
   245→            if let includedLinks = includedLinks, !includedLinks.contains(label) {
   246→                continue
   247→            }
   248→
   249→            // Resolve linked entities with cycle detection
   250→            var resolvedRefs: [[String: Any]] = []
   251→            for triple in attrTriples {
   252→                if case .ref(let targetId) = triple.value {
   253→                    let childObj = resolve(
   254→                        id: targetId,
   255→                        attrsStore: attrsStore,
   256→                        depth: depth + 1,
   257→                        maxDepth: maxDepth,
   258→                        includedLinks: includedLinks,
   259→                        visited: &visited  // Pass visited set
   260→                    )
   261→                    // Skip ghost entities (only have "id")
   262→                    if childObj.count > 1 {
   263→                        resolvedRefs.append(childObj)
   264→                    }
   265→                }
   266→            }
   267→
   268→            // Handle cardinality
   269→            if attr.cardinality == .one || attr.isUnique == true {
   270→                result[label] = resolvedRefs.first
   271→            } else {
   272→                result[label] = resolvedRefs
   273→            }
   274→        } else {
   275→            // Non-ref attributes: take most recent value
   276→            if let latestTriple = attrTriples.max(by: { $0.createdAt < $1.createdAt }) {
   277→                result[label] = latestTriple.value.rawValue
   278→            }
   279→        }
   280→    }
   281→
   282→    // Resolve reverse links with cycle detection
   283→    if depth < maxDepth, let entityType = attrsStore.getEntityType(forEntityId: id) {
   284→        let reverseAttrs = attrsStore.revIdents[entityType] ?? [:]
   285→
   286→        for (reverseLabel, attr) in reverseAttrs {
   287→            if let includedLinks = includedLinks, !includedLinks.contains(reverseLabel) {
   288→                continue
   289→            }
   290→
   291→            let reverseTriples = getReverseRefs(entityId: id, attributeId: attr.id)
   292→            var resolvedParents: [[String: Any]] = []
   293→
   294→            for triple in reverseTriples {
   295→                let parentObj = resolve(
   296→                    id: triple.entityId,
   297→                    attrsStore: attrsStore,
   298→                    depth: depth + 1,
   299→                    maxDepth: maxDepth,
   300→                    includedLinks: includedLinks,
   301→                    visited: &visited  // Pass visited set
   302→                )
   303→                if parentObj.count > 1 {
   304→                    resolvedParents.append(parentObj)
   305→                }
   306→            }
   307→
   308→            if attr.cardinality == .one || attr.isUnique == true {
   309→                result[reverseLabel] = resolvedParents.first
   310→            } else {
   311→                result[reverseLabel] = resolvedParents
   312→            }
   313→        }
   314→    }
   315→
   316→    return result
   317→}
   318→
   319→// Convenience overload that creates the visited set
   320→public func resolve(
   321→    id: String,
   322→    attrsStore: AttrsStore,
   323→    depth: Int = 0,
   324→    maxDepth: Int = 5,
   325→    includedLinks: Set<String>? = nil
   326→) -> [String: Any] {
   327→    var visited = Set<String>()
   328→    return resolve(
   329→        id: id,
   330→        attrsStore: attrsStore,
   331→        depth: depth,
   332→        maxDepth: maxDepth,
   333→        includedLinks: includedLinks,
   334→        visited: &visited
   335→    )
   336→}
   337→```

   370→## Priority 2: TripleStore Garbage Collection
   371→
   372→### Problem
   373→
   374→**File:** `Sources/SharingInstant/InstantDependency.swift`
   375→
   376→```swift
   377→private enum InstantReactorKey: DependencyKey {
   378→    static let liveValue = Reactor(store: SharedTripleStore())  // Singleton - never GC'd
   379→}
   380→```
   381→
   382→The TripleStore grows unboundedly with no eviction mechanism.
   383→
   384→### TypeScript Reference
   385→
   386→**File:** `instant/client/packages/core/src/utils/PersistedObject.ts` (Lines 350-472)
   387→
   388→```javascript
   389→// GC Configuration
   390→export type GCOpts = {
   391→  maxSize: number;     // Maximum total size in bytes
   392→  maxAgeMs: number;    // Maximum age before eligible for GC
   393→  maxEntries: number;  // Maximum number of entries
   394→};
   395→
   396→// GC Algorithm (4 phases)
   397→private async _gc() {
   398→  // Phase 1: Remove orphaned keys (in storage but not in meta)
   399→  for (const key of keys) {
   400→    if (sacredKeys.has(key) || key in meta.objects) continue;
   401→    promises.push(this._persister.removeItem(key));
   402→  }
   403→
   404→  // Phase 2: Remove entries older than maxAgeMs
   405→  for (const [k, m] of Object.entries(meta.objects)) {
   406→    if (!sacredKeys.has(k) && m.updatedAt < now - this._gcOpts.maxAgeMs) {
   407→      promises.push(this._persister.removeItem(k));
   408→      delete meta.objects[k];
   409→    }
   410→  }
   411→
   412→  // Phase 3: Enforce maxEntries limit (LRU by updatedAt)
   413→  const entries = Object.entries(meta.objects).sort((a, b) =>
   414→    a[1].updatedAt - b[1].updatedAt
   415→  );
   416→  const deletable = entries.filter(([x]) => !sacredKeys.has(x));
   417→  if (entries.length > this._gcOpts.maxEntries) {
   418→    for (const [k] of deletable.slice(0, entries.length - this._gcOpts.maxEntries)) {
   419→      promises.push(this._persister.removeItem(k));
   420→      delete meta.objects[k];
   421→    }
   422→  }
   423→
   424→  // Phase 4: Enforce maxSize limit (LRU by updatedAt)
   425→  let currentSize = entries.reduce((acc, [_, m]) => acc + m.size, 0);
   426→  while (currentSize > this._gcOpts.maxSize && deletable.length) {
   427→    const [[k, m]] = deletable.splice(0, 1);
   428→    currentSize -= m.size;
   429→    promises.push(this._persister.removeItem(k));
   430→    delete meta.objects[k];
   431→  }
   432→}
   433→```
